New to politics, I want to be a strong voice for residents who feel ignored. I'll work to tackle potholes and dangerous pavements, stop HGVs cutting through minor roads, and speed up roadworks to avoid gridlock.

I’m married with 3 grown up children and 5 grandchildren. I grew up and have lived in the Orpington area all my adult life and my family all live locally. My mother is a former Councillor for Crofton and Farnborough. After working as a fireman in the London Fire Brigade, I joined the P&O Group and eventually became a Director. In 2006 I took early retirement and have since worked for both National and local charities.

Having lived in Petts Wood & Knoll all my life, this community means everything to me. As a young candidate, I bring a fresh perspective and the energy to stand up for our area and its future. Through my work in the transport and infrastructure sector, I understand the importance of reliable and efficient services.

I know the everyday concerns residents face, and I will fight to help bring down the cost of living, improve safety on our streets, support local businesses, ease pressure on local services and ensure that your voices are heard. It’s time for practical, common-sense leadership that delivers real results for our ward, our borough and our country.

A local resident for over forty years I am passionate about giving residents a strong voice on Bromley Council.
As a self-employed professional with extensive community volunteering experience I will challenge waste, stand up for small businesses and push for fairer central government funding to help reduce Council Tax.

Ben is a second-year university student who has lived in Bromley all his life and attended local schools. He is the Bromley Liberal Democrats youth representative and is passionate about issues affecting young people, including crime, employment and public transport. Ben is also committed to protecting local green spaces in Petts Wood & Knoll. He is standing to ensure young people’s voices are heard and to support a greener, safer local community.

Source: https://www.bromleylibdems.org.uk/2026-bromley-council-elections/our-candidates

I am a retired civil servant and have lived in the area for over 40 years. I have been involved in many local groups over the years, such as scouting and parent teacher associations and am now an active member of the U3A. I have many years' experience representing colleagues as a trade union representative and believe my experience would prove useful in representing Petts Wood & Knoll residents.

I have been a Bromley resident for nearly 20 years where I live with my husband and three daughters who attend local primary and secondary schools. I teach psychology and criminology at a number of UK universities. Lifelong learning is very close to my heart, and I am currently studying for a degree in Environmental Sciences (partly to equip myself with facts regarding the increasing misinformation spread largely by fossil fuel industries regarding the climate crisis).

Since my youth, I have been active and involved in a range of campaign groups and organisations (stop racism and anti-fascism groups, Amnesty International, Bromley for Europe etc.)  As part of the Green Party, we campaigned for 20mph outside schools and safer streets, against the expansion of Biggin Hill airport, and supported efforts for a second confirmatory Brexit referendum. Being an active member in the community, I was also one of the founding members of “Friends of Widmore Green Spaces”, thus know about the need and benefits of community groups.

My overall current concerns relate to deep structural inequalities in our society and how any austerity measures and “cuts” disproportionally affect the poor and most disadvantaged. This is reflected also at council level. Any problems in our society are blamed on immigrants or refugees, the disabled or any other marginalised group rather than looking at the actual causes of these problems (reckless gambling by financial institutions, Brexit, the “mini budget”, decades long underfunding of public services etc.). This divisive narrative is detrimental to our society and community cohesion, and I strongly reject these views.

The climate crisis is inextricably linked with social justice as those disadvantaged will be disproportionally affected by any climate impacts.
The following aims are some of my priorities:
•	Listen to residents’ concerns
•	Accurate and comprehensive monitoring of air pollution (across the borough including Biggin Hill airport)
•	Building a more sustainable and climate resilient borough (e.g. by using green infrastructure such as green walls and roofs, installation of green screens, increasing tree planting programmes)
•	Provide more social housing and fund hostels for rough sleepers with the overall aim to end rough sleeping by 2030 (in line with the Mayor of London’s pledge)
•	Support small local businesses by investing in green renewable energy schemes and promote a local economy strategy
•	Reintroduce vital mental health services; invest in more community and youth services
•	Zero tolerance on discrimination and racism
•	Protect our wildlife and their habitats, our green spaces, our parks and our mature trees
•	Introduce more 20 mph zones which will save lives by reducing accidents and cutting pollution
•	Lobby for better bus services and co-ordination in the south of the borough, and provide better linked and safer cycle lanes

I am standing for fairer and greener communities. #HopeNotHate

Thomas was born in Bromley and has lived in Petts Wood his whole life. He is currently a student in London, commuting from the borough while also working in a local café in Petts Wood. Thomas is passionate about youth services and became involved in local politics after seeing the impact of cuts on young people. He also cares deeply about the environment and is standing to help keep Petts Wood green, clean, and vibrant.

Source: https://www.bromleylibdems.org.uk/2026-bromley-council-elections/our-candidates

“Hi, I’m Mary Ion and I’m running to be your representative for Bexley and Bromley on the London Assembly.

I’m excited to stand in these elections to highlight Green thinking that can deliver real change for Londoners to make our city more people friendly and resilient.

Every day as a mental health nurse I see the impact that the pandemic is having on people. Many are struggling to manage on low incomes and with uncertainty for the future.

I tend to see things through a public health lens and I think that Green Party policies which see people as part of their environment provide solid solutions.

We need a new way of doing things that will protect the health of Londoners by reducing pollution and providing more financial security.

I’d like to see a rapid move away from polluting cars with more inclusive space for walking and cycling that gives everyone the chance to move around under their own steam.

We know that air pollution is killing people. In places like Bromley and Bexley we have an excess of car use. There’s a real opportunity here to transform our local neighbourhoods and make them more people friendly.

The time has come for Universal Basic Income to provide a secure financial base for everyone during these times of uncertainty as we transition away from fossil fuels and towards more automation.

I’d like to see a trial of UBI in London now that the pandemic has reinforced that this is less a fringe idea and more of a necessity.

Sian and Caroline have been working really hard to deliver change. I’m hopeful that we can get more Greens on the assembly and do even more to make London the greenest city in the world.

I'm standing as a candidate for Reform UK in the 7 May local elections in Plaistow Ward, Bromley.

With 30 years’ experience in IT and finance, I have previously served as a Bromley Councillor (2018-2022), which I enjoyed immensely giving back to my community. I served as Vice Chairman of both the Pensions Committee and the Renewal, Recreation and Housing Committee, and also worked locally with residents in improving the area and standing up for our community.

I am committed to fiscal competence via oversight and scrutiny of Bromley’s expenditure, standing up strongly for Plaistow residents, and working with local Police in keeping our borough safe.

I will support local Plaistow businesses, and ensure Bromley is a great place for young people to grow up, learn, start careers, and raise a family. I strongly value preserving Bromley’s green spaces, which make Bromley such a fantastic place to live.

I’m a dedicated public service policy expert who knows what good and bad council policy looks like.

Like many, I’ve experienced challenges in life, from living as someone who is partially deaf, to facing housing insecurity during Covid after standing up to my landlord over problems with my home.

That’s why I’m standing - to help you and your family tackle unfairness in your lives.

I am honoured to stand as a candidate for Reform UK in the constituency I have called home for nearly three decades. Beckenham & Penge is a vibrant and diverse community, encompassing residents from all walks of life. I am deeply committed to ensuring that every voice is heard - a right that has significantly diminished over the past two decades under successive Conservative and Labour governments.

Having experienced life as a single parent, small business owner, and taxpayer, I believe my background reflects the experiences of many in our community. This enables me to more realistically articulate the interests and concerns of the constituents I wish to represent.

The decline we have all witnessed is profoundly troubling. Unsustainable mass immigration, the economic strain caused by soaring taxes and the exorbitant rise in the cost of food, housing & energy bills. Declining public services with millions languishing on NHS waiting lists, in some cases for years not to mention the almost impossibility of getting a face to face with a GP, to the absurd wokeism that has infected our institutions including our Police, schools & universities.

On top of this we have the nonsensical blind charge towards a completely foolhardy and impossible to achieve net zero target. This will only serve to impoverish the most vulnerable in society and make our nation poorer and less productive.

The challenges we face are severe and urgent.

Politicians of the two main Party’s have proven over many, many decades to be arrogant, inept, out of touch, blatantly dishonest and ultimately dismissive of the wishes of the British public to be trusted any longer. In short I believe we have all been taken for fools for far too long and it’s about time we said enough!

Reform UK is the only Party to offer common sense policies based on the needs of the people rather than on ridiculous virtue signalling ideologies that have no meaning whatsoever to the vast majority of British citizens

I’ve been jogging the streets of Shortlands for years – long before I decided to stand for election. You might know me from walking Kosmo on Queensmead Rec (he's the one who never goes anywhere without his ball thrower). I'm also the Site Secretary at Shortlands Allotment – where I’ve somehow managed to grow beetroot, sweet potato and bell peppers.

I was born and raised in East Dulwich, and I’ve called Shortlands home since 2020. I’m a Chartered Management Accountant and spent four years living and working in Belgium.

For the last 10 years I’ve been working as a finance director at one of the world’s leading sustainability and climate advisory firms, so I understand how to deliver long-term value and, most importantly, make money work for residents — not just contractors.

I know this isn't where the Greens usually win. But I believe residents here want a candidate who tells the truth, brings fresh ideas, and works hard for the area — not someone expecting an easy ride.

We need a council that actually invests in our area and plans properly for the future – from our parks to our high streets – not continued decline.

I support the Green Party because protecting our local businesses, community and environment isn’t extreme – it’s common sense.

During this election campaign I'll be running every street in this ward, listening to residents. If you see me, stop me for a chat – I’d love to meet you.

This election is about restoring common sense at a local level. I will be a strong local voice for you and ensure that your best interests are served at the council. I will work to protect our green spaces from unsuitable housing developments, improve the quality of our roads and support measures which cut crime and tackle anti-social behaviour.

I'm Jake Rest, and I've lived here in St Mary Cray my entire life. I know this community, and I’m ready to fight for the things that matter most to you.

As your council representative, I'll be your direct line to action on everyday issues that affect your life. I'll tackle the smaller things that make a real difference: maintaining our local infrastructure, making St Mary Cray safer for everyone and protecting our green spaces.

My name is Shenis Hassan, and I'm a local Goffs Oak resident seeking to become one of your local councillors this year.

Although James grew up in Shepherd’s Bush, he has proudly called Broxbourne home since 2010. He has built his career in senior partnership and strategy roles across the telecoms and retail sectors, bringing a practical, results-driven approach to everything he does.

There’s a saying: “You are a product of your environment.” James believes this applies at every level. By improving the environment in Broxbourne and beyond, we can create stronger communities and a better quality of life for everyone.

The council protects its tax purse, asking for more annually whilst delivering passable services. It's stale and it's inefficient.

Key Issues:
Affordable Housing: With the new Local Plan review beginning this year, I will push for developments that prioritize genuinely affordable homes for local people, ensuring they meet high environmental standards to keep energy bills low.

Road Safety: As someone who walks to work locally, I see the danger posed by speeding firsthand. I will advocate for more pedestrian crossings and speed cameras in high-risk areas to ensure our streets are safe for everyone.

I joined the Labour Party to make a real difference. Growing up, I was a young carer until the age of 15, when I tragically lost my mum to a failing NHS and a broken social care system. If elected as your Labour councillor, I will work to restore and empower our community through a new era of co-operativism—putting people before profit, and rebuilding from the ground.

I live in the Hoddesdon Town and Rye Park ward and am very passionate about our town and surroundings. I am a third generation Hoddesdonian and love living in our town. I believe that our council is not doing enough with regards to:

* Protecting our green spaces and ensuring local infrastructure is fit for purpose

* Scrutinising council spending and having more robust financial projections

* Working to tackle anti-social behaviour and supporting vulnerable youngsters to find positive influences and constructive activities

I want to listen to my fellow Hoddesdonians, so that I can work on what is important for all of us.

I have lived in Cheshunt for nearly 11 years and I now work in corporate affairs for a national trade association representing the British businesses underpinned by heritage crafts, a vital sector that supports over half a million skilled workers and contributes £81 billion to our economy. I joined the Labour Party in 2017, driven by a growing frustration with the deepening inequalities in society and the continued erosion of our public services under Conservative leadership. Everyone deserves the opportunity to thrive, not just the wealthy few. I have lived in Cheshunt all my life and care deeply about the future of our community. I am standing as a Green Party candidate because I believe local politics should focus on supporting residents, bringing people together, and protecting the environment we all rely on.

I work in IT in the public transport sector, supporting essential public services, and understand the importance of practical, reliable systems that work for everyday people. Outside of work, I enjoy walking and bird watching and regularly visit local nature reserves, which has strengthened my commitment to protecting green spaces.

I am standing to offer residents a positive and compassionate alternative in local politics, with a focus on protecting green spaces, tackling fly tipping, improving local services, and supporting safer neighbourhoods in Rosedale and Bury Green.

I believe local representatives should be approachable, listen to residents, and work constructively to improve the community.

My name is Fabio Bonfante and I have lived in Waltham Cross for almost all of my life.

Whilst I count myself lucky to live here, I am becoming increasingly concerned with many issues facing my town and my borough. Sadly, with the area being a ‘safe zone’ for the Conservatives, as long as I have lived here, Waltham Cross in particular is paid very little attention by any level of local government.

Congestion on Broxbourne’s roads is becoming unmanageable, particularly in Waltham Cross and Cheshunt. It is increasingly difficult to do basic things such as get to the shops or drop children off to school. Sometimes a ten minute journey across the borough can take an hour! We have seen a building boom over the last few years, with the Conservative council approving more and more new large scale developments, but without accompanying improvement to our our roads and transport systems. Our bus network is patchy and infrequent, leaving some of our most vulnerable people unable to move about. 

Our rail links into London are vital for our local economy and commuters in Waltham Cross deserve more frequent and better quality services in to and out of London, I want to see our roads and public transport properly planned for, looked after and funded, not neglected. 

Whilst it is important that we build affordable and decent homes for our residents, development has to be sustainable and put the needs of locals first, this is something I want to fight hard for. I recently spoke with some of the elderly in Broxbourne, who told me that they remember a time when the Conservatives had an opposition in the council; I and my fellow Broxbourne Liberal Democrats want to be that opposition and an effective voice to oppose Conservative plans when they don’t represent the interests of our residents.

I want to contribute to our area, rather than just complain, which is why I am standing for election as your next borough Councillor in May.

I want to get the very best for our area, making sure your needs and rights are not compromised and at the same time working hard to create opportunity for us all, securing the future of where we all live. 

So if you have a problem or an improvement you would like to see locally, please get in touch with me, I’d love to hear your thoughts.

As well as fighting climate change, Martin believes that reducing inequality and changing housing policy to deliver more social housing are key priorities locally and nationally. If elected, he'll also campaign for bringing all utility businesses back into the public sector. Martin says " At this election, there's little to choose between Labour and the Conservatives, with both offering little more than rising inequality and continued environmental destruction. In contrast, in the Green Party we offer real hope for real change, with sustainable policies that will progressively reduce poverty and homelessness and increase everyone's quality of life".

We can all see that ‘the system’ is broken. The Green Party wants to try to bring in a fairer system — where we work in tandem with the planet to try to stop the headlong rush to humanity’s extinction.

I will work hard for the people of Shelf and Northowram ward, whilst trying to influence broader council policy across Calderdale, inline with the aims of the Green Party, and my personal deeply held belief in strong, well funded public services, welfare for those in need and fairness and dignity in public service.

I've got over 20 years experience working as a software developer and technical manager at board level across a wealth of local and multinational companies. I help out with local community events, including squirrel club, and previously scouts.

I was raised in Pepper Hill from birth, and have lived here for most of my life. I own a home in the ward and intend to do my level best to improve the lives of others in the ward.

Peter Judge is the Labour Party’s Prospective Council Candidate for Rastrick Ward in the May 2021 Local Elections.

He is a lifelong socialist, and lifelong member of the Labour Party, who recently stood to be the Labour Party’s West Yorkshire Mayoral Candidate, and brought differing ideas, such as an all-Yorkshire devolution deal.

He also served as a Labour and Co-operative councillor on Calderdale Council in the 1990’s and worked in local government for 23 years of his career.

party_name: The Official Monster Raving Loony Party

statement_to_voters:
Adam Wilkinson is one of our three Labour councillors for Sowerby Bridge ward – a position he has held for 9 years.

He is the Cabinet Member for Children and Young People on Calderdale Council and is a qualified teacher. He has also worked in the NHS and in the private sector, but now works as Office Manager to Holly Lynch, the Member of Parliament for Halifax, as well as carrying out his Cabinet role.

He is involved with a number of local community groups and sits on the Sowerby Bridge Development Board. When he is not working he enjoys running, and has raised money for several charities in recent years.

I've lived in Todmorden for 20 years and I work in Manchester as a solicitor so I share with many Todmorden residents the impact of an underfunded and disorganised railway service. 

I want to be a labour councilor as only Labour will protect Todmorden residents from the impact of Conservative cuts and Universal Credit which are causing hardship and suffering for many. If you elect me, I will be working with my Labour colleagues to ensure that, despite the financial challenges we face as a council, we continue to do our best to invest in and support our local community, 

When I'm not working or campaigning I enjoy caving, cycling and watching Rugby League. I live in Medowbottom with my partner and hens. 

I look forward to meeting you and hope you will vote for me in May.

I am standing for the Green Party in Todmorden West because I want to be a voice for fairness, action and real change - not more of the same.

I’m one of the founders of POD, the community car-share in Todmorden and Hebden Bridge. I pushed for a £1 subscription for low-income residents because I believe access to transport and essential services should never depend on your income.

I’ve also worked directly with Calderdale Council and local groups to expand shared transport in our valley. That’s exactly the kind of practical, community-led solution the Greens want to scale up across Calderdale, making it easier and more affordable for people to live their everyday lives.

I don’t just talk about change. I’ve already been delivering it locally. Now I want to bring that same approach into Calderdale Council: backing local projects like community transport, fighting for better and more reliable buses, and creating joined-up services that actually work for people.

Alongside other Green candidate, we want to push to rebuild youth services through local hubs, bring empty buildings back into use, and make sure investment reaches the communities that need it most.

I’m proud of our diverse and welcoming community in Todmorden. And I’m proud to stand for a party that prioritises people, not background or income.

I’ll work hard to make sure everyone feels supported, represented, and able to get around easily, whoever you are, and wherever you live.

I moved to the area 3 years ago and noticed the much higher Council tax straight away. I am committed to ensuring value for public money and access to quality services for all. In particular, I am passionate about the beautiful character of this area and protecting our green spaces which we are so lucky to have.

Im passionate about my local community and having moving back to Todmorden after university I really want to make a change to my local area.

I got involved in politics as a result of the effect of austerity on my family, and as a community we still face the brunt of this catastrophe. Fly tipping, disappearing youth services and unreliable public transport.

I’m standing as a Councillor to fight for renters, young people, those under represented, and for a Green Todmorden.

As a young person I believe I can bring a fresh perspective into local government where younger perspectives been left out.

Diana Tremayne is Labour’s candidate for Todmorden, replacing Cllr Steve Sweeney who has represented the ward since 2012.

Diana writes:

“I love living in Todmorden and having already served as a town councillor I would welcome the opportunity to serve the local community further if elected as a Calderdale councillor. It was a pleasure to be able to support so many local groups when I was on the Town Council and I am proud to have taken the lead in declaring a climate emergency in 2019. Environmental and sustainability issues have always been important to me and as a mum of a teenage daughter this is something I feel even more strongly about now. This means supporting our local community and businesses through small actions like litter picking, gardening and shopping locally, as well as reducing the effects of climate change and issues such as the flooding we have faced here in Todmorden.

“I’m passionate about educational opportunities for all ages and am really keen to help promote these in Todmorden using my skills and experience in education. This was the reason I got involved with the Todmorden Learning Centre project and I’m excited at the prospect of the asset transfer in the coming months.

“The council faces huge challenges after a decade of austerity and the current pandemic but has maintained key services and shown a real commitment to the most vulnerable in society. If elected I look forward to the opportunity to work hard for the town with my Labour colleagues Silvia Dacre and Susan Press in the years to come.”

I've loved living in Calderdale for 18 years, and am keen to offer my skills and experience to support my community. I work on disability and environmental issues, as well as peace, and social justice campaigns while living with a chronic illness. I'm involved with local singing, dancing, hiking and environmental groups.

As your green councillor I will:

* Speak up and campaign for an improvement in local services and amenities so they can be accessible to ALL residents, * Fight to ensure that development in our area is appropriate and sustainable with a council commitment to renewable energy and green technologies. * Promote and encourage communication,  kindness, and inclusion in our communities.

* Prioritise an efficient, affordable and accessible public transport system. * Work hard to promote local initiatives to help combat climate change and flooding. * Help to grow the local green economy through supporting local business and social enterprises.

In the current climate of austerity, apathy and despair the green party offer hope of a more positive caring future.

Rosy Ansell is the 2026 Liberal Democrat Candidate for Abbey Ward. Rosy has lived in Abbey Ward for several years with her family.

If elected to the city council, Rosy will work alongside the Cheney Payne and the Lib Dem team to fight for a fair deal for our city.

I’m standing as your candidate to give working people in Cambridge a real voice. Abbey faces inequality and rising costs, it needs more council homes and community-led decisions. As a local engineer and trade unionist, I see the struggles of the workers who keep this city running. I will fight for residents, not developers or the super-rich. A vote for me is a vote for practical change, fair housing, and representatives who put working people first.

We have the unique legacy of trade unionist and Communist Party branch secretary Ronald Rolph in our ward. He joined the International Brigades and joined the medical auxillery during the Spanish Civil war. Upon returning to Cambridge, he continued to fight for housing, wages and working class involvement in council decisions. Ronald Rolph Court is named for him and his legacy.

A VOICE FOR WORKING PEOPLE
The Communist Party has never been for sale. We cannot be bought-off or silenced. Britain’s Communist MPs and councillors have always stood with working people.

INVEST IN THE PEOPLE OF ABBEY
Abbey needs jobs, housing and investment. We need a council that plans for the benefit of workers, not profiteers and landlords. Let’s build a people’s Cambridge!

FIXING OUR NEGLECTED CITY
Abbey has seen better days. We need planned growth, real community input, and democratic public control and accountability. We deserve better!

I work for my community not just because it is personally rewarding, but also because I believe that together we can change a deeply unjust and unequal society. Living in Abbey for the past 12 years has been one of the greatest joys of my life. I want to join our hard-working team of councillors to continue doing what I can for our local community and environment.

I’m well prepared for casework. I volunteer for Citizens Advice, so I’m already familiar with the challenges of benefits, food banks and housing in Cambridge. I’m also already embedded in Abbey community life. On the steering committee of the Riverside Area Residents’ Association, I’m spearheading a biodiversity project at the Cellarer’s Chequer and helping develop a vision for the future of Riverside. Together with a fantastic group of locals, I’m setting up a charity to restore the deconsecrated church of St Andrew the Less and turn it into a space for community, heritage and biodiversity.

Abbey is a special place, with great people, that has been labelled the ‘most deprived ward’ in Cambridge for too long. I believe it takes all of us who have the opportunity to make a change – that is why I’m stepping up.

Some priorities for Abbey:

Housing and Cost of Living - I volunteer for Cambridge Citizens Advice every week.  What comes up time after time are housing and cost of living issues.  Abbey residents struggle with substandard council homes, rogue landlords, overcrowded HMOs, fuel poverty, food insecurity and mounting debt.  As your councillor I will not only work with residents to help solve their individual problems, but also work to create a fairer system.

Listening and Acting - I recently spoke at a council meeting as a resident deeply concerned about the direction Cambridge’s development is taking.  The evasive and irrelevant answer I was given proved that I was not being taken seriously.  I will never let that happen when I am a councillor.  I will listen and I will respond honestly and proactively.

Community and Green Spaces - About a year ago I began to work to save an abandoned church on the Newmarket Road for community use (see how far we’ve got!  www.standrewtheless.org).  Abbey needs community spaces so we can get together as neighbours again.  I want a vibrant Abbey with places to meet, learn, eat well and relax together.  And I want a beautiful and green Abbey with more nature and space to breathe.

About Me:

I’m standing to be your local Labour councillor for Abbey because I believe Abbey deserves practical action on the cost of living crisis.  Housing stress being the primary driver of this.

My Background

I’ve spent my career working at the heart of decision-making—advising senior Labour politicians, working in devolved government, and helping organisations navigate complex policy challenges.

Today, I work in the aerospace sector, supporting growth, skills, and world leading research to move this highly polluting sector forward on its net-zero journey—experience I will bring to delivering for Abbey.

Why I’m Standing

Like many people in Abbey, I see both the potential and the pressures in our area:

The need for more genuinely affordable housing.

Pressure on local services and infrastructure.

Concerns about roads, potholes, and day-to-day maintenance.

Making sure new investment reaches every part of our community.

The Labour run council is a national leader in building homes for those who need them most, I want to be part of a group standing up for Cambridge and building rather than blocking.
David Smith is your Abbey candidate; he has lived in Cambridge for nearly 40 years and works for Cambridge University Press.

Robert is firmly against the Congestion Charge and is standing both for City and County Council positions. 

Robert is campaigning -Against the proposed Congestion Charge: He organised an open meeting in March with Cambridge residents to discuss this and is holding an open meeting on 26th April in Arbury to discuss residents' concerns

-For Better Roads: Road maintenance is a top priority for Robert, as he is also standing for County Council. This includes fixing potholes, improving road markings and reversing road closures such as the vital Mill Road bridge. 

-For Better Buses: Robert is determined to secure better buses for Arbury. He will fight for the city 1 route, which many elderly people in Arbury rely on. 

Promoted by Timothy Haire on behalf of Robert Boorman, both of 28 Stanley Court, Cambridge CB5 8LW.

I wish to represent the diverse, dynamic community which comprises Arbury. From 2017-2021 I represented Arbury in Cambridgeshire County Council, and know Arbury well having lived in North Cambridge for some 15 years. I have also been a City Councillor (2021-2023) so have experience in both City and County, which is useful in supporting residents with concerns and issues that fit into the City responsibilities or into those for County.

As a councillor, I worked hard in the interests of residents. Amongst other campaigns and achievements, I worked with (then) County Councillor Claire Richards to save Castle Mound and the Shire Hall Green Space around it, so that we could all enjoy access in perpetuity to this important Cambridge landmark - and we won! I also worked on issues such as parking on verges and green spaces, chaired Milton Road Project Local Liaison Forum (LLF) ensuring that the residents' plan for the roadway, footpaths and verges, retaining the trees and gaining more, was implemented instead of the Greater Cambridge Partnership (GCP)'s plan. In this, I ensured that the residents were fully participating members of the LLF, through their residents associations. I also worked with Cllr Mike Todd-Jones and Lilian Runblad (chair and vice chair, Histon Road Project LLF), and with residents who were fully involved as LLF members. I worked with Labour City and County Councillors for more funding for road and pavement repairs, and keeping street lights on, and worked with residents on getting more lights where the changes to street light left great pools of darkness. I am 'at the ready' to work for Arbury, have already held site visits to secure Akeman Street and Darwin Drive on the list for resurfacing and if elected will work to ensure that it is the interests and voices of residents, and your concerns, that are at the heart of my work.

I studied at Cambridge University, am a Barrister and Human Rights Lawyer admitted to practice in all Australian jurisdictions (states and territories), and am practicing at the Bar of England and Wales as a member of the Inner Temple. A writer and filmmaker, my books include Wage Rage for Equal Pay, Different Lives, Women and the Law, Breaking Through, and Taking a Stand. My films include The Incredible Woman and A Greenshell Necklace (with Karen Buczynski-Lee), and Covered - A DVD Installation in 3 streams.

Green spaces, good health, safety and wellbeing for all are the values I will promote and support, together with ensuring Arbury residents' voice is heard in City Council work if elected - and, recognising children's right to play, will and establish playparks in Arbury, including the Arbury Court playpark, a playpark at Brackley Close and Kingsway, and safety for children playing on green-grassed spaces near roads such as Perse Way, Rutland Close and around Arbury.

Fionna grew up in Victoria Park and now lives in the centre of Arbury with her own young family.

After graduating from the University of York, Fionna spent eighteen months working in financial services. She then moved to Southern Mexico to work on a project strengthening community tourism in deprived rural areas. At the conclusion of the project, Fionna moved to Denver, Colorado to work for President Obama's re-election campaign as a Field Organiser.

Fionna returned to the UK at the end of 2012 and took a position as Campaign Advisor to Julian Huppert, Member of Parliament for Cambridge. In September 2013 she began working in Parliament for Martin Horwood MP.

Since 2015 she has worked as a policy adviser, first in Foreign Affairs and now, since the EU referendum, in Foreign Affairs and Brexit.

She now works as a global public health advocate and also wants to give back to the community she grew up in and where she is raising her children.

Fionna is particularly passionate about the future of Arbury Court - and protecting playgrounds and parks in our area.

Fionna says, “We need real change for Arbury. For too long Labour have been taking North Cambridge for granted. As a local Arbury resident, I will listen to you and ensure our area’s voice is heard on the City Council.”

favourite_biscuit: I'll take whichever one you offer me.
statement_to_voters:
**They want to confuse you by endorsing all kinds of weird causes, so you forget what's really at stake: you.**

As the Greens, LibDems and Labour, the parties that dominate Cambridge, sink more and more into populist stunts and extreme ideology, what do you think about it? What hopes can you have for your future, your family’s future, your security...when it all lies in the hands of people who are trying to impress their fans through irrational, foolish acts bordering on sedition?

How safe are your interests in their hands? While you despair about the potholes, crime and dismal infrastructure in your areas, they are screaming at demonstrations in solidarity with various dodgy overseas organisations and regimes, dancing with strippers, clowning around.

I’ve spoken to a lot of people in our ward who are very worried. The only way to overcome this is: **don’t put your future in their hands.**

You've voted for them for years, but lately they have grown feral. Your needs, your concerns, your future? Not interesting. They have bigger fish to fry. Have you seen their antics? The things they say, sometimes behind closed doors, sometimes not? The people they associate with? Do you still think you can trust them? Perhaps you haven’t seen or heard? Would you care to look into it? You’ll be shocked! Do your research, ask around: it’s all out there. Time for a change, before it’s too late. Democracy is not about picking your favourite team or colour. It’s about ensuring you are represented by people who will fight your corner.

Trust me, I’m a doctor. I’ve been fighting for people’s lives for 25 years.

Vote for me, Dr. Khalid, on 7 May 2026. I’m not for any party. I’m Independent. For Castle, for our community, our families, our future.

Luke first moved to Cambridge for university after growing up in Northern Ireland.

He returned to the city after a year working in Brussels, and decided to make Castle his home on Windsor Road.

In Northern Ireland, Luke was involved in campaigns to improve young people’s mental health, mitigate the impact of Brexit, and build a shared community.

Luke works in Cambridge University supporting young people from under- privileged backgrounds to access higher education.

Luke also volunteers with a local scout group, enabling young people to  gain skills for life. From working in Brussels on UK-EU affairs, Luke knows the harm Brexit has done, and is a tireless advocate for rejoining the EU.

Luke loves the green spaces of Castle and our vibrant community. You’ll often spot him at ParkRun at Eddington Lake or catching up with friends at the Castle Inn.

As a local resident, Luke is delighted to be standing up for his neighbours in Castle Ward as the Lib Dem candidate in May’s election.

1. I am against reintroducing congestion charges.
2. I will defend and maintain green spaces and children's playgrounds.
3. I will curb antisocial behaviour, e.g. very fast and dangerous driving in Cambridge.

I originally moved to Cambridge to study psychology and quickly grew to love this city and community. Now, as your Green Party candidate for Castle ward, I am campaigning for social and environmental justice.

Cambridge is a city of incredible resources and affluence, but remains one of the most unequal cities in the UK. We need to work harder to ensure that everyone in our community benefits from that success. Bridging the “town and gown” divide by breaking down barriers between the university and local residents will lead to a more united and fairer Cambridge. I am also dedicated to protecting our vital green spaces in Castle and across Cambridge. These areas are the lifeblood of our local community and must be protected as such.

As a Castle resident for 23 years, with children educated at Mayfield and Chesterton, I understand our community and am proud to serve you as your Labour City Councillor. On 7th May, I am seeking your support for re-election to continue that work.
Over the past five years, I have worked full time as your Councillor to improve local services, strengthen community safety and promote tolerance across our diverse neighbourhoods. I am committed to restoring our natural environment, protecting chalk streams, achieving sewage-free rivers, and tackling climate change. I have decades of experience in local government, planning and development. Over the last three years as Cabinet Member for Finance and Resources I have turned a forecast deficit into a balanced budget.

I’ve called Cherry Hinton home for 11 years, and I know the power of everyday community. In 2022, I organised a Front Door Festival that brought neighbours together for the first time in decades, sharing food, music, laughter and raising funds for the Cherry Hinton Hub.

I’m standing because I believe every street can feel like that: connected, creative and caring. I dream of a Cherry Hinton where there's a Front Door Festival in every street and neighbourhood. Where neighbours know each other and share skills, tools, meals, their time and joy.
Where we hear birdsong and the buzzing of bees instead of speeding motorbikes and the youth address their trauma through art and music instead of resorting to anti-social behaviour. Where the most vulnerable are looked after, making everyone else better off for it.

My strengths lie in organising, facilitating, empathising, envisioning and building community. My background spans human‑centred design in tech and hands‑on work with organisations like Jimmy’s Cambridge, improving services for people experiencing homelessness. I understand how systems, behaviour and trauma intersect, and why kindness and community matter more than ever as we face rising costs, extreme weather and growing instability.

We’re in the same boat, facing the same storms. But when we look after each other, we’re stronger.

Together, let us build a safe, strong, fair and vibrant Cherry Hinton.
Who's with me?

My wife Carole & I have lived in Church End Cherry Hinton since 1983. We were married in St Andrew’s Church Cherry Hinton in 1978. 
I was employed as the security student liaison manager at Cambridge Regional College for 15 years before retiring from that role in 2019 and am currently working as their first aid instructor. I hold an instructor licence for Mental Health First Aid and for over 20 years have been a volunteer Community First Responder for East of England Ambulance Trust covering the Cherry Hinton area, and as volunteer trainer for their first responder scheme. I take immense pleasure in passing on life-saving skills whenever can, and some of these sessions 'Fast First Aid' I run over 90 minutes on the first Saturday of the month at our new community hub on the High Street.

I have been involved in the local community for many years in numerous ways - such as with Cherry Hinton Royal British Legion both as poppy appeal collector and resident bagpipe player at remembrance service every year, as a committee member of Cherry Hinton Residents Association, as the health & safety advisor for our community hub, with the Neighbourhood Watch – where I was chair for 10 years, the Friends of Cherry Hinton Hall, and the Friends of St Andrew’s. Of course, I have also had the honour of representing Cherry Hinton as a City Councillor since 2004 – a highlight of which was being Mayor of Cambridge in 2009/10, 2019/20 and in 2020/21.

Over the years I have been involved in many local campaigns and initiatives including securing environmental improvements, helping raise money to secure CCTV on the High Street, and more recently helping with the plans which finally delivered the excellent community hub complete with the Cherry Branch café.

I continue to be passionate about Cherry Hinton, my continued work with many residents on a wide variety of issues all year round (not just at election times!) is proof of my continued commitment to our village and its residents. We have some big challenges now, such as the risk of over-development and associated and the associated congestion and traffic problems, the proposed development of the old clay pits is an important issue on a number of levels. I would like to bring my knowledge and experience to bear on these sorts of issues. your support on 7th May will enable me to continue the support I have given over the past 22 years as a resident of Cherry Hinton, we live here to - what affects you also affects us.

I am Dr. Ahmad Rushdhi, also known as Dr. Ru or DrAR, and I am the Liberal Democrat candidate for Cherry Hinton in Cambridge. Having moved to Cambridge from Sri Lanka in 2022, I have made Cherry Hinton my home. This has provided me with the opportunity to engage closely with local residents and gain a comprehensive understanding of the critical issues affecting our community.

As a physician specializing in clinical nutrition, my professional focus is on preventive medicine and public health. I am affiliated with Addenbrooke’s Hospital and also maintain a practice in London. My work is dedicated to disease prevention and promoting healthier lifestyles through education, nutrition, and early intervention. I firmly believe that enhancing public health extends beyond healthcare services to encompass the development of robust community well-being.

Since my arrival in Cherry Hinton, I have actively participated in community life, regularly interacting with residents from diverse backgrounds, including those employed in the NHS and other essential services.

Residents have communicated several practical concerns, including traffic congestion, road maintenance and potholes, and the enhancement of neighborhood safety. I am committed to collaborating with the council, police, and community partners to address these issues and implement effective solutions.

Additionally, concerns have been raised regarding anti-social behavior in the vicinity of certain Voi e-scooter parking areas, as well as knife crime, disruptive moped noise, and theft around local supermarkets. I will work in conjunction with neighborhood police teams and residents’ associations to support coordinated action and strengthen community safety initiatives.

Public health remains a paramount passion of mine. I collaborate closely with General Practitioners and other healthcare professionals, and I aspire to promote local community health awareness programs. Furthermore, I also share health education through my social media platforms.

If elected, my priorities will be to engage with residents, foster community cohesion, and contribute to the development of a healthier, safer, and more resilient Cherry Hinton.

Dr. Ahmad Rushdhi (Dr. Ru)
Liberal Democrat Candidate – Cherry Hinton
DrArLibdem@gmail.com

Tim is the local, hardworking choice for Coleridge.

Tim is a retired parent and IT Consultant.

Tim has lived in Cambridgeshire for 40 years; Coleridge is now his permanent residence.  Tim's favourite pastime is hiking, with my wife, anywhere in the world.

If elected Tim will work with Cllr Karen Young and Parliamentary Candidate Cheney Payne to fight for a fair deal for Coleridge.

Sarah has lived in Cambridge for over 20 years. As a mother who has worked in the housing sector and as a teacher, she has observed the inequality of opportunity that is so striking in Cambridge. Sarah says "An obsession with growth has left Cambridge with threatened water supplies, a stripped-back green belt, a broken transport system, unaffordable house prices and shocking inequality. The Greens are the only local party challenging "business as usual." Our record of listening to, and working with, residents saw the Cambridge Green Party draw level for second place in the May elections. There is now a real opportunity in Cambridge to send a strong environmental message to the next government. Want Green? Vote Green!

Coleridge has been my home for over 20 years, and I have had the privilege of being a teacher to many of our young people in local schools. I have been a local councillor for over 10 years. On 7 May, I am standing for re-election so that I can continue delivering for our communities here in Coleridge.

My priorities for Coleridge:

**Build communities, not just homes.** Tackle anti-social behaviour. Champion community grants, food hubs, holiday lunches. Build a new community room and improve green spaces.

**High quality homes for all.** Continue building a new generation of green council homes, including at Fanshawe Road, so that local people have great places to live. Support residents in need with housing and address rough sleeping.

**Cheaper, easier, safer travel.** Improve Cherry Hinton Road cycleway, tackle speeding cars, scooters and e-bikes, fix potholes, fight to save the Tiger Pass, champion better buses.

I’m already working hard for Coleridge. I’ve challenged poor planning decisions, and stood up for local businesses, including shops on Cherry Hinton Road. I’ve installed outdoor gym equipment. I made sure the number of council homes built on Fanshawe and Davy is more than before (up from 52 to at least 94). I brought in the Tiger Pass for young people and free pre-9.30am travel for concessionary bus pass holders.

Most of these things started as issues raised by fellow local residents like you. We have achieved all these improvements working together. But there’s so much more to do.

I want to continue to work with you to address other local issues and secure improvements that can benefit our local community and make Coleridge an even better place to live.

Ania has lived in Cambridge since 2015. Having grown up in Poland, Ania is one of many scientists who have come to Cambridge for work and decided to make it their permanent home.

Having worked for a Cambridge-based company for the past 10 years, and now taking on a freelance role, Ania is keen to make sure that Cambridge works for everyone equitably – residents, businesses, visitors and nature.

She is also passionate about evidence-based medicine, and using best available data to make healthcare decisions.

Her love of dance led her to volunteer for a local dance society to increase access to affordable community social classes.

In her spare time, Ania is learning to play the trumpet and trains with a local club in Latin Formation dancing. Ania is also a keen cyclist and loves going on walks with her corgi.

If elected she will work with Bob Illingworth and Ian Manning to stand up for East Chesterton residents and make your voice heard.

Sarah Haithcock lives in East Chesterton and works at a local special educational needs school. She has dedicated her professional life to service and wishes to bring that same commitment to the City Council as your representative.

As your councillor, she will continue to listen to your concerns, deliver practical solutions and make our area safer, greener and fairer.

Having spoken with hundreds of residents, her key priorities for East Chesterton are:

1. Building strong and resilient communities
She will work with the community and local authorities to tackle anti-social behaviour such as drug dealing, speeding, littering and fly tipping to make East Chesterton safe for everyone.

2. High quality homes for all residents
She wants to support the building of a new generation of environmentally friendly and accessible council homes. She will support residents in need of housing and work with community groups, authorities and charities to tackle rough sleeping. She is committed to protecting renters rights and improving access to affordable homes.

3. Cheaper, easier and safer travel
She will campaign for more frequent local buses, protected cycle lanes and safer pedestrian crossings.

Sarah has been active in the community beyond her professional life. She has listened to hundreds of residents over recent years and supported individuals with their specific issues.

Her work in the community includes:

- Leading police walkabouts to identify anti-social behaviour hotspots with local authorities
- Challenging the County Council on the dimming of streetlights across the city
- Campaigning against cuts to holiday food vouchers for the most vulnerable children in our community

I am a carer, public servant (forensic scientist), trade union member, activist owner of 3 rescue cats. I was born in and grew up in Kings Hedges in a council home. I know the struggles of the working class because I live those struggles, unless you are a millionaire we are all struggling nowadays. Everything is broken and everything is more expensive. Britain is broken but not because of the migrants, it is broken due to decades of unequal wealth distribution and privatisation.
I am standing as an independent because I am fed up of the mainstream party councillors who do not live here, making decisions about us without involving or consulting us, behind closed doors. All they ever care about is showing up around election time for our vote. The other candidates just care about potholes and litter. Indeed, those are issues we need to fix but our issues in Kings Hedges go deeper than potholes and litter. Our issues are due to decades of austerity and deprivation. Kings Hedges is one of the many deprived wards in Cambridge. It is disheartening that we have high food bank usage, in a city tipped to be the next Silicon Valley by the PM. There is nowhere for the youth to play, learn new skills or make new friends. Many cats are run over and accidents happen due to careless driving in Kings Hedges. If elected, want to open a permanent youth club in the ward. I want more CCTV, lighting, and to repair potholes and cracked, uneven paving so that people feel safe getting around Kings Hedges and that cars aren’t subject to costly repairs. I want people to feel safe in and enjoy living in Kings Hedges, we need to thrive not just survive. I will hold regular people’s assemblies with the community so that we can have our say on the council of what we want for our ward. Gloucestershire TUSC Press Release (for immediate release) 24/03/2021

Local councils are facing a new Covid-driven cash crisis. Our communities have already suffered more than a decade of austerity and now face more cuts to public services. Councils are massively underfunded by central Government and Covid-19 has revealed the difficulties local councils face in meeting the needs of people.

The Trade Unionist and Socialist Coalition (TUSC) was formed in 2010 to provide an anti-austerity political voice for working class people. Councils of all political persuasion have continued to implement austerity cuts to local services. TUSC is different from other parties. TUSC councillors will oppose all cuts to council jobs and services. 

TUSC is standing hundreds of candidates nationally in the May election. TUSC candidates include trade unionists, socialists, and social movement and community campaigners standing against pro-austerity establishment politicians.

Gloucestershire has fifteen TUSC candidates standing in twenty seats in Cheltenham, Stroud, Cirencester, the Forest of Dean and Gloucester.





TUSC candidates will refuse to implement austerity and will oppose all cuts to council services, jobs, pay and conditions. They will oppose policies designed to make ordinary people pay for the Covid-crisis.  In the short-term Councils could use reserves and borrowing to avoid making cuts in local services and in the longer-term can build linked mass campaigns to demand that central Government restores the funding it has cut. 


TUSC candidates will not vote for council tax increases or increases in council rent to bridge the gap in funding from central Government.

TUSC candidates will propose the use of the powers that local councils already have to begin a mass building programme of eco-friendly affordable council homes.
 
TUSC councillors will vote against privatisation of council jobs and services where central Government is attempting to impose the transfer of public services to the private sector.  

TUSC councillors will propose using council powers to defend our local NHS, initiate referenda and organise public commissions, consultations, and campaigns to defend local services.


TUSC has a core set of 8 policies that all candidates support below:


• Oppose All Cuts and Closures 

• Oppose Making People Pay for Crisis 

• Fighting Against Racism, Discrimination and Inequality 

• Reject Tax Increases to Pay for Cuts 

• Build Council homes 

• Stop Privatisation of Our NHS 

• Stop Privatisation of Council Services 

• Refuse to Implement Austerity 


Gloucestershire TUSC candidates are trade unionists & socialists from diverse age groups, workplaces and backgrounds – from campaigners against youth unemployment to pensioners’ rights campaigners, from shop workers to carers and transport workers. Committed to fighting austerity, privatisation and the cuts, we are proud defenders of our environment, the NHS and support Black Lives Matter, women’s and workers’ rights. As socialists and trade unionists we advocate public ownership of key utilities and services.

I will be a powerful voice for Coventry East.

Everyone deserves a decent home, good quality education and a health service they can rely on when they need it. Nobody, young or old, should feel excluded, and everybody should be able to enjoy a clean, green city – not struggling to make ends meet.

In my working life, I have helped set up lots of projects for families, young people and older people to increase their quality of life. I also have a detailed knowledge of how local councils function and I would use this knowledge and experience to get the best possible results for the people of Coventry.

I have lived in Coventry since 1991 when I moved here to train as an Occupational Therapist and never left. I have worked in the National Health Service since qualifying in 1994 and currently work with a community team for dementia and older people’s mental health services.

My priorities for Coventry if elected would be to maintain and improve services for people living with dementia and their carers and vulnerable and disabled people more broadly. I would also advocate for the council to take more action on making our city more sustainable for the future and would stand up to preserve green spaces for people and wildlife alike.

Recently retired after a long and very enjoyable career in local schools, I am now looking for new ways to help and support our communities.  
I originally came to Coventry in the late 1970s to study and have lived and/or worked here ever since. My children and grandchildren are Coventry kids, and I’m very proud of my adopted city.
I’m standing for election because I want to ensure that Coventry continues to be a kind, safe city for everyone who is lucky enough to find their way here, and to help build a fairer, more sustainable future for us all.

I've lived in Coventry for three years, and have met such a diverse community here. On a good day, the city centre is lovelier than anywhere in London – people are far more friendly too! I'm a student at Warwick University, studying History.

Like many, I was a Labour supporter who left when it became clear they stood only for power, and I'm proud to be part of Zack Polanski's movement for real change.

All our councils are being let down by the central government, but also by complacent councillors happy to serve it. Change starts at this grassroots level, politics that serves people, not parties or opaque lobbies.

Electing people willing to challenge the narrative of forced decline is how we begin to turn things around.

I am proud to stand as a candidate for the Green Party of England and wales at the upcoming local elections. I’m a creative professional and long-time local resident, committed to strengthening community wellbeing, protecting green spaces and ensuring transparent, accountable decision making at a council level.

I believe local government works best when it listens carefully, acts with integrity and puts people and the environment at the heart of every policy. I am standing to help build a fairer, healthier and more sustainable future for our community.

The last year has been tough. Having contracted Covid-19, along with my wife, last year I know from personal experience what a nasty disease it is. The return to normality has not, and will not, be quick. However we move a step closer to that normality with the return of the local elections.

I have represented you at the Council House for the last five years along with Cllr Julia Lepoidevin and Cllr Peter Male. I am standing for re-election because it has been an honour and a privilege to represent Woodlands Ward as your Councillor. I have always worked hard on behalf of the community on the issues that mattered, large or small.

I’ve helped residents with missed bin collections, got pot holes repaired, supported and organised litter picks and the Speedwatch initiative. At the time of writing we are also very close to a new defibrillator coming on stream in Sutherland Avenue. There have been bigger campaigns too like the fight to secure the return of education at the site of the Woodlands Academy and to secure our public spaces against travellers. I’ve also worked with the Mayor of the West Midlands Mayor Andy Street to save the greenbelt.

I have a strong record of action and I promise much more.
My determination to work hard for the people of Woodlands Ward has not diminished, if anything it burns brighter than it did five years ago. So once again I’m asking for your support so I can continue to be accessible and campaign for what matters to you.

I am a nearly retired IT System Test Analyst who likes to travel in the most ecofriendly way possible and I love colour.

I have lived in Coventry since 1983. I came for family reasons and stayed for the good transport links, the history, green spaces and the diverse people. I have been running a local weekly children’s group for over 30 years.

My priorities for Coventry are to improve Public Transport, by increasing frequency and adding routes but keep costs down. This will ultimately cut down on pollution and our reliance on fossil fuels. I want to preserve our green spaces, which are often full of wildlife. We need to protect and promote them, to let local people know all the different activities they can sustainably carry out in our green spaces, to help them care for and be proud of them.
