Insecure Housing, Lack of Youth Services and Lack of Social Care Provisions and Facilites (including NHS Provisions, and domestic abuse services).

Many homes across North Hanwell are being turned into cramped HMO houses for private landlords to exploit many low paid workers and vulnerable tenants as possible. While there are currently more than 7,500 live applications on the Ealing council housing register. The waiting time for a 3 bedroom house is 12 years! No more Gentrification! Ealing Labour is more for giving contracts to private property developers, selling off our public land rather than implementing a mass programme of council house building and introducing rent controls. We need environmentally friendy council housing, caps on private rent and service charges. Landlord and Housing Associations must be held accountable, so that everyone can afford a safe home in which to live comfortably.

Unfortunately, a lot of these HMOs are housing vulnerable people. There is a lack of domestic abuse services, a contributing factor to the rise of domestic violence especially in those HMOs. Certain individuals have serious mental health and drug related problems, and sadly it has coincided with a rise in anti social behaviour. They have been left to fend for themselves. Unfortunately, they are being deprived of the adequate social care and mental health support to help rehabilitate them back into society, so to lead normal lives. Unfortunately, it all coincides with a lack of social care facilties, and mental health services have also long been crippled with Austerity Cuts. Considering the size of North Hanwell population, there is a significant lack of NHS provisions and facilties for youth services. The last 16 year of Austerity is the biggest contributing factor in all this.

Restore Youth Services, and restore Social Care & Domestic Abuse Services.

Since 2010 until 2024, Ealing Labour had slashed on 70% of Youth services, as they passed on endless Tory led Austerity cuts without any resistance. What's their excuse now under a Starmer led Labour Government? Instead, they have planned the closure of 10 children's centres across the borough! They have failed to reopen Gurnell Leisure Centre, which had been closed since the pandemic, and awaiting refurbishment. 6 years later, it still remains closed, and has been put on the  back burner.

Fight the Government to restore the money stolen from Ealing. Councils can fight cuts to twist the Government's arm into paying up.

Vote TUSC on Thursday May 7th!

Hello, my name is Dominic. I am a candidate for North Hanwell and the fundraising officer for Ealing Green Party.

I have been a member of the Green Party for about 5 years, switching after having grown more and more tired of watching Labour move away from my values, and developed growing concern about our path towards climate catastrophe. The Green Party feels like the only party willing to call out what needs to be done.

I have lived in Hanwell for just over a year and a half, but I absolutely love the community here. In that time, I have started a local Guerrilla gardening group – who I’m proud to say are transforming Hanwell’s green spaces – and spearheaded a campaign against plans for an exploitative 24-hour slots casino in the centre of Hanwell. I’ve also volunteered for ‘LAGER Can’ litter picking group to try and reduce litter in our area, working with the council to have extra bins installed in key areas like Hanwell station.

Although I’m fairly new to Hanwell, I’m all too aware of the issues that face it. If elected, I want to help North Hanwell defeat the blight of HMOs – both for the communities they sit in, but also to help stop vulnerable people being trapped as HMO residents in poor conditions that so often come with them.

I am honoured to be standing as a Green Party candidate to be one of your councillors in North Hanwell ward.

I am, barring the time I spent studying for my Geography degree in Nottingham, a lifelong resident of Northolt. After graduating during the pandemic, I worked in airport security at Heathrow, which helped me develop skills as an effective communicator and taught me how rewarding it was to work with the public, solving problems. I now work as a private tutor for primary and secondary school pupils whilst continuing my own education, and in my spare time I enjoy gardening and foraging, through which I’ve learnt how crucial to our everyday lives protecting our local environment is.

Living in the borough of Ealing has shaped my life and I feel very fortunate to have been raised in such a diverse, beautiful and welcoming community. But I’ve also seen how our borough has suffered in recent years. I’ve long had an interest in politics, but I was driven to become more politically active after witnessing first-hand how soaring rental costs were pricing my generation out of the housing market and forcing young people to leave our community just to be able to afford to start a family. I joined the Green Party in 2025 because, under the leadership of Zack Polanski, the Greens are the only party offering a progressive vision of Britain. One that rejects the politics of hate and distrust threatening to divide our communities, and which stands up for all of us.

As your councillor, I want to focus on the housing crisis in our borough. In particular, I’ll pressure the council to prioritise true affordability, sustainability and the needs of locals over developers’ profits when building new housing. I also want to work on improving access for all to our parks and green spaces, and on delivering improvements in safety and accessibility for walking and cycling.

I have lived in Ealing for nearly 40 years, having brought up a family here and maintained active involvement in green issues. I can build on long experience as a team member in helping to manage voluntary, campaigning and commercial organisations. If I have the honour to be elected, I will serve the needs of my constituents to keep pressure on the council to build an equitable society, ensuring that all facilities especially housing and transport (cycling!) are affordable, healthy and sustainable.  Check out our Facebook page, and please get in touch if you would like to talk about any local issues.

I have been an Ealing resident for 35 years and am now looking to put my skills and experience to use for the benefit of the community. 

I am a recent entrant into active politics as I have come to recognise that it is not sufficient to criticise others. If I believe there is a better way of doing politics then I need to be willing to actively participate. I hope to be given the opportunity to do so.

I’m standing for Northolt Mandeville because, like many residents, I’ve been frustrated by the lack of accountability from the Labour council. Through my career as a data analyst, I’ve developed strong problem solving skills and experience delivering complex projects. I want to bring a fresh voice to the council with a focus on delivering real results for local people.

It has been an honour for Fabio to serve the community, whether working with residents to have deterrent signs for HGVs installed, working with businesses and police to gate off a fly-tipping hotspot or working with colleagues and parents to improve a playground. Fabio is an NHS doctor who cares deeply about health issues. He is particularly passionate about championing the Motor Neuron Disease Charter.

Mark joined Ealing Community Independents to try and make a difference. Mark has always lived within the Borough and has lived in Southall for over 30 years.

Mark is a civil servant and has been a Customs Officer in the past protecting our borders. He is an active disabled trade union campaigner for better public services and was part of the save Ealing tax office campaign before it eventually moved to Stratford.

Mark is a stroke survivor so was involved in the local Trades Council campaign to stop Ealing hospital A&E being downgraded to an Urgent Care Centre.

Born and raised in Southall, Happy has lived, worked, and served in the community that shaped him. His life is guided by duty, justice, and a commitment to defending the rights of his neighbours. Southall is his lifelong home, and his goal is to give back to the place he loves while helping preserve the values that strengthen England. Known for his integrity and independence, he cannot be bought or influenced – his loyalty is to the people alone. He stands for honour, dignity, respect, and love for everyone who calls Southall home.

Jahangir is a technology professional with over 25 years’ experience in technology, research, and enterprise leadership. He currently leads analytics and digital transformation projects within an international organisation. He has also served in policy and non-profit roles supporting sectoral development and child education initiatives.  He is standing in Norwood Green because he believes stronger local leadership is needed to prevent the rise of far right driven by wrong Labour policies and their overall poor economic performance. His priorities would also be about addressing deteriorating living standards in the ward and tackling youth joblessness. He wants to revitalise Southall’s local businesses and create real employment pathways for residents in a meaningful way.

Debbie is a lifelong West Londoner and award‑winning community advocate who has called Perivale home for over 25 years. With professional experience in education, local government and the NHS, she understands the pressures facing families, public services and neighbourhoods across Ealing. Her grassroots work spans campaigns for racial justice, the NHS and local libraries, as well as hands‑on initiatives such as food banks, clothes swaps and toddler sessions created in memory of her daughter. Debbie also supports Windrush families, serves as a school governor and contributes to the London Race Action Plan. She is committed to community‑led politics that protects residents, strengthens services and defends Ealing’s green spaces.

I remember the pride I felt when I first voted in an election, my vote was for the LibDems on the promise of not increasing tuition fees. A life lesson was not all I gained, a student debt now worth double what I borrowed and a 9% “tax” on my salary is the end result, and I am not alone. My parents couldn’t afford to send me to university and while thankful for the education I was afforded, I’m saddened by the fashion with which I had to agree to it. Had I only been born a year earlier my debt would be 1/3 what it is!

The establishment are letting us down and not working for people like us. Unlike other parties, the Green Party have a simple message of environmental and social justice and a rhetoric that things can be different and we should be hopeful not hateful.

I promise to fight for you every day, listening to your struggles and working with you and the council to find solutions. A renter all my adult life, I know the exceptional cost of living, difficulties saving for a deposit and the inequality and often poor living conditions that leads to. In such a large and crowded city, with many living in flats, the green spaces we are fortunate to have are vital for us. I will ensure they are clean and safe so we can all enjoy the outdoors.

I am a scientist working on technologies to treat drinking water, meaning I am data led and make informed decisions, see past the bluster and analyse critically. I will hold the council accountable and ensure they are delivering for us all.

Sarah McCartney was born in Saltburn, Cleveland, and grew up in a making and repairing household in the North East of England. She was educated at Boldon Comprehensive School, Durham and West London Universities, and now lives in Ealing. Sarah managed the Guardian and Observer's events, was Lush Cosmetics' writer for 14 years, and was a regular cos- metics industry speaker on ethical issues. In 2011 she found- ed 4160 Tuesdays, an eco award winning craft perfumery now based in Hammersmith.

Tina has lived in the Borough of Ealing for almost 44 years and in Pitshanger since 1988. She was a secondary school teacher in Ealing and surrounding boroughs before retiring. For many years, she volunteered for the Pitshanger Community Association at events such as Party in the Park, mainly in charge of recycling.  She also introduced and has organised the popular annual charity PCA  Street Wars Quiz for the past 18 years. In addition she has volunteered for Ealing Food Bank and has tutored many students who have struggled at school.

Tina loves this borough and believes passionately in the protection of our urban wildlife and our environment. She joined ECI as she feels it is time for a change to community-based local politics.

I am a local resident who cares deeply about our community, our green spaces, and the people who live here. I grew up in an ecologically minded home where I learned the importance of protecting nature, reducing waste, and looking after the world we share. Those values have shaped my life and are a big part of why I am standing as a Green Party candidate.

I was previously involved in helping to run a grassroots activist group called Mothers Rise Up, where I worked with others to campaign on environmental and social issues affecting families and our future. I believe local action can make a real difference, and that communities are strongest when people feel connected, supported, and heard.

I am actively involved in local life through choirs, conservation activities, and teaching yoga, all of which help bring people together and support wellbeing. I want to help build a greener, fairer, and more caring community for everyone who lives here.

In 2025, I was elected to serve on the Green Party’s Policy Development Committee, where I work to develop practical, forward-looking policies. I am an enthusiastic academic, campaigner, and policy developer dedicated to making a positive impact. My education and research at leading UK universities including Oxford and Cambridge has focused on how institutions can become more accountable, effective, and responsive to public needs.

Ealing has been my home for 15 years, I understand the challenges our residents face, from rising rents and housing costs to overdevelopment without sufficient infrastructure, air and water quality concerns, stretched local services, and limited opportunities for our young people.

Many people feel the system is not working for them. Too often, decisions are made without proper scrutiny or meaningful consultation. Residents want genuinely affordable housing, clean streets, maintained green spaces, safe neighbourhoods, well-supported schools, and transparency in how taxpayers’ money is spent. Managing decline is not leadership. We need ambition and accountability.

In 2022, the Green Party came second in this ward. Since then, we have grown strongly because more people recognise that real change is needed. We are now the credible alternative for those seeking hope, integrity, long-term thinking, and practical solutions.

If we want meaningful change in Ealing, we need Green councillors demanding social justice, environmental responsibility and prioritising people.

I will bring openness, scrutiny and evidence-based decision-making to South Acton and contribute to the wider Ealing alongside other Green elected councillors.

I will listen carefully, and work tirelessly to make sure that local decisions genuinely reflect what our community needs.

Please support me in South Acton and kindly encourage neighbours across Ealing to back Green candidates. Every conversation is valuable, and every vote truly makes a difference.

As your councillor, I will bring openness, scrutiny, transparency and evidence-based decision-making to South Acton and make a meaningful contribution to the wider Ealing alongside other Green elected councillors.

I will listen carefully, offer constructive challenges, and work tirelessly to make sure that local decisions genuinely reflect what our community needs.

Please support me in South Acton and kindly encourage friends and neighbours across all other Ealing Wards to back Green candidates. Every conversation is valuable, and every vote truly makes a difference.

Let us shift from frustration to action and work together to create the fairer, greener Ealing we all deserve.

Miça is standing for election to advocate for South Acton residents who for too long have been let down and marginalised by people in power. A keen socialist and activist, Miça has worked as a mental health nurse in the NHS for nearly 10 years and knows first-hand how our public services are being destroyed by relentless cuts. Miça has been part of Health Workers for Palestine and strongly supports calls for Ealing Council to divest from companies linked to the genocide in Palestine.

Miça has been a vocal opponent of cuts to Ealing’s Children’s Centres, and has worked tirelessly with West London Stand Up To Racism helping to mobilise against the far right in Brentford and West Drayton.

In South Acton, Miça is helping build a campaign to stop the Michael Flanders Centre being closed and to fight for better housing for all.

Miça is now focusing full time on activism and her rugby career – previously playing for Saracens, now for Trailfinders in Ealing, she hopes to bring that same fight and discipline as an athlete to her political work in Ealing Council.

Elizabeth joined Ealing Community Independents to protect public spaces and essential services from being lost to development or outsourcing. She has seen how the closure or sell‑off of children’s centres, adult care facilities (e.g. Michael Flanders Centre, Acton) and other community assets can leave residents without support. Elizabeth previously worked in the NHS and at Birkbeck, where she earned a PhD in cultural studies. Having lived in South Acton and returned over a decade ago, she is committed to ensuring public land, libraries, parks and social care remain in community use. Her goal is simple: a council that puts residents and public services first.

I’ve been a member of the Green Party for 36 years. I’ve lived in Ealing for all that time and I’m now retired from the BBC where I was a technician.
I spent 15 years on the Independent Monitoring Board at Wormwood Scrubs prison. Crime and how we punish it is a particular area of interest to me.
I like hands-on, practical solution;, I litter pick, organised a street sweep when wet leaves were a danger and I work with Abundance to garden small (and not so small) public spaces that otherwise look shabby.
The ability of the public to communicate efficiently with the council is an area I’d really like to get to grips with!

Glen has supported South Acton residents for over a decade through the Redbrick community organisation, helping neighbours navigate regeneration, repairs and local issues. During the Covid pandemic, he worked with Acton Gardens, Acton Youth Centre and local groups to deliver large‑scale emergency food support, leading to his recognition as a Community Champion. Glen also serves on Ealing’s Your Voice Your Town committee, helping fund projects that improve Acton’s environment and community spaces. Having lived and worked locally for many years, he is committed to strengthening community networks and ensuring residents have a meaningful voice in local decisions.

Angela has lived in Southall for twenty years and worked in the London Borough of Ealing at West London College for eighteen years. Angela has campaigned on air pollution firstly establishing Insistent Residents Against Toxic Emissions (IRATE) followed by Clean Air for Southall and Hayes (CASH). She is passionate about raising awareness of injustices affecting residents’ quality of life and has organised children’s play activities with other volunteers. Angela currently works as a teaching support in a local college, assisting students with learning and physical disabilities.

A Southall resident for 26 years, Qamer raised his family here and built strong relationships across our community. He’s campaigned on key local issues and seen first‑hand how Southall has been neglected, with persistent fly‑tipping, anti‑social behaviour, rising crime, poor roads and too few facilities for children and older residents. He’s standing to demand accountability and ensure Southall gets the respect and investment it deserves. If elected, he will be a dedicated voice for residents, working to make our area clean, safe, vibrant and welcoming for everyone who calls Southall home.

People before politics.
Joginder has been living in Southall since 1965 with his wife and two daughters, who have all grown up, married and are living locally as well. Joginder, known by his friends as Joe - has been running a road transport business since the late 80s. He got involved in local politics from the sidelines and used to attend many ward forums held by the council. Many residents ask Joe for guidance and advice on local problems, such as hospital departments that were closing, the parking problems faced by many residents or concerns about the construction of thousands of flats at the old gas works site.

Minni arrived in Southall as a three‑year‑old immigrant and has spent her entire life rooted in our community. Her career was based at Dogra & Co. Solicitors on Southall Green. She served as a school governor for 17 years.

After retiring, she retrained to teach English as a second language. But walking through Southall after the pandemic, she saw the decline caused by decisions made at Ealing Council. Minni began challenging these failures through letters, meetings, Freedom of Information requests, protests, and petitions on issues including overdevelopment, planning failures, broken pavements, the loss of ward forums, and cuts to vital public services.

Minni helped secure a public inquiry into the proposed Dominion car park towers, fought to save Southall Youth Centre, delivered a 4000‑signature petition to Downing Street to protect our Crown Post Office, opposed harmful CPZ extensions, and raised awareness of the proposed closure of half of Southall’s Children’s Centres – now subject to judicial review.

She understands Southall because she grew up in its story. Her commitment is simple: to give our community a strong voice and put Southall first.

Jatinder has lived in Southall his whole life and is deeply rooted in the community. With over 15 years of experience in creative leadership and campaign strategy, he has led national and global communications projects, bringing people together and driving change.

He is standing up to be a voice for those without one and will fight for better services and stronger community spaces for residents, local businesses, and the vulnerable. He wants to restore community pride and secure a better future for our children.

From our WWII veterans who gave everything to those who fought racism and the National Front in the 80s, their struggle was not in vain. Stand with him and shape Southall’s future.

Dan moved to Southall in 2021 after living and working across more than 40 countries. With a background spanning retail, construction, insurance, tourism, entertainment and tech, he brings practical experience and a hands‑on approach to community problem‑solving. Since settling in the Green Quarter, he has joined several local groups focused on improving the area and strengthening resident involvement. Dan has been motivated by concerns about overdevelopment, stalled infrastructure and deteriorating streets. His priorities include ensuring developers deliver essential community facilities upfront and restoring pride in Southall through initiatives that improve neighbourhood upkeep and support a stronger, more connected community.

Sukhi is a 49-year-old independent candidate committed to practical solutions that put our community first.

As a working professional and family man, he understands the real pressures people face, from rising living costs to the need for safer streets and stronger local services.

He believes in transparency, accountability, and responsible budgeting.

His focus is on improving community wellbeing, supporting local businesses, promoting healthy lifestyles, and ensuring decisions are made with residents – not political parties at the centre.

Sukhi is running to bring common sense, integrity, and genuine representation back to local government.

I’ve always cared somewhat about the natural world, and then I realised our environment is our life support system and needs to be regenerated so people can live full, healthy and happy lives. Therefore I joined the Green Party as they are the only ones prioritising our health and economic competitiveness.
Only the Greens have ambitious plans for education, which is the most efficient way to create real equality in our society, and a stronger economy. This, on top of building high quality low energy homes to permanently reduce the cost of living, means the Green Party is focussed on helping people to thrive, instead of just getting by.

I have lived in Ealing for just over 3 years and have always loved the diversity of the borough, both of the environment and also of the community.

I am passionate about human rights and have volunteered in my spare time with refugees and asylum seekers for the last ten years.

I joined the Green Party because I found hope in its values after years of watching and feeling our society being let down time and time again by the government. It’s time for a return to basics – what does this community need to thrive? How can everyone feel a part of it? And how can we make it happen?

Green Party values have answers where others have offered platitudes and promised change which never arrived.

I will listen to the members of this community and be a force for action, representing those who need their voices to be heard and acting in the best interests of the community as a whole.

I believe in making hope normal again. Hope for a safe, affordable place to live, the ability to provide for our families and the hope of a better future for those who come after us. This is what I stand for.

I have lived in Southfield Ward for more than 40 years. My children (now grown up) were both educated for 8 years at Southfield School, where I was active in the Parent Staff Association and as a parent governor.

I first joined the Ecology Party (as the Green Party was then known) in 1978. Although I’m pleased that many of its environmental policies have been adopted by other parties, only the Green Party will take the urgent action needed to prevent catastrophic climate change and to prepare for its consequences, including the extreme weather which we are already experiencing, food shortages, air pollution and the destruction of our environment and wildlife. At local level, we can conserve energy (such as through insulating homes), reduce fossil fuel use (by improving public transport and encouraging safe walking and cycling) and protect our natural resources.

I spent many years advising companies on employee share ownership. More recently, I have carried out postgraduate research into Climate Change Economics. I am a Director and Vice Chair of a Community Energy Society.

A vote for the Green Party is not wasted. It sends a strong message that we want to keep a world fit for our grandchildren to live in.

I grew up in Wigan and studied Genetics at Sheffield University before moving to London where I have lives in West London for over twenty years. I love mountaineering and cooking. I work in data roles and have spent time analysing data for the hospitality sector within marketing departments and also worked in market research.

I became a Lib Dem councillor in 2002 and did so after wanting to help solve problems rather than just blame the council for their mistakes. My greatest achievement was a group effort linking the Liberal Democrats with campaigners so we could save Warren Farm from being developed in a way that would kill off around 20 endangered species of birds, animals, bugs and plants. After the long running campaign where there was a rally with over 2000 people the Council back tracked!

I have lived in this part of west London for forty years, moving to the Hounslow part of Chiswick in 1984. My wife and I moved to Ealing twenty years later. My work career has been largely retail and/or book related. Currently I work for an international charity and manage a part time a second hand bookshop.

First elected in 2010 for Southfield Ward, after standing as a candidate previously in Ealing and Hounslow. For the past fourteen years, local government has been through hard times financially, despite having increased responsibilities. Sadly that is not likely to change anytime soon. But being a Councillor is interesting and one still gets a buzz from helping residents, especially if you can make a genuine difference.

William Francis works at a HGV driving school and does freelance media analysis work as well. He is also keen on championing local concerns, saying: “I aim to be the best local champion I can be for Walpole and ensure that residents have a strong voice in the council. I am determined to reduce the crime and anti-social behaviour in hot spot areas in the ward, to ensure streets are clean, and to alleviate the housing crisis.”

William is Chair of North West London Young Liberals and Vice Chair of London Young Liberals.

Darius has been a resident of Ealing since birth and is  proud to call the borough his home. As a democratic socialist he joined Ealing Community Independents to try to help improve the lives of residents in the area he loves, after being disappointed by the continued failure of the Ealing Labour council, and has campaigned for the divestment of local council tax funding weapons companies. Darius has worked as an articulated lorry driver all across London and has a strong interest in the maintenance of our roads and transport network. He is also very passionate about the preservation of our local parks and wildlife.

Barry has lived in Ealing since 2014, and has a son at a local primary school.  He is passionate about the environment, and he and his family love watching the wildlife and flora in the local parks and exploring natural areas in the borough.  He is a keen cyclist, and having safe cycling routes for all, especially young children, is important for encouraging more active and integrated travel.  Other areas of particular importance are access to green spaces, trees, lowering pollution levels, and social and economic fairness.

I have lived in the Walpole area of Ealing for over thirty years. I moved here whilst I was working at the BBC’s Community Programme Unit producing and directing campaigning programmes on many social issues such as the immigration system, unemployment and bias in the media. I continued the spirit of this work into my subsequent time at Channel 4, commissioning many programmes concerned with human rights and global development. I spent the last phase of my career as Managing Director of an independent production company before retiring a few years ago. I now volunteer as a teacher of English as a foreign language at a community school in Ealing. I have been drawn to the Green Party’s positive campaigning on environmental, racial and social justice for some time and joined the Party in 2025.

I am particularly interested in supporting policies which: address Ealing’s distressing lack of social housing with developments that meet the needs of local communities; support Ealing’s status as a Borough of Sanctuary; resist future threats to our environment and health such as airport expansion; enhance and expand bio-diversity programmes for the benefit of everyone who lives in the borough.

I am honoured to be standing as a Green Party candidate for Walpole.

Since moving to Ealing, I’ve grown to love life here – from evening walks in Walpole or Lammas Park to catching up with friends in our local cafes.

Having lived in Germany from the age of 10, I moved back to the UK to study marketing with economics at university. Over the years, I undertook a broad range of jobs – working in shops, pubs, kitchens, fundraising, volunteering and currently digital marketing. I later moved here with my partner, who works in youth justice.

As a member of Ealing Green Party I’ve had the pleasure of regularly speaking to local residents and campaigners, hearing about the issues facing our community – from fly-tipping to protecting Warren Farm. If elected, my first priority will always be to listen and provide a powerful voice to all of Walpole’s residents.

I believe my love for the area, understanding of local issues, and broad experience has given me a holistic view that would help me serve the community.

Ksenia Maximova, a former international model and founder of Russian Democratic Society, said: “I have lived in Ealing since 1999 and attended Notting Hill and Ealing High School. I am engaged with local issues: campaigning for cleaner streets, fixing infrastructure problems and advocating for better public spaces.”

Long time volunteer with Lager Can helping to keep our local streets and parks clean with her family.

Managed a crowd funded project to do ground water surveys, buy diggers and created a pond as well as funding bins to keep the area clean.

Founder of the Russian Democratic Society, a London-based organisation that opposes Putin and speaks out against the invasion of Ukraine.

Matthew Mellor is originally from Sheffield but has lived in Northfields for over a decade. A resident of Walpole, he lives with his wife and 2 children who attend local schools. Matthew spent 12 years working in local government and a decade working as a contract manager in the NHS. "I'm passionate about social justice and ensuring we have people with liberal values representing our community on Ealing Council. I'm focused on improving our local services and ensuring no vulnerable person in our community gets left behind or forgotten, which is why protecting our local education, health and social care, and communities services is so important". The biggest thing he would change about the Council is it’s bad record of listening to local people. At a ward level, the council must engage better with residents and I will tackle the visible failings of the council including litter, overgrown vegetation, blocked gullies and potholes.

Carl is an energetic, passionate socialist candidate who has lived and worked across West London, witnessing firsthand the corporate decay and bureaucratic mismanagement affecting local communities. A former organiser in a university rent strike campaign and now working in Housing, he has long been committed to standing up for residents. Carl is running in Walpole to protect the area from instability and to safeguard and strengthen the community’s greatest assets for the future.

Richard has lived in Ealing permanently for over ten years but known the area for much longer. Richard is an educator and manager and has worked for theatre companies across the country. He was an active campaigner for Sister Supporter which stopped the harassment of women on Mattock Lane. As a democratic socialist, Richard was previously in the Labour Party but left five years ago in complete despair at the machinations of the local Labour Party in Ealing, and fearing they had abandoned all their principles. He believes that any political party should first serve the interests of the residents, the people it represents, not the interest of those who lead or fund it. As such, he helped form Ealing Community Independents with people from the community properly representing the interests of the community. He supports divestment of the pension scheme away from weapon systems and arms manufacturers and into green renewable industries and technologies.

I am proud to stand for Bishopstoke, where I have lived for over 13 years and where my children attend local schools. I work in a local college, so I understand the importance of education, opportunity and strong community support. I care deeply about the area and the people who live here. I want to protect our environment, support local services, and ensure residents have a real voice in decisions that affect them. I will work hard, listen to concerns, and stand up for Bishopstoke every day and always put our community first in everything I do for local residents.

Representing people, not a party

“Do you feel like I do? That political  parties are not listening to the concerns of local people? That they have lost touch with the wishes of Bishopstoke? 

With a background in local government and a masters degree I felt it was time to give back to my community. These concerns inspired me to stand up for Bishopstoke & Fair Oak. I've been privileged and proud to have received so much support from my local community, now currently representing local people on Hampshire County Council (since 2022) Eastleigh Borough Council (Since 2018) and Bishopstoke Parish (since 2016). successfully run for the Parish Council election in 2016. Together with the local community and my Independent colleagues I have helped to convince the Local Planning Inspector that the potentially 5000+ buildings proposal in the north of our villages would be destructive and I am now actively seeking the same area be protected as a nature reserve. After three years of campaigning for safer indication of the junior school and slower speeds, I was thrilled, that within my first 6months at Hampshire, warning lights and a 20mph limit has been installed. I  have sought to influence decision makers. 

Including: speaking up on behalf of residents at local meetings; helping residents experiencing difficulties with developments; challenging policies on fly-tipping; and, pushed for new footpaths. Bishopstoke has always been home. I  went to the local Infant and Junior school,  I’m a member of Bishopstoke Players  and Bishopstoke History Society. I grew up with its ancient woodland & Itchen and want to see these preserved for future generations”

If elected I will: ✓ continue to fight eco-vandalism that could devastate our ancient woodland, countryside and the Itchen  ✓ keep local people informed of the decisions that will affect us and listen to their views ✓ support services and policies which contribute to the health and wellbeing of local people, our environment and wildlife.

I regularly post information on Facebook so please do 'like' me there.

Published and promoted by Louise Anne Parker-Jones of 4 Drake Road Bishopstoke Eastleigh SO50 6EU.

After nine years of military service, I ran a successful business for over 30 years while continuing to serve the community as a special constable, retained firefighter, and community first responder.

As a parish councillor in neighbouring Allbrook, I remain committed to practical action and strong local representation.

My wife and family grew up locally, and through years of volunteering I have built lasting connections across the area. I understand the challenges residents face — protecting vital services, improving infrastructure, and keeping our community safe, welcoming, and thriving.

I believe in listening first, working collaboratively, and delivering real results that benefit everyone. I am community-focused and dedicated to putting residents before politics.

Anne is Bishopstoke’s longest serving councillor, and the only councillor to have served on Bishopstoke Parish Council since it was created in 1996. A former Deputy Leader of the Borough Council and Cabinet Member for Social Policy, Anne has campaigned for traffic relief on Bishopstoke Road and secured land at Stoke Common Park for public access after its earlier allocation for housing. Anne has been Chair of Bishopstoke Parish Council and also Chair of the County Parish Council Association. She is also involved in several charities and community organisations providing advice, assistance and community facilities where needed.

Rupert was elected to the Borough Council in 2002 and is Botley’s longest-serving councillor. As Cabinet Member at Eastleigh for the environment, Rupert has championed recycling, air and water quality, and drainage concerns.  A past Mayor, he is also a Parish and County Councillor. Rupert led the campaign for Botley’s by-pass, opposed for many years by the County Council, and has recently won his campaign to get pavements along more of Kings Copse Avenue. Next to get the speed limit down! He is working to secure more doctors’ appointments and facilities at Botley Surgery, and a pharmacy at Boorley.

I’m standing as a Green candidate because I care deeply about Botley and Hampshire, where I was raised and have lived locally for seven years. I understand the issues residents face and believe politics should prioritise listening, transparency, and long-term wellbeing over short-term profit. My priorities include protecting green spaces, supporting strong communities, and ensuring development benefits residents without straining infrastructure. I support sustainable planning, improved public transport, safer walking and cycling routes to reduce congestion and pollution. I am committed to addressing the cost-of-living crisis through affordable housing and community initiatives. I will represent residents with integrity and dedication.

Vote for Frankie Coultas on Thursday 7th May standing for TUSC for a better Bursledon and Hound North
Why vote TUSC?
•	No cuts to council jobs and services
•	No increase in council tax, rents and charges
•	£15 an hour minimum wage
•	Affordable and efficient public transport including working with trade unions to establish a better bus service in Bursledon and Hound to reduce air pollution and connect communities across Eastleigh
•	Tackle anti-social behavior including dangerous drivers on Hamble Lane, Lowford Hill and Portsmouth Road
•	Environmental initiatives including holding to account utility companies who pollute our waterways such as the Hamble River and working with other councilors in other wards fighting against the destructive gravel pit proposal in Hamble Airfield
Elect a fighting, anti-cuts councilor who will  campaign to end austerity, reverse cuts and protect our services, safety and the environment as well as delivering jobs, homes and fully-funded services for all.

Tonia is Bursledon’s longest-serving Borough Councillor and is Cabinet Member for Health at the Borough Council, leading on working with the NHS to improve our local health services and on community safety. She is also a member of the County Council where one of her roles is holding the Police & Crime Commissioner to account. Last year she was asked by Hound Parish Council to take on chairing the Parish Council that covers Butlocks Heath in her Borough ward. Tonia is pressing the County Council to tackle potholes and the dreadful condition of Hamble Lane and other local roads.

Keith has lived in Eastleigh for over 40 years and has been active in local politics most of that time.  Inspired to join the Green Party by Zack Polanski's national leadership, Keith is keen to implement Green policies locally. He would work to improve water quality in our rivers, reduce pollution, ensure the environment and biodiversity are protected and enhanced in planning decisions, improve public transport and support sustainable local business.

Alan is Chandler’s Ford’s longest serving councillor. First elected to Eastleigh Borough Council in 1993 he has served on the Council’s Cabinet with responsibility for leisure, has chaired the Council’s Local Area Committee and also represented the area on Hampshire County Council for eight years. Alan has been a member of Chandler’s Ford Parish Council since it started in 2010. Living in Chandler’s Ford since 1971, his children went to local schools. Alan wants to continue to serve the people of Chandler’s Ford the area he loves and knows so well, and get the County to fix the potholes!

Bors has trained as a social scientist and a climate scientist. His expert area is climate migration.
He runs a small research business within healthcare.

His evening job is climate activism.

He is Chair of the Sustainability Committee at the British Healthcare Business Intelligence Association. 
He regularly gives talks about the climate emergency to audiences across the South.

Bors has lived in Chandler's Ford for over 10 years, is an active member of the community and a scout leader.

Bors has 3 boys, all attending local schools. His vision is to leave a fair and liveable planet to future generations.

I am a 7th Generation former soldier. I served in 16th Independent Parachute Brigade, was seconded to the FCO and carried out security duties at Embassies in conflict areas.

I served in Surrey Police after leaving the forces. I am now retired and work as a Physiotherapy Associate Practitioner with the Local NHS community teams. My wife is a Clinical lead locally with the NHS. We have two daughters 1 is a primary school teacher in Yateley and the other works as a projects manager with Southampton Football club.

I have lived in the Forest for about 20 years, my wife was born at the former Fenwick Hospital in Ashurst, her family are lifetime residents here.

Problems with the constituency.

The New Forest is a beautiful place to live for those that can afford to, but take a walk into some of the poorer areas and see the truth. Poor families on council waiting lists, with no houses being built. Planning regulations of a draconian nature exist to throw up barriers instead of facilitating access.

The council refusing to take responsibility instead of doing the “right thing”. Food banks in Totton and Backfields and Hythe because people cannot afford to buy food due to high prices.  Access to services Drs and Dentists, public transport to the General Hospital and other medical services.

The New forest is so poorly served by our local ambulance services that some cannot attend or afford a taxi, which is often the advice given. In the Forest itself, we see younger generations driven away because of high costs in both rent and lack of housing, leading to population displacements we can little afford to accept. We have our community nurses struggling to meet demands as the area is so large they cannot reach everyone and have very few staff to do it. Lymington Hospital is always shouting loud for staff to perform the wonderful services they do.

The council continually failing its people to provide good quality affordable housing and services. Employment has been decreasing limiting access to jobs for young people. Young people simply don’t have the connection or are disconnected from the forest. Local areas surrounding the forest like Totton and waterside are largely built up and are poorly served. For example the wheelie bin scandal is now hitting residents with the unsightly plastic bins left out by many for days causing obstructions and eyesores.. Sewage spillage into the sea around or beautiful coastline are of great concern.

Councils wasting money on art projects in Totton that have little meaning to residents.  Lurking in the distance is the spectre of Associated British Ports and the loss of our military community in Marchwood. Rising rents for waterside clubs who use the waterways. The list goes on, however there is hope. Reform is needed to put things right, to fight to retain our Forest way of life, our schools and medical services. I don’t pretend to know all the anwers but sometimes a fresh pair of eyes in a position of authority not tainted by years of political ambition can make wonderful things happen if given a chance.

Dave was born and raised in Chandler’s Ford and is proud to still call it home. He went to Scantabout and Thornden School, the same schools his children attended. His son is still at Thornden now. Dave’s elder parents also live in the ward, so he sees the issues that matter to residents at every stage of life. Protecting local green spaces, improving local services and facilities for young people, and ensuring the community’s voice is heard are important to him. Working towards a greener future and advocating for issues that matter to the community are his priorities.

I am a local resident deeply rooted in Eastleigh, focused on our community, not personal ambition. Having lived here since I was seven, I am committed to serving those who call Eastleigh home.

My priority is improving quality of life, better healthcare, affordable housing, local jobs, and protecting our environment. Crucially, I believe in society's obligation to protect the vulnerable.

I aim to strengthen the Green Party's voice on the council. With representation, we can join more committees and deliver meaningful change for Eastleigh.

Together, we can build a greener, fairer future where no one is left behind.

I have lived in Eastleigh for over 35 years and currently have run my shop in Eastleigh High Street for over 5 years. I’ve seen our community struggle while the Council wastes money and ignores local people. I’m standing to fight for our small businesses and comunity, tackle antisocial behaviour, and protect our green spaces from overdevelopment

I have lived in Eastleigh for the past decade and am proud to call it home. I’m standing in this by-election because I believe our town deserves better. After 30 years of Liberal Democrat control at Eastleigh Borough Council, too many people feel things are going backwards. It’s time for a fresh start.

If elected, I will focus on the basics: fixing our roads, tackling antisocial behaviour, revitalising the town centre, protecting and investing in our green spaces, and fighting cuts to local bus services. I will push for stronger action on street cleaning, better support for independent businesses, and a real effort to bring pride back to our high street.

I also support Labour’s plans to reform local government. Replacing the borough and county council structures with a single unitary authority and a directly elected mayor would mean clearer accountability, better value for money, and stronger leadership for our community.

I’m passionate about making a real difference for Eastleigh; I hope I can count on your support.

Cameron Spencer is the youngest member of the Borough Council Lib Dem team and was first elected to the Council in 2022. Cameron has worked as the MP’s Chief of Staff in Westminster and Eastleigh, providing a vital link between Parliament since 2024. Cameron is also a member of Eastleigh Town Council, representing Brookwood Ward. He has been a trustee for a local charity, and in his spare time, is a keen runner and hockey player. Cameron is campaigning to get the missing Chickenhall Link By-Pass after the County Council abandoned support for it, to reduce town centre traffic.

Steve is standing for re-election to the Borough Council for North Ward having first been elected in 2022.  Steve has worked for his diverse community of Boyatt Wood, Allbrook and the Twyford Road area of Eastleigh town over his four years. Steve works as a manager of a group of dental practices.  He cycles and has undertaken fundraising including a triathlon across to the Isle of Wight for The Courage Foundation which supports children who have lost a brother or sister to enjoy themselves again through funding of activities such as passes to family theme parks, and also cancer charities.

I have lived in Eastleigh since 2016 and am standing in Eastleigh North. I am heavily invested in the Eastleigh area. My children attend nursery and school in the Borough. Professionally, I run a consultancy near Southampton Airport advising firms on governance and financial regulation.

Eastleigh residents have been feeling the impact of rising council tax for some time. Hampshire’s finances are under severe pressure. Reserves are being depleted, and a significant funding gap is emerging that threatens us all.

My priorities are clear:

(1) challenging wasteful spending and demanding proper scrutiny of council finances;

(2) contesting decisions that increase costs for residents without improving services; and

(3) focusing spending on core services that people in Eastleigh rely on.

At work, I deal with complex financial issues. I would bring that same discipline locally, holding decision-makers to account and standing up for residents facing rising costs and declining value.

Paul has represented South Ward on the Borough Council since 2011 and is a member of Eastleigh Town Council.  Professionally, he is a train driver with over 25 years’ experience. Paul is a past Deputy Leader of the Borough and Cabinet Member for Social Policy and Regeneration. Heavily involved in housing, Paul helped formulate housing policies for the council’s new Eastbrooke homes, was a key member of the team bringing forward temporary homeless accommodation at Bampton House and the redevelopment of the old Post Office to provide the council with new social housing units at Postmark Place in the town centre.

favourite_biscuit: there's only one biscuit worth having and that is a Custard Cream!
statement_to_voters:
I’m standing with Reform UK for election to Eastleigh Borough Council and as your Prospective Parliamentary Candidate for the General Election this year because I’m proud to call Eastleigh my home, having lived in the borough for 13 years and the town centre for three years.

As a taxpayer, I have become increasingly disappointed and frustrated in the level of public services provided by the Council and its stakeholders.

Once elected, I will work tirelessly to slash the unnecessary bureaucracy and red tape to improve the services we receive from the Council which, in my view, have been deteriorating year on year.

We all deserve value for money public services that deliver tangible results; be that something as basic as getting our bins emptied on time right through to revitalising the town centre which has, in my view, very sadly changed beyond all recognition over the last few years from a vibrant shopping hub to a wasteland of empty units. I believe taxpaying residents deserves more than the Council is currently delivering.

A particular issue I am very troubled by is the rising level of violent crime, anti-social behaviour and drug dealing in the town which has been exacerbated by the closure of our police station that not only provided a safe, open place to residents needing to use it, its presence, without doubt, provided a deterrent against crime in Eastleigh itself and the wider constituency.  We have the right to feel safe in our town and constituency with a visible police presence to provide that comfort and assurance, not a remote office on the outskirts of town that you cannot walk into without making an appointment.

About Me

A bit more about me, I worked for the NHS at Omega House for almost five years, supporting a Clinical Commissioning Group Board which gave me a working insight into how public services are organised and delivered… there is a lot of work to do.  I also worked for the Commissioning Support Unit at Omega House in the Freedom of Information Team dealing with requests from members of the public, Councillors and Members of Parliament for Wednesday’s Prime Minister’s Questions.

For a time in 2015, I worked at Prysmian in their centenary year, supporting the CEO and Senior Management Team and whilst there was involved in organising a UK Trade and Industry visit.

Whilst working for a large financial services organisation in Southampton, I was Chair of the UK Employee Forum, representing circa 2,000 employees in Southampton and a further 2,500 across the UK. I also lead a local Leaseholder Action Group fighting for much needed changes in Leasehold law via the National Leasehold Campaign to demand the same rights for Leaseholders that other homeowners enjoy.

My practical career experience, gained in public sector organisations, manufacturing, a social enterprise and professional services, including law and financial services, affords me the knowledge, experience and skills to properly represent you as your Councillor and Member of Parliament..

So, if you are hungry for meaningful change, are disillusioned with the shenanigans of the main parties or just feel politically homeless, why not consider voting for me and Reform UK…what have you got to lose?

Since 2023, I've lived in Eastleigh and fallen in love with our community. But there is work to do. My background in e-commerce and the charity sector has taught me that we don't have to abandon our ideals to help people in order to find solutions that actually work.

For most of us, life has never been harder. We've started accepting the bare minimum as a pleasant surprise. I want to hold the council to account, injecting new energy and ideas. Forget party politics; we need realistic, efficient results that make life better for everyone and protect our planet.

My name is Ben Burcombe-Filer, and I am the Conservative candidate for Southampton Test in this general election. 

My journey to this point has always had Southampton Test at its heart. I first came to Southampton Test aged 18 months having been diagnosed with cerebral palsy and written off. My fightback began with the skill help and support of Southampton General, who have been there every step of the way since. 

“My whole life, professional and personal, has been about overcoming challenges, in environments where failure simply is not an option. I hope to be able to use those attributes in serving and representing the residents of Southampton Test. Together we can ensure bold action provides a Secure future for the City.”

My main aims if elected as MP would be

1.	To ensure the people of Southampton Test feel that their voice is heard and they are represented. With a Labour MP since 1997 and a council on which 70% of the seats are held by Labour there is no check or debate currently. The people deserve an MP who will listen, not just hear, and act accordingly. 

2.	Focus on the things that really matter to people. Continuing to cut crime and antisocial behaviour, cleaning up our streets, further elevating the pride Southampton communities feel in their city. 

3.	Ensure the resilience of infrastructure and industry in the city, making sure the port has the capacity to continue to provide quality jobs for residents for years to come by helping to  attract further investment. As well as making sure our infrastructure and transport network is future proofed so the people and business’ of Southampton Test can plan with confidence and thrive.  

I feel strongly that I have a debt to the people and place of Southampton Test, without them I simply would not be here. Now I want to use my skills and experiences to give back.

Fair Oak and Horton Heath’s longest serving councillor, Nick was Mayor of the Borough in 2023/2024. He is also Vice Chair of the Fair Oak and Horton Heath Parish Council. He led the team that rescued Fair Oak Library from County Council cuts and is an adviser at Citizens Advice. Nick enthusiastically supports the Borough Council’s One Horton Heath project which is on course to provide 2500 much-needed houses at no cost to council taxpayers. He also praises the development of Stoke Common Park. As a Saints season ticket holder, he has recently started to believe in miracles.

I’m a local business owner, but more importantly, I’m your neighbour. Like many of you, I care deeply about what happens in our community, and I don’t think our area is getting the focus or representation it deserves.

For years, Eastleigh Borough Council has been dominated by one party with very little meaningful opposition. That lack of balance isn’t healthy for anyone.

As a business owner, I’m particularly concerned about the level of council debt – among the highest in the country – while residents continue to face rising council tax. Too often, large sums of public money are spent without enough scrutiny or challenge.

If you’re looking for someone who will challenge the current leadership, question how your money is spent and stand up for our community, I’d be grateful for your support.

My name is Ben Parry and I have lived with my family in Fair Oak for over 13 years. I believe it’s time you had a credible candidate that understands we can no longer afford to take a ‘one or the other’ approach on the economy and the environment; I firmly believe I am that credible candidate. The Covid pandemic, and the climate crisis, have shown us that governance at any level cannot continue to be ‘business as usual’. It has also emphasised the importance of a strong community. My children attend a junior and secondary school in the local area. Until recently, I was a teacher for 17 years; teaching in local secondary schools and in an Eastleigh sixth form college. Now, as a director of an Eastleigh-based traffic survey company, I see how heavy investment in local housing has not been matched by investment in proper infrastructure. My election would see me focus on:

Standing up for the economy • support local businesses to be successful and sustainable.

Standing up for the community • Help the community transition towards a carbon zero future. • Fight for a green transport infrastructure that alleviates the stress on our roads. 

Standing up for our green spaces • Protect the communal green spaces and ancient woodland that help protect our physical and mental health.

 Most importantly, I would be an independent voice on Eastleigh Borough Council, able to speak up with your best interests at heart, not the best interests of a party.

On Thursday, May 7th, use your vote to choose a local champion, not a party politician.
𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗠𝗲:
I am a proud Fair Oak resident, a husband, and a father of two children attending our local state schools. My commitment to our community is personal — I want to ensure this remains a safe, thriving place for all our families to grow up in.
I am deeply involved in our local area, currently serving as Chair of Governors for a nearby Primary School. I am also an active campaigner, serving as a committee member for Action Against Destructive Development, where I have helped organise opposition to inappropriate planning applications.
