statement_to_voters:
I moved to Epping with my wife and my two children almost a decade ago. Although I have been a Liberal Democrat for many years, this is the first time that I have been involved in politics. I decided to stand for election because I love living here and want to contribute to the local area. We hosted a Ukrainian family for 9 months shortly after the start of the war and we were moved by the support and kindness of local residents and councillors at both town and district level.

My background is in science - I have a doctorate in physics. For the last few years I have run a large business in the legal sector with over 250 employees across the UK and mainland Europe. I believe that my legal, financial and analytical skills will make me an effective District Councillor, able to advocate strongly on behalf of local residents and hold the Council to account over budgetary decisions. I enjoy solving complex problems and helping people - I’m particularly concerned to ensure that those in most need are properly shielded from the ongoing cost of living challenges. I am planning a positive campaign and hope to represent residents in a collaborative and evidence based way if I am elected, informed by Liberal values of fairness and respect for all.

There is no doubt that the UK faces some very significant challenges at a national level but I am keen to focus on local matters - protecting the green space in and around Epping is something about which I am passionate. I’m particularly concerned with the amount of proposed development in and around Epping and the lack of planned infrastructure growth to accommodate that.

So even if you are not a natural Liberal Democrat voter, I hope you will lend me your vote on 7 May, and I promise to work hard in representing you effectively.

I've been a District Cllr since 2008 and a Town Cllr for Roding since 2004.  At District Council I'm on local planning committee and Overview & Scrutiny.  At Town Council, I've chaired the Recreation Committee for many years and finalised the Fields in Trust Status for the High Road cricket ground.  I was Town Mayor 2010-11.  I've been a school governor, enjoy local history, football and walking in the Forest.  Our green open spaces must be protected from development.

’ve lived in Loughton since 2013.  Married for 16 years, we have three sons in local schools.  I've BSc in criminology & justice and MSc in environment management.  I'm Enforcement Manager for licensing and environment.  My Central Line commute to work is not pleasant, so at weekends we escape by walking, cycling and playing on our green open spaces.  I want to protect the Forest, the country feel of our town and ensure local people’s views are considered and respected.

EXPERIENCED AND PROVEN
Many years of experience in district and parish councils in Epping Forest.  A track record of getting residents voice heard. Knows how to make your voice heard at the council

PROTECTING THE GREEN BELT
John is a strong, clear and experienced voice in planning matters having led on the Local Plan. With Labour’s planning policies putting the Green Belt under pressure, he has the experience to defend our villages, working closely with local MPs and County Council candidate Ray Balcombe.

ALL COMMUNITIES MATTER
John supported local initiatives and speaks out for facilities for local communities. He will ensure focus on Ongar Leisure Centre as well as fighting for better roads and
transport. He has a record of supporting local businesses and recognising the damage of fly-tipping.

I’m south Essex born and a Billericay resident for thirty plus years.  In that time, I’ve been a long-serving local school governor, chaired the Essex Wildlife Trust and completed two terms as the Honorary Secretary of the Royal Society of Wildlife Trusts. So it’s no shock that I know just how vital all of our open green spaces are. 
I currently work for the Professional Footballers' Association, supporting former players living with dementia. I’m also a local football club director.
Like most local residents, I'm deeply concerned about the way that mass housing development is being foisted on our town without care or concern for local people.  Our schools, GP and other health services, roads and public transport are already at breaking point.  Without massive improvements in local infrastructure, our town will cease to function properly.  We simply cannot allow this to continue as it is.
I’m grateful to have been selected as a Green candidate for my town again - and together we can build a real voice for Billericay..

I am currently Essex County Councillor for Bocking Division, having previously served on Braintree District Council for 36 years. The most important thing to me is to represent residents’ views and do what I can for them, along with a wealth of experience of knowing how the council works.

Witham Liberal Democrats have selected Ashley Thompson as their Parliamentary Candidate to fight the Tory incumbent Priti Patel at the forthcoming General Election. Ashley has lived virtually his entire life in Essex, having attended Southend High School For Boys and University of Essex, before embarking on a career in classical music Ashley spent a year as a Choral Scholar to Chelmsford Cathedral and now directs Witham Choral Society and, from April 2024, St. Nicolas Parish Church, Witham. He is a Lib Dem Councillor at Chelmsford City Council.

His work as an educationalist has led him to believe strongly in the need for better mental health support in schools. The Lib Dems are pushing for a state funded mental health support worker for EVERY school in the UK. This will be funded by tripling taxes on the big social media companies, who are so culpable in exacerbating body image and self esteem issues in our young people.

The state of the NHS is another top concern for Ashley, who believes we need to adopt an Invest to Save approach, because out of control and ever rising waiting lists are a total false economy. He is bewildered by the NHS real term cuts of £1.3billion planned for 2024/25 - money which could instead fund 31 million GP appointments!

Ashley says: "It's time the people of Witham stopped being taken for granted and had a proper voice. I've seen first hand the true extent of the toll that endless Tory cuts have had on youth services, child and adult social care, mental health services and most immediately visible of all, local highways. I have experienced at close quarters the effects of the cost of living and housing crises on everyone, but most especially the young, and am more than prepared to fight vested interests in an effort to create a fairer and greener society for all."

Paul Thorogood is the Green Party candidate for Braintree constituency at the General Election to be held on Thursday 4th July 2024.

Paul grew up in the Cressing Road area of Braintree, and attended the Alec Hunter High School (now Academy) before gaining a 2.1 Honours degree in Politics from Southampton University.

Paul has an NCTJ professional qualification in journalism and worked as a journalist for 23 years. He started his journalism career at the Braintree & Witham Times before moving on to the Colchester Gazette, Ipswich Evening Star and several Fleet Street titles including The Daily Mirror when Piers Morgan was editor.

Paul now runs his own small business and lives in Coggeshall and is married with two children who attend local state schools. He became involved in local politics when plans for the Rivenhall Airfield waste incinerator were gaining traction and he began reading about the subject. Now a committed environmentalist, Paul is concerned with protecting and preserving the natural environment from pollution and overdevelopment. He believes strongly in the principle ‘Think globally, act locally’ - globally campaigning against climate change; locally improving services such as schools, saving libraries from closure and protecting wildlife and the countryside.

Paul was elected as a Braintree District Councillor to represent Kelvedon & Feering ward in 2019 and then re-elected in 2023. He was elected as the County Councillor for Braintree Eastern division in 2021.

Richard has been a dedicated parish councillor since 2015, a city councillor in The Lawns since 2019, member of the local Speedwatch group and is an active volunteer for the Chelmsford Litter Wombles & the SUPsect Water Wombles, helping keep our city clean and tidy.

He is committed to community safety, fixing the pothole crisis and listening to residents’ concerns. Alongside Mike, he has continuously stood up for Springfield residents over many years.

Richard will be a strong local champion for families and communities in Springfield. On 18th June, vote for Richard Lee and the Lib Dems.

Terence was born in Colchester and spent his first 10 years moving about with his family as his father was a soldier. After returning to Colchester he completed his secondary education and then worked on a building site for a year before joining the Army himself to fulfil an ambition to train as a Mechanical Engineer.

After 25 years’ service he left the Army having attained the rank of Warrant Officer 2nd Class and now works as an Engineering Operations Manager maintaining plant for wastewater sites.

His current role has given him an insight into the pollution that is sent out into our waterways and beaches by outdated infrastructure which is unable to cope with the increased number of houses connected to it.  He wants water companies to be forced to reinvest their profits on equipment instead of just paying fines.

He decided to stand as a candidate for Reform UK because he found that the Con/Lab/Lib wheel wasn't representing the wishes and needs of our country, with the career politicians failing to keep the promises that had won them elections, showing contempt for the electorate. Someone had to take a stand to give the people of Colchester an alternative to vote for, so he stood up to the task.

Terence has been married to Sharon for 32 years and they have 3 children and one grandson. They both enjoy going out on dog walks or riding their motorbikes around the County’s lanes, dodging the potholes and stopping off for refreshments along the way.

I am standing as your Green Party candidate for Braintree Town, to make sure local people’s voices are heard and respected. I will push for proper support for children and young people with special educational needs, stand up for minority groups and LGBTQ+ rights. Fight to protect our environment for future generations. I believe companies must be held to account for pollution, not let off the hook. Our town centre deserves better transport links and fairer parking charges, so that it can truly flourish. We need genuinely affordable homes for local people, not just luxury homes for the few, we should build on unused and under used industrial land — not by sacrificing our green spaces. As your councillor for Braintree Town, I will put people, equality and the environment at the heart of all my efforts.

I’m standing to be a a representative to the local community on local issues in the forthcoming Hutton South by-election.

Under the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats in Brentwood we’ve seen council tax increase by 46% in the past ten years yet services have suffered. The council even intends to reduce our bin collections to fortnightly and now charges us extra to recycle garden waste. Our roads are strewn with potholes and our High Street shops are increasingly boarded up.

Crime has soared under the Conservative Police and Crime Commissioner. He sits on the local council. Detection rates have plummeted to the extent that criminals committing the most serious sexual crimes in Essex have barely a 3% chance of being prosecuted now.

The Conservative Lib Dem council is now planning to take a bulldozer to our countryside and is keen to build a huge new town within our borough with no consultation amongst local people.

I will fight against all of these failures and expose the huge financial waste that exists within our local authority.

The Lib Dem Tory uni party is not fit for purpose here. I’ll be a loud voice for Hutton South, the area in which I’ve lived for years, as I was when i was a Brentwood councillor a decade ago.

If there is one positive the Coronavirus has taught us, it is this: caring, vibrant, local community life is essential; essential for our quality of life and, at times, essential for our very survival.

The importance of community was clear throughout my 45-year career in education, and it could not be clearer during this global epidemic.

I have lived in Brentwood for more than 33 years and the town has everything going for it.

There are parks, woodland and open spaces within minutes of the High Street. It has history as a route centre since the days of the Romans and the Pilgrims, and is within easy reach of London and the coast. Greens want to revive communities like ours. Give Greens the chance!

Susan and her husband have lived in Warley since 1997. She taught French and German in comprehensive schools for 30 years. Now retired, she works voluntarily as a community adviser, supporting Brentwood residents with issues such as housing, employment problems or benefits.

She loves walking and cycling, and enjoys music and the arts. Genuinely affordable housing is desperately needed here. Susan will prioritise bringing empty houses back into use, giving first refusal to local first-time buyers on new homes and ensuring that developments include social housing and property for older people. She is also keen to require private landlord accreditation to provide decent accommodation at reasonable rents and to increase security by encouraging longer-term tenancies.

Cuts in Council funding threaten the very existence of community groups. Susan will work to secure long-term, stable funding for groups like Mind, Brentwood Community Transport, Citizens Advice and our Council for Voluntary Services.

I moved to Ingatestone 30 years ago and taught in a secondary school in Brentwood for 20 years. As a Parish Councillor I am heavily involved in my local community and this involvement also extends to being Chair of Ingatestone & Fryerning Cricket Club.

I joined the Green Party in 2011 and was selected to be our parliamentary candidate in Brentwood in both 2017 and 2019 general elections.

The last year has shown the vital importance of local communities. We are fortunate to have access to green space, but it must be defended against unsustainable development.

Both Brentwood and Essex councils need Green councillors to raise the issues that other parties often ignore. The climate and ecological crisis that we face needs addressing without delay - a vote for the Green Party is a vote for climate action now.

Richard has lived and worked in Brentwood since 1990 in the local university and as governor for two schools. He acts as a consultant on education and technology as well as leading research in the field. His concerns are that education is badly underfunded, that it should have democratic overview and that the academy and free school arrangements have lead to overpaid chief executives of unaccountable trusts. This affects local residents by making it easy for schools to drop support for a wide curriculum, leaving out the creative subjects and opportunities for children with special needs.

If elected Richard  will work hard to sort out the housing crisis in Brentwood, which leaves many young people unable to afford a home and will pursue education issues working with the County Council.

I have lived in Brentwood most of my life, having moved here with my parents as a very young child

I have always voted, but over the last few years I have become increasingly disillusioned with the incompetence, lies, and broken promises of the prevailing government, and the current party of opposition just offers more of the same. Britain deserves better. Reform UK offer a proper genuine alternative to the current two-party system.

I believe that Britain cannot sustain the massive immigration numbers that we have seen over the last few years. I believe that the race towards net zero is hitting the poorest in society first and ultimately will lead to us all being colder and poorer. I believe in a low regulation low taxation economy that encourages free market economics, in a society where the rights of criminals do not trump the rights of victims, and where children should be protected and the elderly respected.

We managed to find £37 billion to pay for a failed test track and trace system during Covid, yet fail to adequately fund our NHS, Social Care, Education or Criminal Justice system. Taxation is the highest it has been in over 70 years, and government overreach is out of control. This is all wrong. Westminster seems to have forgotten that the government exists because of the people; the people do not exist because of the government.

When I discovered Reform UK, I found a party that shared many of my views. Standing as a political candidate was never on my “to do” list, but circumstances change.

I applied and was accepted to stand for Reform UK at the next General Election, giving the people of Brentwood and Ongar an alternative to the current two-party system. It’s time for people to stop voting for the least worst option, and start voting for what they believe in.

I’m standing as an independent candidate for Essex County Council because I believe local elections should be about getting things done, not party politics.

I live and work in the area, and like many residents I see the same issues every day.

My focus is simple: fix the basics and represent the area properly.

That means:

🛣️ Improving roads, pavements and drainage
💡 Fixing street lighting and local infrastructure
🚌 Supporting better, more reliable public transport
🏫 Improving SEND provision and support for families
🌿 Protecting green spaces and making better use of brownfield land

I’m not part of any political party, so I won’t be taking instructions or voting along party lines. My only focus will be what is best for Brightlingsea, Alresford, Great Bentley, Elmstead Market and Thorrington.

I’ve spent years getting stuck into local issues, from setting up Community Speedwatch and traffic monitoring, to organising volunteer groups to clear footpaths and improve access.

If elected, I will:

Be visible and accessible
Take responsibility for issues and follow them through
Challenge where needed and work with others where it gets results

This election is about who will actually represent the area and get things sorted.

If that’s what you’re looking for, I’d really appreciate your support.

Born in St. John's Hospital, I have lived in Chelmsford all my life, attending Barnes Farm Primary School in Chelmer Village. I joined the Green Party in early 2018; increasingly concerned with the area's issues with the environment, poverty and inequality I joined the only party that made sense to me.

I am a keen squash player, and enjoyed playing football when I was younger

Chelmsford has a lot going for it, countryside within walking distance and in normal times a vibrant city centre - but it needs pointing in the right direction. There is a lot of ‘greenwashing’ from the other parties, but if you truly Want Green - Vote Green!

**Dear Resident**,

My name is Kevin, and I’m standing for you in Broomfield & Writtle division and Broomfield & The Walthams ward.

I live in Broomfield and work locally as a paramedic. Through my work, I see first-hand the pressures on our roads, services and community— I understand how much it matters that we feel safe, connected, and able to enjoy the natural world around us.

**A practical plan for our area**

I will focus on issues that really matter:

· Housing development that starts with services—schools, GP access, buses, and green spaces, and working with police and community safety partners

· Bus-first planning, protecting routes (including evenings and Sundays) and properly linking communities

· Safer school journeys, including a 20mph zone on School Lane and measures to reduce rat-running

· Proper road maintenance—because prevention is cheaper than repair, and residents shouldn’t pay twice

· Stronger support for social care, with reliable, well-commissioned services rather than patchwork provision

· Protection of wildlife and access to nature as a core part of planning decisions

· Transparency in local government and meaningful consultation—so residents are informed and have a real say in the decisions that affect them.

**A note on this election**

As the Green Party is largely funded by members and small donations, we have the freedom to stay focused on local priorities. By contrast, larger parties such as the Conservatives—and newer parties like Reform—rely heavily on large donors and corporations. I often urge voters to consider what interests those funding models could bring with them.

I notice too, that there has been some focus diverted to national issues like immigration. I want to be straight with voters: local councils do not set immigration policy. These elections are about our services, planning, transport, and community wellbeing. Suggesting otherwise risks distracting from the decisions that truly affect our day-to-day life here.

**A local representative you know**

In a time when trust in politics is uncertain, I’m offering something simple: a local candidate with a track record of serving the community every day.

I work with people from all walks of life, often at their most vulnerable. It has taught me how to listen, how to advocate, and how to work constructively with others to get things done.

That’s the approach I would bring to representing you.

This May, I hope you will consider supporting the Green Party.

**Yours sincerely**, 
Kevin 
Green Party Candidate Broomfield & Writtle / Broomfield & The Walthams

Mike Steel is Chelmsford City Cllr for the Broomfield and Walthams ward and Chairman of Great Waltham Parish Council. He has lived in the Chelmsford area for the last 40 years, and currently resides in Great Waltham 

Mike Steel moved to the Chelmsford area 41 years ago after completing a degree in Electronic Engineering in Leeds. He joined the Marconi company where he worked for the next 20 years, followed by 20 years at BT. His last role before retiring in 2018, was  managing a $1Bn global IT contract for the Pharmaceuticals industry. His background is technology and business and he is a Charted Engineer.

Over the 41 years he has lived in central Chelmsford, Broomfield and latterly Great Waltham. He is well known throughout the constituency – 25 years as a Parish Cllr, 7 years as Chairman, City Cllr, Scout Chairman, and a member of many committees – Twinning, British Legion, Road Traffic, Speedwatch, Parish Productions, Housing Liaison. He is also a qualified first aider and volunteers for many local events.   

Mike involves himself in many ECC aspects, being the Superfast Broadband Champion for the area and a Local Highways Panel member. During the 1st wave of Covid-19, Mike and his wife, Joanna, set up a volunteer group registered with Essex Welfare Services and Chelmsford Volunteer Services. He is also a Goodsam responder. 

Mike has 3 children all of which attended the local primary and secondary schools, before going on to University and successful careers. He is an active gym user and 3rd Duan karate blackbelt instructor.

Our candidate for Broomfield and Writtle & for the by-election in Broomfield and The Walthams is Rachel Wheelhouse 👍

Rachel has lived in Broomfield for over 20 years, raised a family here and also worked at Broomfield Hospital, so is a true local champion. She is passionate about sorting potholes and pavements being accessible for all users, the environment, dealing with antisocial behaviour and championing local businesses and talent in arts and music.

On 7th May, vote for Rachel and the Lib Dems for a community champion ready to take on Tories and Reform.

**RE-ELECT ROSS!**

I live on Collingwood Road. I grew up on Church Street and went to school here too. I am Witham through and through, proudly standing again to represent our town.

Being a local councillor isn’t glamorous or high-flying. It’s about putting in the hard work and standing up for residents. Since 2021, I have represented the north of the town. **I have fought hard to get things done and have a record of action and delivery:**

**1. Fighting Witham’s corner for more highway repairs -** I have secured 100s of pothole repairs plus full resurfacing jobs for Chipping Hill, Collingwood Road, Cressing Road, Braintree Road and Colchester Road. Forest Road is scheduled for the next financial year.

**2. Supporting our town centre and local businesses -** I saved one hour free parking for Newland Street and continue to be a thorn in the side of Braintree District Council, ensuring they fulfil their commitment to improve our town centre.

**3. Holding utility companies to account -** They must do more to minimise disruption during road works, ensure better communication with residents and properly repair the highway once done.

I hope you will choose to lend me your support and re-elect me on Thursday 7 May - so that I can continue as our local councillor, and as a champion for Witham Town.

Best wishes,

Ross

Having grown up in Somerset and Devon and lived in Them since, Alphington is now my home. Proud Professional with A Career in the NHS & Lifelong Resident of Whipton, Exeter

I decided to get involved in local government because I believe our community deserves stronger representation, practical solutions, and a voice that truly listens to residents.

I believe local government has a huge, if often unnoticed, impact on people's everyday lives. So many of us are completely dissafected with the establishment parties and with good reason.
Pinhoe deserves better. It deserves reform

I have lived here for 26 years and for the past decade it has been a real privilege to serve Pinhoe as one of your City Councillors.

If you re-elect me, I promise that I’ll keep working hard for you:

I’m proud to live in Pinhoe and Exeter, and while both can be improved, I will keep working to make Pinhoe the best it can be. My record speaks for itself.

I’ll fight to ensure the council delivers value for money, keeping council tax low, with just 8% of your council tax going to the City Council to fund our services and facilities.

I’ll work with the Council, police and local groups to support community projects and initiatives, while tackling fly-tipping, litter and antisocial behaviour in Pinhoe.

I hope I can earn your support at this upcoming election.

Philip Thomas moved to Exeter five years ago and has lived in Priory Ward for four of those years. He works as a physicist at the University of Exeter and volunteers at his local church.

Philip is a strong supporter of transparent, collaborative decision making in local government. If elected councillor, one of his priorities will be to work hard to improve the Council's transparency and accountability. He has spoken to other Priory Ward residents who feel taken for granted by the Labour Council, for example regarding the handling of the development of Edwards Court.

I’m Jack Vickers, your local Green candidate for Priory. I’m proud to be standing for election on 7 May.

It’s been great meeting so many of you, and I’m very grateful for the support people continue to show me here. Speaking with residents on the doorstep has helped me better understand the issues people face day to day. Here is some important information ahead of the election in a few weeks.

I lived on Burnthouse Lane for years, and if there’s one thing I remember about living in the area, it’s the widespread feeling that we’d been neglected and forgotten by the council. Too often our neighbourhood hasn’t had the attention or investment it deserves, and many residents tell me they feel the same today.
I have worked many jobs over the years, from warehousing to retail to security, and I know how to work in a team to deliver results.

I am passionate about tackling the lack of affordable housing in our city, as well as improving transport and cycling infrastructure. I am also committed to protecting our green spaces, such as Ludwell Valley Park, so they can be enjoyed by local families for generations to come.

I am proud to have been born and raised in Exeter, where my family has deep roots. Having lived here all my life, I care deeply about our community’s future. My experience travelling, running a business, and working as a ski teacher and national coach has helped me connect with people from all walks of life. I am standing as a councillor to ensure local voices are heard. I will be approachable, accountable, and focused on practical solutions. I am not a career politician—I am one of you, committed to making a difference.

I’m Rose Lelliott and I am delighted to be standing again as your Labour and Co-operative candidate in St David’s.

I work as a policy researcher and live locally in the ward. I love calling this beautiful part of Exeter home.

I have a track record of standing up for our community, such as supporting the gold Britain in Bloom award, speaking out against the Mallison Bridge cut and getting potholes filled.

I am currently leading the Keep Exeter Lit Campaign against Devon County Council’s streetlight dimming policy, which has received local and national media coverage, alongside becoming the biggest ever petition on Devon County Council’s website.

As a councillor, I will continue to speak up for residents, using  my experience of campaigning to be a hardworking and approachable local representative.

My day job is as a professor at the University of Exeter, where I teach criminology. My work has led to collaborations with local and other police services across the UK and internationally. I want to use this experiences to work with the existing team of Green councillors in the ward and focus on community safety. I am also a committed trade unionist. I have served as branch President and Secretary of the University and College Union among many other posts. I believe every resident deserves dignity and respect — and I will always work to make sure your voice is heard.

To find out about the priorities of the Green Party in St David's and Exeter more widely, visit: https://exeter.greenparty.org.uk/why-green/.

Born and raised in Exeter, and with most of my immediate family still living close by, I have always considered this city home. It should be a place we’re proud of and where people want to visit, but it has sadly become a hollowed-out city centre: endless vape and charity shops, litter, drugs, anti-social behaviour… We can’t continue like this.

The good news is we have the opportunity to change things for the better.

After qualifying as a solicitor and pursuing a career in international finance, including over a decade in FinTech helping expanding micro-businesses all over the world to succeed, I now want to use my experience to transform our city for the better. My background in law and business means I’m well qualified to scrutinise budgets, contracts, and outsourcing, and ensure taxpayers’ money is spent as effectively as possible.

I still love Exeter — I know it really well and am a keen local historian — and I would love to see it restored to a prosperous, thriving, well-maintained regional business hub, and a place worth visiting.

I was born in Exeter and have been a resident of Heavitree for the last 30 years.

I have worked for Royal Mail for 38 years, so have first hand knowledge of how our roads and pavements have deteriorated over the years.

We all know that traffic volumes are a problem. A more integrated and reliable public transport system is needed in Devon to reduce the need for people to use their cars.

The safety of pedestrians, schoolchildren and cyclists also requires addressing. We need a choice of proposals for which everyone who may be affected can have their opinions heard before a suitable choice is selected.

As a born and bred Devonian, I have an undying love for our county and for our city—its beauty, history, and resilience. No matter what is thrown its way, it always recovers. But it deserves more than that; it deserves to thrive.

Witnessing the decline of my local area—shops shutting, streets decaying, and the rise of anti-social behavior, which has been left unchecked by authorities—has persuaded me to no longer be an observer, and instead to take
an active role in improving where we live and making it everything we all wish it could be.

Vanessa strongly supported the Remain campaign, but is concerned to listen to, and represent all the residents of Exeter.

During a transition of this scale, having a strong, experienced voice representing St Thomas will be essential. I hope you’ll place your trust in me to be that voice. Please judge me on the track record I’ve built as your Labour councillor—and on my continued ambition for St Thomas as we move into this next chapter.

Ann is a research scientist, and has lived and worked in Exeter since 2004.

One of her key interests is transport and encouraging better coordination between the City and County councils to make it easier for everyone to travel in more sustainable ways. She is also concerned about development on the city’s vital green spaces.

I have owned the Alehouse with my husband since it opened 7 years ago putting us at the heart of Fareham’s Community and Independent Shopping Scene. And I have lived here since 2020, and before that I grew up in Gosport so I am a local gal with local focus!

Some of the things I care deeply about are youth services and schemes to get young people supported and given the chance to do something positive for themselves and their communities.

**About Matt**

Having moved to Fulham in 2024, it is a joy to be the Green Party candidate for Palace and Hurlingham, to offer to serve a community that has warmly welcomed my civil partner Peter (Vicar of All Saints Fulham),  our scruffy labradoodle, Finley, and myself, as we share in the life, the spaces and places, and the future of this ward.
Through my work for the NHS as it supports and cares for people experiencing homelessness, and in church and community work at St Andrew’s Fulham Fields, I see, every day, the diverse realities of life in our borough where health, housing, quality of life and opportunity can vary from street to street, neighbour to neighbour. 
On May 7th, we will all come to the ballot box across Palace and Hurlingham not just with our different political opinions or party affiliations but with the variety of experiences of life. We may prefer the Hurlingham Club to Craven Cottage, would rather a pint at The Eight Bells than a picnic in Bishop’s Park. We may know the comfort and security of a home where we have grown our families up in, or feel a real and present struggle of finding affordable and appropriate housing or the need for connection and community. When we vote we each carry all our needs alongside the pressures and impact that decisions made locally and nationally have on the people and places we love and care about.

**Why Matt?**

When voting Green this election, we bring our needs, our hopes and our dreams for our green spaces, our river, our air, our safety, our streets, our schools, our vital local services and networks to work in more sustainable, healthy, impactful and equitable ways. 
When voting Green this election, we are saying to those with power, that in a world where violent, divisive and othering rhetoric becomes ever louder and normalised, where the climate crisis is denied, and the value and worth of others is questioned, denied or actively destroyed  -we want to foster and create hopeful, just and compassionate communities across our borough, our country and beyond. 
When voting Green this election, we are expressing our frustrations with the political parties and wider systems that feel broken, we are acknowledging our anger and anxiety at feeling overlooked, unheard, or undervalued, we are demonstrating our right to be seen and heard, and acknowledging a desire for hope over hate.

**What will Matt do?**

Palace and Hurlingham may look to some, on paper, like a single story, a singular vote. But the stories of this place and our lives are varied, dynamic and each of them important and worth sharing, deserving of a councillor who listens openly, speaks honestly, and serves with care and compassion. Someone willing to bring both challenge and change with a hope-filled heart. 
In Palace and Hurlingham you may use up to three votes. A vote for me and the Green Party is an opportunity to do politics differently, to challenge the idea that “this is just the way things are are”. It is a chance to work together to raise our expectations, to be more ambitious for our neighbourhood, and to build a community that works and cares for all.

statement_to_voters:
I’m standing with Reform UK for election to Eastleigh Borough Council and as your Prospective Parliamentary Candidate for the General Election this year because I’m proud to call Eastleigh my home, having lived in the borough for 13 years and the town centre for three years.

As a taxpayer, I have become increasingly disappointed and frustrated in the level of public services provided by the Council and its stakeholders.

Once elected, I will work tirelessly to slash the unnecessary bureaucracy and red tape to improve the services we receive from the Council which, in my view, have been deteriorating year on year.

We all deserve value for money public services that deliver tangible results; be that something as basic as getting our bins emptied on time right through to revitalising the town centre which has, in my view, very sadly changed beyond all recognition over the last few years from a vibrant shopping hub to a wasteland of empty units. I believe taxpaying residents deserves more than the Council is currently delivering.

A particular issue I am very troubled by is the rising level of violent crime, anti-social behaviour and drug dealing in the town which has been exacerbated by the closure of our police station that not only provided a safe, open place to residents needing to use it, its presence, without doubt, provided a deterrent against crime in Eastleigh itself and the wider constituency.  We have the right to feel safe in our town and constituency with a visible police presence to provide that comfort and assurance, not a remote office on the outskirts of town that you cannot walk into without making an appointment.

About Me

A bit more about me, I worked for the NHS at Omega House for almost five years, supporting a Clinical Commissioning Group Board which gave me a working insight into how public services are organised and delivered… there is a lot of work to do.  I also worked for the Commissioning Support Unit at Omega House in the Freedom of Information Team dealing with requests from members of the public, Councillors and Members of Parliament for Wednesday’s Prime Minister’s Questions.

For a time in 2015, I worked at Prysmian in their centenary year, supporting the CEO and Senior Management Team and whilst there was involved in organising a UK Trade and Industry visit.

Whilst working for a large financial services organisation in Southampton, I was Chair of the UK Employee Forum, representing circa 2,000 employees in Southampton and a further 2,500 across the UK. I also lead a local Leaseholder Action Group fighting for much needed changes in Leasehold law via the National Leasehold Campaign to demand the same rights for Leaseholders that other homeowners enjoy.

So, if you are hungry for meaningful change, are disillusioned with the shenanigans of the main parties or just feel politically homeless, why not consider voting for me and Reform UK…what have you got to lose?

I am standing to bring transparency, accountability, and disciplined decision-making to how public money is spent.

My background is in project and commercial management, where delivery, cost control, and clear outcomes are essential. That is the standard I will apply on your behalf.

My focus for Fareham is straightforward:
Infrastructure first - Roads, schools, and GP access must keep pace with development.

Tackling the congestion - Practical, deliverable improvements to reduce the daily pressure on our local routes.
Most importantly, value for money - Clear, accountable spending with measurable results.

Protecting our local costal military character - Sensible, balanced decisions that reflect our diverse community.

What you can expect from me:

Open and Straight answers.
Evidence-based decisions.
Consistent follow-through.

If you have ever asked where your money goes, I am standing to make sure we get a clear answer and better results.

I’m a mum, and I live right here in our community. Two years ago, I decided to stop complaining about what wasn’t working and do something about it by standing as a candidate for Cove and Southwood, and now also for Farnborough West.

Since then, I’ve been listening to residents, working locally and getting things done, from helping upgrade our playgrounds to bringing people together through community projects.

I chair a local preschool and help lead a community forum that connects local groups and residents, because strong communities don’t just happen, they’re built.

As your county councillor, I’ll focus on the everyday issues that matter most locally. I’ll keep pushing for better road maintenance, proper pothole repairs and solutions to parking problems. I’ll work with residents to hold Hampshire to account on road safety
issues along Iveley Road and Summit Avenue, and campaign for more visible policing so our streets feel safer.

You deserve a county councillor who listens, speaks up, and makes sure our area gets its fair share -I’ll be that voice for you.

I have lived in Rushmoor since 2021, and chose to settle here after leaving the Army. I now work delivering real, observable improvements to some of the most complex programmes in the public and private sector across the UK. I want to use this experience to stand up for local residents and businesses.

As your councillor I would prioritise:
-Standing up against austerity and funding cuts imposed by central government
-Tackling the housing crisis and spiralling cost of living - arguing for more investment in public housing and services
-Supporting local businesses to keep public money in our local community
-Ensuring services are delivered for the good of local residents, not to maximise profit
-Safeguarding our environment by tackling flytipping, holding companies to account on environmental damage and protecting our green spaces

Steve Forster has represented Fleet on Hampshire County Council since 2017 and on Hart District Council since 2016. He is the Executive Member for Education, responsible for approximately 500 schools and libraries across Hampshire.

He lives in Fleet West and is active in the community year-round.

What Steve has delivered:

As Executive Member for Education at Hampshire, Steve has approved 1,000 additional specialist SEND places across Hampshire between 2025 and 2030, including six new proposals at his most recent Decision Day. Since 2018, more than 750 new SEND places have already been created, with 350 in progress and discussions underway for 600+ more by 2030. Over 90% of Hampshire schools are rated outstanding or good by OFSTED. He approved the £2.1m refurbishment of Shepherds Down Special School and new Resourced Provisions at five schools across the county. Closer to home, Hartland Village Primary School is due to open next summer, funded through developer contributions.

In Fleet, Steve secured developer funding for the £1.3m Upper Street/Albert Street junction safety scheme, now going to consultation. He brokered the new Fleet-Farnborough bus link over two years with Rushmoor Colleagues, connecting Fleet Station, Hartland Village, Calthorpe Park School, and Hart Leisure Centre. He has delivered road resurfacing on Fleet Road, Kings Road, Hitches Lane, Norris Hill Road, with further schemes scheduled including Mounts Way and Fleet’s high street area.

As just one of hundreds of examples of successful case work,  a safety defect appeared on Fleet Road, he escalated it and had it temporarily fixed within hours.

At HCC cabinet level, Steve supported securing additional pothole repair resources mid-winter and the new lane-rental disruption charge which is expected to raise up to £5m per year extra towards highway maintenance.

Steve publicly and vocally opposed the ruling Hart administration’s 10,000 property Shapley Heath housing development. Working with a majority of residents and the Conservative group, he helped stop the proposed £23m plans to build on Gurkha Square instead supporting an affordable and better plan for refurbishing the Harlington. He helped secure the Hampshire and Solent Combined County Authority - a £1.3 billion investment over 30 years, after eight failed attempts since 2016 - and has fought to keep Hampshire's council tax among the lowest in the region: Band D at £1,690, compared with £1,938 in Surrey, £1,890 in West Sussex, and £2,007 in Oxfordshire.

On community safety, Steve is working with Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones to open a staffed police front desk at council offices, tackle shoplifting and anti social behaviour, prevent drug dealing, and expand Hart's CCTV coverage - with PCC budget now confirmed for CCTV measures. He is actively pursuing pavement parking enforcement and plans to introduce community safety patrols across Fleet.

Steve has worked with Fleet Phoenix for three years on the Hart Youth Achievement Awards, providing some Hampshire County Council grant funding. In memory of his daughter Sasha, he and his family created Sasha's Project, which has supported young people's mental health for the past five years.

Steve's approach:

Steve believes local government works best when it focuses on competence, delivery, and accountability. He communicates daily with residents through social media, responds to reported problems directly, and publishes the detail - funding figures, project timescales, council tax comparisons - so residents can judge the record for themselves.

If re-elected, Steve will:

Continue expanding SEND provision and protecting school standards across Hampshire.

Deliver the Upper Street junction safety scheme, the Fleet-Farnborough bus link, and further road resurfacing across Fleet and Elvetham Heath.

Push for permanent highway maintenance investment and new cycling and walking routes, including the planned 3-metre wide cycle path along Hitches Lane.

Work to get the best outcome for the proposed Hart/Rushmoor/Basingstoke local government reorganisation, which he considers risks becoming financially unsustainable and where there is a risk of Basingstoke and Rushmoor dumping housing allocations on Fleet.

Strengthen community safety with a police front desk, expanded CCTV, shoplifting enforcement, and community patrols.

Continue supporting Sasha's Project and Fleet's youth services.

Steve is accessible, responsive, and visible in Fleet every week of the year. His record is specific and verifiable. He puts Fleet first.

Tonia is Bursledon’s longest-serving Borough Councillor and is Cabinet Member for Health at the Borough Council, leading on working with the NHS to improve our local health services and on community safety. Born in Winchester and living in the Worthys and Itchen Valley since 2018 I combine over 35 years of business experience with a strong record of local service. Jackie has stood up for residents on local councils for over 20 years. Jackie is Chairman of the Tubbs Hall, a Governor at Kings Worthy School, and a trustee of The Watercress Way.

I have lived in the ward, with my young family, since 2014. Gosport Labour is on your side. We rise above childish political games to deliver on the priorities of Gosport’s residents.

Living in Gosport all my life and working over 20 years within the Education sector across the Hampshire region, I am invested and committed to a thriving, safe and greener community. I am seen as being honest, hardworking and someone who really listens.

Please elect Julie Westerby on May 5th.

I have lived in Bramshott near Liphook for 30 years and have both children and grandchildren living close by.

I consider myself a ‘small c’ conservative, having spent a lifetime in business rather than politics. I started and managed businesses (including a local business that employed 30 people) and worked for major corporations both in the UK and abroad, so I understand about managing people and resources, and being prudent with finances.

I was driven to support Reform through desperation at the failure of recent governments – both the last Conservative and current Labour one. I believe in small government, low taxes and high growth. The Conservatives and Labour have delivered the opposite of these things.

So I was delighted to be asked to stand for Reform in the local elections. Listening to local concerns, the number 1 issue in the area is the continued threat of substantial new housing developments without the related investment in infrastructure. National housing targets imposed by central government have led to large housing developments being waived through by the local Conservative authorities despite their talk of protecting rural communities. People feel they have no say in what is happening.

In 2019, The Conservative-run Hampshire County Council declared a ‘Climate Emergency’ – who voted for that? Since then, they have spent and estimated £40m on ‘Net Zero’ initiatives. Their planning policies typically prioritise supposed ‘climate change mitigation over whether local people actually support the proposed development. At the same time, our roads are congested, full of potholes, flood regularly (witness the semi-permanent ‘great flood of Bramshott’) and are often strewn with litter (left to be addressed by heroic local litter-picking residents).

Reform would divert all funds associated with Net Zero to fixing potholes and proving actual infrastructure.

I want to see a greater sense of pride in our villages, with thriving small businesses, shops, cafes - and in particular pubs – that all add to the vibrancy of village life. All these businesses need the active support of their local authority. At the same time I would fight for zero tolerance of petty crime, vandalism and anti-social behaviour.

A vote at this local election is an opportunity to show to both Keir Starmer and the Conservatives that we have had enough of their indifference or at worst – hostility – to our rural way of life. We need to have a say in our future.

and help to reduce speeding, tackle rural crime and respond to climate change.

If elected as your County Councillor I will listen to you and act on your concerns. Again, working with my fellow Councillors at all levels of local Government, I will attempt to bridge the gaps between local council services to better serve you.
Elect me – Get the team!


Promoted by Debbie Curnow-Ford on behalf of Debbie Curnow-Ford, at East Hampshire Conservatives, 14a Butts Road, Alton, Hampshire, GU34 1ND

If elected, you can expect honesty, hard work, and a genuine commitment to our community.

I will:

- Stand up for every resident, not just the loudest voices
- Work collaboratively, but challenge decisions that harm our area
- Fight for a fairer system that reduces inequality
- Protect the environment for future generations
- Support practical solutions that improve lives today

I believe politics should be about people, about making sure everyone feels heard, valued, and supported. It should also be about responsibility: to each other, and to the natural world we depend on.

Our countryside, our communities, and our public services are too important to take for granted. I will do everything I can to protect them, to build a future that is greener, fairer, and more hopeful for everyone.

I am standing for the Liberal Democrats to offer real choice and much needed change to the electors of Liphook, Headley and Grayshott.  The Liberal Democrats are ready to offer a fresh approach.  The Conservatives have been in control of Hampshire County Council for 28 years and have taken your vote for granted.

I have the experience and commitment required to be a successful County Councillor:

**Leadership** I have spent my career running complex organisations under financial pressure.  As an experienced CEO I bring focus and delivery - exactly what HCC needs as budgets tighten and Council Tax rises.

**Community Commitment** I currently volunteer for three organisations supporting people with mental health, alcohol and substance abuse issues.  Early support for these people matters and reflects Liberal Democrat values.

**Councillor experience** I have previous experience as a Parish Councillor with responsibilities including planning permission, highways, facility management and charities.

I want to work with our village communities to
1. Protect and fix our local environment
2. improve access to Social Care for adults and Special Educational Needs and Disability support for children and young people
3. Re-think Road Maintenance so that we repair more defects and not less

I left the Conservatives after nearly 50 years because they are no longer an inclusive party.  They have just been trying to mimic Reform UK.  By contrast, it is the Liberal Democrats who offer responsibility, tolerance and respect as the essential elements of a free, fair and open society, founded on strong local communities,

If you share these values, then I hope you will consider voting for me on May 7th.  Thank you, and I look forward to working hard for you and your families.

My plan with over 30 years experience of delivering for residents is to find and persuade the person who can deliver results. The New Forest has been my home for over 35 years, and I love it. As a GP in Lymington for all those years as well as holding many clinical public service roles, I have frontline experience of what needs to change and improve in our local system. I am passionate about finding sustainable solutions to enable the NHS to deliver quality care for all.



I am committed to addressing social and health inequalities; we have areas of deep deprivation in this constituency, sadly the issues of the vulnerable are often less well addressed in areas of affluence.

Address the issue of lack of affordable housing in the New Forest

Be focussed on rebuilding our public services based on sound economic foundations

Be invested in minimising the effects of climate change and in protecting the environment

Help the young and vulnerable avoid falling into illegal activities including County Lines

Push for robust mental health support across the New Forest, currently tragically under resourced

Work hard on providing more accessible help to victims of domestic violence and abusive relationships



As your MP I will be approachable and commit to working hard to ensure we have a caring, inclusive and flourishing constituency.

I am a transplant surgeon with over 35 years’ experience in the NHS, and have lived in the New Forest for over 10 years. My time is now divided between helping out in transplant units in the UK, and working overseas in conflict zones such as Gaza. I have previously led negotiations on behalf of the BMA for both junior and senior doctors, successfully introducing new contracts for both groups. As a councillor, I would be committed to working hard to improve local services and encourage implementation of Green policies, such as improving public transport. I will actively seek the views of all those I represent throughout my tenure, not only prior to election.

I work in the housing development sector and have a background in commercial property where I gained my experience in Central London. With housing being a matter with an acute shortage of affordable property I have ideas on delivering homes for local people at costs which they can meet.

Hampshire County Council has an impressive property portfolio and my ambition would be to review its assets and explore ways to improve the capital it can generate where surplus revenue can make a meaningful contribution to improving the local infrastructure, such as the ongoing challenge of potholes.

The Hampshire Avon, a precious south coast Chalk Stream, is being tested beyond its capability to deal with the challenges that are presented to it and with my knowledge on how to improve outcomes to safeguard the interests of this truly valuable resource of natural capital and the many species that rely on our healthy rivers I hope to make a difference.

With some much of our County being owned by agriculture, I feel that it is imperative that we work with this sector to meet our environmental objectives. We need to build in resilience into our practices to safeguard ecology and ensure that there is an efficient mechanism for food delivery whilst considering the impacts and reducing these.

statement_to_voters:
If elected as your councillor, my job will be to represent you. I will:

- Attend your Parish Council meetings to listen to the issues that affect you so that I can represent you and your community
- Always be available by phone, letter, email or in person, to listen to your problems with council services and do what I can to help you
- Provide regular updates on the issues I am working on for you

These are some of the important issues I am campaigning on:

**Stop the floods, fix the roads!**
The Council says it can’t afford to fix our roads. Yet flooding is a major cause of dangerous potholes. “We must deal with the flooding, so money is not wasted on repairs that don’t last.” Drains must be regularly maintained and the Council must use its powers to require landowners to clear their ditches. “I will campaign for a more proactive approach which will prevent damage and free up funds to do more repairs.”

**Restore our rural buses**
Many people rely on buses to get about and yet our services have been cut to the bone by the Conservatives. “I will fight to restore the Taxishare service, so no village is left without a lifeline to shops and GP surgeries.”

**Safer streets**
20 mph speed limits in some towns and villages would let people walk and cycle safely. In the forest, animals are being killed by speeding drivers. We need speed indicator signs to deter speeding, backed up by regular police checks.

**Make recycling easier**
“I will fight to keep our recycling centres open and campaign for community skips.” This will make it easier to dispose of large items and deter fly-tipping. We should also help people to recycle by accepting more items, such as foil, pots and tubs.

**Help for our high streets**
Our high streets must be places that people want to come to! We must work with landlords to encourage them to let empty shops. Lyndhurst and Fordingbridge must get their fair share of funding from the new Mayor’s investment fund. This will help to breathe new life into our high streets.

I am a member of the Green Party because I think it is the only political party that has the answers to the most important issues that we all face.

“A vote for the Green Party is a vote for a society which helps those in genuine need and isn’t afraid to stand up to those who would destroy the things we value.”

Please contact me:

**About Me**
I live in New Milton with my two children who attend local schools. I work for a family business in the New Forest aimed at connecting people with our beautiful natural environment.

Affordable Housing 
Sustainable Transport 
Cost of Living
Clean Rivers 
Improving Social Care

I am a Town and District Councillor for Barton on Sea and New Milton where I’ve lived for over 45years. 
Ex Mayor of New Milton
Ex Chairman of New Forest District Council 
Treasurer and joint founder of Milton Heritage Society

It was a great pleasure to recently return to Lymington to live after living in the Midlands being active in the community including as a district councillor.

I have a working background in the cultural sector. I have a keen interest in promoting culture as a positive way of improving and enriching lives.

My main focus will be on green issues and rejuvenating our wonderful high street. We need to find new ways to revitalise our town centres.

I believe in cross-party working and community consultation. There is too much political squabbling in the New Forest. As a councillor, I will offer experience and a desire to break through these barriers to produce effective local government.

I am standing once more as your candidate for New Milton North, Milford and Hordle Division in the Hampshire County Council elections on Thursday 7th May 2026.

It has been a privilege to be your Hampshire county councillor for the past 8 years. My priorities, if re-elected, will be:

Fran Carpenter 
Conservative Candidate, New Milton North, Milford & Hordle Division 
Hampshire County Council

Active in EcoSway and the coast2forest sustainable transport group, Clare is working to build a better-integrated, greener transport network across the New Forest - reducing car dependency and tackling the rural isolation that affects so many residents.

Aidan is standing to represent New Milton North, Milford and Hordle on Hampshire County Council.

His background includes serving as a Foundation College Governor and a Trustee for housing and dementia charities, giving him a deep understanding of the vital services our communities rely on.

Philippa Gray is your local Liberal Democrat candidate for the Bedhampton Ward, where she has lived for over 30 years.

Philippa says, ‘I am inspired by the way that resilient communities can work together and want to use my energy, time and experience to help make Havant and Hampshire a better place in which to live, work and relax.’

Philippa enjoys taking practical steps to build our community and relieve the impact of climate change. She is an accredited Green Liberal Democrat, volunteers at Repair Café Havant and Solent Cycle Project and supports Havant Friends of the Earth and Havant Climate Alliance. Philippa is retired from work as an IT project manager but now works hard and uses her skills as a trustee of Bedhampton Community Centre and a director of Solent Remade Community Interest Company.

I’ve lived in Havant since the mid 1980s and in West Leigh since 2007. I have been active in Leigh Park and West Leigh. I founded the Havant Community Litter Pickers over in 2018. We regularly clear the green by Sharps Copse, the woods by Havant Academy, Great Copse Woods off High Lawn Way, Petersfield Road and other areas. 

I have been a regular runner and volunteer at Havant Parkrun at Staunton Country Park, having volunteered more than 350 times and run over 500 times.

What can I do for you if you elect me? Work to Tackle Antisocial Behaviour in Leigh Park – I will campaign for CCTV in Leigh Park, better community policing, and cooperation between the police and the community they serve. This will help to protect our green spaces.

**I am a local volunteer and have been chosen as Hart Lib Dems’ candidate for Hampshire County Council’s Odiham & Hook Division, and Hart District Council’s Hook Ward**.

I and my husband Tim have lived in Hook for over 30 years, and our son attended Hook and Robert Mays schools. I have experienced both the vibrant and supportive nature of the local community, as well as its increase in its size.

Our daughter Lizzie was born in 2000 with a rare genetic condition, and the 26 years since have been a huge learning curve for me in the SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) world.

I have been selected as the Conservative candidate for Hampshire County Council elections in May 2026, covering the Odiham and Hook Division.
I want to ensure that Hampshire continues to deliver great services and value for money.  I also wish to use my experience on both District and County to guides our organisations though Local Government Reorganisation.

The Council has to work for the people of East Hampshire.

I believe strongly in upholding human dignity, safety and protection from wrong-doing. statement_to_voters:
You will shortly have the opportunity to vote for who runs Hampshire County Council.  I am asking for your support on 7 May. As your current County Councillor—and Leader of the Council—you may know me from my work locally or from the updates I regularly share through our parish magazines and on social media.

I feel privileged to represent our area, and I’m determined to protect it. I will continue to oppose speculative development driven by the Government’s increased housing targets, using every lever available—highways, flooding, education and environmental considerations—to challenge unsuitable proposals.

I remain committed to a simple principle: the Council’s money is your money. I have focused on strong financial management to keep Council Tax as low as possible. Despite misinformation, Hampshire is not bankrupt. We delivered £94 million in savings this year and will deliver a further £40 million of efficiencies.  Our debt remains low and falling—£153 million, just 4.6% of a £3.3 billion budget—and is used only for long-term investments such as SEND provision, care facilities and infrastructure.

Roads are a clear priority. This winter has caused significant damage, and I share residents’ frustration. We are directing every possible resource into repairs, including an additional £15 million this summer and introducing a new scheme to charge utility companies for disruptive roadworks, with funds reinvested directly into highways.

This election is about local leadership, not national politics. It is about who you trust to deliver services, manage your money responsibly, and stand up for our area.  I hope I can count on your support to continue doing so for Romsey Rural.

My Priorities:

Local Conservatives have been active in listening to your views.  If you elect me, my priorities will be:
•	Work to keep Council Tax down
•	While protecting frontline services for our most vulnerable residents.
•	Oppose speculative developments and press for the right homes in the right places.
•	Work hard to ensure our roads are maintained to a high standard.
•	Vigilance over utility company roadworks causing disruption and chaos.
•	Encourage environmentally friendly policies. 
•	Fight our area being split by Labour’s plan for new Councils.

My Commitment

If you elect me you should expect that I will:

•	Keep you informed
•	Be available to talk to you about your issues
•	Put Romsey Rural FIRST – put what is best for our area before party politics
•	Be available to help and find someone who can if I am unable to do so.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.

Gary is a dedicated public servant with deep roots in Lymington and West Wellow.

Local resident and business owner committed to supporting the community, improving local services, and standing up for residents.

I am delighted to have been selected to stand for my home division of Tadley and Baughurst. proud of.

A vote for me is a vote for a local candidate who cares, works hard and
gets things done.

Best regards
Mark Wilson-Thomas

An Andover resident since age three, Linda Sheﬃeld brings a unique blend of public and private sector expertise to her candidacy.
Her 19-year career in Education Personnel at Hampshire County Council, alongside 17 years running her own engraving business, gives her firsthand insight into local services and the challenges facing small businesses.

Linda is standing to preserve British values and rebuild community spirit. By choosing hope over despair and embracing collective strengths, she aims to create a prosperous future that will make the next generation proud to call Britain home.

My husband is a consultant working in the National Health Service. I am standing for Labour because I believe in fairness and equality. We need to protect our most vulnerable members of society including children from disadvantaged backgrounds and families on our housing waiting list. We must value our health and care workers more highly by protecting their working conditions and ensuring that they get adequate pay rises.

I’m standing for the Green Party because I believe in building local government and communities that care for people, for nature, and the environment for future generations.

I’ve lived in Waterlooville since 1999 and run two local businesses here: an IT consultancy and a holistic wellness practice. Fortunate to own/drive an EV, I power my home with solar and grow my own veg.

My priorities:

🚙 Road safety improvements
⚖️ Building fairer economics for the borough
💪 Creating healthier communities
🌱 Securing a more sustainable future for our area

I’m focused on making a difference for the community of which I’m part.

Being the proud daughter of a Royal Marine, I have had the privilege of living in many places - both home and abroad. 
Moving into Waterlooville in 2001, I now know I have found the ideal place for me and my family. Living in a county such as Hampshire is a delight, we have the Downs, the coast and everything in between.

I would like to thank everyone who has supported me since 2019 as your local representative; it has been a privilege to serve you. With your endorsement, I hope to continue to represent you as your County Councillor and Havant Borough Council representative.

You have told me what your priorities are, as your councillor and a resident myself I understand these; our streets to be kept clean and safe, council tax to be spent wisely and effectively and the regeneration of Waterlooville Town Centre to be completed as promised.

With your support, I will continue to challenge decisions which don’t represent the interests of local residents, put Waterlooville front and centre, support businesses and be the strong voice you want and need for our community.

As a lifelong resident of Waterlooville I know the area well having attended local schools and seen the things change over the years. I am a trustee of two local community buildings, including the Waterlooville Community Centre.

Having grown up sailing in Langstone Harbour I am passionate about the local environment and massively concerned about the impact of the proposed Southern Water recycling facility on our drinking water, energy use and the risks to the harbour. I also regularly help out with the local residents’ association environment group looking after our green spaces and removing litter.

I helped found a local Repair Cafe in 2019 to save things being unnecessarily thrown away and continue to help run it. We also run a Library of Things so people can borrow an item rather than have the expense of purchasing it and only using it once or twice.

There is a lot of talk about needing change, and I fully agree with that. We don’t need to look backwards and get left behind, stuck in the past, but forward looking positive change rather that improves things now and for our children’s future.

Having lived in Fair Oak for 20 years I am saddened at how our community is being affected by thoughtless over development. Infrastructure is ignored, so schools, dentists, GP surgeries and roads are overwhelmed.

🙋‍♂️ Introducing Myself — Steve Humby, Reform UK Candidate for West End South

Hi everyone! I'm Steve Humby, and I'm standing as your Reform UK candidate for West End South on Eastleigh Borough Council and Hampshire County Council at the May 7th local elections.

If elected, my priorities will be:

The son of a Royal Marine, Bruce was widely travelled in his formative years.  As a consequence, he studied at ten schools before settling down to study at Eastney Modern for Boys, Portsmouth.

Bruce started his career at Portsmouth Dockyard as an apprentice Laboratory Mechanic. Four years later after leaving school without a single O level he had gained sufficient qualifications to go on to study at honours level an Electrical & Electronic Engineering Sandwich degree course at Portsmouth Polytechnic and from there worked in large scale manufacturing around the country, where his highlight was working in an aerospace & automotive factory in Paris with 1,200 French colleagues. Bruce's role at this facility was technical lead for the UK sales office for which learning to speak French was essential.

Years later his manufacturing career effectively came to an end when British American Tobacco closed its manufacturing facility in Southampton due to a change in government legislation. However by then Bruce had gained a merit pass in a Master of Business Administration postgraduate degree at the University of Southampton.

With his manufacturing career firmly behind him, Bruce turned his attention to politics, where in 2006 he became a Councillor at his first attempt in Eastleigh. By 2011, Bruce had gained another postgraduate degree, this time a merit pass in a Master of Public Administration at the University of Portsmouth and serves on four local councils including Hampshire County Council.

His most recent highlight was being invited by the Chinese government to give lectures on British democracy at several universities in southern China. He strongly supports education and manufacturing, and plans to use his influence to encourage Chinese students to study at British universities. To this end Bruce has enrolled on a Mandarin course at Southampton University.

I am standing as a candidate for Reform UK for the different policies the party is promoting in the local elections. Nonetheless, let me tell you about five false MYTHS the extremists are saying about Reform UK.

MYTH 1: “Reform UK is racist and far-right!”

Not true! Reform UK is a democratic party that welcomes members and candidates from all backgrounds and communities. Seven Sisters ward is one of the most diverse areas in Haringey.
In fact, the two candidates the party is presenting for this election are from a Latino and a Jewish-Latino background, respectively! We believe in treating everyone equally, which means focusing on merit, fairness, and the issues that unite our community: safer streets, better and accountable local government. That’s why Raúl and Miguel Baruc, after living both in the UK for over 20 years, are now standing as candidates!

MYTH 2: “Reform UK will privatise the NHS!”

False! Reform UK does not propose privatising the NHS. The party supports a tax-funded, free-at-the-point-of-use health service. Reform UK’s proposals focus on cutting NHS bureaucracy, increasing frontline staffing, and reducing waiting times. At Council level, Reform UK will also push for better-funded social care to relieve pressure on local hospitals and GP surgeries.

MYTH 3: “Reform UK is a single-issue party that only cares about immigration!”

In reality, Reform UK has comprehensive local government policies covering council-tax reduction, planning reform, housing delivery, public safety, and cutting bureaucratic waste. At the local level, Reform UK councillors will focus on the bread-and-butter issues that affect your daily life: bins, roads, parks, housing, and keeping your streets safe. Immigration policy is set at Westminster. Your local Reform candidates are focused on making your Council work better for you.

MYTH 4: “Reform UK will cut public services!”

That’s not true! Reform UK’s approach is to cut waste, not services. Haringey Council is facing severe financial pressure due to rising temporary accommodation (TA) costs, which increased by 42% to £33 million, with projections suggesting a £41 million spend in 2025/26. Over 2,600 households are in TA as of late 2025, with costs rising due to reliance on expensive nightly lets, forcing a projected £11.7 million budget overspend. Reform UK will audit every council contract, eliminate wasteful consultancy spending, and redirect money to the front-line services you actually need.

MYTH 5: “Reform UK does not care about the Environment!”

Of course we do! Reform UK supports practical environmental measures, such as cleaner streets, more trees, protecting green spaces such as the Tottenham Area Parks, and proper recycling services.
What we oppose is wasteful virtue-signalling policies that cost millions but achieve nothing measurable. Reform UK Councils across the country continue environmental work under practical, affordable frameworks, not unachievable “net-zero by 2030” targets that drive up unnecessary costs.

ON 7th MAY, VOTE REFORM UK!

I am passionate about environmental issues, equity and fairness. I would like to see active transport such as walking, cycling and wheeling become safer and more desirable for the residents of Havering.

Kieron is born, raised and lives in Romford. After commuting to University in London he began working in the Events and Entertainment industries. In an ever more turbulent world he would like to help all residents to not just survive, but thrive.

Upminster has been my home for practically all of my life and it's a great feeling to stand in this election, hoping to represent my local area on Havering council.

I've been involved in politics since 2021 for the Conservative Party, delivering countless leaflets across Havering and holding many conversations with residents. You may have heard about the poor state of council finances but the focus should be on what we can do. We live in a lovely area and that's our standard to maintain for years to come.

Having grown up in the community, Owen understands the issues local residents face and is committed to being a strong local voice.
He is standing as a Green Party candidate because he believes local politics should focus on supporting residents and protecting the places that matter most to the community.
