I’ve been proud to call Cheshunt home for over nine years. In that time, I’ve witnessed how much our community has changed, sometimes for the better, but all too often, vital services have been stretched thin while local voices have gone unheard. I’ve always had a deep interest in politics, but it was the last general election that inspired me to take a more active role in local political life. I believe that change begins at the community level, and that we each have a responsibility to speak up and get involved in shaping a better future for everyone.

One of my core priorities is working with local organisations to end violence against women and girls. Broxbourne must be a place where women feel safe, supported, and heard. That means creating a dedicated safe haven for domestic abuse victims, strengthening the laws that protect them, and properly funding the support services they rely on. But just as crucially, we must invest in education — in our schools, homes, and wider community — to break the cycle of abuse before it begins. Every woman deserves safety, justice, and respect. By coming together as a community, we can build a Broxbourne where those values are more than just words — they’re a lived reality.

I have lived in Broxbourne for over 40 years and I am shocked by the way our local environment has been allowed to deteriorate. Local services  (Schools, Doctors Surgeries, Recreation) are under pressure whilst remaining Green Belt is being concreted over by poorly planned developments. The local elections in May is an opportunity to shake up the local Council and to send a message that enough is enough. Even if you do not usually vote Lib Dem, please consider lending us your vote to send a message that the voters of Goffs Oak will not be taken for granted.

John Graham’s top priorities:

-Tough on HMOs - the only ones permitted should be legal, safe and not diminish the local community and neighbourhood balance

-Saving our Greenbelt - John will campaign against any unsuitable development which compromises our green spaces and clogs up local infrastructure

-Championing our local businesses - Labour are letting down our pubs and shops with a multitude of tax hikes. John supports the abolition of business rates, cutting red tape and scrapping the Carbon Tax to bring energy costs down

-Cleaning up our area - since second black bins were taken away, there has been an increase in fly-tipping. John supports the local Conservatives plan to crackdown on flytippers by increasing the penalties and enforcement.

Knowledge. Experience. Delivery.

I will stand up as a resident against HMO’s and Data Centres. Promoting High Street improvements for the people of Potters Bar and pushing for more transparency in decisions at Hertsmere Borough Council.

Potters Bar has been my home for decades, and I care deeply about our community. I’ve always believed in helping out where I can, whether that’s supporting local families or bringing people together through community events. Now I want to do even more by standing up for residents as a local councillor.

I know how important it is that people feel heard and supported, especially families navigating SEND provision. I will be a strong voice for Bentley Heath & The Royds and work hard every day to get results for our area.

A little bit about me: I live in Hillingdon, West London, and have proudly served as an NHS GP in a practice in the neighbouring constituency of Hayes and Harlington for more than 20 years. My commitment to public service extends beyond healthcare, as I also serve as a School Governor for a local school in Hayes and as a Charity Trustee for a local organisation, that supports older people and those in need across Hillingdon.

Born in Barnet, North London, I attended a primary school in Colindale before my family returned to India. It was there that I spent my childhood and youth and pursued my dreams of becoming a doctor. I have been a resident of Hillingdon since 2016,  living with my husband, in-laws, and my children.

So why am I asking for your support? 

Throughout my entire career, I have been deeply involved in public service. As a GP, I have not only listened to my patients but also acted as their advocate. I have worked in various hospitals around the country including West Middlesex hospital where I worked as a junior doctor in the maternity unit. I have been instrumental in policy formulation and service redesign as a Clinical Leader in North West London, and worked closely with GP colleagues in Hounslow. Additionally, my role as a Board Member of a large Mental Health and Community NHS Trust, as well as my position as a Lead for Nursing Homes in my practice area, have provided me with diverse perspectives on healthcare and social care issues.

My experience as a School Governor has given me valuable insight into our education system and the challenges it faces. These experiences, together with my ability to empathise, listen, and understand people's needs, have led me to believe that politics is the arena where I can make a tangible difference, which is why I started my journey over a year ago. I am eager to utilise my personal and professional skills, accumulated knowledge, and understanding of people's concerns to serve you and the wider society.

I invite you to join me on this journey. Let us work together to create positive change and make our voices heard. Stay tuned for campaign updates, events, and opportunities to connect. Your support and engagement are crucial and deeply appreciated.

Thank you for taking the time to learn more about me and my campaign. I am eager to meet you, listen to your ideas, and pursue the matters that are important to you. Together, let's shape a brighter future.

My name is James Bourke, I am one of the three Conservative candidates standing for election as a borough councillor in South Lake Ward, Woodley.

I've been a student at the University of Reading for a few years now, and for much longer than this I have have known the area through my uncle living here and frequently visiting. In all this time I've become very familiar with Woodley, with all it's great amenities and pleasant neighbourhoods.

Sadly in the last two years this idyllic town has become blighted by poor decisions from Wokingham Borough Council. The roads have become yet poorer in quality, parking charges have risen (they plan to charge you to park on the roadside), council services have been slashed or eliminated, anti-social behaviour has become worse around the Woodley Precinct, and now they want to reduce your weekly bin collections to a bi-weekly schedule.

As a borough councillor, my goal and that of my colleagues will be to reverse or stop the above issues as a matter of urgency and restore respect in the council for the people of Woodley and South Lake. A vote for us, for me, is a vote to get our town back on track.

I grew up here, and genuinely care about our Community.   As your Councillor I will work tirelessly to promote local issues & stand up for what matters to us.  I will fight for safer & cleaner streets, to challenge further inappropriate HMOs, & to prioritise local housing for local people. It’s time for change.

Ed is committed to transparent decision‑making, supporting local services, and ensuring development works for residents rather than being imposed on them. Housing

We will prioritise genuinely affordable homes for local people while protecting the character of our towns and villages. Ed chaired the Slinfold Neighbourhood Plan and successfully challenged developers to reduce proposed housing numbers down from initially over 700 to a final allocation of 77 homes in Slinfold Parish.

Improving River Quality
Our rivers and streams should be safe, clean and thriving for wildlife and residents alike. The Liberal Democrats are campaigning to end sewage dumping and hold water companies accountable for pollution. As a keen canoeist , Ed will push for stronger monitoring, tougher penalties, and real investment so our local waterways can recover.

Protecting Green Spaces
Green spaces are part of what makes Horsham such a wonderful place to live. The Liberal Democrats will fight to protect parks, countryside and wildlife habitats from inappropriate development. These are our Reform UK Hounslow Policies:

Community Safety & Crime

Crime rates remain unacceptably high, and the council’s soft approach to law enforcement has failed to make a significant impact. Residents deserve to feel safe in their own neighbourhoods.We must tackle the increase in crime in Hounslow. Crime in the Borough has increased by 20% in the last 5 years alone.

Solutions:

- Enhanced Policing: Increase police presence in high-crime areas and adopt a zero-tolerance policy towards criminal behaviour. We must both invest in community policing initiatives to build trust and cooperation, whilst also cracking down on violent criminals with consistance & conviction. - Social Programmes: Whilst addressing the root causes of crime is important, immediate action is needed. Such as, Implementing targeted programmes to reduce youth unemployment, detatchment, depression, substance abuse & crime, but, we must not shy away from tough enforcement measures, especially when it comes to weapons & violent crime. - Tougher Sentencing: Advocate for mandatory minimum sentences for violent crimes and repeat offenders. This ensures that serious offenders are kept off the streets and sends a strong message of deterrence. - Stop and Search: Increase use of stop and search powers to tackle knife crime and other violent offences. Ensuring rigorous guidelines and accountability can balance effectiveness with community relations. - Front-Line Policing: Increase the number of front-line officers and enhance their visibility in local communities, such as a local liaison officers. This provides a deterrent against crime and ensures swift responses to incidents.

Prioritse Housing for Citizens and Working People:

The current system sometimes results in social housing going to those who do not contribute significantly to the community. Additionally, there are often long waiting lists for eligible citizens and working people.The primary goal of this policy is to prioritise the allocation of social housing to citizens and working people within the Borough of Hounslow. This approach not only supports those who contribute significantly to the community but also fosters stability and growth, something has forgotten.

Solutions:

- Strict Eligibility Criteria: Prioritise social housing for local citizens, long-term residents, and those in employment. Social housing should be reserved for those who have demonstrated a commitment to the local economy and community. - Allocation Transparency: Increase transparency in the allocation process by publishing regular reports on who receives housing and why. This helps build trust and ensures accountability to you, the electorate. - Supporting the youth: Integrate financial literacy education into the school curriculum, teaching students about budgeting, saving, managing debt, credit scores, and mortgages. To give them a fighting chance of achieving home ownership. - Prioritising working individuals: Promote economic stability by prioritising employed residents in social housing allocations, as they contribute significantly to the economy, paying taxes, and supporting local businesses. - Individuals with disabilities: Ensure that individuals with disabilities receive special consideration and priority in social housing allocation, meeting their specific needs promptly, effectively, and ethically.

Domestic Abuse

We must also talk about and highlight the dramatic 100-150% increase in domestic violence across Hounslow over 5 years which has continued to increase rapidly after the Covid pandemic.

Solutions:

- Zero Tolerance Policy: Implement a zero-tolerance policy towards domestic abuse. Ensure that perpetrators are held accountable through swift and decisive legal action. We also need increased police presence and resources dedicated to tackling domestic abuse. - Training: Provide specialised training for law enforcement officers to recognise and respond effectively to domestic abuse cases. This includes understanding the dynamics of abuse and the best practices for supporting victims. Cutting red tape: Simplify and expedite the legal processes for obtaining restraining orders and other protective measures. Ensure that victims can access legal protection quickly and efficiently. - Establish a neighbourhood watch: Establish neighbourhood watch programs to create a network of vigilant community members who can identify and report domestic abuse, fostering collective responsibility and support. - Expand and improve access to support: Advocate services for victims, including shelters, counselling, and legal assistance, ensuring victims have the resources needed to escape abusive situations and rebuild their lives.

Fly Tipping Prevention

Fly tipping has reached incredible levels with incidents being in the top 5 accross London. Since 2016, incidents of fly tipping have increased by over 100% across the Bourough of Hounslow, these are absolutely ridiculous statistics over such a short period. Fly-tipping is a blight on our community, costing taxpayers over £1.3 million annually and resulting in 24,210 incidents on public highways alone. This included 63,343 bags of rubbish dumped on the streets, costing taxpayers over £1.3 million for removal. This is unacceptable, and it's time for a robust, no-nonsense approach to eradicate it.

Solutions:

- Investment & Training: We will advocate for investing in state-of-the-art surveillance technology to monitor known fly-tipping hotspots. I am 27 years old and running for councillor of Carisbrooke & Gunville as the reform candidate.

I grew up on the Isle of Wight, having lived in the ward for 14 years, and I attended Hunnyhill Primary School, Node Hill Middle School, and Carisbrooke College.

I also helped out at a community club, teaching safe use of airsoft equipment to beginners/kids for 4 years.

Working at a local holiday park, I am known for my approachability and unwavering commitment to service.

I am passionate about improving local amenities, supporting island businesses, and ensuring every resident has a voice. I am excited to bring positive change to Carisbrooke & Gunville.

Since I came second in the last county elections in 2021, I have continued to support residents in Arreton, Rookley, Godshill and Merstone and as a parish councillor for Chillerton.

I am ready to serve you on the Isle of Wight Council alongside a strong team of Greens at County Hall.

Despite growing up in a Conservative household, I always felt myself to be a guardian of the voiceless with strong environmental values.

As a life coach and therapist, I work with a wide variety of people. Working together for the greater good is my motivation for standing for local council, regardless of political beliefs.

I’ve lived and worked here, and I’m passionate about preserving our rural villages while addressing the key issues affecting our community.

With my background in public sector finance and charity work, I have the experience to get things done and ensure our voices are heard.

My name is Claire Critchison (nee Whittington) and I am your Green Party Candidate for Chale, Niton & Shorwell (and Whitwell) in the 6th May council elections.

I'm a 6th generation descendant of this ward, having lived in Chale and Niton all my life and have brought my family up in the two villages.
I am passionate about the South Wight of the Island and support local clubs, projects, charities and community groups including being a Girlguiding Leader of the 1st Niton Rainbows and Brownies and Chair of the fundraising committee for Niton Primary School (FONS).

From being a community champion and speaking up for local issues I enjoy being part of our Island life and if elected I would represent residents to get the best outcomes for all. I work well with others regardless of their political alliances and would not be influenced when making decisions or voting on Island issues.

My career in Event Management for over 15 years with the Isle of Wight Council, working for Island companies and more recently running my own business ensures I have the experience, skills and ability to challenge others and ensure vital services and facilities which are a priority for the ward areas.

I've been selected by the Isle of Wight Green Party as the best person to represent the party for Chale, Niton & Shorwell. I'm very proud that they have put their faith in me and I hope this gives you confidence that I'd be great choice to represent our community at County Hall. I would be a strong voice on tourism, education, infrastructure, planning and prosperity of our Island.

This election will be a two horse race between myself and the Conservative candidate. Votes for Labour, Lib Dems or any other party won't decide the result. A vote for me is a vote for a strong, independent voice free to speak up for Chale, Niton & Shorwell. A vote for anyone else means a return to the same old Conservative complacency and our community not being heard.

I'm honoured to be standing to represent Chale, Niton & Shorwell in the Isle of WIght Council elections on Thursday 6th May and hope you'll put your trust in me.

Please make sure you're registered to vote by midnight on Monday 19 April. If you won't be attending your polling station in person, then you can apply for a postal vote by 5pm on Tuesday 20 April.

Best wishes,
Claire Critchison
(nee Whittington)

P.s. Don't forget, it's only me or the Conservative candidate who can win. Any other vote won't decide this election.

Dan is a teacher who moved down to the island to start a family. He is a young Dad with young children, and is deeply concerned about the state of the world. He says “I want to do everything I can to make it better for my children; their growing up and their future.”

Born and raised in Gurnard,  I was first elected as an Independent IW Councillor in 1995, and have represented Cowes West and Gurnard since 2009.

As Councillor, I’ve held key positions and given residents support in planning, the  environment, coastal protection, flooding, transport, waste, children’s services and public protection.

Outside the IW Council, I actively serve on three parish/ Town Councils, am Trustee of the Footprint Trust and magistrate. I chair the Isle of Wight Local Access Forum and since 2025 served as Chair of regional fisheries organisation Southern IFCA.

As Ward Councillor, I’m committed to being hardworking, transparent and putting Cowes and Gurnard first.

I was born on this lovely Island and have lived and worked here all my life. I have strong connections to Cowes and Gurnard. Myself, my husband and two sons, all born and bred here, strongly believe in the policies and strong common sense principles of the Reform party. Our Island and country is being overtaken and we must return to putting our British values and communities first, encouraging business growth and making work pay.

Sophus was born on the Isle of Wight and is a student at the Isle of Wight college. He serves as a Parish Councillor in Wootton Bridge. Sophus’s main priorities are fighting sewage dumping in the Medina river, plus improving public services across the island, particularly health and justice. “I would be honoured to serve the people of Fairlee and Whippingham Ward as their County Councillor”.

Originally from Teesside, I have lived and worked in London all my adult life, and in central Surbiton for more than twenty years. In a career working as a professional IT Project Manager for inner London councils I specialised in Parking, Finance and Housing, followed by a period working with Unison the Public Service union. I believe strongly that in order to make the most of the power of Local Government we must ensure it is well run, professional and honest in its dealings. It must focus on local issues and put residents at the heart of all decision making.

My name is Florence Sarlat and I am delighted to be standing as your Green Party candidate for Isle of Wight Council, representing Yarmouth and Freshwater North.

I came on the island by choice. I was drawn here by the beauty of the coastline, the friendliness of the community and the sense that this is a place still worth fighting for.

Prior to that, I worked for 20 years as a managing director for a bank, leading major transformation projects in Paris and London. In 2012, tired of managing only cost-cutting projects, I decided to train as a yoga and mindfulness teacher and worked with young people who have experienced trauma, injustice, and adverse childhood.

As a Green councillor, I would work across the issues that matter most to people here - not just environment but housing, transport, health, fairness, and the kind of community where people look out for one another.

Here are the things I am most determined to tackle:
- Cleaning up our water: I want to push for nature-based solutions that work with our landscape, not against it, protecting public health and supporting local tourism.
- Protecting our land and our character: Before any new building, we should be asking: can we restore and repurpose what already exists? Affordable, sustainable homes and community spaces can be created without sacrificing more of the landscape we love.
- Backing our local economy: Our farmers, artisans and independent businesses are the backbone of this community. I want to see the council do far more to support short local supply chains, keeping money on the island, and reducing food miles.

The things which make the Isle of Wight worth living on are fragile, and worth protecting fiercely. I am standing because I want to help keep this place extraordinary.

To do that I need your vote on Thursday May 7th.

Best wishes,

Florence

I have enjoyed being an active member of our local community for 31 years. With a history of “hands on” engagement in protecting our environment and promoting our beautiful area, I was asked by residents to stand for the Isle of Wight Council ward of Freshwater South.

Many will be aware of my role tackling our serious sewage problems head on with Southern Water, resulting in cleaner seas and rivers for us all, and also for supporting many local projects and community groups. I was instrumental in achieving the Conservation Area status for Freshwater Bay.

My priorities include protecting our valuable green spaces and wildlife, ensuring our rivers, estuaries and bathing beaches are cleaner, and that affordable development is in appropriate places with homes that locals can actually afford. I will continue to support our valuable library and West Wight Sports and Community Centre and to ensure our parks are safe, fun areas for our children to play in. I will focus on improving our NHS healthcare, enhancing local policing and tackling transport and infrastructure issues.

Above all, as an Independent Community Champion, I will be the substantial voice for residents to amplify and resolve their local concerns.

I have lived in the Borough for 30 years and currently live in Surbiton Town Centre. I am semi-retired after a career that included spending 20 years working in Local Government for Westminster Council, providing welfare advice and support to vulnerable tenants. Until recently, I was a full time official for the public sector trade union, Unison, advising members working in London boroughs including Kingston. I currently serve on Kingston Council’s Standing Advisory Committee on Religious Education in Schools. I am passionate about tackling inequality through providing decent homes, safe streets and employment opportunities for all our residents.

I am a retired teacher who specialised in working with children with special educational needs.  I am a resident of Freshwater and I am the prospective parliamentary candidate for Reform UK, Isle of Wight West.

I believe that successive governments have placed too much emphasis on education to degree level.  Encouraging and training young people to become the skilled men and women of the future will not only equip them to build a career for life but also help the country find the builders and engineers needed to solve the housing shortage we now face, as well as developing and growing our manufacturing capability as new technologies emerge.

I advocate a ban on any foreign fishing vessels entering British waters so that the pressure on fish stocks is reduced.  Rigorous scientific studies of stock levels and maturity should determine the size of the annual commercial harvest to ensure a healthy, growing population of fish for the future.  I am passionate about beach and small boat angling and a volunteer at the National Coastwatch Institution, Needles.

This country emits a tiny proportion of global CO₂ produced each year and we as a nation should not face the huge financial cost of trying to solve a problem we can have little influence over.  Net zero must stop as we will remain reliant on fossil fuels until real solutions for domestic, commercial, and transport energy needs can be developed.The number of people entering this country as economic migrants is out of control but the small boat crossings from France can be stopped immediately and legally. 

Those already here should be assessed quickly and efficiently regarding their right to enter, and either returned to their home country or allowed to stay, if appropriate, as the burden on housing, health services, education, and the benefits system is overwhelming this country.  A points system should be introduced to allow and welcome qualified individuals, who will benefit the UK, to enter the country and apply for leave to remain.

I think government should plan for the long term, not for re-election.  Fully separating ourselves, and Northern Ireland, from the EU and leaving the ECHR will give us that opportunity.

The Reform Party will promise and deliver for this country.

As an Isle of Wight born and bred citizen, concern for all aspects of the Island is an instinctive priority for Peter. As a resident of Haylands, he can use his knowledge of planning and finance to ensure that this ward is well served and supported.

Peter sits on two national NGO forums, one directly with the Government Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and the other with the Office for Nuclear Regulation. Peter is a professional musician and a volunteer at the Isle of Wight Steam Railway.

Harry Eccles is a local Nurse, Trade Unionist and campaigner.

Harry is an addiction Nurse Specialist (in addiction) completing his masters in Advanced Nursing Practice.

He holds a national nursing leadership role giving him experience of overseeing complex multi-year projects and UK-wide teams with large budgets.

He is passionate about investing in local services, prioritising infrastructure and public need over profits, and protecting the local environment.

Harry has pledged to ensure all candidates have his contact details to discuss with him the issues that affect them most, so he can support them to create the type of change they want to see in Lake South.

I live with my family in the heart of Havenstreet village and already serve the community as Chair or our Parish Council. Most significantly I’ve spearheaded a campaign to get Havenstreet back on the bus network and represented resident’s interests in dealing with the all-too frequent disruption caused by roadworks in the village and surrounding area. This ward, one of the island’s largest, is a mix of larger villages and small hamlets. There are many thriving communities and businesses which deserve a representative at County Hall who will put their interests first at every opportunity.
My career in the British Army has given me wide experience of leading teams, managing change and budgets whilst being accountable for delivering the required outcomes. Just the skills needed on our council.
I volunteer as a Director/Trustee of the Isle of Wight Steam Railway, one of the Island’s top heritage and tourist attractions and a significant local employer. I fully understand the challenges currently faced by all Island businesses and the tourist sector in particular, a thriving tourist economy is absolutely vital for our Island. I strongly believe that our council must do everything it can to support all local businesses.
I am standing to be your Isle of Wight councillor because I believe that it’s time for change in County Hall. The traditional parties and the ‘Independents’ have had their chance. Reform UK is ready to step in and deal with the issues facing us, starting with the council’s finances which are in a dire state – fresh thinking and a push to further drive down costs, whilst delivering the services our residents need and deserve, is urgently required.
I’m ready to play my part in delivering the common-sense solutions that the Island needs. I’m right behind Reform UK’s core values – Family, Community, Country, and am prepared to work hard to serve all members of our Island community with honesty and integrity.

Whoever is leading the Government on June 9th, the Isle of Wight will not be their top priority, however as the Island’s MP it will be my single point of focus. Many people feel it is time we had someone representing them that will be solely focused on representing the Island because successive Governments have failed to understand the unique challenges we face. We know we have the ability to progress with a hand up, not just handouts. I believe we should be looking for an Island deal, an opportunity for real localism, to enable effective local governance and a chance to steer ourselves to a place of wellbeing and prosperity.

WELLBEING & PROSPERITY, Three Principles:

1. Economic -Building a strong, resilient and competitive economy
2. Social - supporting strong, vibrant and healthy communities
3. Environment – Protecting and enhancing our natural, built and historic environment

Economy:
• Small business micro funding and improved support.
• Cut VAT for Tourism.
• Circular Economy and the Island pound.
Transport:
• Back the feasibility study to determine facts regarding any fixed link.
• Work on solutions for rural bus travel.
• Create infrastructure for pedestrians and cyclists for able-bodied and disabled users.
• Road safety -20mph in residential streets and town and village centres.
Education:
• Make wellbeing as important as learning.
• Rebalance academic and vocational studies.
• Adjust the school terms for improved family life and educational attainment.
• Early Special Educational Needs diagnosis with ongoing support.

Health:
• Support the team at St Mary’s Hospital for improving and retaining services.
• Increase mental health provision for early intervention, especially for anxiety.
• Adult Social Care, lobby to end the post code lottery of care.
• More care for carers, so they can continue to support their loved ones.
• Raise aspirations for young people to choose a career in health

Housing:
• Build affordable rental properties in sustainable brown-field sites.
• Support housing that can be built quickly using pre-fabricated methods.
• Counter the negative effects that land banking can have on a community.

Environment
• Campaign for a smart grid for solar energy
• Wind turbines in industrial parks, the Island a beacon for green energy
• Protect our AONB status

More at: https://www.juliejonesevans.org/commitments

“I have spent the last few years disillusioned with politics and wishing Someone would stand and represents my views on the escalating local issues. Having spent a while hoping there was a local Lib Dem candidate I could support the next obvious step was to become that person!

“Now is a time of great political shift and change, and I would like to be part of the process that brings greater community improvements and social unity to our area."

I'm standing as your Labour candidate in Pan & Barton. I'm a local resident, and passionate about driving the positive change agenda of our new Labour government in our local area.
After 14 years of austerity, there is a big mess to fix and we are determined to deliver.
Alongside our three key policies on health and social care, housing, and transport, Island Labour will create more SEND places in mainstream schools using the Island's high-needs capital funding, and ensure primary schools receive a fair share of resources so every child gets the support they need close to home.
We will also tackle barriers to opportunity by investing in youth facilities, backing the island's Local Skills Improvement Plan, and helping young people who are not in education, employment or training into secure, well-paid work.
We will protect our unique environment by backing local renewable energy projects, helping Islanders access grants to cut energy bills, and pushing Southern Water and
regulators to clean up our rivers and coasts while holding the council to its climate commitments.

It has been a privilege to be the Isle of Wight councillor for Parkhurst & Hunnyhill Ward. It’s not just the area I represent—it’s where I’ve lived since 2007 and made my home.

Over the years, I hope I’ve shown that I am a councillor who listens to residents, takes up issues on their behalf, and sees things through.

I’m standing for re-election because there are many things I want to keep working on.
 
For our area, these are just a few:
•	seeing the upgrades to the prison estate roads through to completion
•	improving safety on our main roads and junctions
•	providing more equipment for the Hookes Way play area for young children
•	enhancing our local environment with improvements such as the planter soon to be installed on Hunnyhill near the existing bee hotel

For the whole Island, I am absolutely committed to ensuring the council prioritises poverty reduction, cost of living support, and truly affordable housing for Islanders to rent and buy.

Vote Jen Hughes for Ryde South East!

Local people FOR Local People

I am a passionate, tenacious and driven candidate who will stand up and be the voice for the people of Ryde South East

I am a current Ryde Town Councillor for Ryde South East, having been elected in first place in May 2025. I have worked hard to represent our Ward and have not shied away from scrutinising and pushing for clarity.

I worked tirelessly behind the scenes and helped save Oakfield Primary School from closure. I have also successfully challenged spending at Ryde Town Council, as a member of the finance committee and am not afraid to point out possible issues and money saving strategies.

I believe we need to vote for the best local candidate, and leave main party politics for the General Election in 2029. 
We need someone who has demonstrated genuine care and concern for Ryde South East, not a paper candidate or someone living elsewhere on the island, who may struggle to connect with people in our Ward due to living outside of it and not understanding the wishes of the people who live here.

I have aligned with the island Liberal Democrats, as I believe them to be the most genuine, compassionate and caring Councillors currently serving on the Isle of Wight. We need change and I honestly think these Councillors to be integral to this change, with their people centred approach, as, instead of doing TO people, these Councillors believe things should be done FOR people. I wholeheartedly agree!

I believe myself to be the best candidate and I hope you will agree by voting Jen Hughes on 7th May 2026.
Any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me, either by the link at the top to my Facebook page, or at:

jen.hughes@rydetowncouncil.gov.uk

Thank you for reading.

My name is Sarah Morris. I am an Independent candidate for Shanklin Central, I am a Restore Britain member, and have passed their vetting, but they aren’t standing candidates outside of Great Yarmouth this time.

I believe we need something new and that other Islanders want change too. I am extremely frustrated and disappointed with what we currently have on offer,  so I have to try and make a difference.

We, as taxpayers, deserve a system that puts us first. A government free from corruption and cronyism. We need to stop our money from being wasted and given out in questionable contracts.  Most of those who currently run the country, and indeed those in opposition, have no idea what we are facing now and in the coming years.  Price hikes on food, energy, and mortgage rates, alongside possible food shortages and power cuts.  We need ordinary people with common sense speaking up for us.

A lot of families are on or very close to the breadline, and it absolutely wouldn’t be this way if the country was actually being run for us.  We need innovative ideas to deal with the many costs of lockdown, be it financial, the toll taken on our health system, or the impact on our children’s education.  Restore Britain have policy papers that cover many of the issues that need to be fixed, with more being added all the time.

The political class have been playing games with our lives.  Their bad decisions never affect them.  I am proud to be British, but we’ve lost focus and control.  We need to Restore the systems and get back to ones that work for us…Rebuild a country that we can be proud of, one we can be proud to pass down to future generations.

Locally we need people who are approachable, vocal, capable and willing to listen, work for and help all constituents.

I am always around, and am always keen to chat to anyone who wants to!

I am the only candidate who actually lives in the Shanklin Central ward, and I promise to do the very best job I possibly can if elected.

Why I’m standing for Shanklin South

Shanklin has been an important part of my life since childhood. I lived
in Ashcombe Court on Victoria Avenue and attended Shanklin Primary
School when I was very young. Much of my childhood was spent here,
and I have fond memories of travelling on the number 2 bus to secondary
school in Newport each day. My mum has lived in our beautiful town
for more than two decades and today, like you, I am also proud to be a
Shanklin resident.

I am standing because, I believe Shanklin South deserves a councillor who is visible, approachable and answerable to local residents. I believe these three things can only genuinely be achieved when your local representative is accountable directly to you and not to a national political party whose priorities may lie outside Shanklin.

If you choose to elect me as your councillor, my commitment to you is that I will stand up for you and only ever work in the interests of Shanklin South, without party politics getting in the way of that.

Ultimately, this election is about who will work in your best interests. But it is also an opportunity to send a clear message to Westminster that you are tired of this Island being overlooked. You can do that by electing someone committed to local priorities, who will be locally accountable to you, who uses and supports the same infrastructure and businesses as you and, most importantly, who is independent of party allegiance.

If elected, you are my boss

I'm a data scientist and consultant. I have lived in Shanklin for 10 years, and so understand the needs of the local community. My politics are firmly rooted in the centre ground. I grew up in Nottingham and have previously worked at the University of Southampton as a Senior Research Fellow, on a supermarket shop floor in various roles, in a call centre, and for a geotechnical engineering company. I've been a Labour Party member since 2010.

If elected, I shall:

•	Prioritise finding long term solutions to flooding in the town centre, and the closure of Leeson Road and other local roads
•	Back the Bay Area Place Plan so Shanklin, Lake and Sandown share decisions and investment fairly, boosting jobs and protecting the coast
•	Work with the national government to sort Island‑wide council funding and pressure on services, especially adult social care and children’s services
•	Push for better Island‑wide transport and connections; including ferries, road improvements, parking, and bus services
•	Support more local powers for the Island, fair funding, and building genuinely affordable homes
•	Keep a close eye on housing standards and press for firm action against poor landlords
•	Make sure Labour’s major increase in GP, dental and SEND services on the Island keeps moving forward

Every community on the Isle of Wight faces major challenges following years of decline under Conservative and (ex-Tory) Reform and Independent politicians. With the new Labour government’s positive change agenda, it is clearly essential that Councillors should work hard on behalf of residents to help improve their lives. If elected as your representative, it will be my top priority to be both available and accountable with a view to building a more compassionate and prosperous future for local people. I'm certain that, with your support, we can make a genuine difference in Shanklin South.

I’m a local resident standing for the Green Party in Totland and Colwell, committed to making the West Wight a better place to live, work, and raise a family. With a professional background in healthcare, technology, and public service, I bring a practical, solutions-focused approach to local issues. I believe in improving everyday life through better infrastructure, protecting our environment, and supporting strong, resilient communities. I’m particularly focused on ensuring public money is used effectively, delivering real value for residents. My aim is simple: to represent our community honestly, make sensible decisions, and help build a healthier, fairer future for everyone.

I am standing as an Independent, believing that local decisions should be made by and for those that live here and not according to the policy of a national political party.

I have served the residents of Totland & Colwell for the past 5 years and treated my position of Councillor as a full time role. I continue to hold Ward surgeries each Thursday at Totland Parish Office and variously at Our Place and similar venues, where residents can attend to seek my assistance or simply to make me aware of local issues needing attention. I cannot pretend to solve every issue but I always commit to do my best.

As a Totland Parish Councillor and Freshwater Parish Councillor I am uniquely placed to understand and take action throughout the whole West Wight - including key issues on protecting local greenfield sites such as Birch Close, Heathfield, Brambles, Camp Road and more, maintaining our local dental provision and securing them as NHS only, supporting viability of local businesses including Hursts and the Village Bakery, driving Southern Water to stop sewage discharges into our streams, SSSI sites and coastline, plus smaller matters regarding footpaths, retaining free on-street parking and public toilets and key services upon which we all depend.

My monthly reports to both local Parish Councils detail the donations I make of my Councillor Allowance to support our community - defibrillator training, prostate testing, laptop for Men-in-Sheds, youth services, establishment of wildflower meadows, wildlife support, Our Place and an extended list of local charities and support groups including Barnardo's and children’s support groups.

At Isle of Wight Council I have Chaired the IW Pension Fund since 2021 steering improvement from only 92% funded against liabilities to now some 160%, enabling a reduction in contributions by IWC this year of circa £2million that served to protect critical statutory services including Adult Social Care given our aged population.

Working with Empowering Islanders Group colleagues and gaining support from across the political divides at County Hall, we were able to stop the sell-off of Isle of Wight Council land and redirect analysis to use it for social rent homes, to improve efficiencies, to identify issues in financial calculations and to challenge errors in school place planning proposals. Our unique independent basis includes sitting in the middle of the main chamber rather than with administration or opposition - defining our non-party position working for the benefit of our Island rather than ‘political-point-scoring’.

I invite residents to review my track record of local and Islandwide achievements that demonstrate my focus, tenacity and resolve to improve our lives and improve future opportunities for all, and to select me again to continue as their champion at County Hall.

Thank you for placing your trust in me.

As an Independent, I faced being shut out of decision-making or pressured to support policies I don’t believe in,

By joining the Conservatives under Cllr Ed Blake’s leadership, I can properly fight for our community’s needs where it counts – in the council chamber.

Frequent closures and poor maintenance disrupt daily life – we need proper investment. The ongoing situation with The Graben and Clarence Road is a farce.

Our beautiful villages deserve better support to attract visitors year-round.

Anti-social behaviour and drug-related crime need firm action. We must ensure quality affordable homes while protecting our rural character.

We mustn’t trade away local control for empty promises. Residents deserve a Councillor who’ll stand firm on what matters. Only Island residents should have a say in their day-to-day living and the future.  No other mainland authority can know what day-to-day challenges we face here.

Living in London for many years and originally from Argentina, Jo Dowbor is of mixed Polish, English and Latin heritage, and a community organiser with nine years of frontline activism and a proven record of supporting those around her.

Jo has worked closely with disabled people, migrants, refugees and people experiencing homelessness, supporting some of the most marginalised members of our community in Islington. She understands firsthand how difficult it can be to access services, to be heard, and to secure basic dignity — and that lived experience drives her politics.

As a trained union organiser, a volunteer with Care4Calais and Cosmos and an active member of multiple local groups such as Defend the Whittington Hospital Coalition and Islington Homes for All, Jo has built campaigns, done field work and mobilised communities to win real change.

In 2024, Jo stood as a Green Party candidate in the Hornsey by-election, where she came second and tripled the Green vote share. She has also supported Green candidates across the country, helping to grow their presence and win elections.

Her activism has included organising major demonstrations on international justice and leading mobilisations against the far right, including the protest outside the Thistle Barbican Hotel in 2025. She co-founded Greens for Palestine in January 2024 and helped draft and strategise the motion that recognised genocide in Gaza and committed the Green Party to BDS. This helped position the Greens as a clear pro-Palestine voice in UK politics and inspired many new members to join.

If elected, Jo would be among the first-generation Latinx councillors in the country, bringing vital representation and lived experience into local government.

Jo is committed to working collaboratively with fellow Green and Independent councillors to resist austerity, defeat the far right, and serve — not rule — the people of Islington. She is a strong supporter of Jeremy Corbyn, who remains one of her biggest political inspirations.

Lucas is an energy journalist specialising in energy markets and the transition to a cleaner, more sustainable energy system.
He has experience working on campaigns related to climate action, energy affordability and social justice.

statement_to_voters:
I'm Alan, and I'm standing to represent you in Bunhill Ward. I've been living here in Islington for three years as a student, soon finishing my Masters in Aerospace Engineering at City University. I started campaigning 2 years ago after an illegal eviction, which made me realise how unfair our system is for young people. We suffer from a lack of good jobs, high rent and cost of living, and no access to social housing.

I've spoken to residents everywhere in Islington, north and south: Labour has let down us down, and we need a council that will make every effort to win back our trust. **If elected I will scrutinise the council's work on finances, planning and transport, holding Labour to account on their cuts to council housing, social care and local services.**

A bit about me: I've worked as an engineer in a factory in Leicester, as a spacecraft design researcher in Cardiff, and I'm a reservist in the Armed Forces. My favourite biscuit is a walkers' shortbread, and my favourite pub is the Masque Haunt. On the weekends I enjoy spending time with my partner in St Luke's Gardens or Fortune Street Park, though escaping the city to Epping Forest to feed the geese is also high on my list!

PS: best wishes to Phil Graham from Islington Community Independents. Islington's residents deserve better, and I'm prepared to work with progressives who care about making Islington a better place to live.

statement_to_voters: Standing for re-election as Labour Councillor for Caledonian Ward, which I have represented since May 2006. I am a proud Scot and Londoner. I came to Islington in 1979 and have lived with my family (incl two teenage boys) in Cally for 30 years. Every year since 2010 I have taken the lead Councillor role organising the Cally Festival, Islington's largest street festival. At the Town Hall, I now chair the Audit & Risk committee and have led Islington’s pension investment committee for six years making our Pension Fund one of the most ethical local government schemes. I am also the chair of governors at Robert Blair primary school and a governor of New River College, Islington's pupil referral unit. I am an Arsenal supporter and a fan of 1970s soul music.

I am the Leader of Islington's Labour Council having represented Caledonian Ward since 2014. I was born and raised in Islington and served as the Borough's Mayor before becoming the Leader. I am the first ever Leader of the Council who is a Council tenant. I am actively involved in my church, local community schemes and inter-faith partnerships. My priority as Leader is to work with local people and communities to make sure their voices are heard and to achieve a more equal Islington.

I am a council tenant living in the Cally for 30 years with my wife and children. I have been a dedicated community activist for over 20 years helping residents with housing, education, health, employment and citizenship. In recognition of my volunteering during the pandemic I was awarded the British Empire Medal for outstanding community service. I am an NHS worker and have served as a school governor and charity chair. I want to make sure our neighbourhood is cleaner, safer and more connected community for everyone.

Jorge has worked with young people in care and education for nearly a decade, providing specialist support for children with multifaceted complex needs in schools, youth centres and home settings. Alongside his professional work, he is a passionate campaigner for climate action, affordability and social justice. As a councillor, his priorities would be the well being of young people and housing repairs.

Jorge said “I’m standing to be a Councillor for Canonbury to fight for the changes Islington desperately needs. Islington council has been a bad landlord for far too long, I’ve spoken to so many council residents in Canonbury who have been dealing with severe issues for years that the council have failed to resolve. As a teacher, I have seen the impact the affordability crisis has had on young people. Islington should be one of the greatest places in the country to grow up but for many it is not. As a councillor I would work for the well being of our young people and contribute to creating the brighter future they deserve.”

Kevin has lived at Bevin Court in Clerkenwell for over three years and is proud to call the area home. Before this, he worked as a football coach for an EFL League One club, supporting players at every level—from disabled football programmes to academy players pursuing professional careers.

If elected, Kevin’s main priorities will be:

1. Reducing the cost of living
We will working locally to keep Islington Council Tax below the London average. I am commiteed to preventing new charges being imposed on residents wherever possible.

2. Cleaning up Clerkenwell
Too often, our streets are left in an unacceptable condition.Kevin and the Liberal Democrats will take a hands-on approach to ensure streets are kept clean and well maintained.

3. Fixing our estates
Lib Dems are proud of Clerkenwell’s estates, but too many residents face long delays for repairs, broken lifts, and a lack of clear communication. We supports a plan to replace all lifts with parts over 30 years old and to assign a dedicated, clearly advertised repairs coordinator for every major project—so residents always know who to contact and can hold the council accountable.

4. Repairing roads and pavements
Clerkenwell’s roads and pavements have been neglected for too long. Kevin and Lib Dems will push to reinvest the fines collected by the council directly into fixing and maintaining local infrastructure.

Jara ('Yara') is a Clinical Psychologist and clinical lead in a Child & Adolescent Mental Health Service. She has worked for the NHS for over 10 years, following some years in the charitable sector. After growing up in different countries, she has called England her home for 20 years and is a proud Islingtonian - renting here for many years. Being of mixed Euro-Asian heritage, she brings lived experience of diverse communities and strong inclusive, left-wing, environmental values.

Jara said: “I’m standing to be a Green councillor for Clerkenwell to fight for everyone’s right to a healthy, fulfilling, and meaningful life. Nobody should struggle to access the right support or education or struggle to make ends meet; and I believe access to green spaces and clean air should be a human right. As psychologist, I’ve seen the impact people’s communities and environment have on their wellbeing. I want to put my skills and experience at the service of Clerkenwell residents – to improve living conditions, protect public services, tackle inequality, and make our communities greener, safer, and more connected.”

Jara has experience of organising projects, leading large teams, and supervising colleagues in high-pressured environments to improve existing services and develop new ones. Jara is practiced at collaborating with people with different ages, needs, priorities, and backgrounds, and across competing services. She works hard to empower those voices often less heard, including those from global majority, LGBTQ+, neurodiverse, and disabled groups.

Jara is passionate about working with local residents and organisations to protect Clerkenwell’s sense of community and heritage, while building a fairer, greener Islington where none are left behind.

Benali is a Highbury based Green member.

He's worked on the official Remain and as a campaginer for a health charity.

Benali has led a variety of successful LGBT+ campaigns. Fighting the return of Section 28 in schools and the dealth penalty in Brunei.

Jon has lived in Islington for the past 19 years and worked in the borough for most of that time. He now works as Chief Executive of a national children's charity.

Jon is a campaigner for affordable housing and safer streets and works to promote urban green spaces and allotments.

Warm greetings to one and all,

I'm proudly standing, as a candidate representing the Hillrise ward. Because, I firmly believe, that through building a bond with you, the members of the community.

This can in-turn, bolster the connection between political figures, and members of the community. Where, faith is reignited into the community. In which, I seek to develop social-cohesion within our community.

Where your voice is heard, and acknowledged within the political arena. Moreover, striving to bring forth social cohesion. Whereby, community spirit is channeled throughout the atmosphere.

Striving to decrease crime rates, where we all can feel safe, and walk confidently within our local community.

A stronger, fairer, more hopeful Islington really is possible if we work together.

As Councillor, I promise to work for the benefit of all Hillrise residents - not for a political party.

My Commitment is Clear:

Challenging the system to deliver real change for local people. We can all see how austerity, privatisation, and top-down politics have eroded trust and harmed ordinary people.

I am not afraid to name the source of the problem, successive governments in Westminster which have cut funding while giving councils even more responsibilities.  This has to stop and we need to explain this reality to our neighbours and unite them in order to fight back. If elected as your local councillor, I will fight any budget that proposes further cuts and stand  with the people most affected.

Let's make Islington work for the many, not the few.

Claire has lived in Holloway – on the same estate currently called ‘Hyde Village’ for 32 years and in Islington Borough for 42 years. She lives with her partner and has a 32 year old daughter who lives in Berlin. She is semi-retired and with a 4-hour a week job working for a peace networking organisation based above Housmans Bookshop in Kings Cross.

Leon has lived in London for 24 years, including 12 years in Islington on the border of the Tollington and Finsbury Park wards. His connection to the area goes back his whole life through his dad.

Leon is standing as a candidate because he believes his experience as a chartered structural engineer can make a positive difference for Islington. He is used to solving complex problems and wants to use that skill to make the most of the council’s limited budget and help make the borough a good place to live for everyone.

Leon believes decisions should not happen behind closed doors and that local people must be empowered. He supports participatory democracy, including participatory budgeting, so residents have a meaningful role in shaping their community.

Leon thinks the council should depend less on outsourcing for inspections, repairs and improvement works in council housing. Bringing more of this work in‑house would mean quicker, better‑quality repairs, improved living conditions for tenants and lower service charges for leaseholders.

Leon backs liveable neighbourhoods that reduce traffic and pollution, make streets safer and quieter, and open space for cycling, walking and community use. He has joined the local residents’ group to raise awareness and build support.

I’m a local resident committed to strong education where no child is left behind, full SEND and EHCP support, safe and affordable housing, reliable services, and putting our community’s needs first in every decision.

I am an Islington resident of over 15 years, with a family history in the Irish community of Junction Ward. I am not from a traditional political background, so my motivation comes purely from being a resident myself and witnessing first hand the problems that impact our communities. I am standing to represent my fellow residents and give them a voice in Islington Town Hall. I am also very proud to be part of a community that stands so strongly in solidarity with the Palestinian people, and to have signed Islington PSC's Candidate Pledge for Palestine.

My background is in arts education, and I have worked locally for many years, including mentoring at the National Youth Theatre on Holloway Road, helping young people build confidence, find their voice, and develop skills for life. I have seen first hand the ways in which art changes and enriches lives, particularly for those struggling elsewhere in their lives with housing, health, or access to education. Cultural spaces are something that everyone should have access to and it is heartening to hear from Junction residents that there is already lots of support for the development of an arts centre in Archway.

In Summer 2024, I replied to a call out for volunteers to help elect Jeremy Corbyn as an Independent MP. I had always voted for Jeremy, and felt it my duty to help ensure his victory. I will never forget how nervous I was walking into his office, only to find that I was fully embraced by the whole team. Following Jeremy’s election victory, I became involved in Jeremy’s regular community meetings, working diligently behind the scenes to co-organise and facilitate on topics affecting local residents, such as housing conditions, health and worker’s rights. In Islington, we are lucky to have so many incredible activists, and I have been proud to support local campaigns, including collaborating with my incredible colleague Cllr. Ilkay Cinko-Oner to set up a desperately needed Parents & Carers Union, and supporting Shirley Franklin, founder of Defend the Whittington Coalition, in her unwavering campaign to fight against the defunding of our local hospital, and for a publicly owned NHS.

As someone who always wanted to be more involved locally, but didn’t know how and worried about feeling like an imposter, I understand what it’s like to be a frustrated resident with seemingly no say in what happens on my doorstep. I will be a councillor who bridges that gap, someone who listens, brings people together, and ensures decisions reflect the actual needs and experiences of Junction communities.

Being asked to be a part of ICI has been an honour; a local party solely for Islington residents, founded by four former Labour councillors who made the tough decision to stand by their principles, when it would have been much easier to stay quiet and do nothing.

If elected, I will work for a council that is transparent, accessible, and genuinely responsive. I will stand up for Junction residents and work to build a fairer, more compassionate Islington for everyone.

My name is Pat Prendergast. I have lived in Islington for the past 2 years while studying history at University at UCL.

Despite my short time here in Islington I’ve been committed to helping in the community, volunteering for the Islington North People’s forum, helping with Acorn to oppose unfair evictions, getting involved in our Your Party Proto-Branch, and joining our already well established activism networks. I have met so many kind, knowledgeable and committed people who have helped me find a home here and welcomed me into this community.

At my university I have organised a Your Party society to bring together students across UCL and other London Universities, join the fight for improved workers rights in UCL, and support our BDS movement against UCL’s complicity in genocide. I did this in the hopes of bringing the welcoming community spirit in Islington to other students across London.
Standing as a councillor means supporting the community. I will fight for improved housing, a reliable and supported healthcare, and better support for our young people. But more than that I will be responsible and accountable to our community - bridging the gap between politics and the people who it affects.

I have seen worrying apathy in students and young people surrounding politics, in which it is a separate, unchangeable world for older out of touch people to make all the decisions. I want to bring local politics that is local and community based, ensure young people get their voices heard, and
ultimately do some good and give back to the borough that has welcomed, inspired and uplifted me for these past 2 years.

I am incredibly excited for this election and whatever follows and cannot wait to keep meeting and supporting the many Islingtonians that make this an incredibly special place.

My name is Rasan. I grew up in North London and now live in Laycock, working across local GP practices. I’m Kurdish, and my family came to Britain when I was a baby after fleeing conflict in the Middle East. That has shaped how I think about community, security, and the importance of feeling supported where you live. In my work, I spend a lot of time talking to people about their health, and you quickly see how often the same issues come up: housing, stress, money, isolation, and the environment around us. It’s a big part of why I care about local politics. Health isn’t just what happens in a clinic. It’s shaped by the conditions we live in.

I’m standing because I want an Islington where people can live well, with strong local services, decent housing, and communities that feel supported. I’ll back practical local action that improves health, fairness, and quality of life.

Voting for me will give you a voice. Standing up for what is right and just. Protecting the future. Making Britain great again by focusing on four key issues that affect us all:

> Making our education system the best in the world; > Ending the inequalities in the NHS to provide the best health care for all; > Taking action on the cost of living crisis that has hit many of us in Islington by ensuring fair pay and affordable housing; > Promoting a safer and more sustainable future with more renewable energy and safer streets.

Christopher has lived for 26 years in St Mary's & StJames' since 2000. He was influenced by his step father a long time Labour Councillor in Lewisham to become active locally. As a new resident in 2001 he secured funding for Cross street parking improvements and a new zebra crossing. He is an architect specialising in retrofitting homes for low energy / low carbon and new passive houses. He was course leader for Technical Studies, MA Architecture, Royal College of Art for 8 years.

After the UK declared Climate Emergency 2019, he campaigned for Islington to rethink local planning to encourage innovation. He realized that 50% of the borough is within conservation areas and without heritage climate retrofit the borough would not be able to reduce resident’s energy and fuel costs. During covid he researched one Islington Conservation Area to see where reductions could be made. He collaborated with and wrote the heritage section of the influential UK 2021 ‘Climate Emergency Retrofit Guide’ by LETI.

Christopher campaigned with the Islington Environmental Alliance and the Green Conservation Petition which gathered 2,221 signatures forcing a debate in council for proactive heritage climate retrofit in July 2023. During Covid his Islington conservation area research became a toolkit for action. His drafts were not well received by Islington planners, but the work was published in March 2023 as, "Climate Emergency Conservation Area Toolkit- England". Launched at several trade shows, 500 hard copies sold out (more pdfs) reaching councils, architects, and planners across the country. These multiple resident-led campaigns pressured, Islington to renew and fund work on the overdue "Climate Action SPD" and the "Retrofit Handbook" published in September 2025. Christopher supplied his book to the council and extensive edits to the planning policy team to radically change the early drafts and make sure the new Islington documents would be current.

Christopher said, "I bring passion, detail and expertise for the work ahead. I have now finished my second book on rapidly changing new vacuum glazing window technology, which was briefly mentioned in the 2023 book. It will be launched at FutureBuild one week after the election."

If elected he will bring his expertise and energy to campaigning within the council in areas of climate retrofit, planning reform, rethinking Islington housing (particularly Community Land Trusts), and green space street improvements to make Islington a viable community adapting to future uncertainty.

Alex has lived in Caledonian ward for over thirty years, and has been a candidate in the last three local elections, after joining the Green Party in 2005.

He wants to make the council more accountable to local people, and to mitigate the effects of government cuts on local services.

Martin Lunnon, Liberal Democrat candidate for St Peter's and Canalside Ward, Islington, 2026

I'm a retired actuary, with 30 years' experience in the public sector, and subsequent service on the finance sub-committee of the board of Amnesty International UK. This has given me a wealth of experience of managing risk and financial projections. As such I feel I could contribute a lot to Islington Council as it faces ever greater demands on its services with limited financial resources.
I've a strong interest in planning, urbanism and transport. As someone who currently faces some mobility challenges, I'm concerned about reliable accessible public transport, and about having good pavements so that people who face difficulties getting around can easily access bus-stops and stations.
I'm passionate about human rights and justice, and, as well as Amnesty International, I have a long history of volunteering with charities supporting asylum-seekers and refugees and people living with HIV and AIDS.
Finally, I love Islington. I lived here for 35 years, almost all my adult life, for most of that time in St Peter's ward. I'm training to be an Islington tour guide, and volunteer with a local history group. It would be an honour to serve such a beautiful and vibrant area as a councillor.

Toby North – a charity campaigner, proud trade unionist, school governor and committed local organiser – will be Islington Labour’s candidate in St Peter’s on May 6th. Toby works in campaigns for a children’s charity, putting pressure on local and national governments to improve lives and reduce child poverty. Since moving to the borough, Toby has served as campaigns coordinator for both Islington constituencies and as a ward organiser for two branches, leading on campaigns to protect our NHS build more genuinely affordable homes for local people.
