John has lived 18 years in Islington since 2008, and is an active contributor to the Tenants and Residents Association on the multicultural estate where he has lived since 2009. He joined the Green Party in 2023, and was elected Treasurer of the Islington Green Party in September 2025.

John said,”I joined the Green party in frustration at the stance of the major parties over many issues, particularly Gaza, and fully support the strong stance taken by party leadership and conference on the need for all countries, even our allies, to uphold international law. In my work as a specialist in conflict casualty recording, I see the damage being done by Britain’s support of illegal US and Israel actions in the Middle East, actions which have direct consequences for the people living and working in the streets of Islington.”

John would bring to the council his concern for ethical divestment and making Islington a thriving community safe and welcoming for all.

Trade union activist Mick Gilgunn has been selected as Islington Labour’s candidate to contest the Tollington by-election on Thursday 1st July.

A lifelong activist and advocate of workers’ rights, Mick has played his part in campaigns from defending Council housing and the Whittington Hospital through to workplace activism as a member of Unite the Union and Chair of Islington Trade Union Council.

Mick works in a maintenance department at a London university and has lived in Islington for over two decades. He is passionately committed to the rights of private renters, reducing health inequalities, and tackling the climate crisis.

Mick Gilgunn, Islington Labour’s candidate for the Tollington by-election, said:

“I am honoured to have been given the opportunity to stand for election and represent our wonderful community here in Tollington. Our borough is a fantastic place to live and work, but the impact of Tory austerity leaves us with so many challenges in the years ahead – from cutting crime to building the affordable homes we so urgently need.

“If elected, I will work hard to support the Council’s bold action to protect the environment with more school streets and a new generation of high-quality, skilled, green jobs for our young people. I’ll also do everything in my power to save our NHS, campaigning against the privatisation of GP surgeries and defending local services.

“I’m so looking forward to working with Tollington’s fantastic Councillors – Anjna Khurana and Flora Williamson – and the whole Islington Labour team to help make our borough the best place to grow up and grow old in.”

The 1st July poll will take place following the resignation of Richard Watts as ward Councillor. Residents wishing to register for a postal vote can do so here.

Sophia has lived in Tufnell Park all her life, and is standing because she genuinely loves her area and enjoys helping people; a casework win is a proud moment. She comes from a working-class background and wants to show people that you do not need to come from privilege to enter politics.

Sophia says “The Green Party is the only group that has the environment at its core. Nature will not survive without breathable air and predictable temperatures. I’ve been a member for 5.5 years.”

Sophia used to work in the Community Engagement Team at The British Library, so she’s used to communicating with residents about issues personally impacting them. “For the past year and a half I’ve been door knocking and listening to the concerns of residents, then raising it through our Green councillors to get action. My main priority is being a reliable source of contact that people can come to; someone who listens and resolves. Areas of interest to me are social housing, both council and housing association properties, and processes around recycling and waste management.”

Sheridan is a former software engineer turned ecological economist, who has lived in Islington since 2020. She works on developing policy and education programmes to show how we can build a different kind of economy that actually works for people and planet.

“People all over Islington are seeing their council tax bills and business rates rise at an alarming rate, and yet services are being cut all over the place,” Sheridan said. “So much of the blame lies with the Labour government refusing to restore critical funding. We’ll work with Green councillors all over London to expose this dereliction of duty and insist the government step up to do what’s needed.”

She’s also running to help change how decisions are made in Tufnell Park, to ensure residents have a stronger say on issues affecting their lives, with a focus on participatory budgeting and collective decision-making. “We’ll work to ensure that people aren’t just having things done to them — we’ve been knocking on doors for years now, and will keep doing that so everyone knows their opinion and contributions are truly needed and valued.”

As the lead pastor of a Christian church in Islington (The Angel Church) and as a resident of this borough for more than a decade I am well aware of the many positives and negatives of life in our borough. There is no other place in this city or country where I would rather be. I am deeply invested in seeing the lives of those around me bettered and truly want to see each individual in Islington, no matter their age, stage, or ability flourish. This is, I hope, well evidenced in my church and community work which spans interaction with every type of person with every type of need you can imagine.

Local government plats a very important role in helping achieve the best for each individual person as part of the larger collective of our city and of our nation. I am not in the business of toxic negativity that is consuming so much of our politics across the political spectrum. I have no desire to impugn or discredit any of our public servants in the tasks they have undertaken, I am sure to the best of their ability within their capacity. I do know and believe we could do better. I believe the people of Islington could be better looked after and I believe the people of Tufnell Park could have better representation. I will not make promises I may not be able keep due to democratic procedures or beurocratic red tape, but I can promise my complete commitment and attentiveness in representing the people of Tufnell Park fairly and well.

I hope to receive your vote.

Devon was just 124 votes away from becoming the first Green Councillor in Tufnell Park in 2022. She’s worked and volunteered in community centres and programmes across Islington over the last 7 years, and her priority would be to make sure that residents can easily access the support they need.

“Tufnell Park is my home. I want to work with you to make sure that the day-to-day things that would make your life easier are being done by the council”, Devon said. “Actions speak louder than words — that’s why I’ve reported over 100 potholes this year. When I tell you I want Tufnell Park to be a safer, better place to live, you can see we’re already doing the hard work”.

Much of her local paid and voluntary work has enabled her to build deep relationships with residents over many years, listening with patience and respect to the range of diverse viewpoints that make up our community. She would continue to fight for all of your everyday problems like bins and drains to quality of life issues like damp and mould.

Sarah was elected to the Council in 2016, and has lived in Abingdon Ward for over 27 years with her husband and three children. She has chaired the Family and Childrens Services Scrutiny Commiitee and was more recently the Lead Member for Adult Social Care and Public Health.  Sarah is currently a Governor of Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust.

Anne has lived in Kensington all her adult life and went to school in Chelsea . She has been a Councillor since 2016 and became the Lead Member for Communities in 2018. Before becoming Lead Member, Anne sat as a Trustee of the Westway Trust. At the same time, Anne was a member of the Planning Committee and on Family and Children’s Services scrutiny. Anne is married with two children.

James is committed to serving all Abingdon’s residents and local businesses.  He has particular interests in education, planning and the quality of our streets and public spaces.  He is a Governor of St Philip’s and St Barnabas primary school and within the council, is Chairman of the Planning committee. He lives in the ward with his wife, Munna, and they are keen supporters of their local residents’ association, ESSA.

I am standing in the local elections for Hans Town & Brompton, an area I have lived in, grown up in and gone to school in.

This is not just somewhere I am campaigning, it is somewhere I genuinely care about.

I understand the character of the area, the pressures residents face and the importance of maintaining the high standards people rightly expect from the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea.

I want to help ensure our streets remain clean and well maintained, that residents feel safe, supported and listened to and that the Council delivers the level of service expected in one of London’s most iconic and historic communities.

I am not a career politician. Alongside my professional work, I am standing because I believe local representation should come from people who are genuinely connected to the area and invested in its future.

Whether residents have lived here for decades or have recently made Hans Town & Brompton their home, I want to be a visible, approachable and proactive local voice for the community.

OUR PLEDGES TO YOU
• Protect local policing and community safety by installing more CCTV cameras
• Re-open Albert Bridge as soon as possible to all traffic
•Deliver continued investment in the Cremorne and World's End Estates to makes homes warmer and safer
• Protect our twice-weekly bin collections
• Maintain residents' boroughwide parking permits

I've lived in London for 16 years, working in Housing with both Crisis and Hammersmith Council. As a committed human rights advocate, I've fought for voices that are often ignored. I know the housing system well, so I know how to drive change within it.

Monica has lived in North Kensington since 1996 when she came back from directing Oxfam's post-war programmes in Iraq and she and her Iraqi husband chose to live in Colville because of the diversity and comfortable mix of cultures, and the vibrant character of Portobello Market.

I grew up with damp and mould, waiting for urgent repairs that never came. My mum’s health suffered because of it. Now I work designing policy to tackle health inequalities, so that health systems work for everyone. That focus and approach is what I want to bring to Colville.

As a Dalgarno resident for the past 11 years I have a deep understanding of your local issues, I have always been passionate about helping others, and I hope that you can give me the opportunity to serve you as your local representative. I am committed to working hard to make Dalgarno a better place for everyone, and I will always listen to your concerns and ideas. Together, we can create a brighter future for our community. As a computer science graduate, I hope to bring my technical skills and knowledge to the table to help solve some of the challenges that our community faces, as well as providing a perspective from the younger generation that is severely under-represented in local politics. I am dedicated to promoting inclusivity, diversity, and equality in our community, and I will work tirelessly to ensure that everyone's voice is heard. I believe that by working together, we can create a stronger, more vibrant community that we can all be proud of.

I was raised in Kensington, and this community has shaped who I am. I’ve seen first hand the challenges families face, and I’ve spent years working locally to support residents and strengthen our neighbourhood. I chaired our local residents’ association for two and a half years, led our Area Review Board, worked in RBKC’s voluntary sector, and carried out casework for our former MP, Emma Dent Coad. These experiences have grounded my commitment to listening, acting, and delivering for our community.

I founded Homemade Teachers, an organisation that supports parents in helping their children succeed and better understand the primary curriculum. This is because when families are empowered, our whole community thrives. As a teacher, I’ve taken GCSE students abroad to broaden their horizons and explore different cultures. I also volunteered internationally during my gap year in North India and organised annual excursions to Spain, experiences that deepened my commitment to equality, opportunity, and global responsibility.

I am a graduate of Queen Mary University of London, with a postgraduate degree from the University of Cambridge, specialising in Geography and Education. I bring a strong commitment to social and environmental justice.

It would be a privilege to represent the residents of Dalgarno Ward. I am determined to ensure that the voices of those living in the north of the borough are heard, and that every concern is met with fairness and persistence.

At the moment we are being let down.
The council’s recent low grading from the social housing regulator highlights serious failures to meet Decent Homes standards. Without it, our health, our children’s education, and our opportunities all suffer.

Together, we can achieve.
Let’s build a greener, fairer, and more compassionate future for Dalgarno.

I’ve lived in Dalgarno for 27 years. I’ve worked with schools, community partners and youth services to tackle antisocial behaviour, keep young people in schools and demand support for children with SEND. I’m committed to defending our most vulnerable residents and fighting for a safer, fairer and more resilient community.

I worked as a business manager until my youngest daughter was diagnosed with a serious illness. I then became her Carer for 22 years. I was then invited to work with the local Council, Police and Probation, helping to create music and employement experience projects to help young people into work or college, and into useful, fulfilling lives. I took over the community safety strategy for a local estate and localised crime fell by 25% in the first year. We did this by partnership, community-building projects and tons of fun! In my spare time, my husband, who had come to England as a refugee,  and I ran a refugee drop-in centre, providing translation, support, and assistance to new refugees. In recent years, having seen how inaccessible the local areas can be for disabled residents, I have worked with Councils, developers and planners to change their vision of what true 'accessibility' is. Moving beyond access, I would like to see everyone in our community being able not just to get around but to have a real say in what we build locally. Let's go beyond mere access to agency.

I am now involved in the development of small housing properties in a voluntary position, and in community safety. As a Neighbourhood Watch Coordinator for 14 years, I take a keen interest in networking and community building to not only help one another but to ensure our areas stay safe and people feel cared for.

I am standing as a Candidate for Reform UK in Dalgarno Ward as I absolutely love the diverse community, and the clear passion for life that is evident on every street! As a single parent myself for many years, I recognise how the cost-of-living crisis is stretching families to the limit, and how energy and food sustainability is just not there in London. Reform UK's plans to cut waste, streamline services and rebuild our local police forces seem to me to be the only policies really addressing todays issues. I would like to bring the skills that I have learned, in work, in volunteering and in life,  to help build on the amazing community projects that are already there, and give them all a real voice and sense of agency in what the local Council does on their behalf.

I live and breathe for community, was raised to serve, and will do everything in my power to ensure that Dalgarno residents and groups get the very best support they can to continue, and build on the work they are already doing to make Dalgarno the very best ward in RBKC to live in!

I was born here, so I’m clear eyed about the issues we face and the work needed to address them. I know what can be achieved when someone listens and then takes action.

I am Mona Adam, the Green Party parliamentary candidate for Kensington and Bayswater constituency, I have lived in several countries and multi-cultural communities.

I am standing for:

3.    NHS: Better health services from GP to hospital, money for upgrading and rebuilding our hospitals, more NHS dentists, better mental health services with the Gordon Hospital beds saved, palliative care with the Pembridge beds saved, better and more social care services.

4.    Immigration: I understand the importance of compassionate and fair immigration policies. I will work towards creating an inclusive society that welcomes diversity, protects the rights of immigrants, and fosters a sense of belonging.

5.    Homelessness: Tackling homelessness is a priority. I will work towards implementing comprehensive solutions, including affordable housing programs, support services for mental health and addiction, and collaborations with local organizations to address the root causes of homelessness.

As your councillor since 2018, I’ve worked with residents on numerous campaigns, from saving Morley College, to protecting Edenham & Trellick. I studied biology at ImperiaI, and I believe that safe and healthy housing is the bedrock of public health.

Ellie has lived in London for over twenty years. She has worked in fashion all her adult life, working as a stylist and designing her eponymous dress label. She has always loved Portobello Road for its vibrancy and its individuality, often frequenting it through her work and with friends.

A strong believer in supporting small businesses, Ellie loves the brilliant offering of independent stores, restaurants and businesses of the Portobello area. I’ve lived locally for two decades, working in Compliance to make sure standards are met and people are safe. I’m on the board of my block of flats and I know how complex housing can be. Having worked for an MP and studied law, I know how to achieve change.

I have lived in Golborne for over 30 years, and was a councillor between 2018 - 2022. I know what it’s like to be forced to fight for access to a safe home. I also serve on my local Resident Steering Group and as a North Kensington Law Centre trustee.

I’m a local business owner and strategy consultant, with leadership experience in the energy and charity sectors. I’m pragmatic, results-driven and committed to fixing broken services, ensuring value for taxpayers, and delivering safer, cleaner neighbourhoods.

I’m a long-standing Kensington resident, working in healthcare research, with extensive business management experience. Having volunteered in education and mental health, I am passionate about giving back. I will ensure local concerns are listened to and addressed with practical and effective solutions.

I will stand up for your concerns and make sure they’re dealt with. I will listen, be visible and accessible, and give residents the chance to SHAPE decisions, not just respond to them. A resident here for over 30 years, former researcher and lecturer, long-standing community campaigner, and witness to the Grenfell Tower Fire. As your councillor, I've been pursuing justice, accountability and change for residents, our lives and our wellbeing.

I grew up here. I’m a councillor, Eco Church project Chair, and food bank trustee. I founded the African Caribbean Cultural Centre & work a lot with Bay20. I’ve been standing up on housing disrepair, community safety, and support for all those affected by Grenfell.

I have been living in Notting Hill for the last 8 years, right here in Pembridge for the last 4. I love our community here, the most vibrant and caring in London!

Pawel Urbanski is the Liberal Democrat candidate for Queen’s Gate. My name is Tom Bennett, and I am your Conservative candidate for Ealing Southall.

Tower blocks aren’t the answer to the lack of housing. I would push the local Council to take advantage of the clean-air subsidies that are being proposed by the Conservative Government, and plant hundreds of new trees, and install 2,000 new electric-car charging points across the borough.

I first came to Southampton 33 years ago and over the years I have seen how fantastic Southampton is to live and work in. With excellent universities, a world class port and a historic football team, Southampton is a very special city. I have recently moved to Southampton. 

In my twenties I served for six years in the British Army Reserves with the Honourable Artillery Company and got to understand what hard work, dedication, and public service are all about. My parents were both born in Ghana and they moved to London in the 1960s. I was born and raised in London. My parents instilled in me conservative values of helping others and hard work.

As a local councillor I work every day for my 6,000 constituents dealing with local issues that matter to them. For example, stopping crime in stairwells of flats, improving housing by installing double-glazed windows, and providing support to those that need help with the cost of living.

I will support Donna Jones, Police and Crime Commissioner, to make sure that Hampshire Police have the resources they need to serve and protect us. I will also work hard to have houses built, especially in Townhill Park.

I am pro‑business, pro‑enterprise and pro‑innovation. I believe that businesses are both the life blood of the economy and great for society. I will work to create job opportunities and prosperity for everyone. The more jobs and businesses we create, the more we can support our nurses, teachers, doctors, and other public sector workers.

I am a keen sportsman and play many team sports, including football, cricket and rugby. I have won the Armed Forces Real Tennis and Rackets Championships on multiple occasions. We won promotion from the championship to the premier league. In fact we won the premier league the following season.

I am standing in the local election as I have lived here since 2005. During this time the Conservatives have been in power and I believe they have become too comfortable . They have run up a debt of £520 million , evidence that they are “ living beyond our means” .

I have something to offer as a politician with a vast wealth of business experience and everyday application of current affairs on a domestic and international basis at my fingertips.

I have noticed a complete difference of character in this country. It's changed. London has changed. I am here to support the Reform party and Farage to listen to the views of my constituents and be the voice and platform for Kensington and Bayswater.

I am a campaigner and community organiser living and working in North Ken. I come from a family of veterans so I know what it means to serve. I work on energy investment projects and previously worked abroad, designing economic development programmes. Louis Graves is your local Labour Champion at this years election.

I’m a proud local campaigner for the Green Party in Avenue ward.

As a proud member of the Green Party, I’m standing to represent residents in Boothferry ward because I believe our community deserves a stronger, greener, and more responsive voice on Hull City Council.

Too often, people feel overlooked by politics. I will listen, act, and stand up for Boothferry with honesty and integrity. Together, we can build a fairer, healthier, and more sustainable future for our area and for Kingston upon Hull.

I was born in Hull; I still live and work in and around Hull.

My Working background includes Motor vehicle engineering, Web/Graphic designer, Window/conservatory fitter, Property maintenance, along with HGV driver and Specialist Recovery Operator.  I have enjoyed my working life, meeting new people along the way shaping who I am today.

I was late coming into the political world because I never really believed in any one party. This is the correct time for me to stand for what I believe in, and what is good for, our country.

I know I would be a good vote for you, I stand for you all. I am not afraid to put in the demanding work that it will take to put our country back on track.

Voting for me gives you a voice, I will never forget that as a politician, primarily, I work for you.

For too long the Liberal Democrats have managed the decline of our council, selling factions of it off to private companies now charging the taxpayer a fortune, allowing big US corporations to come before our much adored but struggling local businesses, and hiking up council tax to cover the cost. It would be an honour and a pleasure to serve you as councillor of the very ward I call home. If you have any questions or would like to help my campaign, please email me at tee.drypool@outlook.com

Hi, I’m Deborah.

Hi, I’m Alex Gibb! My name is John Francis Gilling, and I will be standing as an independent candidate for the Orchard Park Ward on 7th May.

Luxury flats do nothing to alleviate the shortage of decent housing for Kingston people. Labour can win in Kingston.  All it takes is your votes.  Kingston deserves more than just more cuts to services and more tower blocks.  Please vote Labour – the real alternative.

After 24 successful years as a Merton Councillor, I moved to Kingston to live with my partner. As a Councillor, I served in many roles, including Cabinet Member for Sport & Leisure. I was responsible for rebuilding Colliers Wood Library at no cost to the taxpayer and delivering Morden Leisure Centre, almost identical to the new Kingfisher, but with no loss of service, very little delay, and at a fraction of the cost of what we are seeing in Kingston.

I now lead a quieter life, helping at the CREST Tuesday food bank, presenting popular and often chaotic rhyme times for children twice a week in Mitcham, and looking after my three grandchildren. I am also a keen walker. I followed the Grand Union Canal from London to Birmingham last year, and I am currently walking from Rome to Lecce in Southern Italy in stages.

I enjoy working with people and staying active. I bring a practical, imaginative, and cost-effective approach to everything I do. I believe Kingston would be better served with me as a Labour Councillor.

Coombe Vale has been home to my partner and me for 25 years, and our son attends a local state secondary school.

Our daughter goes to the local state school in Coombe Vale and we know first-hand the way the council has failed to give strong leadership to education in the borough.  It’s time for real change; both nationally and locally it’s only the Labour Party that can renew our country.

I have lived in the borough of Kingston since 1974 and in New Malden for over 30 years. Since my retirement from primary school teaching in 2016 one of the first things I did was to become a Labour party member, becoming active in the party shortly afterwards as a local election candidate and as joint secretary for Kingston and Surbiton CLP. My other community involvement is with Kingston Environment Centre where after becoming a director in 2019 I recently took over as Chairperson. I am also the lead volunteer on our recycling, gardening and weekly Community Fridge projects.
One of my main priorities as Chairperson has been to make good use of the building as a low cost, inclusive meeting place for a wide range of community groups so that now we have an almost full timetable with cycling, mental health, exercise and senior citizens groups meeting regularly as well as the Square1 café and an after school club.
My background with Kingston Environment Centre and other voluntary groups has given me an insight into how many people in New Malden are struggling financially, with mental health issues, poor living conditions, council services that do not work for them, traffic congestion, leading to increased air pollution and a distinct lack of provision for children and young people that does not cost a fortune. I believe that Labour has the best policies to tackle these issues.
Taking other Labour councils in South West London as a lead as a Labour councillor I would push for genuine value for money for residents. Thousands of pounds have been wasted on plans and consultations without any results, the Fountain Roundabout being a prime example of this. I would also work on communicating council decisions effectively to residents. As the local Labour manifesto says:
Labour will aim to “Improve transparency and democracy by giving residents clear, accessible information on council structures and how to contact officers, so everyone can engage effectively with local decision-making”.
Finally, I believe everyone should have a chance to vote for their preferred party so my advice to voters is there is no need to vote tactically, vote for the party with the policies that you agree with.

Having lived for most of my adult life in New Malden and raised a family here. I have watched with growing concern how our Liberal Democrats Council (they have 42 out 48 seats at the Guildhall) is giving free rein to private developers with no comprehensive plan for New Malden.

As a result today’s children will struggle to find affordable housing in ever more, oversized developments.

Aside from the City of London Corporation, Kingston has the worst record in London for the provision of social housing. The average wait time for a three-bed affordable home in Kingston is now over 25 years! In addition despite the extra Government funding to fix Kingston’s poor roads, our Royal Borough has been assessed with a red rating (the lowest) for road maintenance. And yet we are charged some of the highest rates of Council Tax in London.

Across the By-pass in neighbouring Merton (a Labour-run borough) residents pay £400 less a year for their council services.  Our Council can and should do more.

Vote Labour on May 7th and we will show you how.

The election on 7th May provides a crucial opportunity to vote for a desperately needed improvement in governance and financial management. 
The litany of failure and ineptitude inflicted upon the borough by the Liberal Democrats has had a demonstrably detrimental effect on the area. 
Let’s vote to end a protracted and ineffectual period of quasi-one party local government.

The highest Council Tax in London, and a conspicuous dearth of justifications, let alone improvements.

This must stop!

I’ve spent my working life in education and international development, and I have lived in Kingston for 15 years, having moved from the borough of Lewisham to be near family.

My roots are in a Welsh mining village and Liverpool, so standing up to power is in my DNA. I have been a Labour supporter all my life, though I was happily married for many years to a Liberal Democrat supporter.

I believe we urgently need a return to a more polite and rational political discourse, and that is even more important now than it was three years ago. We need calm thinking, careful analysis and practical solutions rather than slogans and rhetoric, and a commitment to helping those who are less well off.

Amongst the many challenges we face, the overriding one is the Climate Emergency, even while the cost of living is front of mind for many families. Better-insulated homes would make a real difference, reducing both energy bills and emissions.

I spent much of my adult life living and working in Africa, and have worked as a teacher and in international development.

I am active in faith, community and charity affairs.

In my spare time I play bridge and visit Kew Gardens.

'Chessington is one of the poorer wards in the borough, and too often it feels like decisions are made elsewhere, for elsewhere. As a Green Party councillor, I won't be beholden to the Lib Dem majority — I can speak up for our community and put Chessington's needs first.'
'Our ward is crying out for better public transport — too many journeys that should be a quick bus ride are either hopelessly convoluted or just easier by car. And when it comes to planning, major developments keep being waved through with little thought for the impact on our green spaces, our local services, or the people who already live here. That has to change.'

I am a lifelong local resident and have dedicated over a decade to serving my community, playing an active role in supporting and enhancing local spaces and schools, through involvement in a park Friends group and school PTAs. I have held  Treasurer and Chair positions throughout this period.

I am passionate about protecting the environment and preserving the character of our local neighbourhoods, working to bring people together and strengthen community relationships. I have regularly organised large-scale free community events in Old Malden, campaigned on highway issues and supported on setting up school streets.

Alongside my community work, I am a finance professional and a mother of two, balancing my career, family life, and civic responsibility with energy and care.

My decision to stand for election is driven by frustration with the inaction of current ward councillors and a firm belief that our community deserves more proactive, responsive representation.

Gia Borg Darcy - Putting You First

I am a mum, business owner, and community leader. 15 years in Kingston, wife to Michael, mum to three beautiful daughters. Founder of a private Tuition business and active in our community as Chairman of Kingston & Surbiton Conservatives as well as police ward panel Chairman, former school Governor and a volunteer for local community lead events. Loves singing choral music locally, Fighting for transparency, SEND, our environment and supporting local businesses, but most of all holding the current council to account. Prioritising our community's needs, not party politics.

I have lived with my family in Kingston for 15 years. My children go to school locally and I am a trustee at The Kingston Academy, an amazing school.

I am very proud of Kingston, I think it is unique. Our schools, university, hospital, the town centre, the river, the green spaces, the people. We are a city in a city.

The next decade will shape us. The world is changing, Kingston is changing, we can all see this. We need to grip the things that the council can control: housing, new developments, education, services for the vulnerable.

What will improve things? Strong leadership in the council, people not afraid to ask the hard questions, to challenge the status quo, and with the ability to find solutions that work. Why is our council tax so high when we can’t even manage to have a swimming pool for our children?

Let me tell you about my politics. It’s basically about making and doing. Not making do.

What’s true for Kingston is true for the country.

Kingston has a proud heritage of aviation manufacturing. We used to make things here, products that were the envy of the world. We can still do this, but there is now a real urgency to get making. I believe the council should focus on balancing residential development with encouraging employers to relocate here, who wouldn’t want to walk to work in Kingston?

We need to do, with ambition. There are too many voices demeaning London, Kingston and the country. Yes, we have problems, but we solve them by doing things, not talking about it. Vote me on to the council and I promise I will focus the whole council on doing.

The Labour party is not perfect, but it is laser focused on delivering a better life for everyone, not the few, not just a chosen few. That’s why I am Labour.

Socialism for me is about collective and individual responsibility. Wealth and power are generated from society, not just individual efforts, that’s why we must govern for all. It is not about handouts, it is about support when you need it, and contribution when you are able.

The council must support those that need it, creating an environment for success, through education, social care, good housing and encouraging employers to locate here.

The unspoken truth is that many Labour voters vote tactically in this ward. If this does not stop then we will never succeed here. Vote for me, for Labour, and start the change we want.

statement_to_voters:
Kingston has been my home since I moved here to study at Kingston University in 2008, and it’s where I’ve built my life, my work in the community, and where I am now raising my lovely daughter. I love Kingston’s strong sense of community, its diverse culture and rich heritage, and the beautiful green spaces and riverside we are lucky to enjoy.

Kingston residents have now experienced two full terms of Liberal Democrat council control. Labour believes Kingston should be a borough that puts community at the heart of decision-making — a place where everyone who lives and works here can thrive.

I am proud to stand on the platform of our local manifesto: “A Borough That Works for Everyone.” Real change happens when national progress and local action work together.

I worked in the voluntary sector in Kingston for over a decade and currently serve as a trustee of a local disability charity. I have also worked with the Kingston and Richmond NHS UNISON branch, supporting health workers and advocating for strong public services. Through this work I see every day how vital our local services and community organisations are.

I have been an active campaigner for equal rights, and if elected I will champion access and inclusion across our borough. Disabled people should never be excluded from participating fully in community life, yet too often they still are. I want to help change that so Kingston truly works for everyone.

I am passionate about tackling issues that matter deeply to residents. I have campaigned on environmental issues such as sewage pollution in our rivers, including visiting the Hogsmill sewage treatment works, because our natural spaces must be protected for future generations. I have also campaigned nationally to improve access to affordable childcare so families can thrive and parents are properly supported. I am proud that Labour is delivering support such as free school meals for those who need them and new breakfast clubs for children.

Housing is another urgent issue. Kingston currently has over 1,000 children living in temporary accommodation. I will fight for investment in good homes and strong public services, because these are essential for a society that is caring, fair and supportive.

Our high streets and shop parades are the heart of our communities. I want to help them thrive by backing local businesses and introducing community wealth building so more money stays and circulates in our local economy.

The Labour government and the Mayor of London are already working hard to repair over a decade of cuts and neglect, investing in public services and infrastructure. Kingston deserves a stronger Labour voice locally to ensure our borough benefits from that investment.

Having lived around Kingston all my life, I've always loved the strong encouragement of arts, our beautiful green spaces, and the diversity of shops and cuisines. Since moving in to the borough itself, I find myself falling in love with the communities and opportunities around, and I endeavour to continue bringing out and developing the best Kingston Town has to offer.

Coming from a low-income background, and being care experienced, I find myself connecting with residents all around Kingston about the struggles faced as a result of poor services, high council tax, and worries about the future if these conditions continue. As a renter, I understand that soaring housing prices only add to those fears. Kingston Town needs more affordable and social housing, and services which are worth their costs. Following the examples of local Labour boroughs like Merton, I aim to push the council towards council-run services, and a local plan with social and affordable housing as a priority. We can see all over Kingston that when profit comes before people, we get unaffordable high rises that drive local residents away instead of housing them. Alongside my colleagues, I aim to put residents and their needs at the forefront, rather than modern looking housing which serves no one.

As the eldest of four, I see firsthand the impact of declining spaces for children and young people. I've been there, trying to find places for my siblings to attend youth clubs or teen-friendly events, and I share the same concerns as so many parents and grandparents; we aren't providing enough for our children, and this must change. As someone who was never a fan of sports, due my disability, I worry for the young people like me, who don't want to or cannot participate in sports clubs, whose only options are to find parks to hang around at with friends. In a borough with such love of street art, theatre, and diverse festivals and musical events, we don't provide nearly enough of these opportunities to our children. I aim to work with Achieving for Children, local schools, and our wealth of artistic organisations, to bring more opportunities to our youth. I also intend to bring more awareness of council grants and funding, helping to fund free spaces for disadvantaged youths, making sure we provide for our children.

As Secretary of the Kingston Disability Network, it is my duty to understand and advocate for the needs of disabled residents and organisations across the borough. I know there is still so much more to be done to support disabled residents, but I believe that a combination of lived experiences like my own and an open mind in listening to residents is key to working towards equal access and opportunity in Kingston. I also recognise how deeply accessibility benefits communities overall, with its positive impacts touching more than just those with disabilities. Improving street signage and markings helps all of us to move safely around. Running more bus routes means not only do mobility impaired residents have a greater chance of getting a seat and reduced likelihood of injury, but parents can board with their buggies without worrying their children will be bashed or tripped over, encouraging them to take trips out.

On the doors in Kingston, we hear so often about bad rubbish collections leaving waste across the streets, and even with amazing local groups like the Friends of Fairfield Park, our green spaces could still use some extra love, especially the areas without a Friends of group to keep them clean and litter-free. In Council, I aim to push connections between Glendale and local communities, making it quick and easy for residents to arrange local clean ups, and ensuring our contractors do their fair share. I lead by example, having organised and attended park clean ups, and in connection with local organisations like the Kingston Environment Centre, I know our borough is so well equipped to shine, if only we make it easier to take those steps.

Our local businesses make Kingston Town such a wonderful place to visit. Still, we hear all too often of small businesses struggling to keep afloat with high business costs and rents. I aim to foster closer connections with Kingston First to support our small businesses, as well as taking time to share our local gems. It's so important to support these often family run shops, and I strive to work closely with owners to identify and solve the problems they face.

statement_to_voters:
I don’t think our council of 42 Lib Dems has listened to residents in a long time. I want to see a council that focuses on:

- help with the cost of living
- building communities, not skyscrapers
- clean, green and safe streets

I’m standing to help stop the overdevelopment of central Kingston. Plans for a twenty storey tower block and the overdevelopment of Middle Mill are unacceptable and would make residents lives a misery. These plans do not respect the special character of the area.

- About me

I’ve lived in Kingston upon Thames for 20 years and I’ve loved it from day one! We have an amazing community here.

You might have seen me over the years in the local parks or walking, very slowly(!), down the streets with my basset hound Rosie.

One of the great things about having a dog, particularly a very friendly, very slow walker like a basset, is the chance it gives you to interact with people every day. You see what’s going on in the area, hear some of the local gossip and get to know what’s on people’s minds. It is one of my favourite ways of feeling part of the Kingston community.

I work for the NHS and it is an honour to be part of something I feel is best about Britain and its people. Like many, I owe my life to the NHS. It was there for me when I was diagnosed with cancer and I will never forget the debt I owe to the amazing care and support I received from the doctors and nurses as I fought the hardest battle of my life.

That’s why I use the time I have been given back to fight hard for other people who might need my help.

- Why I am standing

I’m standing for Kingston Town because I want to help make things better for people. I believe strongly that we can achieve great things when we all work together.

Having previously worked with a number of public sector organisations and businesses, I have first hand experience of how to get things done and ensure prompt action from the likes of Kingston Council, Transport for London, etc.

I have led campaigns that have:

- INCREASED RESIDENTS PARKING spaces in a Kingston Town road when the Lib Dem council wanted to remove them completely
- Forced Kingston Council to provide residents living in flats over shops with a RECYCLING SERVICE after years of broken promises and fines
- PREVENTED THE SALE of dangerous, very high alcohol drinks from a known anti-social behaviour hotspot
- Pressured the current Lib Dem councillors into a PUBLIC U-TURN on their support for the removal of a Kingston bus stop relied on by disabled and older people for their independence.

If you have an issue and would like my help, please do contact me.

Being a councillor is a privilege that should be about helping your neighbours and your community. A councillor should be there to listen to the people, not to play political games.

I promise to put residents first.

I’ve lived in the borough for 14 years, and like many residents I’ve seen both what makes this a great place to live and where things could be done better. As someone with a family here, using local schools and services, I understand the pressures people are facing — from the cost of living to the strain on local services — and the feeling that too often people are paying more but not getting the value they should.

I’m standing as a Labour candidate to give residents a stronger voice locally. I care about this area and the people in it, and I want to see a council that listens properly and focuses on the things that matter day to day — decent housing, clean and safe streets, and reliable local services.

Labour’s plan is about delivering a fairer, greener and more caring borough, with better value for money and real investment in our communities.

If you want a council that works better for residents, I’d be grateful for your support.

I have lived in New Malden for 8 years and as well as being a Captain for a major UK airline I am a senior representative for the pilots’ union and have worked both nationally and internationally to make the aviation industry safer and greener. As a Labour councillor I will represent the views and needs of all Motspur Park and Old Malden residents – not just property developers and private landlords. The current Lib Dem run council charges £400 more per year in tax than the Labour council in neighbouring Merton, and that money should be in your pocket. Your Labour team are on your side, whether that’s in preserving the character of the High Street or making sure any new homes are truly affordable for residents. Only Labour has a plan for Kingston that protects and invests in our public infrastructure, rather than auctioning it off to the highest bidder.

I have lived in Motspur Park and Old Malden East all my life. I grew up in our local schools and now work as a lecturer at the University of London. This community has shaped who I am, and I am standing as a candidate to be a strong voice for our residents on the council.

We are out knocking on doors, listening to residents, and understanding both the joys and the challenges facing our area. I know how much people care about our neighbourhood, and I share that pride.

I want to bring fresh energy and new ideas to our ward, while respecting and protecting the things we value most. I will raise our concerns with the Mayor of London over the gas holders development, tackle parking problems and graffiti, and work hard to improve our streets and public spaces in a practical and caring way.

If elected, I will offer consistency, availability, hard work, and a genuine commitment to delivering results for our community.

Terry has lived in Motspur Park for over thirty years his children attended local schools. He was a Met police officer, working across London in specialised areas. He now runs a small business locally and continues to use his experience working with local Police, as Safer Neighbourhood Board Vice Chair locally and as Chair For The Royal Borough of Kingston’s Safer Neighbourhood Partnership, working with Police, and other community sectors across the Borough.
Always encouraging residents to join ‘Met Engage’, Terry also volunteers locally and has been working hard on neglected parts of his ward MPOME.
Supporting local residents, the local environment & small business is his passion.
Terry describes his local area as neglected.

statement_to_voters:
Mark Durrant:

Mark is a councillor for the Liberal Democrats in New Malden Village. He believes in the Lib Dem vision of a fair deal for all.

Mark is a Councillor, MPs Caseworker, and former Media Executive who lives in London, with his wife, a Tutor, and  former Maths Teacher.

He is a passionate believer in local communities working together for the common good. He was honoured to be re-elected to serve his community after running successful campaigns in the UK Local Elections of 2026, in a special election in 2022 and in the UK local elections in 2018.  He believes in housing with good planning and good access to doctors, dentists, and good schooling. He is proud to be part of an administration in Kingston that is building the largest number of new council houses for over 40 years. He serves on the committee that is overseeing  the renewal of the Cambridge Road Housing Estate in Kingston, which includes over 800 much needed affordable and council homes. He also served on the Corporate and Resources Committee which oversees the budgeting for the council,the pension panel, and the Children and Adult Social Care and Education Committee.  Within his own ward he has overseen a significant improvements in the local parks including new playgrounds in all three of our local open spaces, and a significant investment to bring the pavilion at Beverley Park back into use as a much loved cafe. At the local train station Mark has advocated for a newly installed waiting room on platform 4 with another new waiting room coming on platform 1.

He is most proud of helping to get the funding and see the building of a new Burlington Junior School - a £32 million investment in our children’s future

He is a seasoned campaigner having won his own seat three times. He is well known to local residents, and this has come about by being an active member of his local community, regular canvassing, and intelligent use of social media to get across local news.

He works for Paul Kohler MP as a Senior Caseworker. Before that he had a near 30 year career in Advertising in major media companies. More recently a technology start-up, and so understands the importance of small business to growing our economy.      He has 3 grown up children, and a new grandchild in 2023. His Stepson is a Management Consultant, his Step Daughter is an Environmental Consultant having studying for a Masters Degree In Climate Change at Newnham College, Cambridge University. His son has Autism and receives full time care from his local authority in Suffolk, and so Mark has first hand experience of being a carer challenges therein.

Lucy has lived most of her life in New Malden. A teacher by profession, she has also volunteered locally with Kingston Hospital, the Kingston Environment Centre and the Malden & Coombe Horticultural Society, as well as organising litter picks with the Green Party. Lucy stood for the Green Party in New Malden in the Council elections of 2022. With 10% of the votes, she was in fourth place after the three Lib Dem Councillors who were elected.

"I loved growing up in New Malden and chose to come back here to raise my own family. New Malden is a wonderful place, but when I've spoken to residents, many people are unhappy with the level of overdevelopment here, and feel that New Malden has been taken for granted as somewhere which can just absorb more buildings. If I were elected as Councillor I would stand up for the interests of local people and do my best to keep New Malden as a great place to live. For example, the Sure Start centre in Burlington Road was so helpful for me as a new parent. This has now sadly gone, and if I were elected as Councillor, I'd campaign for New Malden to get one of the new Best Start Family Hubs which are currently being rolled out.

As a teacher, I've had the privilege of working with students who are preparing for their A levels and university applications, and I've seen the immense amount of pressure our young people are under. If I were elected as Councillor I'd campaign for the needs of young people and families, including their mental health, to be prioritised. Of course, as a Green, I understand the vital importance of green spaces for our mental health - protecting our parks and our natural environment is a top priority for me too."

Raju has lived in Surbiton since 1968. He studied at Hollyfield Secondary School and worked for BT until he took early release in March 2012. His community voluntary work over the past thirty-five years includes as Local Authority school governor, and as an elected Councillor in Kingston from 1994 to 2002. He was a founder member of the Kingston Group for Religious Understanding which has now become Kingston Racial Equality Council.

I was born in Fulham and lived in rented accommodation with my Mum, but with the help of a local councillor we got a flat on the Alton Estate in Roehampton. This provided secure housing for my Mum to raise a family. In the early 1980’s I worked at The Victoria and Albert Museum where I was active with the Civil and Public Services Association Union. From 1987-2005 I worked at the Post Office and was Assistant Secretary for our Union Branch. From 2005 I ran the family business, a residential moorings, in Hammersmith for ten years. During this time I volunteered for Beanstalk, a charity that helps children with reading difficulties. I also raised my son as a single parent. From my early personal experience social housing is key to building stronger, secure communities, so we must build more and take care of what we have.

I’m a journalist who has lived and worked in Kingston for most of my life. I’m married and raised my two children in the borough, which means I have a strong personal connection to the community and the issues local families face.

I’m passionate about improving everyday life for residents in Norbiton. I care deeply about creating better opportunities for young people in Kingston and believe that investing in youth services, education, and positive activities is key to building a stronger community.

I’m also a strong supporter of grassroots sport and local facilities, recognising the vital role they play in bringing people together, supporting health and wellbeing, and giving young people positive opportunities to thrive.

Emily Davey, 47 (as of April 2018), is a housing solicitor with over 20 years' experience working for tenants and social landlords. She has also conducted training for Shelter and the Chartered Institute of Housing.
Emily lives in Kingston with her husband, Ed (MP for Kingston & Surbiton), and their children, John, 10, and Ellie, 4.
Having spent the last two years helping people in Norbiton with legal advice, she is determined to fight for a better housing deal for local residents.
Emily was central to Ed's campaign last June, when the Liberal Democrats once again beat the Conservatives in Kingston & Surbiton.

Kevin was born in New Malden and brought up in Old Malden having attended Burlington and Beverley Schools. He is a school Governor in Kingston and has run and established a number of innovative charities in the education sector. He has run a Kingston-based business as well as being the Chairman of a Trust in the centre of Kingston that is raising the profile of Kingston as a place of national historic importance.

I’ve lived in Kingston for 40 years and since I retired I have been active in a residents’ association, in community gardening, and chaired Healthwatch Kingston, the local watchdog for health and social care, where I sat on two council committees and got to know several councillors. In 2024 I was elected as a governor for Kingston and Richmond Foundation Trust (including Kingston Hospital). In 2025 I was given a Mayor’s Community Award- my nominator said ‘she seeks practical compromise but she has a terrier-like determination’, qualities which I hope to put to the service of residents in Norbiton.

I started my career as a public health nurse and then moved into university teaching with a spell at the Department of Health. So I have a great interest in health and social care, and in how we can work together to improve living conditions  and life chances, particularly for babies and young children. It is a disgrace that so many children live in poverty in Kingston, and aren’t  ‘school ready’. At the other end of the spectrum, I am an Age Friendly Ambassador and keen that the move to digital does not exclude older people from participating in local democracy.

Why I Am Standing

As a long-standing Labour Party member I am proud to represent my party in this election and would love to put my skills and experience to use in Norbiton. Having been a senior member of a university managing NHS training contracts I would bring experience of getting things done, including committee work. As a research manager at the Department of Health I worked on evidence-based policy making and I notice how RBK committee papers rarely draw on any research evidence, or comment on how other local authorities tackle the difficult problems that they all face. We can all learn so much from each other.

Olly is 46 (as of April, 2018) and earns his living as a drinks journalist. He has lived in Norbiton for six years with his wife, Jo, and their seven-year-old son, Conor.
Olly also has a dalmatian, Beano, who can be seen being walked twice-daily all around Norbiton.
Olly is a firm believer in offering support when and where support is needed. He also has a passion for environmental issues and a strong interest in education - currently at primary level!

I love and care about Norbiton. Our community is our strength. But we need to protect our local democracy.

I’ve heard on the doorsteps

-	how services have declined while your council tax keeps rising;

-	how critically important cycle lanes have been designed so badly that they endanger cyclists and pedestrians;

-	that many of you are worried about the decline of your communities as fly-tipping is out of control; and

-	that you don’t feel you have a voice in the key Council decisions that affect you.

We need to change this.

For too long, decisions in Kingston Council have been made behind closed doors.

I believe that when people are trusted and have a direct say over how council tax is spent, our communities and our local democracy will grow stronger.

Labour is committed to giving you the power to decide how money is spent in your neighbourhoods under our manifesto commitment ‘Your Money, Your Choice’.

This direct democracy has been introduced in Labour-run councils in Camden and Newham. It’s been a huge success. It challenges the status quo. It offers an alternative to the traditional top-down relationship between councils and residents. It puts power back in your hands and allows you to work as a community.

At its heart, the 7 May 2026 local election is a choice about values.

1.	The Lib Dems charge you for removing bulky waste, which unfairly punishes people on low incomes and fuels fly-tipping.

LABOUR IS COMMITTED TO INTRODUCING A FREE NEIGHBOURHOOD SKIP SERVICE TO END THIS UNJUST AND PROFOUNDLY UNEQUAL POLICY.

2.	Lib Dem Council decision-making is opaque. Many of you feel you are being ignored and you don’t have a voice in how Council Tax (the most expensive in London) is spent.

LABOUR IS COMMITTED TO DIRECT DEMOCRACY AND GIVING YOU POWER OVER HOW COUNCIL TAX IS SPENT IN YOUR COMMUNITY.

3.	The Lib Dem Council has designed cycle lanes which endanger everyone – pedestrians, cyclists and drivers.

LABOUR WILL PUT CYCLIST AND PEDESTRIAN SAFETY FIRST AND CALL FOR AN IMMEDIATE SAFETY REVIEW OF CYCLE LANES IN NORBITON AND THE BOROUGH.

I have spent my career tackling corruption, reducing red tape and bureaucratic fiefdoms, and fighting for local democracy.

I love Norbiton and will work day and night to rebuild your trust by giving you (not the councillors or administration) power over key decisions in your community.

If you want change in Norbiton, vote Labour on 7 May. Let’s bring democracy back to Kingston and give you a voice again.

Mike Massimi serves as a councillor for Old Malden in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames, where he has earned a strong reputation as a visible, hands-on representative with a clear focus on delivery and real results for local residents.

Over several years he has worked closely with fellow councillor Elizabeth Park, between them raising more than 1,100 resident enquiries and casework issues (by far the highest across the Borough). 
His approach has always prioritised practical action over promises, concentrating on what can genuinely be improved on the ground and then seeing it through.

Community safety has been a particular priority. Through regular ward walks with police, early intervention on environmental and street issues, and sustained engagement with residents, Old Malden has seen measurable and meaningful improvements. 
By the end of 2025, the ward ranked as the safest in London for thefts, burglaries and robberies, placing first out of more than 625 wards across the capital according to Metropolitan Police data, measured both by total crime and by rate per 1,000 residents.
Other notable achievements include over 230 residents trained in CPR and lifesaving skills through St John Ambulance, and one of the highest concentrations of defibrillators and bleed control kits anywhere in London. 
Old Malden also became home to the UK's first Department for Transport approved hedgehog crossing signs, a scheme subsequently adopted nationally.

Road maintenance improvements in the ward were highlighted by the AA as an example of best practice, and Mike has maintained a consistent record of protecting local green spaces, biodiversity and conservation areas, alongside a zero tolerance approach to fly-tipping and environmental damage.

His working style is straightforward: listen, act, deliver, and remain accountable to residents throughout. He is known for quiet delivery over political noise, with a preference for tangible improvements over headline-chasing.

At the 2026 local elections, Mike Massimi was re-elected with the highest share of the vote of any councillor in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames. He received 26% of the vote and grew his total vote by approximately 20%, rising from 1,093 votes in 2022 to 1,311 in 2026. The result reflects sustained local support and broad recognition of the work he has put in on the ground.
The result speaks for itself. Mike's approach has remained consistent throughout: deliver for residents, challenge where challenge is needed, and hold those in authority to account, whether officers, agencies, the Metropolitan Police Service or private management companies. The focus has always been on real results, not rhetoric.

I have lived in the Borough since 2014. I currently work for an insurance company in Human Resources and I am Chair of Governors at Hollyfield Secondary School in Surbiton. I have two children who both go to school in the Borough. I am passionate about supporting young people, and if elected I will work to reopen the youth clubs that the Lib Dems have closed, as well as working hard for all the residents of Old Malden.

I have lived in the Borough since 2011. I have worked for over 40 years in various roles in the social housing sector, with a focus most recently on tackling homelessness and rough sleeping. I am passionate about housing issues and, if elected, would work hard to increase the proportion of affordable housing included in new developments in the borough, and to ensure that the Council takes full advantage of government initiatives to reduce homelessness. I have experience of being a Labour Councillor in LB Richmond from 1998-2002. I am a season ticket holder at Fulham FC and a member of Surrey CCC.

I grew up in New Malden and have lived in the Borough all my life. I am a trade unionist and political researcher and know that we can do better for our area. Both the local Conservatives and Lib Dems are complacent and have failed to make the most of our outstanding local resources to promote the borough either economically or as a great place to live. Residents deserve so much more, and restoring a Labour voice to the council would bring in new thinking, challenge existing cronyism and ensure a fresh commitment to support all who live here.

I have lived in Kingston for more than 30 years. I am a retired local solicitor and remain closely connected to the community I have served throughout my career.

I am particularly interested in supporting both young and older residents with access to legal advice and guidance. My children attended local primary and secondary schools, and I am proud of my long-standing ties to the area.

My priorities include improving the local environment and street cleanliness, cracking down on graffiti and fly-tipping, and taking firm action on vandalism. Kingston Labour is committed to a cleaner, safer borough, stronger neighbourhood services, and better value for residents.

Kingston needs stronger accountability and more transparent decision-making, where residents are properly listened to and services are delivered consistently. Kingston Labour will put local people first and focus on delivering real results for our community.

I have lived in Surbiton for the last four years, and feel lucky to have found such a welcoming community in such a lovely area. I believe we can do better as a borough than the options currently provided by the Liberal Democrats and the Conservatives and as a result am excited to be standing as a Labour candidate in this election. I am very proud of the manifesto we are running on, and as your councillor would particularly fight to see an increase in truly affordable homes in the borough. I feel lucky to be living here and more people should have the same opportunity.

Today, I am proud to be raising my young family in Tolworth. I was born and raised in Chessington and have lived in every part of the borough, giving me a deep, personal understanding of our community and the issues that matter most to local residents.

I’ve been in Kingston since 1963, attending Beverley Boys (now Coombe) and despite a difficult start with my Father dying of a drug overdose followed by my elder Brother from alcohol addiction, I’ve had a rewarding life. Whilst working as a mechanic on the Portsmouth Road, I studied for a degree in the evenings at Kingston University, which enabled me to join the Civil Service, winning an ‘Outstanding Achievement’ award for the 2012 London Games. I also won the Policy Award at the 2015 Civil Service Awards and served with the World Health Organisation. Over the years I’ve always tried to give back to the community that has been so kind to me in my hardest times, volunteering with Kingston Rugby Club & Rowing Club and currently as an England Boxing coach and Secretary of Surbiton Boxing Club. It would be an honour to now serve as your councillor.

Andrew Wooldridge lives in Berrylands and his children attend local schools.

Andrew is working to promote business in Kingston, and is standing to help make our Borough fairer.

Jamila has been running her own business for the last 12 years in Kingston. In that time she has got to know the residents and issues concerning Kingston town centre. She is passionate about making Kingston a welcoming place for all by protecting green spaces, investment in parks and stopping anti-social behaviour. Jamila volunteers for a wide range of charities and community groups, working families and children to give them self confidence, including girls guiding, supporting a soup kitchen and a domestic violence charity.

Andy is running for the Ashbrow ward in Kirklees on a ticket of improving policing services and community safety.

Martin Price is the Green Party ward candidate for Ashbrow on Kirkees Council.
He lives in Kirklees and is an active member of Mirfield in Bloom, a 'Recycling Champion Hero' and a trustee of a Church of England owned ancient woodland in Birstall. My name is Fouz Ul Azeem Butt and I am standing as your Labour candidate for Batley East in the local elections on Thursday 7 May.
I am a local business owner in Kirklees, with over a decade of experience creating jobs and working closely with customers and communities. Through my work in retail, I see first-hand the pressures families are facing every day, from rising costs to overstretched local services.
I have been an active Labour Party member since 2015 and have campaigned across Kirklees for over a decade. For me, it has always been about listening to residents and working hard to get things done.
If elected, my priorities for Batley East will be:
	•	Fixing roads and tackling the pothole backlog
	•	Cracking down on fly-tipping and keeping our streets clean
	•	Supporting and revitalising Batley Town Centre
	•	Protecting and repairing Batley Library
	•	Addressing anti-social behaviour and improving community safety
	•	Tackling nuisance parking and improving access for residents and businesses
	•	Securing long-term burial provision for all communities in Batley
	•	Supporting families through the cost of living crisis
	•	Creating better opportunities for young people
I believe Batley East deserves a representative who is visible, accountable and committed all year round, not just at election time.
I am here to listen as much as I speak, so please feel free to get in touch with your concerns and ideas.

I’m Akhtar Kasia, a local resident, business owner, and someone who genuinely cares about Batley and the people who live here.

I’m standing as an independent because I don’t believe our town should be run by party politics. Decisions should be based on what’s right for Batley, not what suits a party agenda.

Over the years, I’ve been actively involved in the community, speaking to residents, supporting local initiatives, and highlighting the real issues people face day to day. The same concerns keep coming up: cleanliness, accountability, lack of investment, and slow or no action from those in charge.

We all pay into the system. We all deserve better standards.

If elected, I will focus on raising standards across the board. That means holding the council to account, pushing for visible improvements in our streets and services, and making sure your voice is heard where it matters.

I won’t disappear after the election. I’m already out there, and that won’t change.

This isn’t about promises. It’s about doing the job properly.

If you want someone who will speak up, challenge where needed, and represent Batley with honesty and energy, I’d appreciate your support.

Local. Independent. On your side. Born in Dewsbury Hospital, raised in Staincliffe, at the heart of our community.

Statement: 
Independent. Local. On Your Side.

Dear Resident,
Batley West isn’t just where we live, it’s our community, and it deserves to come first.

I’m asking for your support to continue serving you as your local councillor focused on people, not party politics.

Through my work in the NHS as a mental health professional, and as a long-standing community campaigner, I understand the pressures local families face because I see them every day and live them too.

Over the past eight years, I’ve worked to deliver real results for Batley West supporting residents with local issues, standing up for transparency in council decisions, and helping local businesses through challenging times. I believe being a councillor means being visible, approachable, and getting things done.

In 2024, I made the difficult decision to step away from party politics because I could no longer support decisions that were not putting our community first.

I answer to you, not a political party.

Across Batley West, I hear the same concerns: rising costs, stretched services, and people feeling unheard. You deserve a councillor who listens and takes action.

I will continue working with you to:
Keep our streets safe and tackle local concerns
Maintain cleaner, well-cared-for neighbourhoods
Support both physical and mental health in our community
Invest in young people and local community projects
Ensure fair, open, and transparent decision-making

Being your councillor means being present, listening, and acting, working side by side with residents to build a stronger, safer Batley West.

This election isn’t about party labels, it’s about who will stand up for you.

I would be honoured to advocate for the residents of Liversedge and Gomersal as your local councillor.

I want to support local people to work alongside each other and change the growing culture of hate. We need to make sure our LGBTQ+ communities feel safe and welcome in our community.

I hope to be a voice for these key issues on the council and listen to resident needs to ensure my opinions are informed by local experience.

I would like to briefly introduce myself and give you a background of my history. Not for sympathy but to highlight the fact that I have so much first-hand experiences, that it is easier for me to empathise with others and to be able to find help and offer support.

I was raised with a brother with severe disabilities. My mum suffered with mental health issues and consequently I became a young carer, spending lots of time visiting both in hospital while struggling with issues myself. I became a mum at the age of 17 and I’m pleased and proud to say I have two amazing sons who work hard, and I also am pleased to say that I have a beautiful granddaughter now also.

After my brother passed away in 2015 I felt passionate about using my time to help in the community wherever needed. I have been heavily involved with organising events such as the Batley festival, Heckmondlight and the great get together. I have organised summer fairs for residents on my estate and Christmas lunches, helping people in the local community connect with others and make new friends. I have volunteered as an NSPCC school service volunteer delivering workshops and assemblies to both key stage one and key stage two children. sadly, there is an increase in need to remind children that they have the right to say no and that there is always someone to turn to if they feel unsafe.

I am part of the North Kirklees interfaith group and have worked with refugees, sign posting them to different services and helping them become active in the community. I am also a volunteer co-ordinator with the Royal Voluntary Service. Before Covid, I was running intergenerational groups helping senior people and children connect with each other.

Most recently I have opened a community café which provides opportunities for people to gain work experience and build confidence. It also provides a place for support groups to meet regularly, and other activity sessions will be available.

One of the main issues that I want to tackle, is the lack of provisions and support for families since many of the Sure Start Children’s centres have closed. I was once a crèche worker at the centres and it was evident how vital these places were for families. They were a lifeline for many people. When this service was taken away, there was nothing put in place to replace it. I have now set up sensory play UK which allows families to bring their children for some much needed “time out” from the stresses that life brings.

If I am elected, I will fight for better support for families, better support for older people, better support for people dealing with mental health issues, better support for vulnerable people and better support for victims of crime.
