I work for Newcastle City Council, developing coordinated responses to homelessness and financial exclusion. I've seen the impact of the welfare reforms which have already taken millions out of the pockets of North Tyneside residents, and the cost of living crisis that will affect us all. Now is an excellent time to make changes locally to move to net zero and focus on sustainable development that benefits all residents.

I live in Cullercoats with my young daughter, we love the parks, cafes and beaches. In my (limited!) free time I enjoy running, yoga, books and drinking strong coffee!

I was born in North Shields, and lived here most of my life, and it’s true, I love North Shields!

We’ve got such an amazing heritage, a thriving creative and cultural scene, and some people doing incredible things.

But not everyone has the same experience, and within North Shields, we have growing inequality, and some serious issues with the cost-of-living, poor housing, poverty, anti-social behaviour and more.

The Town centre may have had some attention but it’s still not firing on all cylinders. There is a lot more than can be done.

I have been a councillor before (I was elected between 2019 – 2023) and I know what it takes.

I have already been working to improve North Shields through my job and volunteering, and I am committed to work hard all year to get things done. And, importantly, unlike some of the other candidates, I have a clear plan what I want to do for North Shields.

I have detailed some of my main priorities in my election leaflet which includes:

- A cleaner, greener North Shields
- Making local infrastructure work again
- Arts and culture everywhere for everyone 
- A fairer, more equal North Shields
- Revitalising the Town Centre
- Better democracy and more communication

The people of North Shields deserve a independent voice after decades of Labour councillors representing the area, and would promise to be a hard-working, community minded councillor who listens to local voices and acts on their concerns rather than taking the party line.

I have lived in North Tyneside for almost 25 years, raising my family and running a successful business at the coast.  I now work in adult education with a focus on SEND and children and young people's mental health.  I am standing as a Green Party councillor in Preston with Preston Grange which is currently dominated by three Conservative councillors – having a Green Voice to represent a different set of values can only be a good thing for the ward. 
I have an interest specifically in school-based attendance issues and have concerns about school provision for children who are unable to attend mainstream schools.  For older children, I am interested in increasing opportunities for young people to gain work experience and employment – there’s a distinct lack of opportunity for teenagers in the local area to get weekend jobs.  
I am a sea swimmer and so I am concerned about water pollution, particularly at Cullercoats Bay.  Litter on the beaches is also an obvious concern, alongside anti-social behaviour in the summer months.  I can see how this links to a lack of 'third space' for young people in the area to access and I would love to see youth spaces with pool tables etc to keep young people off streets or disappearing online.  
Having an elderly relative with dementia has allowed me to see the challenges faced with accessing support for the elderly – I would love to see community centres and libraries open for general support on a more regular basis.  
I've links with the refugee centre in Wallsend and have very good friends who are fearful of the growing anti-immigration sentiment. I am also keen to see more support for campaigns against violence to women and girls which seems to be systemic in places of power. 
As a single income household, I access food waste charities such as That Bread and Butter thing, and Olio.  I also have lived experience of claiming Universal Credit and the barriers this can present. I love that the Green Party represents local people, not big business.  
My aim would be to ensure local policy decisions were taken with the community as the priority rather than profit.  I’d be aiming for decisions to be made for the long term, with an emphasis on care and community, rather than to meet short-term objectives of profit and greed.

I am committed to working towards an environmentally and socially sustainable world, including all communities, leaving no-one behind in this process.

What this means for us here in North Tyneside is that we need to tackle together the three major challenges that impact on our lives right now: The climate emergency; The environmental crisis and Social inequality.

These issues are inextricably linked and I recognise that solving one of them cannot be achieved without solving the others.

I also believe that in order to bring these about an increase in democratic activity and greater transparency in Council decision making is necessary.

Greens have been successful in getting councillors elected in many places and have a good track record of standing up for people and doing politics differently. Green groups in South Tyneside and Darlington have grown over the past 4 years and proven that where Greens are elected, they work hard and are liked.

To challenge the status quo and provide some much needed scrutiny please consider a Green vote.

I’m standing as a Green Party candidate because I believe politics should feel that they represent and speak for the needs of everyday people. Politics should be for all of us.

Connection and community sit at the heart of what matters to me. Feeling part of something, feeling supported, knowing someone is listening. These things really shape our wellbeing.

Through my work supporting people with their mental health, I see how much the pressures around us affect how we feel. The cost of living, worries about housing, isolation and safety, a sense of not being heard can really impact our wellbeing.

I want to help to build our community as a place where people feel seen earlier, supported sooner, and not left to cope on their own.

Living in a coastal area like ours brings so much to be proud of.

At the same time, there are real pressures. Housing becoming less affordable for local people. Seasonal increases in visitors bringing challenges as well as benefits. Older residents feeling more isolated. Young people needing more spaces to go and a stronger sense of belonging.

These are the things I want to focus on.

Supporting homes that local people can afford.

A focus on practical, local solutions to energy and cost of living. This includes supporting renewable energy, improving energy efficiency in homes, and helping reduce bills while moving towards a more sustainable future.

Improving the re-cycling rates at NT council by utilising a reduced incineration policy.

Working with others locally to improve access to community mental health support and early help.

Strengthening support for children and young people, including prioritising SEND provision.
Making sure older residents feel connected and supported, not overlooked.
Protecting the green spaces and coastline that matter so much to people here.
Backing local businesses and helping keep our community strong and connected.
Supporting a balanced, preventative approach to community safety.

I also believe people deserve openness about how decisions are made and how public money is used, and that these decisions should reflect fairness, ethical integrity and responsibility.

I’m not a career politician. Standing as a council candidate is not something I ever envisioned. However, politics that divides, excludes, and privileges some while harming others is a real concern I feel I need to speak to.

I will focus on what we can improve locally, while standing up for the wider changes we need.

I’m standing to bring people together, not to divide, and to help build a community where people feel more connected, more supported and more hopeful.

Views my own.

I’m standing in this election because I love Tynemouth and Marden, I live here, and I want to stand up for the area I call home.

Like many residents, I feel our community is being let down. People are paying more in council tax, but too often feel they are getting less in return. Roads and pavements need attention, local services need to improve, and residents deserve to feel properly listened to.

If elected, I will work hard all year round to be a strong local voice for our area — focused on the issues that matter most to residents, including road safety, protecting Tynemouth’s character and heritage, keeping our area clean and cared for, and making sure local taxpayers get value for money.

This election is about who will best stand up for Tynemouth and Marden. I will always put residents first, speak up for our community, and challenge decisions that do not reflect local priorities.

I would be honoured to have your support.

Jay Bartoli
Local Conservative candidate for Tynemouth & Marden

Hi, my name is Richard and I am a retired inner city GP and have lived at the coast for over 20 years. During my working life I acquired a great awareness of how social problems impact on health and wellbeing.

As a member of the Green Party, I understand how social justice links in with climate justice and the environment. I have been involved in several local community projects aimed at improving our surroundings by increasing biodiversity.

I also strongly support active travel and believe that new housing developments must have easy access to reliable public transport and safe cycling and walking routes.

A local resident aged 92 said to me recently ‘we're sleepwalking into a catastrophe and no-one is doing anything about it’. The council could and should be doing more to achieve their stated carbon net zero target by 2030.

As a local councillor I would listen to local residents and challenge the decision makers on their behalf.  North Tyneside Council could do a lot more to help with these problems, and will do when Green Party members are elected.

I’ve long supported green principles but, as a father, have grown increasingly concerned that too little is being done to build a fair, sustainable society for my children.

I have a background in data analytics - and joined the Green Party as I can see the evidence for acting now against the Climate Crisis is overwhelming. Action is needed both to stop the decline, but also to deal with the problems we're always witnessing.

However, I'm not exclusively standing to fight for the environment. As a business owner, I see the suffering and injustice of our current society every day. I can see what needs to be done, but also understand the challenges businesses face in trying to do their part, and the kinds of support which would make a real difference. For my part, I have previously worked with a number of charities to promote digital inclusion and currently volunteer as a STEM Ambassador, helping inspire young people and open new opportunities for their futures.

I want to see a society which not only survives, but in which everyone thrives, and will work tirelessly towards that end.

I have recently moved into Wallsend North, in order to be closer to my family. It has not taken me long to feel at home and totally committed to my new community. 
I have a deep desire to contribute to the well-being of Wallsend and being involved in the Green Party is an important way of demonstrating this. 
I believe wholeheartedly that local citizens should have a real say in what happens in their neighbourhood because they know it best. In representing Wallsend North, I would make sure that I listen thoughtfully and meaningfully to the voices of local people, in order to represent them on North Tyneside council.
I have worked for 40+ years in local authority children's services, a national children's charity and as an independent trainer. Prior to this, I was a nurse in the NHS.
The reason I am an active member of the Green Party is that I believe in its values of social and environmental justice, as it works hard to improve the everyday quality of life of ordinary people - not just the privileged few. I already know that it often takes courage to speak up for these values, particularly when confronted by messages of hate, division and cynicism in the wider political arena.
But I don't let this put me off. On the contrary, it makes me more determined to reach out to my local community with warmth and a genuine interest in the stories and lived experience of people living in Wallsend North. 
It can only be a good thing for North Tyneside council to have new voices with positive messages of hope and optimism, and constructive challenge, woven into its decision making for local communities, including Wallsend North. 
I am determined that I would be such a voice, on behalf of my community.

I have been a Green Campaigner since I got the vote back in 1969 casting my vote for the "Homes before Roads" candidate in my home town of Brentford. In the 1970s I joined the Young Liberals where I learned a lot about community campaigning. In 1979 I joined the Ecology Party, which evolved into the Green party, mainly due to their non-GDP growth economic policy. I spent most of the 1980s in Ashford, Kent campaigning for the developing Greenist Policy portfolio and standing in borough and county elections. 

In 1988 I moved to Wallsend where I still live, to read for a Botany degree as a mature student. Over the years since I have stood as a Green Party Candidate in numerous times at local and national level.

I have carried out a range of campaigns in Wallsend and North Tyneside covering Trees, Housing and more specific projects such as The Buddle Arts Centre and a Town Council for Wallsend.   When elected I will campaign for the council to work with the "Trees for Streets Project" to improve the arboreal profile of the Borough and to get safety a priority on our footpaths and roads.

Hi, my name is Helen and I’ve lived and worked in the North East for the past twenty five years. I joined the Green Party because I want to make a difference for the future of our children and I feel that this is the Party which can offer hope to the next generation.

I’ve been impressed by the knowledge, commitment and passion of our local activists and I’m proud to be standing as a candidate in Whitley Bay North. Our local area needs to be protected and supported so that all of our residents can thrive and I am committed to working towards social inclusion for all of us.

As a teacher I am well aware of the disparities in our area and I would want to work towards a fairer and a greener future for all. Social justice and climate justice are fundamentally linked and I feel that Green voices on our council can only help to promote and develop these goals.

Local democracy is vital and I would like to promote real youth inclusion in our area rather than the division which can so easily take root. We live in a fantastic area and I feel that Green policies can only improve on this by embedding the changes we need for our shared future.

My name is Ben Mooney, and I am proud to be your Reform UK candidate for Whitley Bay North.

Born and raised in North Tyneside, I understand our community, its values, and its challenges. I am currently training to become a solicitor, driven by a strong belief in fairness, justice, and standing up for what’s right.

I’m standing as your candidate because I believe our area deserves better. Whitley Bay is a beautiful seaside town with incredible potential, but for too long, it has been overlooked by the local Labour leadership.

I have always liked to give something back to my community whenever I can. Since joining the Liberal Democrats I have been encouraged to engage in local politics, campaigning to improve my local area and the lives of fellow residents.

Voter participation and engaged democracy are things I care for passionately and have worked to improve all of my adult life, particularly amongst younger voters. Whilst campaigning for Remain in the EU referendum, I spoke and took part in events motivating voters to sign up and make their voices heard and I believe that the public should be given the opportunity to have a vote on the final Brexit deal.

I am also passionate about the environment, as a member of several organisations and volunteering with conservation groups.

Born in Norwich, I live locally in Sewell, and work in the city centre.

I’ve lived in Bowthorpe for over two decades and feel deeply for the community that I live in. I am standing for election in Bowthorpe as I want to offer a real, hopeful alternative to the traditional two-party system that has compassion and grassroots organisation at its core. I’ve spent my adult life working in health and social care, including at the NNUH, St Martins Housing Trust, New Routes Integration and as a frontline worker during the COVID-19 pandemic.

In 2026, life is hard for so many; expensive bills, inefficient services, inadequate mental health support, benefit cuts for the unwell and disabled, a crumbling NHS and no new social and council housing. If elected, I would like to support those struggling with the cost of living, tackle antisocial behaviour, advocate for residents regarding the future of the ward and protect and promote local green spaces, such as the Bowthorpe Marsh and Bowthorpe Southern Park.

A vote for me is a vote for a local girl who genuinely cares about those around her and who will always call out corruption, collusion and injustice.

I’m standing for Reform UK because I want to leave a better country and a better future for my children. This expectation that the next generation should inherit a better world from the previous generation has in the past been a given but now it is very much in doubt. The Conservatives, Labour and the Liberal Democrats have all presided over nearly three decades of managed decline of our economy, rapid change to our society and a sustained attack on our values.

Britain deserves much better and Reform UK are the only party offering real change and hope for a better future. The three legacy parties all believe in mass immigration, big government, high taxes, expensive energy and the woke agenda. Reform UK are the only party to reject this orthodoxy.

I have voted for the Conservatives in ten general elections but never again. Ideologically my position hasn’t changed over the years but the Tories have abandoned me and moved to the left, embracing globalist, corporatist values that I don’t align with. We need to put our country and its people first and that’s what Reform UK are proposing.

I have lived in Norwich for 23 years, I have raised my family here and started a small business here. Norfolk needs a fresh mandate in order to end decades of financial mismanagement. Tax payers deserve better services and better value for money from their local authority. Reform UK will run the council for the benefit of the people who pay for it rather than the people who work for it.

I would like to serve Catton Grove as it’s Councillor (City/County) by:
• Attend meetings to put forward your views and vote for resolutions 
• Take local issues seriously and do my upmost to resolve
• I would look to provide the best services as possible whilst being as efficient as possible
• I will work hard to try and reduce the 900 million pounds debt which currently incurs 200 million pounds interest per year. Just to put that in context it’s around 100, 000 households paying council tax to pay the interests, and when you factor in loan payments it’s probably nearly 50% of Norfolks households paying for the debt, which means around 50% of households are paying for 100% of the services ( This is only an estimate as I do not know what the payments are on the loan balance) - either way it’s an awful situation to be in

Tony has lived in Norwich since 2009 and has been a member of the Green Party for nearly 30 years. He has previously been a Green Party councillor in Dereham, having been elected to Dereham Town Council three times and to Breckland District Council for one four-year term.

Tony ran a wholefood shop in Dereham for 17 years until 2002. He was chairman of Dereham Chamber of Trade for two years. He also co-wrote the proposal that brought the local “Nipper” bus service to Dereham. He now runs an organic veg-box scheme based here in Norwich.

He has chosen to stand to represent the Green Party because he feels impressed by the caring and responsive manner with which it tackles issues facing our community today. He is particularly interested in supporting local businesses and shops to help make our local community more vibrant. He believes that the old saying ‘think global, act local’ is still relevant today and his actions are a testament to that.

He has been pleased to champion a more holistic, sustainable way of life and would be proud to represent the Green Party again on a local council.

When not campaigning, Tony can be found playing table tennis, performing music, or out trying to learn birdsongs on the meadows by the River Wensum.

Our Labour priorities for Crome

1.	We will work with colleagues across Norwich City Council to support low-income and no income people who have kept our country running while many of us were in lockdown or isolating at home.

2.	We will take action to improve air quality both inside and outside our schools, working with local schools to educate children and parents about what they can do to help. We will continue to protect and cultivate our open, green spaces.

3.	We will fight to improve outcomes for young children and young people

4.	We will continue work with the safer neighbourhood police team and other agencies to combat anti-social behaviour and County Lines drug dealing, aim to secure more CCTV, and work with Norwich City Council to tackle the causes of crime. We will work to improve the lives of vulnerable women via community safety structures across the city and county.

5.	We are pleased for the community that our campaign for a 20-mph speed in 5 roads including Wolfe Road is successful, following Norfolk County Council’s response to our question to them that it is appropriate - and our fight for further speed limits in residential areas will continue.

I’m Richard “Dicky” Eminson. Im a semi retired airline steward, that worked on the airlines for eleven years. Born in Southport, on a horticultural farm. I had a strong work ethic drilled into me from around 8 years old, as I helped my father work the land, producing seasonal crops.

After obtaining a business degree at Lancs uni. I moved directly to London. After various jobs, which included 5 years as a floor manager in Harrods. I eventually settled in the East End of London with my partner. After a friend of mine, who was cabin crew, found that easyJet was recruiting. I found my dream job! I am the ultimate people person that thrive on hospitality.

Activities outside these work scenarios, I have volunteered on a befriending course for Crisis (the homeless charity). I have raised over £10,000 for The Anthony Nolan Trust, via two London marathons. As well as many fun runs for Cancer charities.

After living in Brighton for 7 years and running my own business. I came to Norfolk for a short break over a year ago and simply fell in love with the people  and relaxed vide. I reside in Central Norwich, so very accessible. I class myself as likeable and approachable.  And more importantly I try and be as supportive as I can to any community I reside.

As a council tenant here in Lakenham, I see what you see every day, I know it’s time for a change. 
I’m running to get the basics right: cleaning up our streets, ending fly-tipping, and ensuring our children have safe, clean places to play. I understand the frustration of waiting for the system to work, and I will be the voice that finally demands Lakenham’s fair share.

​For too long, we’ve been represented by people who don't live our reality. I am committed to fighting for the high-quality social housing and reliable services we deserve. 
If elected I will to take our shared experience to the Council to ensure no resident feels disenfranchised or ignored again.

1. **​Practical Politics** : I believe in common-sense solutions that make our lives easier—better maintenance, warmer homes, and cleaner streets.

​ 2.**Working for You**: I’m ready to put the hard graft in. You deserve a councillor who is visible, reachable, and understands the value of a pound.

​ 3.**A Green Future for All**: Going Green shouldn't be a luxury for the wealthy. It should mean lower bills and better living standards for everyone in our community.

​Lakenham doesn't need more empty promises. It needs a councillor who knows the reality of life in social housing and is willing to work for it.

Dr Gurpreet Padda (she/her) has today 20th March 2024 been selected as parliamentary candidate for Waveney Valley.



As an environmental scientist, Gurpreet is committed to working hard in the area of environmental science and conservation. She has worked at the Centre for Environment Fisheries and Aquaculture Science (Cefas) lab in Lowestoft and is working in government, and completed her PhD in Environmental Sciences at the University of East Anglia. Gurpreet is founder of Black Ocean Citizens, a non-profit aimed at connecting diverse and underrepresented communities to water-based and ocean sciences. As well as working in Norwich, she also serves Lakenham ward as Norwich City Councillor and is involved in decisions concerning the provision of affordable housing, tackling crime, equality & diversity, climate change and creating opportunities for local training and employment.



With ties across Waveney Valley, Norfolk and Suffolk, Gurpreet lives in Norwich with her husband, two children and Luna the dog. Daughter of first generation immigrants, Gurpreet understands the value of hard work and being part of a community. She enjoys listening to music, spending time with her family and friends outdoors and on the river, fishing.



Gurpreet says "I am aware of challenges facing the Waveney Valley community including poor services as a result of dwindling public finance and not having enough low carbon affordable homes to support growing local families. With Labour marked as the succeeding party, no other candidate can and will ensure local voices are heard in Parliament."



"I am excited to be representing Waveney Valley. With Labour in government, I want to be a strong advocate for local people in Westminster. Issues that are important to me are:



Cleaner -- As part of Labour's Clean Energy goals, hold water companies to account to ensure Good Environmental Status is achieved regarding the health of River Waveney

Greener -- With Labour's Green Prosperity and Great British Energy plans, mandate for low carbon affordable new homes to support local jobs and services



Fairer -- As part of Labour's modern childcare system, support local families with child care to enable families to stay local with better paid, good quality jobs, and low carbon affordable new homes."

Sean is a local writer and communications specialist who has lived in Norwich for almost a decade. Based in Bowthorpe since coming to Norwich to attend the UEA, he has been a proud and active member of our fine city’s community from the very start. He is thrilled to be standing to represent the people of South Norwich as their MP and looks forward to speaking to many of them over the course of the campaign.

Denise has represented Nelson ward for the past eight years. She wants to continue to represent local residents and stand up for her community. Denise has successfully campaigned for a 20mph speed limit on a number of Nelson streets and plans to continue this campaign until the whole ward has a 20mph limit. Denise has also fought for the right of residents to maintain grass tennis courts at Heigham Park and for a community group to look after the courts. She believes that the city council should use the money it plans to spend installing more modern tennis courts should be spent, instead, on maintaining children's playgrounds in other parts of the city.

Denise has been a staunch supporter of local shops at Earlham House, dealing with a number of issues to do with the building and its environs over the years. She is hoping that recent government legislation can be used to make the company that has been handing out harsh fines to shoppers act more responsibly.

On a city-wide level, Denise is keen to see Norwich take its fair share of action in the battle against climate change, consistent with the Paris Agreement. She has proposed motions to the city council to create a strategy to adapt to the effects climate change and to declare a climate emergency. Her work in this area has been very important. There is still much to be done to persuade the Labour administration of the importance of these issues.

Denise's background in planning and transport has been useful in her life as a city councillor. She has served on the council's Scrutiny and Planning committees, as well as committees dealing with transport and planning issues, Norwich Highways Agency Committee and the Sustainable Development Panel. She is currently the Leader of the Green Group, and the Leader of the Opposition on the city council.

Denise has lived in Nelson ward for 35 years, along with her husband and their cats.

Having lived and grown up in Sewell Ward- I know what it is like to be a child, young person, and adult in this area and I know first hand what needs to be done for our community to thrive. I’d like to focus on loneliness and isolation, litter, flytipping and keeping our area safe and clean for everyone to enjoy.

Dear Resident,
I've lived in Norwich for over forty years where I have worked in the print trade, served as a police officer and now in the NHS. My children have grown up here and I consider Norwich to be a fine city but, it could be so much better. Years of mismanagement under Labour and Conservatives have left us millions of pounds in debt due to complacency and poor decision making. We in Reform UK believe the tax paying residents should be central to any spending plans. Value for money, accountability and transparency in local government must be central to everything we do. delivering better value for money and stimulating the local economy will be my focus. 
We all know Britain is broken and needs reforming. Vote Reform Uk on May 7th and together let's start that process. Thank you

If the voters of Thorpe Hamlet place their confidence in me, I will:

1. Fight for adequate social housing and scrutinise developments to make sure they benefit the whole community, not just a handful of landlords.

2. Demand that the rights of the river and the people and wildlife it supports be upheld, holding polluters to account.

3. Ensure that green spaces are clean and parks and playgrounds are fit for purpose.

4. Push for safer streets.

I retired recently from working as a laboratory technician at the Quadram Institute Bioscience. This has given me the free time to become more involved in community concerns. I have lived at my present address, in the ward, for over 25 years and have formerly been a City Councillor.

Traffic congestion and parking problems are a big concern for me. I think much more use could be made of the Park and Ride service so that it becomes commonplace to get a bus into the city.

There also needs to be a way to mitigate the impact of student houses in Nelson, as overflowing letter boxes and bins left in the street are upsetting for long term residents.

It annoys me when contractors dig a hole in the pavement, put barriers round it, then nothing gets done for days or weeks to finish the job, as has happened many times locally. Such disruption must be minimised.

I have represented Town Close Ward since 2019 and am proud to work closely with Green and Independent colleagues. Norwich is a fantastic place to be - we're big enough to enjoy city life, but small enough that you can know your neighbourhood. My guiding principles are climate justice and social justice and a firm belief that community, as well as government, should help take care of us all. When the basics are covered, people have time and space to enjoy life, and there's no good reason why that's not possible!

statement_to_voters:
**About me**
Hi! I live in Wensum, never done politics before so I'm stepping up to try and make a difference. I have a keen interest in politics and I've always paid attention to environmental issues. I've leafleted Wensum Ward for the Green Party, chatted to residents about their concerns, and I was impressed with Zack Polanski’s politics so I joined the Green Party in 2025.

I came to Norwich in 1998 and have lived in Wensum Ward for 5 years. Now I have a family I’m far more aware of how essential local community is to all our lives. I’ve been widely involved in community projects over the years, from theatre to anti-fascist activism, and have recently become a volunteer at the Wensum Community Centre.

**What I can bring?**
I am a good organiser with experience coordinating groups of volunteers. For 10 years I worked in Film & TV production, I've also worked in museum and educational settings, utilising my arts and acting experience to engage students.

My priorities as a city councillor for Wensum would be:

- Housing: I'm passionate about engaging with local residents to learn their needs and housing is often a top priority. 
- Green spaces: keeping parks tidy and well maintained, but also the smaller spaces that we see and use every day - footpaths, hedges, grass verges. Fly tipping is a constant issue round here and much more needs to be done to deter the culprits. 
- Wellbeing: I think talking to people who live near you is the best cure for nasty, divisive right wing politics. I want to support and develop resources like our community centres, where residents can come together to feel happy and safer.

I have ADHD; it's not a superpower, most days it makes my life difficult, but I'm an effective problem solver when I lock on to something (please bring snacks!)

**Why vote for me?**
I'm interested in what people care about and why. I'm ready to listen but I will speak up if I disagree and explain why. I think we owe it to one another to be honest - with others and with ourselves - which doesn't seem to be a very popular way of seeing things in many areas of politics but that's their problem, not mine!

I'm not interested in political jostling or rivalries, inside of or between any political parties. I don't have all the answers, no one does, but I'm stepping up to this ready to work.

I think there is no difference between the environmental crises we face and the problem of growing wealth disparity and inequality - money is power and without power we can't change things. We need better democracy, we need to ignore the mudslinging, challenge the lies and bring people hope that real change can happen.

Having gone from studying Law at the University of East Anglia to training at a Norwich City firm and rising to partner level, before founding Gordon Dean Solicitors, my personal and professional life has been consistently intertwined with Norwich.

With an office on Princes Street and a home near the city centre I have enormous pride, in my family, my staff and my business, comparison to which, gives some humility.

I have previously been a County Councillor and am on board of Norfolk Community Law Service (NCLS), which provides free advice on employment, family, debt, housing and discrimination law.

Passionately opposed to Brexit and Homelessness.

Ben has lived in Norwich since moving to the city in 2001. A gardener by profession and father of two children, he has been a Norwich city councillor since 2012 and a Norfolk county councillor since 2021.

Ben is standing for both the county and city seats in Wensum because he wants to help bring real positive change to local residents, and feels that both the Labour and Conservative administrations have simply failed to deliver.

Ben has a good understanding of the issues that matter to the people of Norwich. He has worked alongside residents to solve local problems, while trying to effect positive change across the city.

Ben acutely understands the importance of biodiversity and the impacts climate change is having on the natural and human worlds

He brings extensive experience in governance having served on the county council’s Strategic and Corporate Select Committee, and chaired the city council’s Audit Committee with distinction.

As the Green Group’s lead on finance at County Hall, Ben has consistently proposed budget amendments that prioritise the community’s future—reallocating funds from the costly road building schemes, toward better buses, safer cycling, and walking infrastructure.

Hello and welcome to my Reform UK page and the local issues my General Election campaign will focus on. 

Plymouth Independence Day

Vote Reform UK on the 4th July so Sutton and Devonport get an MP who is independent of the Labour Party, the Labour Council and the Conservative Police and Crime Commissioner.

Someone who will hold them to account and get things done. No more excuses, just action.

1. Safer streets for everyone.

2. Stop polluting our sea and rivers. 

3. A centrally funded toll-free Tamar.

4. Military pay and housing they deserve.

5. Transform empty offices into affordable homes.

6. Uncover the facts about the Armada Way budget. 

Why vote for me?

To help answer that I’d like to ask you to imagine you telling your friends and family that you're going to stand in the General Election to become an MP. 

If you did tell them, I'm sure you'd get a similar response to what I did (although there were other responses!).

"Wow, that's great, we need more “normal” people like you as an MP".

It's funny though isn’t it, how Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak are both working so hard to reclaim their working-class roots, toning down their parent's work and showing the public how "normal" they are.  

I can't tone down my first job at the council as an apprentice vehicle mechanic fixing anything from lawnmowers to gritters. I can't even claim I was any good at it either which is why I was planning to get into sales as soon as I'd qualified. My Dad was in sales and he played golf every Friday so it looked like an easy option. But my Mum was a crazy artist and she encouraged me to go off travelling to "see the world". So I did. And survived. But there were some times when survival was looking a little less likely (I can bore you with my survival stories in the pub sometime.)

But I've done OK for a normal person. I did eventually get into sales, then fell into recruitment, then got wowed by the Internet in 1998, built a software business, sold it, lost it, started again with nothing, and managed to survive as a self-appointed Internet Recruitment Guru (I'd be known as an Influencer today!). 

In between all of my jobs, I did what Mum said and travelled. Australia, South America, North America, North Africa and more. I also somehow managed to find myself a wife and she even convinced me to settle down and have kids. But though my travel had been curtailed, I still managed to fit in numerous crazy ultra marathons in great places such as the Sahara desert, Amazon jungle, and the Yukon. 

But it's not all about me 

My wife and two daughters have all worked in the care sector; a community physio, a nurse and a Navy medic (although our daughters have picked up the wanderlust now). Having seen them all do work that has a real purpose (unlike selling software), and working throughout the pandemic, when we moved to Sparkwell in 2021 I decided to start working as a volunteer at the Plymouth Soup Run. To do something with purpose, to have a positive impact on those less fortunate.

Why homelessness? 

It all stems back to a travelling incident in Cusco, Peru in 1994 where I fed some homeless kids for a few days. It's another story for the pub but that experience left me regretting not being able to do more and since then I've always stopped and talked to street homeless people no matter where I am. 

Plymouth Soup Run

Life on the streets of Plymouth has got progressively worse since COVID and we have massively increased the number of meals we serve on a Sunday night to over 125. As the numbers increase it becomes far more tense for both volunteers and clients, and the streets feel less safe, so it’s vital that the police can provide a rapid response when (rarely) needed.

Do more

My first-hand experience on the streets of Plymouth made me realise to be able to do more, I had to do more. So I joined Labour in 2022 hoping I could do more, but that was not to be. So after almost 2 years with Labour, I resigned, thwarted at every step by party politics. Not the party or the people for me. All too angry with the Tories and no focus on the important issues. 

But I’m not someone who gives up easily or makes excuses so I researched Reform UK and realised they have policies I support. Common sense ideas that will make a difference. Not more wishy-washy flip-flop Labour twaddle or delusional Conservative cons. 

Which is why I am standing for Reform UK in Plymouth Sutton and Devonport.

Let’s be honest though; we've all lost trust in politicians who spend more time on political point-scoring and less time on real work. We need business people to fix the country, to hold the councils and the police to account, and to make sure our essential services such as water and housing are at a high standard to ensure the health and well-being of the community. This is why if I am elected I’ll be making LOCAL issues my priority, working with people, regardless of party, to get things done. No lame excuses, just hard work and focus.

Emma is a long-time Green Party member with a strong passion for social justice, which she knows is tied to the climate crisis and economic justice.

Kristine works in the beauty industry in North End and is soon to become the mother of her first child.

I’ve spent years working in education, supporting local arts, and campaigning at the grassroots level, standing up for the things that make our community thrive.

I’ve fought to save local buildings and green spaces, and campaigned against destructive developments, both locally and nationally, that threaten our environment and identity. Milton deserves a representative who listens, takes action, and delivers practical solutions, protecting our green spaces, supporting local services, the arts, and building a better future for everyone.

Steve served in the Royal Navy for over 20 years and now works for SERCO in the dockyard commissioning new tug boats.

**Steve Andrews lives here and has a record of local service and action**

"I am seeking election to Portsmouth City Council as I believe the Green Party offers a new approach to local government, which many people will welcome. Sustainability is an increasingly important factor in decisions made by local and national government, but is continually side-stepped in favour of short-term financial issues, putting problems off for a few years. We must take sustainability into account when we make decisions now, for example requiring all large developments and all public buildings to generate at least 10% of their own energy on site and constructing all seafront properties to withstand current and future levels of flooding.
Portsmouth is an island naturally suited for cycling, yet it is one of the most dangerous places in the country to do so. We have one of the worst rates of childhood obesity, areas of the city that continually fail air quality standards, and terrible traffic and parking problems. Making the City safer and more attractive for cyclists represents an instant win on all these fronts, yet the council continues to pay no more than lip service to the idea.

We are seeing the last of the Island's green spaces increasingly sought by developers to build houses, while we have far too many empty properties and underutilized brownfield sites. We have to stop building dormitory developments for people who commute to jobs elsewhere, and start developing more affordable properties for small businesses and start-ups, with particular support for co-operatives and social enterprises. Our local shopping areas are dying, with shops closing and new businesses unable to find the money for high rents and business rates.

Labour, the LibDems and the Conservatives are all committed to increasing the privatization of public services in the name of "leaner" government. As a Green, I believe in investment in real jobs, supporting local businesses instead of minimum wage-paying chains based in tax havens. I believe in local accountability for schools, not academies set up by anyone who has the money to establish a curriculum that suits their own agenda. I believe in public management of essential services not driven by corporate greed.

The City Council must support the arts and tourism, and capitalize on our current economic strengths. The arts and tourism are important to Portsmouth and should be encouraged, not cut.

I have been out and about on Green clean ups in the Central Southsea area where there is a significant problem with litter. I will work to take action against the landlords that allow their properties to become litter problems for their neighbours. I am currently talking to the University to discourage students bringing extra cars to the City and also pushing for a joined up citywide strategy for parking.

Michelle and her family live in the heart of Paulsgrove. Her kids go to local schools.

She works at the hospital and cares about the NHS.

Michelle stood in the Paulsgrove by-election late last year and nearly tripled the Lib Dem vote.

Alvie is committed to ensuring Portsmouth is a city that everyone feels comfortable and proud to call their home. Born and brought up in Portsmouth, he has witnessed how local government decisions affect the city he loves.

Alvie has campaigned with local groups involved with increasing community cohesion, rejecting racism and identity-based hatred, and advocating for local and international human rights issues – such as in Palestine – to be recognised and resolved.

Since graduating from the University of Portsmouth, he has worked as a data engineer on environmental monitoring sensors, enabling companies and local authorities to make more informed decisions – and prevent pollution, flooding, and expensive maintenance.

As your councillor, he would be a passionate and reliable voice for St Jude’s, making sure that resident concerns are duly represented and considered in council, and that Portsmouth is a welcoming and tolerant city for all.

People across our area know that Denise Perry, Councillor Hugh Mason and the local Lib Dem team get things done.

Committed. Generous. Energetic. That’s what Portsmouth Green Party members said when we asked them to describe our candidate for St Thomas Ward, Jay Mercer.

Dear Resident,
I’m Paul Smith, your truly independent candidate for the vacant Councillor position in Llandrindod South Ward.
I’m standing because I believe residents deserve a councillor who will work solely in their best interests, free from party politics and without having to follow any party line.
I have lived in Llandrindod Wells for 15 years and am a father of three. My two youngest children attend local schools, and I am an active volunteer in our community, giving around 20 hours each month to support my son’s school as a parent governor, PTA volunteer, and reading supporter.
For the past two years, I have served as a Town Councillor, always on a completely voluntary basis, claiming no allowances or expenses. During this time, I helped instigate the Station Crescent toilet refurbishment and new Changing Places facility, supporting disabled residents to remain independent.
Professionally, I am a former Director of Adult Social Care for Herefordshire Council and currently run a successful business from my home on a full-time, flexible basis. My experience across both public service and business gives me a strong understanding of finance, governance, scrutiny, and customer service.
I believe Powys County Council can do better, and I am standing because I want to bring stronger accountability, better decision-making, and better outcomes for local residents.
While I don’t typically use social media, I have created a dedicated Facebook page for this election to make it easier for residents to contact me, discuss local issues, and access my research.
For further information on what I believe is important for our area, please refer to my campaign leaflet below.  Further information is also available on my Facebook page.
I would be delighted to hear from you.
Paul Smith
Your truly independent candidate

Rachel is standing as the Green Party candidate in the Ashton ward this May.

Rachel has lived in Ashton for over 20 years and is proud to call it home. Rachel cares deeply about local green spaces, clean streets, and ensuring Ashton remains a great place to live for everyone.

She is standing to help build a fairer, greener Preston, one where local voices are heard and real improvements are made to the issues that matter day to day.

If elected, Rachel will work hard, listen to residents, and stand up for Ashton.

Robin is a 50-year-old father of one. He grew up in Leicestershire and moved to Preston at 19 to attend UCLAN, and has now spent the majority of his life in or near the city.

Jonathan Grisdale, known as Jono (as named by his mum), is 57 and works in the NHS. An electrician by trade, he is currently seconded into Trade Union Partnership Officer roles.

Tina is a lifelong resident of Preston and has been a Broadgate local for the past five years.

Tina is ready to be a fresh, local voice within the City Council, working to protect our environment and build a sustainable Preston for all.

Dr Kevin Rigotti has lived in Deepdale since 2014. He originally came to Lancashire for a role reviewing aircraft safety evidence and decided to stay in Preston to pursue a research degree at the University of Lancashire.

A member of the Preston Green Party since 2018, Kevin has supported successful campaigns in North Herefordshire, Worcestershire, Cheshire, and Manchester.

Chris was born and raised in Preston and has lived in the city for most of his life. He recently graduated from UCLan with an MSc in Psychology, where he also served as vice-chair of the Neurodivergent Society.

In his spare time, Chris enjoys spending time with his dogs, Annie and Rusty, as well as playing chess, watching documentaries and sports, listening to music, gaming, and video editing.

Helen is a long-time member of the Green Party and has been standing in local elections for around 15 years. She has also served as a nominating officer and elections agent for over a decade.

Helen is passionate about protecting local green spaces and ensuring that local voices are heard and properly represented.

Jacob has spent most of his life in Preston and has enjoyed volunteering and working with the Lancashire Wildlife Trust. He is currently finishing his PhD in Chemistry at the University of Southampton.

Toby is relatively new to Preston, having moved to the city nearly two years ago. He has quickly grown to love it, describing it as a place that’s small enough to foster strong communities, yet large enough to offer plenty to do.

Keith is standing in the hope of promoting kinder and more supportive policies. He believes society should help those who are struggling, and that we all have a role to play in offering support.

He began his career as an engineer for Leyland Trucks, later retraining as a maths teacher, and spent the last 20 years of his paid working life supporting families with preschool children. Keith has lived in Preston and Leyland since 1984 and has been a resident of the Lea and Larches ward since 2014.

Since retiring, he has volunteered by giving talks in schools on kindness to animals and personal safety, and he currently facilitates a mental health support group in Preston.

My family has lived in Plungington for more than 50 years, and I’m proud to call
it home.

Councillors connect communities to the council and its services. That’s why I put all my effort into monthly meetings with residents at Eldon Primary, Plungington Community Centre and Noorani Masjid, as well as ward walkabouts with fellow Labour councillors, council staff, and police.

Pav

TUSC is a group of workers, trade unionists, young people, older people, students, ethnic and religious minorities, etc. I am one of many young students with working class parents just trying to get by, that is standing and campaigning for TUSC, because we're fighting for protections to the NHS, fighting against cuts to vital areas of funding that other brilliant and hard working workers need such as the winter fuel allowance, disability protections and school funding. Gabie is Preston’s candidate for Plungington in the 2026 Local Elections. She works in retail at a petrol station and is also a student. Gabie holds a bachelor’s degree in Media and Communication combined with Religious Studies and is currently pursuing a master’s degree in Writing.

Karen grew up in Longridge and returned there six years ago. She is a co-chair of the Longridge Environment Group, a student of sustainability, and a parent.

Concerned about the future, Karen highlights the interconnected crises of climate, nature, and inequality, which are already having real and profound effects on people’s lives.

She is committed to working locally to do whatever she can to build a brighter, fairer future where people and the planet can thrive together.

My name is Danny, and I’m proud to be standing as your Green Party candidate for the Preston Rural North ward this May. Offering a positive alternative to the usual politics.

I’m standing because I believe we can do better: protecting our local environment, improving services, supporting local businesses, and ensuring residents’ voices are properly heard in decision-making.

I’m particularly passionate about protecting our local green spaces and making sure new developments are carefully planned, with the infrastructure needed to support them. Rural areas like ours should not be overlooked when it comes to investment and services.

Thank you for taking the time to read this. I hope to earn your support.

Dan moved to Preston in 2022 from Worcestershire. He is severely sight impaired and has been involved in campaigning for disability equality throughout his life.

He has been an activist within the Green Party since 2014, as well as a trade union steward for most of the time since 2012. While not originally from Preston, Dan has grown to love the area he lives in and the wider city.

He is committed to making life better in any way he can – from challenging local issues to taking practical steps such as litter picking and ensuring problems that need reporting are addressed.

Amy was born and raised in Preston and has lived in the Sharoe Green ward for the past 14 years with her partner and son, who attends a local high school.

A long time employee of the NHS, Amy worked for many years at the Royal Preston Hospital before specialising in mental health.

Amy cares deeply about her community, and helping people is at the heart of everything she does.

I’m proud to be standing as your Labour candidate in St Matthew’s on 7 May.

St Matthew’s is a community I care about deeply. My grandparents settled on Skeffington Rd when they came to the UK 60 years ago. My family live off Ribbleton Lane, and my child attends Quwwatul Islam on Peel Hall St. 
 
In my day job, as an NHS nurse, I see the pressure people are facing every day and how public services improve people’s lives. I’m active in the community, volunteering and advocating for women and disabled people. I’m also proud to support a  faith-based charity that helps people in Preston.

**Supporting people in St Matthew’s**
- Preston Labour has been delivering real support for our residents:

Elect me to continue working on these issues and ensure residents are heard at the Town Hall. I won’t let you down.

Takhsin

Gareth was born and raised in Preston, with strong roots in St Matthew’s Ward, particularly the Ribbleton area. He attended St Matthew’s Primary School, and his mum still lives in his childhood home.

Gareth lives with his partner and their two beagles. In his spare time, he enjoys cooking, travelling, gaming, listening to true crime podcasts, and enjoying the emotional rollercoaster of supporting Preston North End.

Karen Rowland is an Abbey ward resident, passionate about achieving the best possible quality of life for everyone in Abbey. She is invigorated by our historic town-centre ward which is also at the epicentre of Reading's rapidly evolving future. However, Karen is determined that this progress does not come at the expense of the most vulnerable in our society, nor does it make Reading a town we cannot recognise in 10 years. She lays a large amount of blame directly at the feet of the current government for the sustained austerity that has negatively affected residents' public services and their quality of life.
Whilst completing her Masters degree in Historic Conservation, Karen has been a very engaged community activist, starting the Baker Street Area Neighbourhood Association(BSANA) in 2012 to resolve issues in her own area. Her natural eagerness to meet and engage with residents has helped to get to the roots of some very challenging issues and she has learned the right buttons to push in order to tackle them. She is a great believer in the power of communities to work with the Council in tackling issues; something that she hopes to encourage if elected. 
Additionally, Karen is a proud trustee of both the Reading Association for the Blind and the Reading Community Learning Centre. Both are organisations that work hard to maximise integration and opportunities for our large disabled and BAME communities. 
Karen is a pragmatist and prefers to keep her politics real, effective and focused. She knows that the Labour party's goals of a fairer life for all can be a reality. Moving to Reading as an EU immigrant in 2012, the way Brexit is managed in the years ahead is also of personal concern to her.  She is eager that residents contact her with their concerns.

Promoted by Chris Gavin on behalf of the Reading and District Labour Party, PO Box 8188, Reading, RG30 9LE

I was born right here in Reading Central, in the Royal Berkshire Hospital, and grew up in Spencers Wood.  Like you, I’m tired of feeling that Britain just doesn’t work any more.

After leaving to study Computer Science at university, I returned during the Covid-19 pandemic to train as a teacher at the University of Reading.  I now live here in central Reading, and proudly work for the local NHS in digital services, having previously worked as a civil servant and consultant.

I see first-hand, through my work in the NHS, the disastrous state the country is in - so I’m standing for Parliament to do something about it.  Fixing our NHS, our economy and our country won’t be easy, but with your help, we can get our town the fair deal we know it deserves.

I was born and raised in Battle Ward and have been part of this community for over 40 years.

With a background in corporate work and experience training professionals in mental health and social care, I bring both practical knowledge, lived experience and genuine compassion to issues that matter in Battle Ward.

I've volunteered locally for many years, including running support groups, working in suicide prevention and helping adults from diverse backgrounds build confidence in English and Maths.  My community activities currently include musical performances with a band, for local care homes, which brings me joy as much as the residents(I hope!)

Now retired, I'm standing for Reform UK to offer common  sense representation - respectfully listening to residents, supporting access to services and working to keep Battle Ward safe, inclusive and well served.

I live in Caversham where I was raised, my father having run a sub-Post Office here in the 1970s and 80s. I want Caversham to be a good place for us to live, with fewer flats being built for commuters and more support for local businesses. 
I am standing to offer voters a better alternative, and if elected my priorities include protecting our green spaces and increasing road quality and safety. Councillors are elected to work for you, and that is how it should be, not the other way around.
I am standing as a candidate for the Social Democratic Party (SDP) as I believe they have the best policies for fixing Britain, through stopping mass immigration, developing our agriculture and industry, and promoting community and family life.

Anthony Spencer is a resident of Caversham ward who moved to Reading in 2020. In his free time, Anthony focuses on keeping fit through various outdoor activities; he also has a keen interest in technology and the environment.

Anthony stands for ensuring residents of Caversham receive the services we should expect: walkable pedestrian paths and pavements that aren't submerged with every rainfall. He is also a strong believer in better bus routing to connect Caversham with all the rest of Reading.

I've lived in Mapledurham Ward for nearly 30 years and brought up my family here. It has meant so much to me to be able to serve the community as Ward Councillor for the last 15 years.

When I stood for re-election in 2016 I pledged to sort out the two big issues for our community: the dilapidated Pavilion and a permanent home within the Ward for The Heights School.

I am delighted therefore that I'm delivering on both these promises.

It is wonderful to receive so much positive feedback and to see so many of you out enjoying the revitalised Mapledurham Playing Fields.

Between now and the Elections, do carry on raising council-related matters and I'll do my best to help. To learn a about some of the work I've been doing, do have a look at my Blog: https://www.IsobelBallsdon.com

I hope you will lend me your vote on Thursday 6th May so that I can continue thereafter to work hard for our community.

Having lived locally for a decade, I’m standing as a councillor candidate to help shape a positive future. With a career in marketing, property and asset management, I will support residents, strengthen services, and back local businesses—ensuring our community continues to grow, prosper, and offer opportunities for everyone.

I'm standing to be a Councillor for Caversham Heights because I care about the local community and the people who make it.  I've listened to hundreds of voters around the ward and I'll stand up for the issues that matter.  My number one priority is road safety, addressing the problems of excessive speed and lack of lack of adequate crossing points.   I'll continue the work I've begun as a candidate by supporting residents to get their streets cleaned, drains unblocked, and potholes filled, as well as working hard on residents' individual problems.  I've always worked hard, and if elected, I'll work every day to maintain and protect the local environment and to ensure quality services for the people of Caversham Heights.

Jo is a LibDem activist and council candidate for Thames Ward, where she lives. statement_to_voters:
I have lived in Reading for many years, working in the computer industry, and want to help the town continue to be a great place to live and work whilst ensuring voters’ money is spent wisely.
Over my career of decades I have worked in a variety of different technical roles up and down ‘the Uk’s Silicon valley’ and have observed how things can ‘wander off-track’ if not properly supervised. I am semi-retired now and have enough time and energy to help prevent this from happening. The Thames ward is an attractive place to live in the town (especially where I live near the river) and I want to help keep it that way, as well as the rest of Reading.
The SDP is a sane alternative to the failures of the Conservative, Labour and Lib Dem parties, and the absurdities of Reform and the Greens. The party is culturally traditional and economically left-leaning - you really can have the best of left and right in one party!
If I were elected to the council, I see my objectives as being:
-	Ensuring the council concentrated on the necessary core work that makes everyday life in Reading possible (roads, neighbourhood services, social care etc) and avoiding spendthrift policies and vanity projects 
-	Scrutinising proposed new housing development projects to make sure they prioritise the needs of Reading people
-	Focussing on achieving maximum value for council taxpayers when buying in services and supplies from the private sector
So vote SDP, the party for people who love Reading - but don’t want to overpay for it!

I want to stand as a candidate because I believe local government should focus on delivering the basics properly and efficiently, and that is increasingly not what many residents in Thames Ward and the wider Reading area are experiencing.
Through both my professional experience and my day-to-day life locally, I see the impact of systems that are under pressure and not always delivering. Whether it is the rising cost of living, housing pressures, transport reliability, or access to services, people are feeling that things are becoming harder while getting less in return.

Working in a safety-critical, public-facing role within the rail industry, I deal with real-world problems every day, from disruption, vulnerable passengers, antisocial behaviour, and the need to make decisions quickly and responsibly. That experience has given me a clear understanding of how important it is for systems to work properly, because when they don’t, it directly affects people’s lives.

In my role as a Union Health and Safety Representative, I represent colleagues, raise concerns, and work constructively with management to improve safety and working conditions. This has reinforced the importance of accountability, transparency, and addressing issues early before they escalate.

My approach to local government is built on three principles: practical delivery, financial responsibility, and long-term thinking. I believe councils must move away from simply reacting to problems and instead take a more strategic, investment-led approach. One that generates sustainable income, reduces long-term costs, and reinvests directly into frontline services.

That means focusing not just on today’s pressures, but on building a council that is financially resilient and capable of delivering consistently for future generations.

Locally, that translates into clear, practical priorities:
• Fixing congestion and improving traffic flow at known problem junctions
• Delivering visible improvements in cleanliness, waste collection, and street maintenance
• Increasing transparency so residents can see what is being fixed, where, and when
• Taking a more preventative, long-term approach to housing and homelessness
• Investing in infrastructure and services that support working residents and key workers
• Improving community safety through visible enforcement and early intervention
• Protecting our local environment, including the River Thames and River Kennet, while improving air quality

I also believe the council should do more to generate its own income. Through investment in housing, energy, infrastructure, and the local economy, reducing long-term pressure on council tax while improving services.

I am not a career politician. I come from a working, professional background and understand the pressures facing ordinary people across the Ward and Reading. I want to bring a practical, common-sense approach to local government, one that is focused on delivery, accountability, and measurable outcomes.

Reform UK to me represents an opportunity to challenge the status quo and refocus local government on what matters most: the people it serves.

I am also a husband and father to two daughters who have struggled through education due to late identification and a lack of support for special educational needs. That experience has given me a personal understanding of the challenges many families face, and it strengthens my commitment to improving early intervention, support, and outcomes for children locally.

Dear Resident,

My name is Thomas Jose, and I am proud to stand as your Reform UK candidate for Bridge Ward. I first made Redbridge my home in 2004, and this community means a lot to me.

I am not a career politician. I have over 20 years of experience in business, education, healthcare, and the UK railway. I understand the real challenges facing local families, workers, and small businesses.

I am standing to bring honest, corruption-free leadership and a common-sense approach to local politics.

My priorities:

✔ Corruption-free leadership✔ Better local services✔ Support for local businesses and jobs✔ Safer neighbourhoods

I believe in working hard, listening to residents, and delivering real results.

Redbridge is my home, and I want to help build a stronger and safer Bridge Ward for everyone.

Vote Reform UK. Vote Thomas Jose.

Aside from this I am also a highly productive and highly skilled multimedia artist working in graphic design, photography, music and video. I like to see the bigger picture and I have a real passion for learning and gaining different creative skillsets.

I have lived in Bridge ward for the last 3 years, moving from the Midlands to work within the audio visual industry. Prior to this I had worked throughout the entirety of the UK’s National Testing Programme in the fight against Covid-19. It is here where I witnessed the complete incompetence of the Conservative Government and their inability to effectively and efficiently role out the appropriate measures to fight off the pandemic and support the public. It is also here where I witnessed how corrupt the whole testing programme was and how much of the taxpayers money was being well and truly wasted and sent to line the pockets of the Tory Government’s wealthy benefactors.

For most of my life I have worked on many different creative projects, primarily in music. Over recent years my artistic output has been heavily focused on covering more political themes such as capitalist exploitation, socio-political anxiety and general economic frustration. As an artist I have always strived to create work that critiques and questions the society we live in. I always wanted to make a difference to better the world and decided that getting more directly involved in politics might offer me the opportunity to help lead real change for the country and the community.

I had always thought politics wasn’t a place for people like me, a real working person, and was just a place for those of privilege. The Green Party gave me hope that we can fill Government positions with real people who can make real decisions and make real difference for the country. It felt like politics needed to change and I believe we can change this country for the better.

I want to see that the money in our councils is being used effectively and efficiently. I want to see our communities prosper through supporting the need for third spaces for people of all ages, races and genders. I want to see local economy prosper through supporting local independent businesses that choose to make Redbridge their home.

It is of high importance we work with local groups committed to protecting and improving our green spaces especially when we have one of the best green spaces in London right on our doorstep.

I’ve lived in Redbridge since 2020, raising four young children here. I see waste collection issues, streets that don’t feel safe, and tenants struggling for basic repairs and respect. I see a healthcare system that erects barriers rather than opening doors.

I’ve spent 25 years working in health services—most of that time helping low and middle-income countries bridge gaps in care. That work taught me that progress is slow, hard, and only possible when communities lead it through community clinics. The same is true here.

But change doesn’t come from one person. It comes from us—together. As a co-op governor, I worked alongside parents and staff to lift a local school from Requiring Improvement to Outstanding.

I’m not here to be the answer. I’m here to help us build it. That’s my promise to Redbridge.

What i Stand for:

I am standing for the Green Party because we refuse to accept how Redbridge is being run.

Too few council homes. Tenants’ rights forgotten. Fly-tipping everywhere, but enforcement is weak and uncreative. The recycling centre is difficult to access. Green spaces are disappearing, even as housing options for our communities shrink. And residents have no real say in how their own money is spent.

These aren’t small problems. They are signs of a leadership that has stopped listening.

I have raised these issues again and again—at meetings, in letters, with neighbours and councillors. I’ve spoken up and shown up. But time after time, I’ve watched them be ignored or brushed aside.

That frustration didn’t break me. It moved me.

I’m not standing because I want a title or a political career. I’m standing because I want a different way. A way where we listen, act, and build together—on housing that is genuinely affordable, on waste systems that actually work, on protecting our green spaces, and on putting budget decisions back where they belong: in the hands of residents.

No more empty promises. No more being brushed aside. Together, we can build a Redbridge that works for all of us.

Wanstead is a great place to live. I want to help protect what’s good about it while making practical improvements people will notice day to day.

Real hope. Real change. Right here in South Richmond.

Becca’s campaign foregrounds a fresh, hopeful approach in our politics. In practice that means improving the lives of residents through real investment in the NHS and social care systems on which so many of us rely. Likewise, we need to provide far more affordable and social housing, helping young people in particular to gain their independence. It is also vital that together with tackling further climate change, we counter the effects already with us such as the repeated flooding in the Borough.

She has always been actively involved in the community — as a Brownie Leader (Little Owl), a member of the Monton Green Primary School PTA, and as a School Governor for four years. These experiences have shaped her strong commitment to supporting children, families and local communities.

Representing the people of Eccles as your Labour Councillor over the past five years has been the privilege of my life. I'm proud to once again stand to represent the community I was raised in as your Labour candidate.

During this time, I have worked to deliver major regeneration for Eccles. I will continue to ensure residents' voices shape our plans as we develop a masterplan to transform our town, creating a vibrant centre, improving green spaces, and protecting our historic buildings.

We have already begun, with investment in the Town Hall and restoration of the Carnegie Library at the Gateway. I remain committed to making Eccles a better place for everyone.

I have also supported local community groups, especially those helping older residents, through fundraising and volunteering at events such as Eccles VIP activities and the Ellesmere Park Estate Supper Club.

My experience as an academic, trade union representative with GB and UCU, and trustee for local charities has strengthened my ability to stand up for local people.

Over the next four years, I will focus on a greener Eccles, safer communities, stronger local groups, tackling fly-tipping, and improving our roads.

I would be honoured to continue representing you and hope for your support.

I'm standing as someone outside the political bubble - a working dad of two young children who cares about the kind of place families actually have to live in day to day.

I’m not here to make big promises I can’t keep, and I’m not pretending this is a safe Conservative seat. But I do think residents deserve someone willing to listen properly and speak honestly about what’s going wrong; whether that’s anti-social behaviour, poor planning decisions, or feeling like local voices are ignored.
Labour has held this area for years, and Reform will offer protest. I’m offering something simpler: a fresh set of eyes, a willingness to challenge decisions that don’t make sense, and a focus on the everyday issues people deal with on their own streets.

Even where I can’t win, I can make sure your concerns are heard - and that’s worth doing properly.

“A vote for the Greens is a vote for hope”.

You might have heard this line before, you might not, but it is something I firmly believe in. The tide is changing as more people across the country become aware of the Greens’ simple and honest promise to put our communities first. I am standing on that promise.

I work to promote Greater Manchester as a great place to live, work, visit, and invest in. I see opportunity right across this borough, and especially in the pockets that have previously been neglected or forgotten. And I’ve seen places change for the better when people are encouraged to come together and unite.

I know the Greens might not be familiar to some residents of Higher Irlam and Peel Green, but we are here to listen and do the work. With Green Councillors on Salford City Council, we will champion our communities, be proactive, make climate-positive decisions, and push for greater opportunities. Higher Irlam and Peel Green deserves that.
