DELIVERING REAL RESULTS FOR OUR COMMUNITY

I’m Mishal Saeed, your local Councillor for Higher Irlam and Peel Green—and I’m standing for re-election because I believe local politics should be about one thing: getting things done for our community.

I’m proud to call Salford home. It’s where I’ve built my life, started my family, and committed over 15 years to public service—from grassroots volunteering to standing up for workers, families and local communities.

Over the past four years, I’ve focused on delivering real, visible results:

* A new children’s play area at Brookhouse
* Investment in community spaces and local groups
* Funding for schools, grassroots initiatives and local charities
* Action on flooding, antisocial behaviour and road safety
* Improving the quality of roads by resurfacing Brookhouse Avenue, Northfleet Road, Broadway and part of Liverpool Road
* Protecting our area from the A57 lane reduction scheme
* Supporting our allotments and voluntary groups
* Protecting and enhancing our green spaces

I don’t just talk about change—I work with residents to make it happen.

⸻

A LOCAL VOICE THAT LISTENS — AND ACTS

Politics can feel disconnected from everyday life. I do things differently.

Whether it’s holding organisations like United Utilities to account, working with GMP to tackle antisocial behaviour, or standing alongside care workers fighting unfair conditions—I make sure your voice is heard where it matters.

When residents raised concerns about the potential closure of Astley and Monica Court and about the impact of A57 lane reduction scheme, I listened and campaigned—and we won those campaigns together.

That’s what local representation should look like.

⸻

FOCUSED ON WHAT REALLY MATTERS

This election isn’t about national political noise or divisive headlines.

It’s about:

* The condition of your roads
* The safety of your streets
* Investment in our community
* Enhancing our green spaces, play areas and allotments
* Opportunities for our youth and children
* Supporting our community groups
* Improving our public services - social care and mental health

As a new mum, I understand first-hand the pressures families face—and how important it is to build a community that works for everyone.

⸻

SECURING INVESTMENT — AND PUTTING RESIDENTS FIRST

Peel Green is set to receive £20 million of investment through the Pride in Place programme.

I will make sure that:

* Residents shape how this money is spent
* Investment delivers real, lasting improvements
* Our community gets its fair share

Because investment should never be done to a community—it should be done with it.

⸻

MY COMMITMENT TO YOU

If re-elected, I will continue to:

* Fix the basics — better roads, cleaner streets, protected green spaces
* Support young people and families with safe, accessible community spaces
* Take a zero-tolerance approach to crime and fly-tipping
* Back local groups, volunteers and businesses
* Stay visible, accessible and proactive to help

⸻

WHY THIS ELECTION MATTERS

At a time when politics can feel increasingly negative or disconnected, I offer something different:

A proven track record.
A strong local voice.
A year-round commitment—not just at election time.
And a focus on getting things done.

⸻

RE-ELECT MISHAL SAEED ON MAY 7TH

Let’s keep moving our community forward—together.

As an Independent candidate for West Bromwich East it is my mission to improve the lives of the whole community with a caring leadership style. To date, I have worked closely with residents within a number of capacities and I am confident that I can be that voice to bring the concerns of West Bromwich East to Parliament in order to make a long lasting and effective change through strong leadership. 

Some of the issues that I would like to tackle:
Crime
I would like to support the agenda to reduce the level of crime within West Bromwich East by providing services to boost aspirations and opportunities.  
I also plan to introduce an effective anti-corruption task force.  This is to replace ineffective complaints processes in order to root out corruption within industries which exploit society's most vulnerable people.  This will make a fairer society for all people. 
I am aware of antisocial behaviour that occurs out of boredom.  I want to actually address THE WHY by creating practical solutions and opportunities for growth and development that young people can actually enjoy.   
As the MP for West Bromwich East, I will EFFECTIVELY UTILISE current community buildings and land to create functions catered to meet the needs of the community as a whole.  I will encourage a culture of community engagement which will lead to a more stabalised society where young people can access much needed guidance through safe, regular schemes and programmes.      
Programmes will focus of positive outcomes such as life skills and basic academic training for career development which will lead to young people utilising their time more efficiently.  This will encourage them to be motivated and proactive to become professionals and obtain economic stability to join the property market, deceasing demand for social housing, decreasing the current waiting list, so that the most vulnerable can be housed.   
This move will also impact on the various issues of lack of budgets for social funding within the public sector, as well as reducing current anti-social activity and money spent on the process to criminalise.     
Many issues and funding for our youth can be resolved from actions such as these and these are just the tip if the iceberg for the plans I will implement for change.


Education
I would like to see:
- More funding for education including funding for independent schools, sites for schools and safer zones for children.
- Inclusion and socialisation through engagement with breakfast clubs and after school clubs, reviewing the criteria to subsidised places for parents on low incomes. 
- A review of the current Pupil Premium scheme and how access is not proportionate to all parents and children that fit the criteria, while addressing more effective methods of distribution to parents so that they have more informed choices on supply of payment. 
- A reassessment of the council budgets allocated to each department and reviewing the percentage needed in relation to demand. 
-  Implement dedicated Safe Zones, in particular within modules/subjects of computing, to stop the current issue of unwarranted embedded sites from popping up, as the current structure of internet is not as effective.
- A restructuring of the current allocation of budgets for SEN and their agencies, as well as their codes of practice; as many parents are still complaining in 2017 about lack of support and access to the service.  As a result, many pupils within all levels of education from infants to post graduates are at a disadvantage as their learning needs are not being correctly identified.  Unfortunately, this results in not being able to receive necessary assessments to enable them to access much needed support within their level of education. 

Enterprise zones
I would like to create designated zones to inspire entrepreneurship and enterprise for the ordinary person.
Under my leadership I would bid for a review of current Business Rates – reviewing the current method used by the VOA (valuation office agency) which adjusts the rateable value of business properties to reflect changes in the property market, as this will impact on small businesses and startups significantly.  With your support I will ensure that all businesses are able to receive help to access the current business rates relief scheme if they are eligible. 

Jobs and opportunities
I would like to provide services to support those who are unemployed and help them to gain the passion, skills and confidence to get them back into work.

Leisure services
I would like to support the NHS and create a culture of health and fitness within the community.

Accommodation
I would like to support regional and national targets to see more people living in affordable and comfortable homes with fair energy bills. 
I will also review the current policies and processes that HomeOption uses to prioritise the existing list for social housing in order to reduce the waiting list.  
I would like derelict buildings and abandoned houses to be incorporated into a specialist scheme of occupancy. 
I will review the current system of taxation in relation to First Time Buyers and the existing subsidised deposit scheme. 
Reviewing the current policies and processes for repairs and maintained work would be another priority in terms of creating more effective social housing.

Retirees teaching the young
I would like to provide opportunities for retired individuals to engage more within the community and reduce the skills gap by passing on their skills to the young.

Community allotments and care for wildlife
I would like to see families and individuals benefit from the nature that is rich within WBE. 

Derelict sites
I would like to see that unused buildings and land are brought back into service to benefit the community.  (Also see notes on crime and accommodation)

Although I was born and raised in Bearwood the Tipton Green Ward has been my postcode for a while and needs serious support to get it back on track by removing politions who are too comfortable taking no action against challenges and experiences of this community.

With 3 weeks to go I’m elated to share I’m running as a candidate to become a councillor in the Tipton Green Ward and have been welcomed with open arms by all @sandwellgreenparty who are an ever growing community of likeminded people that are passionate about changing the lives of others in their wards.

A Tipton resident, to stand up for Tipton Town and work hard for my neighbours. You can choose three candidates this year, but, as the only Independent standing in this ward, you will always get the truth from me, with no party politics.  Whatever else you vote, make the INDEPENDENT one of your choices.

Who I Am

My name is Tom Lewandowski and I live here in Tipton Green.

I'm not a career politician — and I never planned to be one. But after years of seeing our area being neglected by those meant to look after it, I decided it was time to step up instead of just complaining.

Why I'm Standing

Simply put — I got fed up.

Fed up with streets not being cleaned properly.
Fed up with problems being ignored.
Fed up with a council that seems more focused on its image than on getting things fixed.

Everyone can see things aren't working as they should.

Tipton Green deserves a councillor who lives here, understands the problems first-hand, and isn't afraid to speak up when something isn't good enough.

That's exactly what I aim to do.

What I Do

I work in the private sector, where results matter.

If you don't deliver, you don't last — and I believe the same standard should apply to public services.

I believe in practical solutions, not political waffle.
In getting things done, not explaining why they can't be.
And in treating every pound of taxpayers' money with care and respect.

My Connection to Tipton Green

This isn't just an area on a map to me — it's my home.

It's where I walk my dog, do my shopping, and know the people around me.

When I knock on doors, I'm not visiting — I'm speaking to neighbours.

The problems people raise are the same ones I see every day.

And that's exactly why I want to represent Tipton Green — to make sure those issues are properly heard and properly dealt with.

I have lived or worked around the Blackheath area for decades, and my children grew up in this area. I have decades of experience in industry and the voluntary and public sectors, including a lot of community development work in Sandwell. I have been an educator for most of my career, and am currently a lecturer in public health at Birmingham City University. I have seen how local people have been let down by Sandwell Labour, and by right wing politicians. The local economy has been neglected, as have social conditions. The physical environment is also unhealthy - and only the Green Party is serious about putting the quality of life first. Vote for the Green Party, for a real, positive alternative.

I’m not standing for the title or for my career. I’m standing because I care. Our ward has never had an independent councillor before, and I would be proud to be the first.
I know many of you want change, and so do I. Some of you may be thinking, “Why should I vote for you when I don’t even know you?” That’s a fair point. I tried the political party route, but it became apparent that politics wasn’t accessible to people like me when it should be. Politics shouldn’t be about games or point‑scoring, it should be about people’s lives, especially ours.

As a South Asian disabled woman, I’ve always wanted to get into politics, but I’ve experienced many barriers. I know I’m not alone in that. These barriers aren’t about avoidance, they’re about a lack of accessibility. Part of the reason I’m standing is to improve representation, but also because I don’t want others to go through what I have. My motto has always been: “It doesn’t matter about me, what matters is that you don’t have to go through what I have.”

I’m not here to say I will fight XYZ. I’m here to say I’m by your side. If I’m elected, I may hold a title, but I want to use that title only to make our community and your life better.

I’m not your typical independent. Graves Park Ward – Community First Manifesto

Putting Residents Back at the Heart of Decisions

Graves Park Ward is one of the most valued and distinctive parts of Sheffield. From its green spaces to its strong community spirit, it deserves leadership that listens, protects, and delivers.
This campaign is built on a simple promise: local people come first.

1. Protecting Our Quality of Life
Residents deserve to feel proud of where they live. That means tackling the everyday issues that affect daily life:
* Safer streets – Working with police and local groups to reduce anti-social behaviour and improve community safety
* Cleaner neighbourhoods – Prioritising street cleaning, tackling fly-tipping, and improving waste services
* Smarter traffic solutions – Addressing congestion, speeding, and unsafe junctions with practical, locally informed measures
Our goal: A cleaner, safer, and more liveable Graves Park Ward for everyone.

2. Defending the Character of Our Area
Graves Park Ward is unique – and that must be protected.
* Opposing overdevelopment that erodes green space or local identity
* Ensuring planning decisions respect the history and character of our communities
* Protecting valued public spaces for future generations
Our commitment: No change without respect for what makes our area special.

3. Real Community Voice in Council Decisions
Too many residents feel decisions are made about them, not with them.
* Introducing genuine public consultation on major local decisions
* Giving residents a stronger voice in planning and development
* Ensuring local concerns are heard early—not ignored until it’s too late
Our promise: You will be listened to—and your views will matter.

4. Restoring Trust and Transparency
Trust in the council has been damaged by secrecy and unclear decision-making.
* Ending “behind closed doors” decisions wherever possible
* Publishing clear, accessible information on council plans and land use
* Holding decision-makers accountable to residents
Our pledge: Open, honest, and accountable local government.

5. Protecting Our Public Assets – Especially Graves Park
Our parks and public land belong to the community—not to private interests.
* Defending publicly owned land from inappropriate sale or privatisation
* Ensuring Graves Park is protected, properly maintained, and accessible to all
* Establishing clear safeguards on how public land can be used
Our position: Public land must stay public.

6. Resolving the Norton Nurseries Dispute
The ongoing situation at Norton Nurseries has caused deep concern and division.
* Calling for a fair, transparent resolution
* Ensuring all decisions are made in the public interest
* Bringing the community into the process to rebuild trust
Our aim: A solution that respects both the community and the long-term future of the site.

7. No to Asset Stripping – Yes to Investment
Residents are right to be concerned about the future of local assets.
* Opposing the sell-off of community land and facilities
* Pushing for proper investment in maintenance and improvement
* Ensuring long-term planning, not short-term financial decisions
Our belief: You don’t fix finances by selling off the future.

8. Investing in What Matters
Neglect costs more in the long run. We will:
* Fight for better funding for parks, roads, and public spaces
* Ensure maintenance is proactive—not reactive
* Support community-led initiatives that improve the area
Our focus: Sustainable investment that benefits everyone.

A Fresh Start for Graves Park Ward
This manifesto is about restoring balance:
* Between development and protection
* Between the council and the community
* Between short-term decisions and long-term wellbeing
Together, we can protect what matters and build a better future for Graves Park Ward.

Protecting our ward, restoring trust, and standing up for our community.

Both Labour and the Conservatives tell us they see the problems we face, but neither is truthful about the scale of them. Reform tells us they see the scale of our problems, but their solutions are based on targeting scapegoats while they sell off what little is left of the NHS and our country, all to line the pockets of their rich backers. Only the Greens are brave enough to name the scale of the problem, and honest about the kinds of solutions that will help everyone, not just a few. But we can build a future which begins to make an immediate difference to our cost of living, quality of life, and in the longer term prevents the crisis with our climate from getting worse.

This starts with us, at a local level, making changes that work for our communities, building a better world, right here, right now, in Sheffield. I’m Dermot Reid, standing for Reform UK in Blythe.

I live in Tidbury Green with my partner and young son, so like many of you, I care about the basics being right, safe communities, well-run services, and council tax being spent properly.

I spent nearly 14 years in the Royal Navy Submarine Service, working in a close-knit crew where there’s no room for passengers and nowhere to hide from responsibility. You learn quickly to make decisions, take ownership, and get things done properly. That’s a big part of why I’ve decided to stand.

In my day job, I manage large contracts and budgets across buildings and services. It’s about accountability, planning, and making sure things are delivered properly and not just talked about. That’s exactly the approach I’d bring to how the council runs services and spends your money.

Too often, decisions are made without real accountability and residents are left dealing with the consequences. You can see that in places like Blythe Valley, where many feel underrepresented or Tidbury Green where every blade of grass seems to have a planning proposal pending.

And importantly good leadership isn’t just about making decisions, it’s about being willing to review them and change course when they’re no longer working (cough cough, cycle lanes).

If elected, my focus will be simple:
* Clear accountability on spending

Hi, my name’s James Vessey-Miller, and I’m pleased to be standing for election to Southend City Council for the Green Party.

This isn’t my first time standing for the Greens. I’ve been a candidate in every election in Southend since 2018, and for nearly a decade I’ve also been attending council and community meetings, helping residents and local groups get answers on important local issues, and doing my bit as one of the city’s many active citizens.

Some people will know me from that local work. Others might know me from my background in business management, including managing hospitality venues and public events here in Southend. That’s given me a practical understanding of what local businesses need, and of how important our tourism, arts, music, and nightlife are to the life of our city.

I now work in Westminster for the Green Party, and I’m very open about that. I mention it because it’s given me valuable experience and a close view of how politics and public administration work in practice, including in places where Greens are already running councils and getting on with the job. But my roots, my record, and my reputation were built here in Southend long before that, and my focus remains firmly on this city and the people who live here.

My social media also gives a snapshot of that track record, and of the many issues I’ve worked on over the years for residents, local groups, and our wider community, including alongside the Green city councillors we already have here in Southend.

I’m genuinely impressed by the Green candidates we’ve got standing across Southend in these elections. We’ve got a strong group of thoughtful, hardworking people, and I’d be very pleased to see more of them elected. I’m not only asking for support for my own candidacy. I’m also working hard to help get our other Green candidates elected across the city too.

For me, local politics should be about making life better for people here, and looking after the place we all call home. That means decent local services, support for residents and our local economy, cleaner air and water, and protecting the things that make Southend special, from our communities and local businesses to our parks, beaches, wild spaces, culture, and nightlife.

I think it matters that we have councillors who are prepared to graft, who understand how the council works, and who take local people seriously. Having attended council meetings voluntarily for nearly a decade, I believe I’ve shown that I’m willing to turn up, ask difficult questions, listen carefully, and work constructively in the interests of residents.

I also think it matters that candidates have a serious local plan for what they want to do if they’re elected. Not every candidate in these elections can point to that. I can. The Green Party has a detailed local manifesto for Southend, and I’d encourage anyone interested to have a look on our website.

At the end of the day, these elections are about who you trust to help run the local services we all rely on. I’d simply ask people to consider not just what candidates say, but whether they have experience, whether they understand how the council works, and whether they’ve shown a real commitment to the community they want to represent.

You might not agree with me on everything, and that’s fair enough. But I hope people can see that I care deeply about Southend, that I’m open about what I believe, and that I’d work hard to represent residents honestly and conscientiously.

Thank you very much for reading. I’d be really grateful for your support in this election.

Milton ward, it would be an honor to stand up for you and to serve you. It is time for councils to remind themselves of their obligations towards the public; no decision should be made without a clear transparent legitimate public consultation, to us the people.

Having been a Southend resident for 17 years, I have long loved this city and hate to see the state it has fallen into. We desperately need change from the old parties which have repeatedly let us down! 

As a home educator, and someone who runs multiple community projects, such as the people's health alliance hub, I am very in touch with the residents' issues, concerns, wants and needs. Many of which I experience daily myself. 

My main priority is to stop southend from becoming a ‘15 minute city’.  These models that have been rolled out by other councils, in spite of residents voting against them, they take away our freedoms, in many different ways and levels and are completely ‘miss sold’ to the public.  And oppose the related issues linked to agenda 2030.  As well as:  Better management of residents housing issues including mold, for both private and council tenants.  Stop the spilling of sewage in the sea.  Transparency in spending on emergency services, and spending more money on training police officers, that will actually come to reported scenes, and making sure our police staff spend less time and money on monitoring twitter and political correctness and more time dealing with physical assaults and real crime.  Allow all local businesses to thrive, not only the high street but hamlet court road and all those in betweens should be able to benefit from any schemes that are introduced. Free use of the public library, particularly for the home education community, And the removal of inappropriate materials for children from it.  Stop rampant development, and stop over riding residents' opposition to do so, protect our historical sites and listed buildings.  Clean up our city, force landlords to provide walls, fencing and bins to the front of properties, to stop rubbish spilling onto the streets, via rats, seagulls, animals and unfortunately the homeless. Keep regular bin collections for retail and restaurants as well as residents, which should help cull the rodent issue that spreads across the entirety of the city including our parks and beaches.  The opening of a permanent community center in central southend, and a swimming pool nearer to this area.  Keep women's spaces.  Allow transparency and parental rights over children's school curriculum. 

Part of our local and national manifesto is to stop rampant development, especially when all residents oppose, for example the residents of royal terrace, who all voiced concerns about the building of the ‘Seven hotel’ on their doorstep. Not only does the modern building ruin the historical aesthetic of this conservation area, the residents are now left with the issues of parking, noise and smoke pollution.  Too many perfectly good structures, such as the victoria hotel which once stood opposite the metro bank in southend high street, have been replaced by ugly square concrete blocks, which the majority of the residents do not appreciate. 

There are too many empty lots and abandoned houses to warrant new developments, and the cutting down of trees and loss of green land to build blocks of unaffordable, small flats on.  The average family can not afford to buy or rent a family home, and struggle to afford and fit into these small modern flats.  I call for better management of council houses and the monitoring of private landlords to meet the basic needs of tenants, such as dealing with root issues of mold and damp problems.  On a national level the Heritage party has some great solutions to housing and related issues. 

We need to stop the spilling of sewage into the sea!  Our seafront should be one of the biggest sources of income for our city, in terms of tourism. How can we encourage people to come here, when newspapers are printing warnings not to, due to the health risks of the waters!  The large sum of money used to build the structure at the end of the pier has been severely underused, and again the public were not consulted on what they would like to see at the end. A missed opportunity for increased revenue, and a waste of funding that could have been used on countless other priorities and city issues. 

Equally our high street needs attention, there is no opportunities for local and independent businesses to thrive, and there needs to be regulations and schemes put in place to help and support everyone who is not a major corporate chain store.  I do not forget the many beautiful family run businesses in hamlet court road, in milton ward, which seems to be better than southend’s main high street in some regards.  Stop punishing residents for trying to earn an honest living from their businesses. 

In the cost of living crisis we are in, we could at least allow residents to visit parks for free.  So we therefore oppose the implementation of car parking charges or any charges to enter our parks including; Southchurch Park, Southchurch hall park, Priory Park and Chalkwell Park. Whilst I do NOT oppose any spending that improves the lives of children or the mental health and physical well being of the residents, one simple thing we can do to maintain these things, is simply not charge people to walk and play in our parks.  Many smaller parks such as christchurch park, and the skate and micro park opposite warrior square would benefit from public toilets and benches.  We also oppose the proposition to charge for the use of public toilets city wide. 

Southend has a thriving home education community, but many of us are outpriced from renting the rooms in the library which are upwards of £30 an hour.  Our central library runs as a business, and we deserve a free public service, especially for those wishing to use the space casually, and not for ticketed events. I have recently attended an event at Southend library, where my 10 year old was deliberately given a magazine which contained cartoons and photographs of sexually explicit acts, and my 6 year old similar.  Home educators should also not be penalized for their life choices, they are tax paying citizens as well, and should therefore not have to pay for their children to sit GCSE’s if they so wish to. So I am in support of keeping and improving all schemes that allow home educators or children not in schools for other reasons to have the opportunity to do so for free. 

To further help with the cost of living, and to help local businesses establish community connections, we suggest a resident discount card scheme, for our local attractions, seafront and shops. This should however not be solely digital. Individuals should not have to sacrifice privacy and allow others to make a profit from harvesting their data, and older generations that do not have smart devices, or anyone who ‘runs out of battery’ should not have to forgo the benefit of this. A non-digital version of this also saves money on app development. 

On a national level the Heritage Party fights to stop the eradication of cash, and on a local level we feel all businesses should uphold the legal rights of all residents to pay in cash. 

Whilst I am a part of so many micro communities in Southend, many residents feel there is a lack of community spirit, we once had.  With many well loved events being canceled such as the southend air show, we need new replacements. I have many ideas for merging micro communities and re-establishing this, without spending the amount of money the council has previously on events such as the luminosity festival. Which whilst ok, was still an affront to people struggling to pay their electric bills, and is also contradictory of the council members who are for the globalist net zero agenda. 

As previously stated, we have far too many community officers, and signposted staff to monitor twitter spats about political correctness, and wasted budget on printing flyers that promote southend police on social media, and a shortage of constables to attend to serious call outs.  From talking to Milton residents, I have found that I am not alone in my personal experiences, and the amount of ignored calls and police requests to attend the scenes of serious crimes like stabbings is ridiculous.  Many Milton ward residents feel the need to invest in personal CCTV, and to keep objects that could be intentionally used as weapons to hand in their homes.  We need police to reduce crime in our area, and allow us to feel safe, not egg on ‘cancel culture’.  Spending more money on CCTV cameras and vans is useless, if emergency services still can not respond at the time of events.  We need police to turn up and stop assaults from happening, not look back at it on video.  Residents report very specific general issues, such as open drug use by groups of individuals in the queensway underpasses at peak school run times. 4 years later the problems persists. 

We are aware of the homelessness issues in our city, and that other councils give their homeless residents one way train tickets to southend. I fully support the homeless charities in southend, and the good work that they do. However many of the solutions we have discussed to resolve this would not suffice, if the feeding of the problem continues by external councils.  And many of the issues that lead to homelessness are systemic national issues that sadly at this level we have little control or influence over, other than to support the good work of the homeless charities. 

The Heritage party received instant slander from the Echo, and other elected council members, attempting to label us ‘far right’ and ‘fascist’ from the offset. It is ludicrous to think that our elected council members do not even understand the actual meaning of such terms that they throw around in an attempt to discredit other parties.  And that an average concerned resident such as myself, with no political background, has the capability to write an entire essay explaining how this makes no sense, and is purely a projection of everything that the main parties are themselves in current times. 

I joined this local election with less than 5 weeks to go until voting day, and with no clue to the formalities of the system. Myself and fellow Heritage candidate in Kursaal ward, have been ‘canceled’, name called and oppressed, yet I know from the short amount of time I have had, talking to residents, that we stand for what the people are craving; Freedom, Family, Nation. 

Please stop being complacent about voting, and take back your voice and power.  Please stop voting for the same parties that have repeatedly let down you and this country.  They are not your only option! 

Milton and Kursaal ward, please VOTE HERITAGE!

In Southend, Labour made five fully funded local pledges at the last election - and delivered all five. That record shows that when we make commitments locally, we keep them.

As a constituency resident and Digital Infrastructure Engineer, I believe in careful planning, responsible finances and public services that work for everyone. I want Southend to continue investing in our communities, protecting essential services and planning for long-term prosperity - not returning to short-term cuts or divisive politics.

With major changes ahead, including new regional powers and local government reorganisation, St Luke’s needs strong, sensible representation focused on stability, fairness and real-world delivery.

My commitment is simple:
Work hard. Protect local services. Deliver for St Luke’s.

Let’s keep building a city we can be proud of.

I am your Reform UK candidate for St Luke's Ward in the local elections taking place on Thursday 7th May.

I have lived in the Ward for the last 5 years, and have lived in the Southend area my entire life.

I am brand new to politics and just want to see Southend become a safer, nicer place to live.

I have a young family and am really passionate about improving our local area and supporting my neighbours.

I will represent our area against the destruction of the nearby Green Belt land. There is no chance this project will include the required infrastructure improvements. I will also stand against the HMOs that seem to be creeping further and further from the town centre, commonly bringing anti-social behaviour with them.

The Labour administration of Southend City Council has dragged Southend down for too long, with wasteful projects like 'Better Queensway' and zero support for residents and local businesses. Their only priority seems to be increasing their income and cutting the services they should be providing.

I have been unfortunate enough to experience the incompetence of this Council too many times. Even having a dropped kerb installed is a year long saga costing thousands of pounds.

All we need from our local Council is for them to charge as little tax as possible, and at least provide the very basic services they should be providing. We can't allow them to continue failing on both counts.

Together I am confident we can improve Southend. I will work tirelessly to do all I can for you.

Southend is broken. Southend needs Reform.
If elected The Moon And Serpent Party will ignore the law and unilaterally open cannabis cafes around Southend.

As a Southend resident, I care for our community. I cannot stand back and watch our city degrade into a dystopian 15 minute/ Smart City.  I do not support south church park becoming the "biggest beer garden in essex", the park is first a formost and place of tranquility, peace and for families.  I do not support the use of digital ID to access park facilities. I stand with protecting our enviroment, protect wildlife, mature trees and stop the irresponsible desposal of sewage in our sea. I will improve maintence of our local area and keep regular rubbish collection. I support local independent businesses. I stand for freedom, family and the Nation

"The Lib Dem team are doing fantastic work bringing about real change for Leigh and its residents. I'm particularly impressed with all they are doing on the environment which is so important to protecting people's health and ensuring a future for the next generations.

"As a Councillor for West Leigh, I will aim to work hard to build on this change, ensuring residents' voices are heard and the issues which matter to them are given full consideration."

I am standing for re-election as an Independent. I live in Thorpe Ward and have served on Southend City Council as an Independent for 22 years. I am staunchly and proudly independent. My politics are in the sensible centre ground. I am not interested in polarised, extreme or trendy politics. Over the the years I have worked with Conservative, Lib-Dem and Labour colleagues to deliver the best outcomes for Thorpe Ward. Thorpe Ward is a fantastic place and I think the best area in the city. This did not occur by accident, it is due to the hard work and dedication of Independent Councillors who have represented Thorpe Ward for 20 years. My son and I both own our own homes in Thorpe Ward, these are often our most valuable assetts. It is therefore logical that is my shared aspiration with residents to protect Thorpe Ward and all its great assetts. The most hotly contested issue is the Green Belt. The Independents will not agree to any overdevelopment, or any large development without the appropriate infrastructure incl Roads, Health, Schools, and Drainage. It is not possible for any party to gain an overall majority in this election. Once again the Independents will have the leverage and influence to get things done for Thorpe residents. Independent is the most powerful vote you can cast.

Hi there, I'm so excited to introduce myself! My name is Jolene Hills and I'm a proud entrepreneur who has owned and operated multiple businesses in Southend. My mother is one of my biggest inspirations and she has shown me the business ropes having run many across Southend.  One of my recent ventures is the Cobham Hotel in Westcliff, which I acquired just before lockdown which, as you can imagine, was a difficult time.  However, we successfully got through it and I am proud to see the business thriving.

​

I have 2 children who I adore and who I want to grow up in a city that will give them the best chance of being happy and healthy.  As it happens, one of my daughters is studying politics so she will always be on hand if needed!  

​

As a born-and-bred Southend resident, I've always had a deep love for our city. However, I couldn't help but notice that there were areas for improvement. For example, I strongly believe that Southend Pier, one of the town's most iconic landmarks, needs more at the end of it.  Perhaps I am pointing out the obvious!

 

As a can-do person, I'm always eager to roll up my sleeves and tackle any challenge head-on.  I manage on the ground-floor, so I am used to dealing with all manner of people issues.  It is this experience I hope to bring to the residents of St Luke's.

​

I am thrilled to be getting more involved in my community to see what I can do to help. I believe that by working together, we can make Southend an even better place to live, work, and visit. ​

I am enormously excited to be the St Luke's Confelicity candidate and look forward to meeting residents throughout the year in my journey to become a Councillor at the next local elections.

Peter Walker is the Green Party Victoria Ward candidate.

A retired schoolteacher, Peter now spends much of his time as a Piano and Chess tutor, an avid cross-county cyclist, and as a member of the Southend Bach Choir.

Peter has long been involved in environmental conservation and the local Green Party, and he was also the Green candidate in Chalkwell in 2015, and for Blenheim in 2019.

Dear Resident

I am asking for your vote on May 7th to save the Westborough ward.

My name is Ben Aldridge and I am your Reform councillor candidate for Westborough.

As a former police officer with 15+ years’ service in community policing, Southend is broken. We cannot allow the current status quo to continue. 
I’m a father of two, employed locally and use to love Southend and be proud to live here. I want that feeling back and for my children to be proud of the place they grow up in. Not having to step over fly tipped rubbish on the walk to school. Not having to hope Dad avoids the pothole when we go out for a drive, as we cant afford to fix the car or buy a new tyre. Not having to hope the library is open as its Saturday and they don’t have the staff.

I am new to the political world and never felt I belonged but Reform aligned so strongly with my beliefs and the changing shift in UK politics I felt I had to do something. Not for me, but for the future generations.

The plans this city has to build on green belt land, which Reform will oppose and the amount of HMO’s I’ve seen just in this area, cannot continue. Our services are at breaking point and Southend is full.

Join me in the fight to bring hope back. Southend needs Reform.

Ben Aldridge
REFORM Councillor Candidate

I was born and raised in Southend on sea, where I grew up in Southchurch Village (Beautfort Street), with my mum, dad and 2 brothers. I went to school in Hamstel infant and Junior school and joined the King Edmund School.

statement_to_voters:
As a local resident, I see first-hand the everyday issues that go unnoticed and unresolved. It’s clear and come to my attention that some people have received little to no support when they’ve reached out to the council on certain issues. 
Residents have reported problems with roads, only for tickets to be closed without any action being taken. I’ve personally reported issues like fly-tipping and graffiti, and too often it feels like only selected jobs are actually completed.

No one in our community should feel forgotten or left to deal with things alone. I want to be someone you can rely on—someone you can simply say, “Ask Amy.” If I don’t have the answer, I will make sure I find it or connect you with someone who can help.

I want to be a strong voice for our ward and a true champion for our community.

As well as working to improve the area, I bring a solid background in supporting others—whether that’s help with employment issues, completing forms (such as Blue Badge applications), appealing parking fines, making complaints about goods and services, advising on pet care concerns, or supporting those affected by scams.

Together, we can make sure our community is heard, supported, and no longer overlooked.

Stephen Jordan is one of the Green Party candidates for Westborough.

Stephen is an HCPC-registered social worker and qualified as a social worker in 1988.

From November 2004 until March 2011 he worked full time as the Curriculum Leader for BA (Hons) Social Work at South Essex College. Stephen has worked as a lecturer for University of Essex since September 2014.

Stephen has been involved in the work of the local Green Party for nearly 20 years, holding several committee roles and first standing for election in 2006.

Over the years, Stephen has been the Green candidate in Milton (2006-2007), Victoria (2008-2010), St Luke's (2015), West Shoebury in 2016, and Westborough (2012 & 2019).

Like you I live in Westborough with my family, I know many of the issues which affect us locally and some of those you have raised with me and my campaign team. You want a clean, tidy, and safe local area to live in, so do I.

In Westborough you will have seen new pavements, extra street lighting and more trees. The Labour led administration is putting £10 Million each year into roads and pavements as part of the plan to make our city better.

We can only do that by providing value for money with the council tax you pay.  Our council tax is lower than Rochford and Castle Point which are run by the Conservatives.

We are increasing the pay of social care workers who provide care to the most vulnerable, giving them more security and ensuring we have staff to deliver these vital front-line services.

Building on the full-fibre rollout and our investment in the city's digital infrastructure, Southend is fast becoming a leading location for digital businesses, attracting more investment and highly skilled jobs and career opportunities to the city.

Achieving city status gives us the opportunity to take the next steps forward in building the city we want to become, and Westborough will be a part of that.

I hope you will consider supporting me to be our local councillor at this election.

- Councillor Kevin Robinson

Simon Gittus is the Green Party candidate for West Leigh.

Simon lives locally in Leigh-on-Sea and works as a designer, planning and shaping spaces in the retail and leisure sector. For the past year, he has been working closely with residents across West Leigh, alongside local Green councillors, taking up issues and pushing for solutions. He regularly attends Southend City Council meetings, holding decision-makers to account and raising concerns on behalf of the community.

Simon has been a clear voice on protecting our green belt, including Hadleigh Farmland and Bournes Green, improving bus services so they work for residents rather than private companies, and getting long-standing local issues sorted - finally getting the Marine Parade shelter fixed.

I am standing in West Shoebury because I believe local people deserve a councillor who will put residents first, speak plainly, and challenge poor decisions.

West Shoebury is a wonderful place to live, but too often local people feel ignored while overdevelopment, pressure on roads and services, and everyday issues like pavements, parking and cleanliness are not taken seriously enough.

If elected, I will work hard to be a strong local voice for West Shoebury — listening properly, asking difficult questions, and standing up for the people who live here rather than simply following a party line.

I believe local politics should be about common sense, honesty and accountability. That means supporting sensible development, protecting local character, improving the basics, and making sure residents are properly heard.

Ahmed has lived in Beacon & Bents for 25 years and since 2016 has worked in it too. He served as an Independent councillor for the ward from 2008 to 2012 and remains active in the community, using his experience to address local issues and help local people. Known for speaking directly on important matters, Ahmed is committed to representing local interests. His key goals include banning future HMOs, enforcing zero tolerance for anti-social behaviour, improving adult social care and children's services, ending excessive salaries, scrapping town centre parking charges, revitalising the town centre, promoting tourism, and increasing council spending with local businesses.

I encourage local people to get engaged and do their bit.

Printed (Hosted) by Democracy Club, Published and Promoted by Dr Phil Barron, Liberal Democrats, 3 Baldwin Avenue, East Boldon NE36 0EL

I am patriotic but that's because I love our people.
Because I love our people in all their diversity I want to serve them and improve the quality of life for all of us.

"It is an honour to have been selected to be the candidate for my home ward of Westoe, in the 2026 local elections. I was born and raised in Westoe, and it’s where my heart will always be. After studying to become a teaching assistant at South Tyneside College, I spent over a decade working in education, specialising in special needs. I understand the importance of strong, inclusive education, and I will always fight for better funding to ensure every child has the support they deserve. Recently I made a career change and now help people with their housing and neighbourhood needs, making a difference in their community every day.”

“As a younger candidate, I bring a fresh perspective and energy to the role of councillor. I’m committed to giving Westoe’s youth a real voice and creating opportunities for them to thrive. Westoe deserves more. For too long, some areas have been overlooked, with more affluent parts receiving priority for things like parks and barriers, while other communities have fallen behind. I believe in governing with care, putting people first, and ensuring all areas of Westoe receive equal attention and resources. Together, we can build a future where everyone has the chance to succeed”

I have lived in Borough my whole life and I grew up seeing suffering around me I find unacceptable like homelessness right next to skyscrapers that are held up as signs of progress or how it is now normal for secondary schools to collect food for food-banks. How have we let things fall this far? I have spent my whole life driven by a desire to improve the world and wish to leave it better than I found it. Having the honour of representing Borough & Bankside would allow me to pursue this goal of helping people and making hope normal again.

Hellen is a former journalist now working in digital marketing. Originally from Brazil, Hellen has lived in Borough and Bankside for a number of years. She has been the Vice Chair of Living Bankside since 2024 because she is passionate about our community. Hellen is passionate about improving community safety in Borough and Bankside.

Victor has lived in Borough since 2014 and has been your local councillor since 2018. Since 2022, he has been the Leader of the Opposition on Southwark Council working hard to get a better deal for residents across the borough. 
During his time as a councillor Victor has led the campaign to save the RV1 bus, fought for better air quality, has represented residents' concerns in the planning system, secured a permanent memorial to the Borough Market and London Bridge attacks.

He is chair and cofounder of Pride in Southwark and helped secure a new LGBTQ+ space at Bankside yards. He is a trained planner and has a professional background delivering affordable housing and new health facilities.

In the Town Hall, Victor has used his position to challenge Labour's poor record on affordable housing and tackling the climate emergency.

Contact Victor: victor.chamberlain@southwark.gov.uk

I have lived in Southwark for 35 years, and after a varied career in education, as a childminder and early years specialist, I now work as an Educational Officer for the London Wildlife Trust. Working with and for families I know how important it is that we ensure that all have the opportunities our great Borough can offer. We need to work hard to make Borough and Bankside a safe and accessible space for all who work and live in this historic ward.

Alastair has lived in London most of his life and over 3 years in Borough. Having finished a sales career and child care responsibilities; he qualified as an Adviser for Citizens Advice in 2012 managing welfare, debt, money and energy issues. He volunteers with Citizens Advice Southwark helping local residents with digital support. Alastair stands for social justice and a fairer, greener borough.

David first moved to the borough in 2006 and has worked locally in SE1 since 2015.

He believes passionately that we have an opportunity to re-shape Southwark for the better after the pandemic. That includes protecting and increasing space for parks and trees, building more affordable housing, and putting local residents at the heart of the Council’s decision-making.

David has worked in the public and charitable sectors on policy development, partnerships and negotiations. He is currently director of communications at a global affairs think tank and a trustee for a charity combating bullying in schools.

I've lived in Camberwell for nearly 10 years. I work as a teacher and promote Camberwell in my free time. I have been involved in many environmental campaigns, but I'm keen to make real changes to reflect the green transition that many of us want.

Priorities: Southwark Council's Repairs team is currently failing its suffering residents. This must be fixed as a start to then making Southwark look more like it's part of a world city in a wealthy, advanced country. We must use unoccupied buildings as homes. I'll be more transparent with council activity and support expanding our capacity to generate renewable energy, e.g. from food waste and on new council buildings.

Councillor Dora Dixon-Fyle has been a hard-working Camberwell Green councillor since 1998 and has advocated for thousands of residents. Dora moved to Southwark from Sierra Leone aged 3, attending local schools and then South Bank University. Dora received her MBE from Queen Elizabeth II in 2011 for her services to local government.

I moved to Camberwell when I was 3, from a flat off Walworth Road. I’ve seen local council services deteriorate here. Austerity hasn’t made anything more efficient, it’s just pushed financial burdens onto individuals and families. Diminishing the state's responsibility for necessary services. Taxes go up, and new fees are introduced, while the value and quality of services goes down.

For me, well-being is the number one priority. It’s what politics is about. That means:  
- working with residents on community projects, 
- championing independent local business, 
- fighting government cuts, and 
- reassessing council contracts with private entities to make sure they’re fiscally responsible and working for the public good.

I’ve worked across Southeast London, in hospitality, at libraries, and as a park gardener. I see how much community spaces, nightlife, and natural landscapes mean to people (I also know how many jobs you need to stay afloat these days).

As a councillor I will focus on protecting those spaces from funding cuts. Additionally, surveillance overreach is a priority for me, making reviewing any existing contracts with tech firms, and the rising appliance of facial recognition on our streets other focus issues.

James Moyse moved to Camberwell Green in 2014. He supports his neighbours with housing issues by being involved in his local residents’ association, and has previously worked as a journalist at the BBC and Sky News. James volunteers at 1st Southwark Scouts, giving local young people opportunities to learn and have adventures.

Jen Thornton is a campaigner who has worked with neighbours, charities, businesses and unions on local and national campaigns, winning for working people and communities. She has been a union rep, supporting colleagues with issues at work, a school governor, and is on the board of a national charity which makes digital tools to improve access to democracy.

South London born and bred, Councillor Sarah King is leader of Southwark Labour and has represented the people of Champion Hill since 2014. Sarah is passionate about tackling the housing crisis, making our communities safer and leading a council you can trust to get things right, having previously served as Labour’s housing lead for two years.

Michael Millar is a retired NHS hospital doctor, who has lived in Camberwell for 18 years. His support for the Green Party comes from a desire to ensure that the natural world that our children inherit is rich and diverse, and that the potential to live well is not constrained by environmental damage. Cycling is his main mode of transport and he strongly supports further development of the cycling network in London. He continues to support medical research in a variety of ways and has become increasingly concerned about the relationship between inequality and ill health. He favours those social, housing and educational policies which help children develop their full potential, and which reduce inequality of opportunity.

Environmental issues are a strong motivator for me: I work in climate and energy policy, supporting environmental NGOs with technical research and analysis on topics ranging from deforestation to the electric vehicle transition to corporate emissions reporting. But whatever the topic -- and lets face it, there are few non-nuanced topics left out there -- I hope to bring a balanced-but-reasoned approach to framing the discussion and finding solutions.

I've lived in London for much of my life (with prolonged stints in New York and New Delhi). I've never voted anything but Green, and have followed the steady efforts of our Green representatives in Westminster and in councils across the country. The recent surge of enthusiasm and ambition has been pretty astonishing. I mean, we all want to live in a vibrant, healthy, and humane society, and I see the Greens as offering unique clarity on the values that will guide them towards that goal, as well as openness to engage seriously with practical detail (love a bit of detail).

It's glib maybe but I've been so impressed by my fellow Green candidates who are prepared to stand for their values while also fighting for the interests of their communities and constituents. We are uniquely placed to offer an alternative-but-constructive voice on Southwark Council: on safer quieter streets, social and economic inequality, improved air, green space and wellbeing, school amenities, support for those walloped by the cost of living, on the responsiveness of the council infrastructure to issues raised by residents, etc. Check out the Southwark Green Party manifesto here https://www.southwarkgreenparty.org.uk/manifesto, and note there may be items you agree with or disagree with, but the important thing is to have to opportunity for an honest discussion.

A couple more things about me. I have a PhD in physics but numbers still scare me sometimes. I believe volunteering is a wonderful way to push one's comfort zone and cross unexpected paths. I think curiosity and open-mindedness are top virtues, as they enable a foundation of compassion and an impetus towards understanding. I love it when people make weird or playful art just because they want to, and even more when they they subject their friends and family to it. But above all, I would love to have more Green voices on Southwark council pushing the needle on all the important issues!

Originally from Germany, Irina has been a London resident and civil rights activist for 25 years. From 2019 to 2020, she represented Londoners as a Member of the European Parliament.

Irina lives locally here in Southwark and feels strongly about improving housing, air quality, and access to essential local services.

In her day job, Irina is a lawyer and business consultant specialising in social and environmental sustainability issues. Throughout her career, she has volunteered for multiple human rights charities including Refugees at Home and The Medical Foundation (now Freedom from Torture).

Bill Williams has over 30 years social work experience, working with London’s homeless for a major central London charity. He is passionate about resolving the housing and the climate crises. Bill is currently the Constituency Office Manager for Neil Coyle MP in Bermondsey & Old Southwark, and previously served as a councillor in Rotherhithe ward (2014-2022).

I have lived in Southwark for 15 years, attended university in South London and now work here too. I have a strong and long-standing connection to this borough and care deeply about the people who call it home.  I am a passionate Liberal who believes in equality, social justice and making sure everyone feels safe and supported.
I have volunteered with Crisis at Christmas, helping the homeless, and I have worked with former Councillor Poddy Clark on community engagement and casework, listening to residents, tackling local issues and standing up for those who need help.  I have recently joined the campaign to keep the public counter at Walworth Police Station open 24/7, because accessible policing and safer neighbourhoods are essential for all of us. This work has shown me how much stronger Southwark becomes when everyone has a voice.I am standing to fight for safer streets, better housing and a fairer society. I will be visible and represent our community with honesty and hard work.

Felix has lived in Elephant and Castle for over a decade. In his career, he has focused on global climate policy with WWF, decarbonisation with Boston Consulting Group, and community impact with HX Expeditions. He will bring his expertise in managing large budgets and teams to ensure that Southwark delivers.

Pascale is a mother, carer, and school librarian who has lived in social housing in Southwark for over 30 years. She has organised to defend local estates through campaigns including  Fill Empty Homes and Yes to Fair Redevelopment. She supports rent controls, decent repairs, SEN provision, disability rights, and full divestment from companies complicit in the genocide in Gaza.

Saidat Oketunde has spent over 20 years supporting women, young people and families. As Chair of the Southwark Muslim Forum, founder of Faiths Women Community UK and a school governor, she has built local partnerships and supported residents with skills training, food security, mental health support and community safety projects.

Robert Smeath has lived here for over 30 years. He is a solicitor who has volunteered as a housing lawyer and debt adviser with the Mary Ward Legal Centre which now runs Blackfriars Settlement. Robert is a former school governor and charity trustee, distributing grants to groups supporting elderly people across Southwark.

Councillor Joseph Vambe grew up on the Rockingham Estate in Chaucer, the ward he now represents. He is now the Labour lead on young people and community engagement, championing residents’ influence on local decision-making. Joseph was the first ‘Stormzy Scholar’, awarded a fully funded place at the University of Cambridge.

Suzanne has lived in Chaucer for nearly 4 years and London most of her adult life. She has worked in business as a lawyer and sustainability expert. She chairs a London environmental charity and sits on the board of a large Essex based social housing provider. Suzanne is an experienced leader who knows how to get things done in large complex organisations. She campaigns to save London's green spaces, for wealth taxes and a more equal society.

Everyday, I look forward to contributing to this ever inclusive, multinational city called London. I receive a great sense of satisfaction working alongside colleagues from other Countries within our treasured NHS where I work as a Nurse. I get a great sense of security and stability from living in the same area where I was born. I am concerned that future generations may not be so lucky. I will always fight for mixed, sustainable communities. These cultural exchanges has enhanced my life and adds immense value to our Nation. I am a Liberal because I believe in a fair, free and open society. I want to make London equal.  I want to make London Liberal.

Tori Griffiths has lived in Dulwich Hill for 5 years and she loves this neighbourhood. Backed by 15 years of working in the voluntary sector, Tori believes in the power of community-led change, and the value of every neighbour’s voice.

William Houngbo is a former councillor who left the Southwark Liberal Democrats to join Labour, citing the lack of community representation amongst the Lib Dems. He has worked on projects including safe spaces for domestic violence survivors and fundraising to protect the environment. William loves our diverse borough and enjoys cycling and running marathons.
Ed Hill-Smith, your Liberal Democrat candidate for Dulwich Village. I live in Dulwich, raising a family and a keen member of Dulwich Lawn Tennis Club.

Councillor Richard Leeming was elected in 2018, serving the needs of the variety of people who live in the ward. Richard’s family have lived in Dulwich since the 1980s. He’s a self-employed innovation consultant working on digital projects for public benefit. Richard is the Labour lead on sports and leisure.

Councillor Margy Newens has lived in Dulwich Village for over 20 years. She is a school governor and has volunteered locally as an adult literacy tutor and for a group supporting refugees. After roles in international development and trade, she currently works for a social enterprise supporting sustainably minded small businesses.

Ruth Bannister has lived in Dulwich Wood for almost 20 years, and has long been an active member of the local community. During the pandemic, Ruth managed a local mutual aid group. If elected, she will be a strong advocate for improving housing services, green issues and Dulwich Wood’s schools.

I have 20 years’ experience in the social justice sector internationally, advocating for access to education, criminal justice reform, decent work and humane migration and asylum policies. I founded a consultancy practice that provides strategy advice to funders and charities and offers pro bono services to community-based organizations. A leader in the London softball community, I am committed to functional green spaces and inclusive recreation opportunities. Having settled in Dulwich 6 years ago, I am eager to put my passion and policy know-how to work for my neighbours in Southwark.

Sean Hannigan has lived in Dulwich since 2022, and previously volunteered at a Southwark advice charity and with the conservationists in Dulwich Wood. Sean has made Southwark his home, and if elected, is determined to promote community empowerment.

Lewis has lived in Southwark for several years. He regularly volunteers for a local food poverty charity and believes in giving back to the community. Throughout his career as a parliamentary caseworker he assisted people with a wide variety of issues, from bin collections to housing. There I found the UK's companies are constantly attacked by states such as China, Russia, North Korea and Iran. There are countries out there actively hostile to the UK – we need to recognize that.

I have also watched the UK change beyond recognition. Successive governments have become increasingly divorced from what the bulk of the UK wants. Both Labour and the Tories have lived well beyond the country's means, piling up debt it will take a generation to reduce. We have mortgaged our future by spending hundreds of millions of pounds a day we don't have.

The second issue is mass immigration. The UK has a long and proud tradition of offering political asylum. Until 2004, this was 50,000 a year – a level the country could easily accept. Now, because of Labour and the Tories allowing a mass of economic migrants in, it's many hundreds of thousands annually. The 2021 census (see https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/sources/census_2021) gives the country of birth of English residents. 6.6% are from the EU, 2.8% from Africa, 5.7% from the Middle East and Asia and 1.4% from the Caribbean. It's time to put in place a government that respects the wishes of the silent majority. I’m Ellie Plater and I’m proud to be re-standing as your Labour Candidate for the Bedwell County Division election on Thursday 1st May 2025.

I was honoured to be elected to this position in a by-election last August and I’m asking for your support to serve another term.

But it still remains the case, that for too long, the Conservative-run County Council have let down our residents and schools and left roads, transport and social care to deteriorate. We all deserve so much better.

1. Tackle the Cost of Living Crisis - I’ll push the County Council to invest in Stevenage, boost our local economy and leave more money in your pocket.

2. Be your champion on the County Council - It’s time to move on from a failing Conservative County Council and elect Councillors who truly care about our community.

3. Introduce a SEND taskforce - We’ll set up a SEND taskforce of parents, schools and representatives to address the mess left by the Conservative County Council.

Since you first elected me, the world has changed. The Government was unprepared for the pandemic and mishandled it. On the plus side the UK came up with a vaccine ahead of other major countries. Today, we have a serious cost of living crisis affecting everyone, and our NHS is struggling. Hello, I am Maureen McKay and I am proud to have been chosen to stand as your Labour & Co-operative candidate for Pin Green.  I have lived in Pin Green for over 50 years and really feel part of this community. Originally from Scotland and the eldest of four, I married at 19 and moved to London with my husband Gerard and I worked for IBM. Unemployment rates were high in Port Glasgow where we grew up.  We moved to Pin Green, Stevenage in 1964 as part of the London overspill and I had 3 daughters all born at home. The Lister Hospital wasn’t built then but all the doctors were obstetricians and we had great midwifery services. 

Stevenage offered great facilities for families: good schools, local churches, play schemes, adventure playgrounds, Bowes Lyon etc. The large companies we worked for (BAE and Kodak) both offered great social facilities for employees and their families. 

I retrained to be a teacher in 1974 and taught Maths at The John Henry Newman school in Stevenage for 25 years. I was the NUT (now NEU) representative and took part in many demonstrations in London fighting for an increase in teachers’ pay.  I really enjoyed my years of teaching. Even now after years of retirement I constantly come across ex pupils and it is always a pleasure to chat to them about what has happened since they left school. 

In my retirement, I have enjoyed being a local councillor for nearly 9 years. I am very grateful to the Stevenage Borough Council and our wonderful community for the support that we as a family have enjoyed over the years. I now feel that I can continue help to pay some of this back by supporting and helping others improve their quality of life in our town during this most difficult time. 

I am a Labour and Cooperative councillor, and a member of the Labour Women’ s Forum which supports the Co-operative principles of equality and collaborative work. I look forward to supporting all residents, small businesses and schools/playgroups and nurseries in the Pin Green area. I am particularly interested in young people and would like to help enable young people to take part in leisure and cultural activities as well as encouraging them to secure future career opportunities. 

I have been involved in many projects to help improve our area, which I have highlighted below.  I am also very keen to hear the voices of residents in Pin Green about any issues that are important to you and your families and promise to work hard to support you if you elect me to be a Pin Green councillor. 

Community Projects 

■ I helped local residents resolve many issues such as housing problems and repairs, parking issues, noise problems, anti-social behaviour, lighting, potholes and drugs issues etc… and reported them to the appropriate officers in our Council/ Hertfordshire County Council.  I attend meetings with the Police to discuss many of these issues. 

■ I worked with a County Councillor and Herts Highways to organise the laying of a dropped kerb for mobility scooters in a path to the Oval from Arthur Gibbens Court and Martins Wood House.  This was paid for from our local community budgets and the County Councillor’s local budget. 

■ The Oval Community Garden was reinstated and run by a local resident and her volunteer team including local councillors. The garden is used by young people, local schools and nurseries and often local residents. A new path, gate and fencing has been installed to enable pushchairs, wheelchairs and mobility scooters access to the garden and two other councillors supported this from our local community budgets.

I'm Thea Pendlebury, your Labour Candidate for the Roebuck Stevenage Borough Council by-election. I’m sending you this letter because I would like to persuade you to vote for me in the Roebuck by-election on Thursday, 30th October.

Whether it’s getting the lighting and windows upgraded at the Crossroads Community Hub, working with the police to tackle anti-social behaviour at Shephalbury park, or leading litter picking sessions in the ward, your councillors have been working hard for you. However, there is more to be done. I will work closely with our MP Kevin Bonavia to keep delivering for Roebuck.

Reform councils have been focusing their efforts on pushing ideological policies. They should be working on improving local services and making their communities stronger. As your Labour candidate, I will work hard to improve everyday life for residents.

Thanks to Labour’s investment in Roebuck Surgery, local patients will be getting better access to appointments and improved services. At the same time Reform continues to talk about replacing our NHS with insurance companies competing against each other, putting profits before patients.

Please give me your support by voting for positive change and a county councillor that's on your side. Thank you.
