statement_to_voters:
I wish to offer the voters of Harlow a different choice from the tired old parties. My main concerns are the poor state of our NHS, sewage in our waters, the cost of living crisis and profiteering of the big banks, energy and water companies. We need to have positive practical solutions to the daily lives of people, not the gimmicky, punch-and-judy politics of late. I believe the Liberal Democrats can offer those solutions, providing families with some relief from their daily expenses, the elderly and infirm dignity in their care and the young with hope to look forward with.

The two big parties will say that a vote for Liberal Democrats is a wasted vote – but I believe that our positive policies compare incredibly well with theirs - and a vote for me will send them a message that they cannot take you and your vote for granted. I will be a strong voice and MP for you, championing your causes and ensuring things get done here. 

If you have always voted for other parties, I would ask you to be bold, embrace change, and give me your vote so you can get a fresh, new MP who will work hard and work diligently for you, your family and your community.

I dream of a future where families, children, elderly & loved ones across Stevenage are given the opportunity to thrive. I'm tired of watching our town be torn apart by divisive politics and want to bring the focus back to serving the people in your community.

Many of us right now probably feel like we aren't being heard, let alone understood. Brexit, COVID and almost a decade and a half of austerity are all still having rippling effects across all communities. We face many challenges but to overcome them, we have to start by listening to those who have the most at stake. For me, that means representing those in St. Nicholas so we can build a fairer future together.

I am standing for the Green Party because I believe that the Greens have the best plan for the economy as well as the environment. I favour a holistic approach in politics at the local as well as the national level.

As a keen allotment grower and having many years experience as a professional gardener, I am very interested in encouraging the promotion of home grown vegetables as a way of reducing the food bill and helping the environment. A personal growth and fitness enthusiast, I have been teaching Tae Kwon Do for over 50 years and I hope to promote fitness and relaxation as well as environmental improvements in our area.

I’m Claire Parris and I’m proud to be standing as your Labour Candidate for the St Nicholas County Council Division election on Thursday 1st May.

I was born and raised in Stevenage and I take pride in calling St Nicholas my home.

The current Conservative County Councillor has been unseen and unbothered.

He’s let down my area. My home.

But I know what real public service looks like.

I work for our NHS, at the Lister, and I’ve served our community as a Borough Councillor for the past 6 years.

For too long, the Conservative-run County Council have let down our residents and schools and left roads, transport and social care to deteriorate. We all deserve so much better. It’s time to Heart Herts!

I want to be your champion on the County Council, fixing these issues one by one. It’s time to vote for change. And you can read my plan for change below!

My plan for change in our area

1. Tackle the Cost of Living Crisis - I’ll push the County Council to invest in Stevenage, boost our local economy and leave more money in your pocket.

2. Be your champion on the County Council - It’s time to move on from unseen, unbothered Conservative County Councillors and elect a Councillor who cares about our community.

3. Introduce a SEND taskforce - We’ll set up a SEND taskforce of parents, schools and representatives to address the mess left by the Conservative County Council.

4. Crack down on anti-social behaviour - We’ll introduce a zero tolerance approach to anti-social behaviour, from enforcing fly-tipping fines to ensuring rapid police responses.

5. Finally fix Potholes - We’ll establish a road and transport improvement plan to tackle potholes and ensure we have reliable, affordable public transport.

I believe our community deserves better than being taken for granted. For too long, decisions have been made without any challenge. When one party dominates for decades, accountability slips and local people are left dealing with the consequences.

I work for a local charity, supporting people through some of the most difficult moments in their lives, and that experience has shown me how deeply issues like housing, mental health and underfunded services affect our community, and how often people feel ignored.

I grew up in Symonds Green, still live here now, and I want to listen, challenge poor decisions, and stand up for this area in any way I can.

I’ve lived in Old Stevenage with my family for more than 25 years. I’m a businesswoman and I know it’s my time to give back. I can’t just leave it to someone else to take the reins, it would be passing the buck. I am keen to step in and deliver improvements for the residents of Old Town and Symonds Green.

I know I’ve got big shoes to fill. Cllr Graham Lawrence, who is retiring as Old Stevenage’s County Councillor, did a lot to improve the Old Town and Symonds Green. He also ensured that any changes to the High Street were done using common sense and for the benefit of both businesses and residents. I want to build on these successes and make our High Street more inviting.

Somewhere people want to spend a little time either getting their hair cut; some flowers for their beautiful wife or mother; and then in the evening, wining and dining with friends after a hard day’s work.

County Council has a plan to rejuvenate the High Street; to make it a little safer; a place people will want to buy a coffee or have their car repaired.

We, the Conservatives in Hertfordshire County Council, want to do all this but we can’t do so without your vote.

I grew up in Hertfordshire and I moved to Stevenage a few years ago, looking for a quiet spot to live with my two rescue cats Indy and Nala.

I am a lawyer working in criminal justice and I prosecute and defend in some of the most serious cases, including as a specialist in organised crime and rape and serious sexual offences. I volunteer to support those from disadvantaged backgrounds in gaining entry to the law.

If I was elected as your councillor I would advocate for your needs and improving your local area and access to essential services.

I have lived in Stevenage since 1956 and have grown up in the town, attending Longmeadow Infant and Junior Schools and Barnwell when it was a Secondary Modern School. 

I married in 1975, had two children, a girl and a boy, who attended local Schools and then when onto Universities. 

I have previously been a Stevenage Borough Councillor for a total of 28 years, serving on many committees, which has given me a wealth of knowledge and experience within Local Government, which I can take forward at County level. 

During my time as a Borough Councillor I also had the honour of being The Mayor twice-2018-2019 and 2022-2023. Carrying out many Civic duties and engaging with the many wonderful organisations throughout our town. I have also for many years been a member of some of these organisations, The Stevenage, Ingelheim, Autun Twinning Association. The Stevenage Kadoma Link and a local Community Association. I have recently become a member of a Primary Care Patient Participation Group and a Trustee of the Stevenage District Scouts. 

I have in the past been a School Governor, serving for over forty years. 

I enjoy spending my free time with family and friends and supporting the Performing Arts.

I first moved to Stevenage with my parents back in 1967 and have been in love with our town ever since.

Growing up in the town, I became aware of the great sense of togetherness and community we had and it's saddening to now see people working actively to take that away from us.

I initially became involved in local politics in the 1970s and have been an active member of the local Green Party since 2015. As Woodfield's first Green councillor I will be there to listen to you and represent your views, especially regarding the social and environmental issues currently prominent in the area.

No party politics 
Local politics for local people and local issues.
Born and raised in haydock all my life.
Happy to be called a yicker.

Mum and nanna

I want whats best for Haydock and will take on every issue of complaint from my constituents if elected.
An environmentalist passionate about protecting nature, enhancing public spaces, doing the right thing and fighting the rise of fascism, racism and corruption.

I’m the quintessential Briton - born in Oxfordshire; spent the first few years of my life in London; then grew up in central Scotland before moving to Glasgow for university. I then moved back to England for work three years ago and now live in Newton. My ancestors are from all over Britain - two of my great grandparents came from Hartford, Cheshire.

At university I studied mechanical engineering; I enjoyed the research-focused parts of the course the most, so I stayed on to do my doctorate too. I primarily studied metallurgy, and conducted research on the crystallographic phases of ferrous alloys for industrial engineering applications.

In my spare time I enjoy amateur photography (Pennington Flash - excellent) and play drums decently enough - for which I grew up playing heavy metal but also enjoy some jazz!

I’ve always been interested in politics, and have been through the complete spectrum of political leanings, being more liberal in my teenage years but more right-leaning as I grew up (as is common to do so).

I’m a firm believer in British sovereignty - I voted leave in 2016 and then supported the Brexit party in the European elections in 2019, before then voting for Boris for the first time in the 2019 General because I believed he would get Brexit over the line (ouch). Democracy is important to me - I believe that referenda are good things - let the people have a say!

I joined Reform in 2023 after feeling betrayed by the Tories - Brexit in name only, mass immigration, highest taxes ever, mass invasion of illegals coming across the channel, and an NHS that has ground to a halt. I chose to stand in the Leigh & Atherton constituency because it’s on my doorstep and has been tremendously let down by successive Tory and Labour governments, with a perpetual Labour-controlled council that takes its voters for granted (good in-roads being made by independent candidates!).

Green space is incredibly important to me - probably as a result of growing up in rural Scotland. I’m an old-school environmentalist - let’s look after our forests, lakes, rivers, open green land - instead of concreting over them to build endless housing estates. The Leigh & Atherton constituency (including Lowton, Golborne, and Tyldesley) is being massively over-developed, with new housing estates being built on every available inch of land - reducing the quality of life for all residents in the constituency.

School places are full, traffic at a standstill, a huge lack of social housing - and despite all of these people moving to the area - an incredibly run-down high street in Leigh. Something is clearly not working. The primary driver of this over-development is mass immigration - which drives down wages, drives up house prices, and dissolves our British culture. Does Leigh really need so many empty cash-only barber shops?

Traditional red-wall voters have been betrayed by the Labour party, and betrayed by the Tories, many of whom kindly lent their vote to for the first time in 2019 to get Brexit done (myself included). Now where do we go? A Labour party that can’t say what a woman is? A Tory party with the highest levels of taxation ever?

Leigh, Atherton, Lowton, Golborne, and Tyldesley need Reform. We are serious about changing politics for good

On July 4th, vote for Britain, vote for Reform, vote for George Woodward.

Do you want your country back?

I am standing as a True independent candidate in this year’s local elections in the Earlestown ward. I intend to be a truly independent voice in our town, not one that is constrained by what you must do for your party and having to vote the way you are told and not the way you wish. I feel the time is right to challenge and scrutinise some of the current ruling parties’ decisions and on many occasions, some of their councillors’ attitudes towards their electorate, as it leaves a lot to be desired.  I believe all councillors should use the Nolan principles as their guide and sadly this falls down in many cases.  I certainly believe we need more polite politics in our town.

The Nolan Principles •	Selflessness. •	Integrity. •	Objectivity. •	Accountability. •	Openness. •	Honesty. •	Leadership.

  I am standing in Earlestown, mostly to listen to residents’ concerns and to be able to represent them fairly and equally, this I believe is the main role of any local councillor. Much too often our local councillors are not visible within their communities and in many cases are not known to the electorate. I wish to change that and be a councillor that people know they can approach for an even and unbiased view to help and mediate their concerns.   I worry about the lack of policing in our area, this concerns many residents greatly, we need more on the beat, particularly at night around known anti-social behavioural hotspots.  If elected I would lobby the new Police & Crime Commissioner on this issue.   I would also arrange regular meetings with local police to discuss residents' worries and concerns.     I am all in favour of the growth and regeneration of our town centre and Town Hall and would be happy to work with all sustainable plans to implement this.  Over the years, there have been many promises for this to happen. Labour have left the Town Hall closed for 13 years, we can now watch to see if their promised plans and allocated monies come to fruition, if they remain in power.  If they do and it is sustainable then I would be happy to work with them. Our town also needs new initiatives to control littering and fly tipping. This is a big concern; discussions need to be held urgently on this matter.   I worry very much about the youth, borough wide and feel they are a little lost, we are missing a connection with them and need to work hard to try and offer them more ways of employment and a better vision for their future.  We need to know their concerns and why so many of them appear to feel angry.   Having lived in N-Le-W for the last 49 years, running a successful business that has trained and employed many from our town.  Being a trustee of local Charity Business for Youth that has just finished a 13-month response to the pandemic for those in need and being a proud part of the rejuvenation of the Earlestown Christmas Lights. All this has taken a lot of hard work and hard work has never worried me and that is what I will give if I am elected. 

I am proud of our town, its heritage and its people, if elected I will be an honest, respectful and hardworking councillor for our community.

I have called St Helens home for the past 15 years. Having gone to school and college here, and now as an adult working in the town too, this community means a lot to me.

It has given me so many opportunities and I feel such a sense of belonging here because of the incredible people I have come to know, I now feel it’s time for me to give back.

As a working class woman raising a little girl, I feel compelled to be a part of the movement of hope. One that protects people and planet.

I’m standing in Rainford to be a passionate, practical local voice on the council, speaking up for residents who feel overlooked and working to ensure no one in our community is forgotten or left behind.

I believe we can build a fairer, greener future, one where no one is left behind and everyone has a voice.

My name is James Tasker, and I am excited to announce my candidacy as an Independent for St Helens South and Whiston in the upcoming general election.

As many of you know, I have served Rainhill as an Independent councillor for the last six years. I have always been deeply committed to fighting for our communities and ensuring our voices are heard.

Today, I am taking this commitment a step further. Our community needs a representative in Parliament who is not bound by party politics but is dedicated to addressing our real issues.

I am running as an Independent candidate because I believe St Helens and Whiston deserve an independent voice—someone who prioritises our residents’ needs and interests above all else.

As a councillor, I have seen the difference that dedicated, community-focused leadership can make. I am proud of our progress together, but much work still needs to be done.

Jilly is a tireless advocate for people in Cheadle East and Cheadle Hulme North. Jilly has also spoken up for residents affected by local flooding and transport changes, ensuring that their views are properly considered. I’m a Mechanical Engineer, BEng(Hons) Graduate and retired University Senior Lecturer. I’ve lived in Cheadle Hulme for twenty six years and am standing with the Green Party because I believe in social justice, fairness, inclusion and protecting the environment we all share.

Helen has represented Cheadle Hulme South for many years and continues to be one of the most dedicated local voices on Stockport Council. She has fought to protect the character of Cheadle Hulme, supported initiatives to make our neighbourhoods greener and safer, and stood up for families and small businesses. Helen’s deep roots in the community and her track record of delivery make her a trusted and respected councillor who always puts residents first.

Ian is well known for his hands-on approach in Gatley and Cheadle West. From organising litter picks to supporting local shops on Gatley and Cheadle High Streets, he’s a visible and approachable councillor who puts community first. Ian has been at the forefront of efforts to tackle traffic problems and protect local green spaces, while making sure residents’ voices are heard in Stockport Town Hall. He’s passionate about keeping Gatley and Cheadle great places to live and work.

Alice is a local mum and community campaigner with deep roots in Davenport and Cale Green. She’s been a passionate voice for improving accessibility at Davenport Station, working to ensure that everyone – including parents with prams, older residents and people with disabilities – can use the station safely and easily. She’s focused on practical solutions to help our community thrive, from supporting local shops to improving public transport and green spaces. Alice brings energy, empathy and a real understanding of local issues – exactly the kind of representative Davenport and Cale Green needs on the council.

My name is Ashley Walker and I am a working-class man born on Bridge Hall. I am a socialist and a member of Your Party. I am also a member of several local organisations working to improve rights and living conditions for the people of Stockport.

As a working-class man who lives in Adswood, I have seen how cuts and the hoarding of wealth by the rich has destroyed, our schools, our health services, our youth services, our communities and so much more.

I am standing for election because I want to see our communities thrive. Whether that’s the communities of the ward I am standing in, and live in, or all the other communities of Stockport.

I know our best hope of building a better future is working together to build a socialist society!

I want to assure you I will always do my best to help you with any issues.

I will respond to emails and messages. I will hold regular surgeries and walk arounds. I will meet with concerned residents as much as I can. 
I will do my best to keep you informed of local matters.

I will always treat people with respect and maintain the highest standards of conduct. If I make a promise I will keep it.

I’m Jess Meller, and I’m standing as the ECA candidate for Edgeley to help keep the seat for strong, independent local representation.

This campaign is about continuing the hard work and determination residents expect: listening to concerns, being visible in the community, and taking action on the issues that matter most — parking pressure, cleaner streets, anti-social behaviour, and protecting Edgeley from overdevelopment.

I believe Edgeley benefits from councillors who focus on the area, not party politics. If elected, I will work closely with Cllrs Wynne and Caton to make sure residents have a strong, consistent voice and that we keep delivering for the community.

If you see me out in Edgeley, please stop and say hello — I’m keen to hear what matters to you.

Anna has worked as a councillor on issues affecting residents across Heald Green ward, raising local concerns through council work, casework and engagement with residents.

• Continued to raise ongoing parking concerns with the council and GM Police

Independent Ratepayer councillors have represented Heald Green ward for many years and must live in the ward to be selected.

Nasser brings fresh energy, enthusiasm and a deep commitment to Heald Green. As a local resident, he understands the challenges facing the area – from traffic and transport to the need to protect green spaces. Nasser has been active in community and charity work for years, and he’s determined to use that experience to make a real difference for local people. His experience bringing about change in the NHS will prove invaluable to Heald Green. He’s passionate about giving Heald Green residents a strong and effective voice on the council.

My name is Hélèna Mellish and I'm the Green Party's General Election candidate for Stockport, my buzzing home.  I'm proud to represent the Greens as I truly believe they're the only party that has meaningful solutions to today's problems. In light of all the craziness that is going on, they're the only party that stands up for morality and the issues that really matter.   Common sense. Security. Justice. That's what the Green's promise - for our environment, for our economy, and for our people. Green policies are underpinned by core values and rooted in fairness, not the self-interest of a few. We won't be scared into silence and we're ready to take advantage of the incredible opportunity before us: --- the opportunity for a green industrial revolution that energises the economy, whilst protecting our planet and all us people on it. Us folk work hard, we deserve political leadership that works hard for us too! As a small business owner within the food industry, I'm excited to champion local commerce and a transformation of our food systems. We need to take back control of our resources, nationalise essential public services and invest in the technology and infrastructure that will fuel our futures.

Dominic has brought energy and commitment to representing Norbury and Woodsmoor, always focused on practical solutions to local issues. He’s worked with residents to address speeding, parking problems and traveller encampment concerns, and has campaigned for cleaner, safer streets. Dominic is proud to represent a community with such a strong local spirit, and he’s determined to make sure Norbury and Woodsmoor continue to get their fair share of investment and attention from the council.

I live locally in Napton-on-the-Hill with my wife Laure and two energetic sons.

I want to see our local infrastructure improved and our community listened to.

I am fighting to make sure our decision-making is kept locally with a South
Warwickshire Unitary Council, not from miles away in Nuneaton.

I will strive to continue the great work achieved by Nigel Rock, who stepped down
after 20 years of service to our community and I will I’ll work alongside Cllr Natalie Gist to make sure all of our area is properly represented at the District Council.

It would be an honour to serve our community as your new District Councillor.

Hello, residents of Kenilworth and Southam Constituency,

I am honoured to introduce myself as your candidate for Reform UK. I am dedicated to serving our community and advocating for real change. In these challenging times, it's crucial to have a representative who understands the pulse of our locality and has the experience and determination to address our pressing concerns.

I extend my heartfelt gratitude to all of you who have shown unwavering support, whether by attending our pop-ups, engaging in social events, or voicing your thoughts and aspirations for our constituency.

Let me share a glimpse into my journey and the principles driving my candidacy. With a career spanning the public sector since the age of 17, I've had the privilege of serving in two vital services: Policing and the NHS. These roles have afforded me invaluable insights into the myriad issues facing our communities and have equipped me with the skills necessary to navigate the complexities of governance effectively. I have completed advanced policing leadership courses and obtained CMI qualifications, enhancing my leadership skills and strategic capabilities.

My name is Jon London and I am the Liberal Democrat District Councillor for Exning. I look forward to being County Councillor for Exning and Newmarket. Seamus was born and schooled in Felixstowe and after a career in education and international development moved back to the UK with his family in 2008, choosing to settle back in his hometown where his dad had been a GP for nearly 40 years.

Seamus' work as a town councillor has already brought real benefits for Felixstowe. Electing Seamus to Suffolk County council will, simply, be very good for Felixstowe.

Jan Candy is passionate about our coastline and the people who inhabit this beautiful planet. Former president of a UK Human Rights organisation and campaigner for soil and water sustainability across the globe. On the surface Felixstowe Coastal looks amazing but just scratch a little further beneath the Tory Gloss and you will find hardship and such sad tales of loss and deprivation- it need not be this way. Tony Love is the Reform UK Prospective Parliamentary Candidate for the Ipswich constituency. Below is short summary of his background.

I was born in Shoreham-by-Sea, West Sussex, in June 1955. My father was in the Royal Navy for 17 years, joining as an artificer and leaving as a Chief Petty Officer. The family were shuffled from one port to another, mostly along the south coast although I did live for a short time, aged six months, in a flat above a chip shop, near the lighthouse in Harwich!

Children of naval servicemen in the 1960s were eligible to attend The Royal Hospital School in Holbrook, Suffolk. These were the most important years of my life where I was transformed from a toerag into an acceptable human being. Mental arithmetic was my strongest attribute and aged nineteen I was working in the Playboy Casino in Park Lane, London.

I was there for seven years as a Dealer and then Inspector of Blackjack, Roulette and Punto Banco (similar to Chemin de Fer) before training croupiers to do the same. When the Playboy Casino closed I moved to a casino in Hans St (SW3) which then relocated to Curzon St, Mayfair.

In 1987 I opened my first Licensed Betting Office in Haslemere, Surrey and spent the next 30 years as an independent bookmaker. Eventually regulatory costs and internet competition overwhelmed the ‘independents’ and I closed my last shop in Liphook, Hampshire in August 2018. I then moved to Felixstowe and now have an antique shop in the town, on the High Street.

Politically, I was selected to stand for the Brexit Party in the Suffolk Coastal constituency in the 2019 general election. We had the only Brexit Shop in the country in Hamilton Road, Felixstowe, where we spoke to hundreds of electors from all sides of the political debate.

The Brexit Party stood many of their candidates down but our team collectively decided I should continue as an Independent. During the campaign we had promised to stand up for those who felt disenfranchised.

At the Brexit Party we were attracting Labour voters hand over fist, many of those who came to speak with us came from Ipswich. It was sad to see so much unhappiness. This Conservative Government was handed a huge mandate by the voters of this country to implement the Brexit that we voted for in the Referendum. They have failed entirely.

They have most certainly failed the people of Ipswich. I feel strongly that the Reform Party will stand up for the people of Ipswich and not treat them as expendable. Both Labour and the Conservatives are culpable when it comes to making promises they do not keep, even worse, do not intend to keep.

I am in a long term relationship, previously having been married for eighteen years having three adult children. My Mother has lived in Nacton for over 30 years during which time she has been Chairman of The League of Friends for Ipswich Hospital.

For three successive years I ran a football competition in conjunction with The League of Friends, Ipswich Town FC and Orwell Park School to raise money for the cause. I feel privileged to represent the Reform Party in Ipswich and to demonstrate our intention to represent you - The People.

I have been in Suffolk for 18 years, my career has been in infrastructure management, both nationally and internationally at a senior level. I have entered politics as I struggle to believe what is happening to our Country. We are the greatest Country in the world but we are in trouble. I am originally from a part of the UK I no longer recognise. I know from experience how somewhere you call home can be lost, we can never allow Framlingham and Wickham Market to lose it's unique identity in this way. I will protect our culture and heritage, I will oppose the urbanisation of our towns and villages, large scale property and solar developments, retain the charm of our market towns and beautiful food producing countryside, implement flood mitigations, slow the flow, more attenuation. I will support housing local people and military veterans not illegal migrants. I am not a career politician, I am just like you, I am so dissapointed with all the traditional parties that have let us down, we can be better than this, I want to play my part in our renewal. Help me to help you on 07 May.

“Improving services and facilities will combat antisocial behavior and improve the neighborhoods we all live in. I want to empower residents and communities to live well and be safe in our town,’ said Liz.
YOUR PRIORITIES ARE MY PRIORITIES
RESIDENTS FIRST, PARTY SECOND 
Liz has always put the interests of her residents first, even when it has clashed with her party's views. She worked with the Rivers Action Group representing residents opposed to the Upper Orwell Crossing, which helped result in the scheme's cancellation.
BOXING CLEVER! 
Liz has worked with Patrick’s Boxing Club in York Road which helps and encourages young people to take up boxing as a sport. If re-elected, Liz will fight for more to be done for young people in the area.

I'm Daniel Davey, I was born and raised in Ipswich. I've had the town in my heart throughout my working career in the pub and leisure industry. It has been a real privilege to serve our community. I have worked hard to be visible, accessible and active so residents always know who to turn to. We may not always agree, but I will always stand up for our area and do what I believe is right.

Too many politicians change party because they fear defeat or lack the moral compass to stand firm. I will stand on my record and let the people decide.

Local elections are about knowing your councillor and who can make a difference. I believe I can.

I’m proud to raise my family here in Suffolk.I believe that our history and traditions should never be forgotten. Challenging the status quo with a common sense approach. Supporting local businesses, infrastructure and schools, whilst protecting the Suffolk landscape. Ensuring taxes are used intelligently.

I’m proud to be standing as the Green Party candidate for Gipping Valley in the County Council elections on May 7th. I believe that an effective County Council should focus on delivering essential services well while protecting the countryside and environment that make this area special.

Across Gipping Valley, residents are raising practical concerns about deteriorating roads and pavements, flooding that continues to affect homes and businesses, and the difficulty many people face getting around without relying on a car. Mark has lived in Claydon for over 15 years and knows the area well.  He is active in the community running the local Scout group and was previously the Scout County Commissioner for all of Suffolk.

Mark is a business and marketing strategy expert and works with small and medium sized businesses across East Anglia so has a good working knowledge of the challenges that businesses face.

“I am a strong advocate of community and bringing people of all walks of life together. When we work together, we achieve far more for the area we live in.”

Graham and his wife Maureen have lived in Gunton & St Margarets for more than 35 years. Graham is an experienced and caring Town Councillor and believes it's important to listen and communicate with residents locally.

I am proud to be the local Conservative candidate for Halesworth, Holton and our rural villages. 
Practical, pragmatic leadership. 
Nurture what works, fix what is broken. 
Sick and tired of being ignored…?
I listen, I act, I follow through.

Drawing upon experience across both private and charitable sectors, I am keen to give back to our community. I have spent 40 years running my own businesses in Suffolk, most recently an accountancy firm in Bury St Edmunds.
This gives me strong roots in the town and a clear understanding of the challenges local people face. These are not abstract problems, they affect safety, local businesses, and pride in our town. I believe in speaking up, practical solutions and visible action, not empty promises.
I am hardworking, fair and straighttalking, and care deeply about Bury St Edmunds. It deserves attention from people who are prepared to work hard to improve the quality of life for everyone who lives and works here.

James is born and raised in Bury St Edmunds and has lived here for much of his life. He is a former CEO of a local agriculture company and used to be a university lecturer. Now he works in property while being one of the lead campaigners for the Liberal Democrats in Bury St. Edmunds.

As the partner of a nurse at West Suffolk Hospital, James understands the burden that is on our local NHS and wants to see greater support for primary care providers such as GPs, dentists and pharmacies with priority for lowering business rates as well as free parking for NHS staff at West Suffolk Hospital.

He wants to see our road quality problems tackled by being tough on our repair contractor, introducing traffic calming to stop our roads being damaged in the first place, and opening up public car parks for residents in order to reduce parking overcrowding on our roads in the town centre.

A member of the Bury St Edmunds business community for many years, James has been disappointed to see much of our local economy struggle and not getting the support they need. He will back our local businesses and strive to create a thriving job market for all, making sure that business outside of the town centre also receive the support they need.

I value this community and want to see our principles and values reflected in decisions that affect us, now and into the future.

I have lived on Barons Rd in Bury St Edmunds for 15 years, during which I spent time as a primary school governor and continue to volunteer in grassroots football.

When I offered to stand for the Hardwick County Council seat, I understood that the local party's resources would have to be directed at those seats that were identified as more winnable targets, but felt it was important that a Green candidate appeared on the ballot paper - not just for committed Green voters but also to give an option for anyone disenchanted with the so-called "main" parties.

The massive Conservative majority in Hardwick at the last election is under real pressure and an increased Green vote will mean that, even if we do not win this seat, then our voice will have to be heard by any elected representative.

We have a stronger message and appeal than ever and next week's elections give us a tremendous opportunity to build on our progress in Suffolk.

As an Army veteran, local business owner and family man, I am standing for election to provide an honest, competent County councillor for Hartismere and Suffolk. My core priorities are spending public funds sensibly, seeking value for money, fixing our infrastructure, and transforming council services to deliver a bright, prosperous future for our community.

Contact - pjbreformuk@gmail.com

Hartismere deserves a councillor focused on Hartismere - not Westminster point scoring or hard-left Green politics.

While the Greens back covering huge areas of Suffolk countryside with giant solar farms and pylons, I’ll fight to protect our villages, farmland and rural character. And while Reform seem more interested in shouting about national politics online, I’m focused on the issues that actually matter here - safer roads, protecting black bin collections, standing up against pylons and getting Suffolk’s basics right.

I love this area, I know this area and I work for this area every single week. Hartismere needs a strong local voice, not political tourists. On May 7th, vote Colin Noble - the local Conservative candidate with a real Plan for Hartismere.

As a Mid Suffolk Councillor I would bring the perspective of local services to Local Government Reorganisation and as a Green Party Member of the County Council I would work to ensure that the progress made by Mid suffolk District Council on improving our response to Homelessness, biodiversity, improving our town cintres, making grants available to communities to improve the environment, wellbeing and resilience is maintained and incorporated into the new Unitary Authority.
I have worked consistently to ensure local voices are heard on planning decisions whilst trying to achieve the best possible outcomes in the face of government priorities.
I enjoy listening to and working with local groups especially Parish Councils as they work for their communities.
As a former teacher and artist I maintain should look for and celebrate what we have in common and recognise we each have a role to play in protecting and improving our environment and community.

I believe the right people in the right places can make a real difference to the lives of people and companies.

My wife and I moved to Hundon nearly four years ago. I play golf, cricket, bowls and mentor  businessman to keep me busy but I am now ready to again put my shoulder to the democratic wheel

 I have a range of experiences and skills that I can contribute to our community.

I have run small charities and been a parish councillor. 

I spent 20 odd years in the RAF, as an aircraft engineer, was the IT and quality director of a computer chip company, and then the CEO of an IT support company which I grew from 4 people to over 80 in the UK and Sri Lanka in six years before selling the company.

I took my cabinet to Wisbech and St Neots to make it more accessible to the public, first time ever out of shire hall. 

I am as happy speaking to large forums as I am giving TV and radio interviews or canvassing on a one to one basis.

My name is Chris Connor, and I’m standing as the Liberal Democrat candidate for Haverhill East & Rural.

I live in Haverhill with my wife and our four-year-old son. We’ve chosen to build our life here, and this town means a lot to me.

I’ve spent over ten years working in public service, including at Cambridge City Council where, as a Democratic Services Officer (City Clerk), I was  a part of the democratic decision-making process and saw first-hand how local government works. I now work here in Haverhill, and I care about what happens in our community.

It feels like one of those moments where people are asking what kind of place they want to live in. For me, Haverhill is a town where people look out for each other. At the end of the day, I’m thinking about the kind of place my son will grow up in and that’s why I’m standing.

Vote for who you believe in—that’s what democracy is about. I hope you’ll consider me for your vote.

I would  hope to serve my community and focus on things that matter. Pot Holes need to be permanently  fixed. We need to look our SEND systems and ensure they are supporting people in the best way possible.  Plus ensuring local areas get invested to florish.
Bringing people together is a key drive ensuring we have an amazing community full of amazing people.

I'm Luke and my life has been somewhat of a minor miracle.

My life experience, and membership of the Family Education Trust, makes me a unique candidate to tackle the mental health crisis and the many problems in our country, I will work to improve the teaching of computing and inspire young people. I know how vital transport is for young disabled people to have a social life and of course, public transport is also vital for employment and the wider economy of Suffolk too.

Politics is about winning friends and influencing people and through my involvement with the Suffolk Association of Local Councils and Chatham House, I can confidently say that I am a candidate who can influence decisions that matters to Suffolk.

I have always been local but for the last 10 years Kedington has become a home for myself, my wife and my young children.

At work for nearly 20 years I have managed money on major construction projects. I now run the regional office for my firm, and am a regional board member for the RICS.

In my personal time I enjoy being out in the countryside whether that is going for a run, walking through the woods or paddling on the river.

Since moving to Kedington we have been regular hosts for the open gardens, we’ve participated in scarecrow competitions, duck races and even performed at Meadowlark. More recently I have been helping to fundraise for the Regeneration of the Kedington Community Centre (£30k to date).

I am not a career politician but I cannot sit back and watch the continued failure of the central parties. I am frustrated with the ever increasing cost of living, the deterioration of public services and the lack of investment in vital infrastructure.

I want a world my children can afford to live in.
I want them to play in the stream without worrying about sewage.
I want everybody to be excited about the future.
I want change.

Haverhill is a growing town and this continued growth must be sustainable. Investment in improved travel infrastructure to Cambridge is essential for Haverhill’s future prosperity and I will provide a strong voice within the council to see
improvements and schemes that benefit the town.
I fully support the continued investment in the Business & Research parks bringing new jobs to the town, and we will support initiatives that will see our businesses, High Street and wider community recover from the difficulties COVID 19 has caused. Local organisations and volunteer groups have also been negatively affected, and I
will do whatever I can to support those who contribute so much to the town.
I am hugely thankful to all those who have worked so tirelessly in the Health & Care Sector. We also recognise how COVID 19 has impacted negatively on many people’s health and well-being. I will continue to campaign for new facilities and improved access to Health & Mental Health Services in the town.
I am passionate about protecting and caring for our local environment, and I will support initiatives that tackle climate change and ensure our green spaces are well cared for.
So please lend me your support, so I can work for you and the people of Haverhill.

About Joe Mason
A teacher for 28 years, Joe Mason, has dedicated himself over the years as a public servant, working with young people to develop their knowledge, skills and aspirations.
He is currently a West Suffolk District Councillor and Haverhill Town Councillor for the Haverhill North Ward. For West Suffolk District Council he sits on the Overview & Scrutiny Committee, and the Citizens Advice Board of Trustees. For Haverhill Town Council, he is a member of the Leisure & Community Committee.
Joe Mason is active in supporting the community beyond his role as a Councillor. He is a member of the Unity Healthcare PPG committee. He is keen to see improved health facilities and access to services for residents of Haverhill and the surrounding villages.
He is Chairman of the Haverhill Show - Haverhill’s largest fundraising event for local charities and good causes. He is also the Founder of Keep Haverhill Tidy - a very active and successful litter picking group with nearly 700 members making a real difference in the community and encouraging a sense of civic pride.
Joe Mason’s other interests include seeing improved transport links with Cambridge and initiatives that support sustainable development, protect the environment and tackle climate change.

Mark has lived in East Anglia since a young boy, going to school in nearby Ely. He has been running a successful social enterprise business from Suffolk for 25 years to help and support charities and community organisations grow and develop their services. Mark served as councillor in Bury St Edmunds, including as Deputy Leader and driving forward the creation of a music venue (Apex), setting up the town's food bank with faith and voluntary groups, better recycling (brown and blue bins) and bringing safer cycling and pedestrian links. He served two terms on Suffolk County Council as the only Green in West Suffolk.

Haverhill is not just where we live, it’s who we are. I’ve had the privilege of calling Haverhill my home for over 24 years now, and in that time, I’ve seen our town go through tremendous changes. Some very positive, but like any community, there are areas where it could be better. For years, I’ve found myself thinking, ‘I wish this was different,’ or ‘Someone should fix that.’ But I’ve come to realize something important: change doesn’t happen by chance. It happens when people step forward and take action. And that’s why I became interested in standing to be part of the town’s voice. Haverhill has always had a strong community spirit, proud residence, a rich history, and recently an ever-growing population. But it still faces some challenges, whether it’s improving local services, creating more opportunities for young people, supporting our businesses, or making our town an even better and safer place to live. These are not problems for someone else to solve. They’re opportunities for all of us to work on together and make them our common goals. I believe regeneration isn’t just about buildings or infrastructure, it’s about people. It’s about creating a town where families feel proud to live, where businesses thrive, and where everyone has a voice in shaping the future. That’s the kind of Haverhill I want to help build. Like I said, I’m not just talking about what needs to change, but to be part of that change. Whether it’s through volunteering, supporting local initiatives, or working with the council, I’m ready to put my energy into making a difference. Because real progress happens when we come together as a community. Let’s make Haverhill not just a place we live, but a place we truly love. A town that reflects the best of all of us. Join me in shaping Haverhill’s future and let me be your voice.

statement_to_voters:
Haverhill is often seen as the poor relation of Suffolk. Its position on the periphery of Suffolk means that it is often overlooked for the major infrastructure schemes seen elsewhere in the county. Despite being a rapidly expanding town investment that would ensure that public services keep pace with its growth has been conspicuous by its absence. Investment in local authorities by this Conservative government has halved since it came to power on 2010. Having witnessed first-hand the real effect of years of austerity, I have become increasingly aware of the indifference from both the conservative & Labour Party towards the hard-working people of the North East, as a former Labour Party member I strongly believe like many others, labour has deserted the working-class voters who built the party, it is time for change and reform within our society which is why I chose to join Reform UK.

I am passionate about making a difference within our area and striving towards becoming a stronger, better-represented Washington.

I am incredibly proud to be selected to stand up for my ward in Washington North.

Commenting on the selection Cllr Paul Donaghy, Washington & Sunderland west spokesman said

" Elizabeth knows Washington North very well, She understands what needs to be done and how to best help the residents across the ward. Elizabeth is part of the Reform team who will be working to put Washington first"  To keep up to date with Elizabeth`s campaign visit  www.facebook.com/reformwaswnorth

I believe in prioritising the needs and concerns of the community above all else, focusing on people before politics. I am dedicated to creating positive change and serving the people of Washington, the North-East and ultimately our country. I want to shake up the political landscape both locally and nationally.

I am not your ‘typical career politician’ that`s for sure, and that is what we need in the Northeast, someone who will put people before politics.

I got involved with politics in 2019 because I wanted to improve the lives of those around me, so I joined the Conservative Party because traditional British values are important to me and I was lead to believe that this was the home for patriots; I was later elected as a Councillor for Washington in 2021.

Democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect are all things that matter to me, and I had expected to see this within the party, however the Conservative Party are no longer conservative, they no longer represent the values I, and many others believe in, and so found a home in Reform UK, defecting in 2023.

I could see that our flawed political system was a magnet for those seeking power, rather than serving the public, too few politicians are focusing on the public's interests. There is a real lack of quality Councillors and MPs, many serve their own interest and those of the party they serve, with the public being an afterthought. Like many people I believe we need to have strong politicians with leadership skills and the ability to inspire and unite communities.

I want to address these underlying issues by promoting transparency, accountability, and inclusivity in politics and help attract and retaining competent individuals as Councillors and MPs.

As your next MP, I will be committed to transparency, integrity, and accountability in politics. Reform UK have NO whip system which means I am free to vote and work in your best interest, not that of any political party or union.

I began my professional career in the Royal Navy, training as a chef I served around the world traveling to every continent. As a Royal Navy Veteran, I am proud to have served my country and proud to have been a part of such a prestigious and historic institution. The training and discipline instilled a deep sense of pride which will never leave me, but I like many others see pride in our country at an all-time low, we need to change that.

Our culture is being eroded by woke ideology, our taxes are going up in the name of net zero, and our democratic freedoms along with it. We need to take a stand and say enough is enough, we want our country back, we can do that by electing Reform UK Councillors and MPs who will work for the people not against them.

My pledges to you
If elected, my number 1 and overriding priority is to do my best for the people in Washington North Ward.
I will strive at all times to work hard and fight for Washington’s fair share from our city.
I want to foster and bring back a sense of community.  I want to create more awareness of things to do locally, both new and established. Youth clubs, groups etc. Helping to create a sense of pride and community in where we live whilst reducing anti-social behaviour
 Support residents and be a mouthpiece to highlight issues. Assist in getting them resolved in a timely manner.
 Always respond to queries in an honest and timely manner. I might not know the answer or be able to get a response that pleases everyone but I pledge to answer honestly with reasoning and if i don’t know – find someone who does! I want to be open, visible and approachable

offices in Sunderland. I want to stand up to years of failure, neglect and complacency
from Labour’s council bosses in Sunderland and fight to improve our communities.

Washington deserves better than just another Labour councillor who is more
interested in Sunderland than our own town.

Hello, I'm Peter and I'm the Green candidate for Washington South. I live in the Teal Farm and I am proud to call Washington my home. From Nissan Factory to the Galleries and beyond, I love being part of this great community. After serving in the merchant navy for over a decade, I now work in naval regulation and development. With these skills and knowledge, and your support, I will be your effective voice at the council.

Hello, I am Fiona Miller. I have been an elected member since 2011. During this time, I have had the honour to work for you and support local projects and residents’ associations. A firm believer in supporting my local community and listening to what you want done in the ward. Working with you and for you. I pledge to be your voice on the council and ensure your voice is heard in the council chamber. I will fight for decent and affordable housing and good transport links in my ward.

A proud Washington resident for over 50 years, Robert is a married, retired time-served tradesman who helped build the original Washington New Town back in the day. Starting on the tools, he worked his way up to Clerk of Works for the Regional Health Authority before setting up his own successful company. He went on to deliver major projects for health authorities, Durham University and local councils across the country and internationally, working in Northern and Southern Europe, Africa and South America – but always taking the same practical, no-nonsense approach.

With strong experience in highways and road construction, Robert knows only too well the difference between proper reinstatement and the repeated pothole patching that continues to frustrate so many residents. Now retired and living in Fatfield, he is standing for Reform UK in Washington South because it’s time for straight-talking, common-sense representation that actually puts local people first.

Robert is determined to make a real difference right where he lives in Fatfield and right across the South ward communities of Rickleton, Harraton, Staithes, Teal Farm, Mount Pleasant, and the Wear & Pattinson areas.

Robert’s Priorities:

- Fixing our roads properly - Drawing on his highways expertise, Robert will demand genuine, lasting reinstatement works so we stop wasting money on the same potholes year after year.  
- Standing up for Fatfield and local services - Making sure Fatfield and all our estates get the attention they deserve on roads, verges, drainage, bin collections and cleaner streets.  
- Better value for council tax - Fighting for reliable services and sensible spending that delivers real results for residents and businesses across Washington South.  
- Sensible development - Supporting community-led improvements that genuinely benefit local people, such as better sports and recreational facilities with adequate parking, while listening carefully to residents and protecting our valued green spaces and existing neighbourhoods from over-development.  
- Straight-talking representation - Bringing his lifetime of practical experience to the council table so Washington South finally gets the honest, no-fluff voice it needs.

As George Washington said: “Truth will ultimately prevail.”

Elouise is a passionate health professional and dedicated towards championing local issues. She has lived in Washington with her family for many years. Her long career working right across Wearside has given her extensive hands-on experience delivering public services, so she really understands the everyday challenges that families here face. She is determined to fight for real change and make sure Washington, and especially our ward, gets the investment and attention it deserves.

For years, Elouise has supported children, young people and their families across Washington and Wearside. She has made a real difference to their lives. She has also represented the North East at national level, helping to shape policies that actually improve things on the ground.

She is standing because she has had enough of Washington being treated as second-best to the city centre. For far too long our ward has been overlooked on investment, local services and having our voices properly heard. While millions have been poured into the city centre, our families and young people have been left behind – whether it’s decent community facilities, safe places to play, or simply being listened to. That stops now.

Elouise is warm, energetic and fiercely determined. She brings fresh energy, real-life experience and a direct approach. She is committed to standing up for residents who feel ignored or let down.

Elouise focuses on:
- Fair funding and proper investment right across the ward: in Rickleton, Harraton, Fatfield, Staithes, Teal Farm, and Mount Pleasant; along with our industrial areas of Wear and Pattinson
- Better facilities and community spaces for families, children and young people
- High-quality local services that actually deliver
- Strong support for local clubs and community venues
- Ensuring residents’ voices are heard loud and clear

Her aim is simple: she will listen to residents, stand up for what really matters, and do her utmost to get things done. No more excuses, no more broken promises.

It’s time for real change in Washington South, use your three votes for Reform UK to put our families and our community first.

Hi, I’m Theo, one of your Green Party candidates for Washington South. I live in Washington and I am part of this wonderful community, but I feel how let down Washington has been by the council and the Government. I’m passionate about changing this and being a voice for the people, standing up for the vulnerable in our community and working together to build a safer, happier place to live.

John is a longstanding Harraton resident. Fed up with years of the same old Labour control that’s let down our communities, John’s throwing his hat in the ring to fight for real change - putting Washington first and making sure our voices are actually heard at the council table.

John knows what matters to families and workers around here. He’s seen first-hand how decisions made in the council chamber affect everyday life in Washington – from potholed roads and creaking services to housing pressures and the cost of living squeezing people. Right at the top of his list is holding big housing providers like Gentoo to account so that local tenants actually get the decent homes they pay for.

John’s key focuses:

Holding Gentoo to account - Cracking down on the damp, mould and repair delays that are blighting homes across Washington, pushing for faster action on anti-social behaviour, and making sure tenants’ rent money goes on fixing properties – not high executive salaries or pet projects elsewhere. Enough is enough! Washington deserves better from its biggest landlord.

Fixing our streets and services - Proper maintenance of roads, pavements and parks so Washington looks and feels like a place we can be proud of again, not an afterthought.

Standing up for Washington’s identity - Protecting our green spaces, opposing over-development that ignores local needs, and ensuring new housing comes with the infrastructure to support it.

Cutting waste and bureaucracy - Ending the endless spending on consultants and pet projects while front-line services struggle.

Safer communities - More visible action on anti-social behaviour so people feel secure in their own villages.

John believes Sunderland City Council has been run in the interests of the few for too long. With Reform UK, he wants to bring straight-talking, accountable representation that delivers for the many - ending the grip of the old parties, getting tough with under-performing landlords like Gentoo, and finally getting things done for Washington South.

Born and raised in the ward Joanne is a passionate advocate for residents, Well known for her years of volunteering in the area and her warm and friendly nature. On being asked why she was running she simply stated "I'm not the most political person but I've reached the limit to what I can achieve as a resident, By running I'm hoping I can go further and help more people " After meeting her while she was out on her campaign I found her an absolute breath of fresh air, A very genuine young lady who comes across as refreshingly honest with a keen sense of humour.

I am standing for re-election to Sunderland Council on May 7th 2026 for the new Washington West ward made up from the villages of Ayton, Blackfell, Oxclose & Springwell Village.

I live in Ayton, ensuring a local representative can be voted into Washington.

FIXING OUR ROADS
- £1M extra funding secured to resurface our roads.

MORE LITTER AND GRIT BINS
- We will fund areas which need more litter and grit bins.

BETTER PLAY SPACES
- Investing in local play equipment across parks.

FUNDING YOUTH PROVISION

CCTV IMPROVEMENTS
- To tackle flytipping, littering, and anti-social behaviour.

WORK ALL YEAR ROUND AS YOUR COUNCILLORS

I moved to Washington a few years ago to join my partner and family in their hometown, and they have passed on their love for Washington to me absolutely. Washington West is a vibrant area with a fantastic community and so many beautiful green spaces - it's just been allowed to be forgotten by Sunderland Council. The community here is so strong and has welcomed me with open arms, and I will use my voice in the council to make sure that your voices cannot be ignored any longer.

Renewable energy is very close to my heart. I believe it can help us tackle climate breakdown and pollution on an international level while providing good quality employment. I also believe it is part of the answer to the cost-of-living crisis. As a councillor, I would campaign for the council to stop investing in fossil fuels and instead invest in community owned renewable energy sources. These could provide cheaper energy to residents and businesses and attract new investment to the area. More money in people’s pockets would provide a boost to the local economy. It would give me great pride to represent our community and be involved in such positive changes. Vote Green for a brighter, more sustainable future.

I worked in adult mental health for over 26 years and spent a decade as a union rep. Like most people I used to find myself following the herd and backing Labour, but I’ve seen too many families in our communities too scared to leave their homes and too many children getting hurt on our streets. As a foster carer I couldn’t stand by any longer, so I joined Reform UK to protect our children and families from unnecessary harm and to fight for the safer neighbourhoods we all deserve.
Whilst I live just over the county boundary, I work across Washington and Sunderland. • Tackling anti-social behaviour by working with residents, the police and the council to reclaim our streets and make Washington West safer for everyone
• Improving provision for children and young people with better local facilities, activities and support so our kids and teenagers have safe, positive places to go

I’ve lived in Springwell Village for 20 years. I’m an RAF veteran, former vocational training manager for a Sunderland charity, and now work as a Quality Consultant for a vocational qualification awarding body.
For too long, consecutive Labour councils in Sunderland have taken Washington and Springwell Village for granted. After more than half a century of control, they’ve poured money into the city centre and seafront while hitting us with above-inflation council tax rises, yet delivered little in the way of services for Springwell Village, Blackfell, Ayton and Oxclose.
We deserve far better!
That’s why I’m standing. If you elect me and the other Reform UK candidates as your councillors on 7th May, you will never be ignored again. We will always be there, standing up for Springwell Village and the whole Washington West ward – fighting for what matters most to you.
This election gives us a real chance to send a clear message to Keir Starmer and Westminster, and to change local politics for good. It’s a straight fight between Reform UK and Labour.
A Reform-led council would bring exciting plans for the area, including better youth services and improved parks. I will put local residents first and ensure Washington West is never overlooked again.
My priorities include:
• Improving road safety - fixing potholes and tackling dangerous and reckless driving
• Protecting our green belt, parks and heritage
• Improving social cohesion by cracking down on crime and anti-social behaviour
Don’t waste this opportunity. Use all three of your votes for Reform UK candidates in Washington West on 7th May and help change local politics for good!

I focus on:
• Better maintained and safer roads with proper enforcement
• Proper crackdowns on anti-social behaviour (ASB) so families can feel secure again
• Support for more effective community policing with stronger prevention measures to improve neighbourhood safety
Your local Original Action Team is about putting local people first, and I’m proud to be part of the team making that happen on the ground in Washington. With three votes available in this election, please use all three to back Reform UK and get the real change Washington deserves.

The politics of Labour and Reform are extremely similar. They don't see the value of investment into public services. They will keep cutting and cutting what you rely on and value until there's nothing left. The Greens are the only party to say no to this. Austerity hasn't worked globally, it hasn't worked nationally and it doesn't work for Washington West.

As a Labour candidate I am standing on our locally agreed policies and pledges:

1. We will focus on the cost of living not see you go further into debt. We will ensure all residents are aware of the cost of living improvements the Government is making and actively encourage take up.Locally we will provide secure, quality job opportunities and attract new business - especially cooperatives and mutual - into our borough and promote wider business commitment to the London Living Wage. We will also seek full implementation of the Employment Act and support enforcement where we are legally able. Poverty and the need for food banks should never be allowed to happen in Sutton.

2. We will support increased locally based Policing to tackle crime and support victims. We will invest in CCTV, better lighting and community safety hubs and work with the community to improve women’s safety locally.

3. We will provide secure affordable homes for our younger people who are priced out of the borough and build more genuinely affordable council housing in our borough.

4. We will commit to: Cleaner Streets. Cleaner Air. "Community Spring Cleans" and monitored local "pop up skips". We will look at ways to withdraw from the Beddington Incinerator and its waste disposal contract that the Lib Dems shockingly brought to this borough.

5. We will always fully consult residents over parking and traffic schemes and seek strong local consent. Future schemes should be resident petition driven, not a simple statistical exercise by Council officers.

6. We will protect our local environment. We will ensure the council plays a key role as part of the Declaration of a Climate Emergency and seeks funds to remediate the threat of flooding in lower lying areas of the borough such as near the River Wandle and Beverley Brook.

7. We will protect and improve and keep local our health and social care services. We welcome the reduction in local waiting lists and push for further big reductions in the next 4 years.We further welcome over £7m early investment at St Helier Hospital and will fight to keep all acute services at it.

8. We will provide Education and Inclusion for all. We support the excellence of our locally rooted primary and secondary schools that already provide places for more than 90% of Sutton pupils and will help support them to increase that. We support the demands of Sutton Parents campaigning for better SEND support and improved transport.

9. We will stop the decline in local arts, sports & culture and revitalise our High Streets with more “meanwhile use” and pop-up shops as well as support a strong post office network and our credit union to reduce lack of financial access. We will work with local shopkeepers to improve local shopfronts like Labour Merton Council has done. We will also work with the Mayor of London to review public transport links to improve accessibility including the option of more express Superloop bus services locally. We will seek to increase free access to sports facilities -especially swimming - for the less well off from both a cost of living and a public health perspective.

10. We will listen. We will consult. Too many people cannot get hold of their current Councillors. We will bring in a new listening and consultation strategy led by local residents and encourage local “resident juries” and a “People’s Question Time” to hold services to account. We will develop stronger more accountable local committees, with the opportunity for them to become proper local community councils, but only if residents petition and vote for them. We will press for revision to existing contracts so the Council treat employees fairly as part of a longer-term plan to in-source more services so the Council directly provides them again. We will ensure the Council’s own funds and investments are ethical and also fully comply with UK Law and International Law regarding all conflicts across the world & would seek divestment from any investments that do not.

Local business leader and former Royal Navy officer. I have built and scaled high-growth training organisations, delivering skills, jobs and opportunity which I hope to bring to the community. As a Reform UK candidate I will bring disciplined leadership, economic focus and practical solutions to serve local communities.

Liz is a Scot by birth and moved to the Swindon area in 1988. She is married with two grown-up children and 4 grandsons. Liz worked as a GP in Swindon for 20 years and finished her career in a South West regional health service management role.

This is why Liz is a member and wants to represent her local community and become part of the solution.

Growing up in the Ridgeway and Chiseldon ward, I have developed a vast sense of pride for my local area and the community within it. I want to be a passionate voice who will advocate for the community's interests, ensuring that local people are heard and that residents feel represented by their councillor. I am someone who is extremely enthusiastic about the ideas they present and is passionate about the cause they push, that's why I want to become a councillor.

I’ve proudly lived in Swindon for 9 years after moving from West London. I work hard and love helping people. My priorities: Safe streets, reduced crime. Cutting waste to help ease the cost of living. More job and training opportunities. I will listen, act, and treat everyone with fairness and respect, regardless of background, culture or race, together we can build a better Swindon.

I have lived and worked in Swindon all my life. My father served as a town councillor after a career in the military, my grandparents worked for GWR before running a local pub, experiences that grounded me in the values of community & service. I bring a creative, compassionate & community focused approach, with strong skills in research, planning & problem solving.

I have lived in Swindon my whole life. I have over 15 years’ experience leading transformation programmes & working knowledge of Swindon Council. I am focused on building a secure future for our children and our town.

I grew up locally and came back in 2023, shocked by the decline. I’m standing to bring back pride, improve our town and build a Swindon that embraces its potential and offers real opportunity for everyone, not just be a commuter town with a famous roundabout.

I am a dedicated member of the local community, committed to making a positive difference for all of our residents. I understand the real challenges people face every day. Passionate about improving local services, supporting families, and creating opportunities for everyone. I am focused on delivering real solutions that benefit our whole community. I believe in listening, working hard, and standing up for what matters most to residents. Family, Community, Country.

Leroy Roberts is a British Army veteran and currently works as the Executive Officer of a Credit Union. As a Parish Councillor and governor of a local junior school, he is hoping to use his community experience to serve the residents of Haydon Wick on Swindon Borough Council.

Ravi Venkatesh has been a Borough Councillor since 2023. He has deep roots in the community, with both of his children having attended Haydonleigh School. He is passionate about listening to residents and building a safer, stronger and more connected community for everyone.

Stanka Wilson has called the Haydon Wick ward home for ten years and has served as a Borough Councillor since 2023. She is committed to building a better community and works tirelessly alongside residents to create lasting improvements. Outside her professional duties, Stanka listens, acts and champions positive change for all of us.

Marcus Kittridge is one of your Green Party candidates for the brand new Kingshill Ward.

Marcus has lived in the ward for 45 years, raised his family here and his grandson is growing up in the same community. He wants him, and every young person to inherit the best version of Kingshill and Swindon.

Marcus is standing for election because he wants our community to get the best possible outcomes from the local council; better amenities, practical solutions to long-standing problems, and a stronger voice for residents who deserve to be heard.

Marcus was an engineer for 30 years. He switched career and drove Swindon Dial A Ride community transport minibuses for 8 years and more recently he ran a successful local independent business in the heart of Swindon for the last 10 years.

If elected in the local elections in May this year, Marcus will work tirelessly on your behalf.

I’m Rosie Leather, one of your Green Party candidates for the new Kingshill ward.

Born and raised in Kingshill ward, I am now raising my own young family here while actively supporting local community projects.

I have worked in the public sector for over 20 years, including in the NHS and now in research and innovation. You may recognise me from working at Swindon Pulse Wholefood Co-operative during this time too.

I am a former South Swindon Parish Councillor for the central Swindon area and supported improvements to Westcott Rec, Cambria Bridge and GWR Park.

I am committed to fairness and equality and determined to build a brighter future for Kingshill and Swindon.

Peter Major - Reform UK candidate for Kingshill

Swindon has been my home for 26 years. My family is here, my children grew up here, and my grandchildren are growing up here now. When I talk about safer streets and services that actually work, it's not campaign language - it's a question about the town my grandchildren will inherit.

26 years here is long enough to see how Swindon has changed - both ways. Antisocial behaviour has crept up. Council tax goes up every year while services don't. Potholes outlast the seasons. The town centre after 8pm is not somewhere most residents want to be.

Reform UK is the only party today willing to cut through bureaucracy and demand answers from those spending your money. I'm asking for your vote on 7 May to bring those standards into the Council Chamber.

Josh is a resident of Lower Stratton where he lives with his family. He wants to play his part in making the area safer and an even better place to live by representing Lower Stratton and Coleview as a borough councillor.

Swindon is my hometown, where I've lived all my life, and I hold a deep sense of community and local pride. I am passionate about delivering solutions together and improving critical public services. I believe this work is urgently needed and I am dedicated to making it happen to help our community thrive.

Leon has lived in Grange Park for nearly 25 years and in Swindon for over 30 years. Leon is a product development manager at a local pharmaceutical development and manufacturing company where he has been employed for over 25 years.  In this role he has gained experience of risk management, negotiation, planning and budgeting all of which help in the role of councillor.

As a Parish Councillor I have been involved with South Swindon Parish’s projects to improve our parks, play areas, allotments and our Library. As an IT Consultant, Andy has worked for some of the biggest global names in finance, retail, and manufacturing. As an Old Town resident, I’m proud to be standing for election where I Iive.

Please vote for me as your Labour & Co-operative Party Candidate on May 7th.

Jocelina has dedicated herself to helping others through her work with the Helping Heart charity. She is driven by compassion and a commitment to making life better for locaal people. Jocelina understands the challenges families face and will fight for fairness and dignity for all. With deep roots in our community, she will be a powerful voice for local people.

Swindon has been my home for 50 years, growing up as a farmer’s daughter and granddaughter of a railway worker, both who also fought for our country, gave me a strong foundation. I want to be a voice for the people of Parks & Swindon to listen & act!

I have lived in the Swindon Parks Ward for over 50 years, and I am concerned about the great many potholes and the high cost of house prices and rents. The cost of living crisis has made life very hard for everyone in Swindon and especially the young generation who are just starting out in life.

Jamal has been a Borough Councillor for Walcot and Park North since 2021 and has served on South Swindon Parish Council since it was created.
