Charli has lived in Swindon for her whole life and works in the adult social care sector as a Care Manager. Charli has worked in the sector since 2019 and is passionate about enhancing the lives of those with complex needs.

Charli cares about the environment and is keen to get locals involved with community efforts to uphold this.

Charli volunteers at an animal sanctuary and a community interest group that runs accessible events for adults with additional needs.

Charli is a member of the Young Greens and wants to do more to engage the younger generation within the local community.

I’m Paul Park, and I’m standing to be your **Labour & Co-operative** councillor because I believe in the power of communities working together to create real change.

I’m proud to stand as a Labour & Co-operative candidate, because I believe in social justice, equality, solidarity, and the power of people working together to improve our community.

Working with the council to ensure roads and footpaths are properly maintained

Pushing for more reliable timetables, better routes, and stronger links across North Swindon

Working with residents and local groups to protect natural areas and improve access

Supporting enforcement action and practical solutions to keep our area tidy and safe

Building on the success of local youth initiatives to give young people more opportunities

Energy, integrity, and teamwork in everything I do

Paul has been a councillor in Swindon representing Eastcott ward since 2015. He is currently the Cabinet Member for Children's Social Care. I live in Swindon and have been a local councillor for Eastcott since 2018. Swindon residents are crying out for change and this can only be achieved by a change of local Government.

We have to reverse the gross inequalities that force families on low incomes to rely on food banks and we have to pursue policies that promote genuine social inclusion.

I hold a higher degree in Psychology and Human Resources, and I work as a Technical Recruiter in a technology company. My professional background has taught me the importance of listening carefully, understanding people’s needs, and making balanced, evidence-based decisions. Every day, I work with individuals from different backgrounds and countries, which strengthens my belief in international collaboration and cooperation.

As a single parent, I understand the pressures many families face — especially with the rising cost of living. I know how difficult it can be to balance work, childcare, and financial responsibility. That is why I care deeply about practical support for families, accessible education, and strong local services.

I’m Stan Pajak, I was born in Swindon, and I’ve lived here here all of my life. I am married to Dawn and we have four children. My two daughters perhaps following their mum are involved in education in local schools with one a secondary school assistant head and the other teaches at primary level. As for my two sons one works in Epic Games as a QA specialist - just as well he ignored me telling him not to waste his time playing games! While the other is a project manager in digital media. We have four grandchildren. Which I’m told keep us young!

It was very early on in my life I realised I wanted to get involved in local things and local politics. At work I became a trade union shop steward working for people and helped fight the threat of redundancies.

I first got elected in 1985 as a Wiltshire County Councillor when the Liberals together with the SDP took control. In 2002 I became mayor of Swindon. It was an amazing year. I became one of the few mayors ever to take part in the Moonwalk a walking marathon through the night time streets of London raising funds for breast cancer. I had the honour of speaking for the Council at the funeral of Wroughton’s famed councillor Harry Garrett who is remembered in the village through Harry Garrett Court.

Having retired I work as a volunteer at the Prospect as a volunteer at their Media shop. I have never been a great athlete but enjoy running and last year ran the Swindon Half Marathon raising funds for the Prospect. My marathon running days are over!

This is my second time standing for Wroughton and Wichelstowe and the issues have not changed under the Conservative and Labour administrations - too many houses in Wroughton under both the local plans of the Tories and Labour, our campaign for a new Health Centre in Wichelstowe - it should have been built years ago and the tackling of the disgraceful amount of potholes on our local roads.

If elected I will be dedicated to the people of Wroughton and Wichelstowe keeping in touch and getting things done.

I am standing as Green Party candidate in Ashton Hurst to ensure the people in my community have the opportunity to vote for a party that represents their best interests. For the people trying to get by during the cost of living crisis, yet feel no support from those in power and to offer an option for unity and solidarity in a world that’s evermore divided.

I joined the Green Party because it feels like a beacon of hope in UK politics. We offer an alternative to parties that use division and hate as a means of distracting electors from the key issues affecting daily life. The cost of living, the housing crisis, climate change, drug abuse; the Green Party aims to tackle these problems at the root, reemphasising what should truly be at the heart of politics- the People. I believe that at its core, we all want the same thing; to see improvement in everyday living, to ensure our families and our communities are looked after and to keep our streets safe. I believe the Green Party best resonates with this message and serves as our best chance at seeing real change.

Danny is a lifelong Tameside resident, a happily married family man, and someone who understands the area and the people who live here.
With a post-graduate qualification from the University of Salford in employment law policy and practice, alongside a successful career in operations management, Danny brings a strong understanding of how organisations should work - and where they often fall short.

In his current role as part of the HR operations team of a national health and social care charity, he sees first-hand the pressures facing services and the importance of getting decisions right for both staff and the public.

That experience gives Danny a grounded, practical perspective on how Tameside Council can better deliver for residents - particularly when it comes to improving Adult Services and ensuring support is consistent, accountable, and effective.

We are proud to support Danny as our candidate for Ashton St. Michael’s. He will be a thoughtful, reliable voice on the council - focused on delivering better outcomes for the people of Ashton St Michael's and Tameside after 48 years of neglect.

Our communities deserve better.

Better than rising bills, stretched services, and decisions made without local people in mind. Better than pollution, neglected green spaces, and short-term thinking.

The Green Party stands for a different kind of politics - one that puts people, planet, and future generations first.

We will:

Protect and improve local green spaces
Push for properly funded public services
Support affordable, energy-efficient homes
Back local businesses and good jobs
Demand honesty, transparency, and accountability in politics

Local politics should be about what works for our communities and delivering for people. Labour have neglected Tameside, and Reform have no answers for the local concerns of residents. Vote for hope over fear and division.

A vote for the Green Party is a vote for practical solutions, fresh thinking, and real change.

It’s time to do politics differently.
Vote Green.

I’m Emma Jones — Waterloo business owner, community champion and now your truly independent candidate for Waterloo in Ashton-under-Lyne in the local elections on Thursday 7th May 2026.

Born and bred in Waterloo, this community shaped who I am and I’m committed to its future.

​

I’m standing as an independent because there’s too much playground politics locally and not enough focus on real solutions for real people.

As the founder and owner of a multi award-winning local business, I’ve built my career around care, respect and putting people first. My approach has always been hands-on, practical and personal. I will bring these values directly into public service.

​

I’m married, with two children and two dogs. Family life keeps me grounded in what truly matters. I love the outdoors, country walks and spending time with family and friends. I believe our community deserves practical, compassionate leadership that listens, is inclusive and delivers.

​

I’m not a career politician — I’m a working mum, a neighbour and someone who sees the issues on our streets every day. Whether it’s supporting vulnerable residents, improving access to mental health services, protecting small businesses or giving local people a stronger voice, I will always stand up for fairness community, and common sense.

​

I’m asking for your vote, not just to represent you, but to work alongside you. Let’s bring compassion, independence and trust back into our council.

I’m proud to stand as your Labour candidate for Ashton Waterloo Ward.

Having lived in Ashton-under-Lyne for over 20 years, I understand our community ,its strengths, its challenges, and its potential. Through my work with community organisations, I’ve helped residents access support, create opportunities, and strengthen local connections. I’ve seen firsthand that strong communities are built on fairness, responsibility, and people who care enough to take action.

I am standing in the May 2026 election because I want to make a real difference. I will listen to residents, understand local concerns, and work hard to ensure residents of Waterloo Ward feels supported, heard, and valued.

My Priorities

Safer, Cleaner and Greener Waterloo
I will work with residents, the council, and local partners to tackle litter, improve street cleaning, and ensure our neighbourhood is safe, tidy, and welcoming for all.

Standing Up for Older Residents
I will champion the needs of older residents, making sure their voices are heard and they receive the support and respect they deserve.

Supporting Young People
I will work with schools, youth groups, and community organisations to create more opportunities for young people and help them reach their full potential.

Bringing Our Community Together
I will support local groups and community activities that bring people together, building a stronger, more connected neighbourhood.

IT HAS been a privilege to serve as a councillor in Audenshaw for the last three years, working hard to act on your priorities.

- I opposed developers who wanted to turn Fairfield View Care Home into a 57-room ‘co-living’ HMO. We took action to stop these plans.

- I am supporting small businesses like The Pearl in their fight against a supermarket giant; proposals that would cause chaos in Audenshaw.

- I helped to stop proposals for a housing estate and business park on Fairfield Golf Club; I’m now working to secure the long-term protection of the site.

- We brought events like Band In The Park, Film Nights and our Christmas Lantern Parade to Audenshaw – events enjoyed by families across the town.

- I secured improvements to our roads, got potholes fixed, streetlights repaired and worked to keep our town clean.

I have a track record on working hard for our town, and hope to continue to be able to do so.  If re-elected, my priorities will be:

1) Protecting Kingswater Greenspace
2) Improving road safety, pushing for a crossing on Audenshaw Road and to reduce speeding on Manchester Road
3) Protecting small businesses, opposing the plans for a Lidl on Manchester Road
4) Investment in our highways, parks and play areas
5) Fighting flytipping across Audenshaw and keeping our towns clean.

The Green and Reform candidates have not set out any plans for what they would do if elected; I am the only candidate with a positive plan for Audenshaw.  Please re-elect me on May 7 so I can continue to deliver for you.

Through my interest in amateur dramatics, I have met people of all ages from the whole of Tameside, many disenchanted with politics both national and local. I was among them. Until I was introduced to the Green Party which offers real hope to real people from real people.

I am passionate about Tameside, especially my hometown of Denton, passionate about improving life for all of us, and passionate about listening to what matters most to our residents.

There is much to be proud of in our area but also much that needs to change. Houses are springing up on any piece of available land, reducing our access to health-giving green spaces and compounding problems with parking. Meanwhile, empty properties stand neglected, our teenagers roam the streets for want of affordable alternatives, as we choose between heating or eating.

Vote Green and I will fight for a fairer deal and better future for everyone in Denton North-East and Tameside as a whole.

A lifelong resident of Denton and a happily married father of two young boys, Aron is deeply rooted in Denton North East.

Aron is a Christian actively involved in the running of a Denton-based church. He has also led a successful 15 year career as an IT professional, currently leading a service team as well as contributing to the running of a small family business.

Aron brings a strong sense of responsibility, organisation, and service to others. His background reflects both leadership and a practical understanding of how to get things done efficiently and effectively.

Passionate about ensuring young people have access to sport and recreational opportunities, Aron recognises the role this plays in building confidence, discipline, and community spirit.

He is committed to protecting Denton’s green spaces and standing firmly against overdevelopment, ensuring the area remains a place families are proud to call home.

As a branch, we are proud to support Aron as our candidate for Denton North East - a principled, grounded voice for local residents on Tameside Council.

Hi - I’m Alex

I’d like to tell you a bit about myself and what I believe in.

I was born in Manchester and I live in Tameside, and I believe deeply in the power of politics to make things better for people. We can see the impact that Labour has had on Greater Manchester - now the fastest growing city in Britain.

I want to make my pledges for Denton South clear:

I’ll stand up to developers - on sites like Two Trees Field and Bredbury Parkway

I’ll advocate for more youth services in Haughton Green

I’ll take on United Utilities and protect the Tame Valley from further pollution

I’ll push the council to invest in our roads, and undo the damage of years of underinvestment by central government

I hope that you’ll consider me, it would be an honour to serve as your councillor - if you need anything from me, please drop me an email or Facebook message.

Born, raised and residing in Denton and Haughton Green, Audra has a lifelong connection to the local area and the local community.

From helping in her parents’ newsagent on Mill Lane to running a successful floristry business for 15 years, Audra understands the value of hard work and the every day struggle to provide for a loving family whilst operating a local business.

Audra has extensive experience working in local governance in amenities and waste and has first hand experience of the real challenges facing residents, as well as the road blocks getting in the way of getting things done in the public sector environment.

Her contributions to award-winning work has focused on tackling fly-tipping, improving neighbourhoods, and maintaining green spaces, giving her a practical, hands-on approach to delivering visible results for local people.

Currently working in community projects and with experience in the Prison and Probation Service, Audra brings a disciplined, grounded outlook and a strong belief in setting the right example.

As a mother of three, she is committed to improving opportunities for young people, supporting families, and restoring pride in Denton South.

As a branch, we could not be more excited to support Audra as our candidate - a committed, experienced voice for the people of Denton South and Haughton Green.

I am delighted to stand as a candidate for the Green Party in Denton South.

Having lived in the area for over 10 years, I know how it feels to be left behind.

I have been campaigning nationally for gambling reform since 2023. In my opinion, the gambling industry is one of the most blatant displays of a transfer of wealth from the most vulnerable in our communities directly into the pockets of billionaires.

I have had first hand experience of politicians putting the interests of powerful lobby groups ahead of the people they are supposed to represent, and I am determined to fight back.

I work full time in supply chain management,  alongside my work with various gambling harm charities.  I regularly help people who have been ignored to have their voices heard, whether this is in the media or in parliament.

This is what I want to do for the people of Denton South.  For too long, our votes have been taken for granted by the Labour Party.  We proved recently that we won’t be taken for granted any more.

Vote Green in May for a Councillor who cares.

statement_to_voters:
Dan is a lifelong resident of Denton West and a proud supporter of Denton West Cricket Club with firm family roots in the area and a genuine understanding of the community he is standing to represent.

As an NHS worker and IT professional, Dan brings both frontline public service experience and the technical expertise needed to modernise how Tameside Council operates. He is focused on improving digital infrastructure, cutting waste, and ensuring taxpayers’ money is used efficiently to deliver better services.

Dan is committed to protecting Denton’s green spaces and standing firmly against overdevelopment, ensuring the character of the area is preserved for future generations.

Honest, approachable, and determined, Dan is a man that residents can rely on. As a branch, we are proud to support him as our candidate - a competent, committed and capable voice for the people of Denton West on Tameside Council.

I’ve supported the Green Party for decades though only recently become active within Tameside helping my friends, family and neighbours resist divisive alternatives.

Work brought me to Denton, with my family, 5 years ago. I love the area so decided to retire here: To a friendly town with good transport links and enough countryside we can still breathe.

I want to improve our NHS, protect our open spaces and improve public transport options.  Denton is our home and I am keen to protect and promote all it’s wonderful diversity.

Your Party candidate for Droylsden East my hometown. Lifelong socialist and Trade unionist. UNISON national committee member for 16 years. I led strike action recently as UNISON Branch Secretary Greater Manchester Transport against Andy Burnham our political boss and gained improvements in pay, maternity pay and other improvements. 
Labour has neglected Tameside. There are boarded up shops, congestion problems, fly tipping problems in Droylsden centre. Labour has sat there passing on Tory cuts in funding from central Government for too long. I will be accountable to residents.

I’m honoured to stand as the Green Party candidate for Droylsden East, offering my friends and neighbours the chance to vote for real change.

After nearly a decade as a member of the Labour Party, I came to realise in recent years that the pressing, everyday challenges facing local people were simply not being addressed. I know many others feel the same. That’s why I’m now standing for the Green Party – to show that there is a genuine alternative to the 2 party system ingrained in our country. The growing, grassroots support for the Green Party, and the fantastic response to the campaign in Gorton and Denton by Hannah Spencer MP and her team, shows that a different way forward is not only possible, but already taking shape.

As a science teacher, I see first-hand how deeply environmental, social and personal issues affect our young people. They are facing challenges we could hardly have imagined ten or twenty years ago, yet what stands out most is their determination and eagerness to be the change they want to see in the world. By investing in youth services and giving young people more opportunities to get involved in their community, we can help people of all ages feel empowered to shape the future of our area.

Our green spaces should be something everyone in Droylsden East can take pride in. We need to protect and improve our parks, waterways and open spaces, making them safer and more accessible for all. Doing so is not just an environmental issue, but supports our health, strengthens our community, and makes our area a better place to live.

As your councillor, I will ensure that local people of all ages are heard and given genuine opportunities to engage in local decision-making. By working together, we can build a stronger, fairer and greener future for everyone in Droylsden East.

As Labour’s candidate for Droylsden West, I am proud to stand for the community that has shaped my entire life. I was educated at Droylsden High School for Girls, have worked locally at The Pig on the Wall, and now serve as a registered nurse associate, caring mainly for elderly patients. Every day, I see the importance of dignity, compassion and strong public services.

I am raising my daughter here with her father, my partner of almost 20 years, and like many local families, we want a safe, supportive and inclusive place to call home. As a union representative, I stand firmly for fairness, equality and respect at work and in society.

I believe our community is strongest when we come together. At a time when division feels all too common, I am committed to listening, representing everyone, and building a Droylsden West that works for all.

I am standing for Droylsden West to give people a chance to vote for something different.

Having moved to the Droylsden area not long ago I have seen both the growth and the let downs of the current council. I want to give a voice for our green spaces, local community and those who want a new, fresh voice to speak for them in their area.

I used to vote Green as a voice against the current system, I now stand with the Greens because I believe in their manifesto and mantra; hope not hate.

I am standing in the local elections to give the people of Dukinfield an opportunity to vote for positive change. That change is the Green Party.

The Green Party puts the people first, committed to a fair society with improved opportunities and strengthened rights for everyone; a more just society that holds exploitative corporations accountable for their actions; and of course, a green society that invests in renewables, lowering our emissions, and ensuring our national energy security.

While Central Manchester has become one of Europe’s fastest growing city economies, the boroughs of Greater Manchester are struggling to feel the benefits of this growth. As a Tameside resident, I want to see our potential unlocked too, with towns that thrive, not just survive.

As your Councillor for Dukinfield, I will work tirelessly to help our town flourish, calling for investments that improve wellbeing and create a
healthier, and greener community. I will advocate with integrity, representing residents’ best interests and voicing concerns effectively to the council. And I will champion community-led action, backing important local projects that bring people together and create lasting impact. With the historic victory of Green MP Hannah Spencer in Gorton and Denton, the message is clear: Tameside wants change. So let’s turn Tameside Green.

I am standing for the Green Party in Dukinfield and Stalybridge to help give every single person the opportunity to vote for a council that genuinely cares for local residents and listens to our concerns. As a resident of Tameside, I take great pride in the wonderful community projects and spirit that help to make this borough a beautiful, welcoming, and joyful place to live. But I also believe that the incredible volunteers who dedicate their time to our community are forced to do so to replace services our council is supposed to be responsible for. When society functions on the back of unpaid, uncredited hard work, the system is broken. I will look to work closely with the organisers of community projects to ensure that their services are both supported and properly reimbursed.

I have worked full-time in retail for 15 years— whilst also studying towards a Master’s Degree in Philosophy, so I know very well how regular working people have been left behind. I want to make a difference. I want to show that there is an alternative version of politics in which we are not the football but the players. The Green Party will always put people’s needs before corporate profits: The Green Party will always protect the interests of our communities; And I will always listen, engage, and communicate with the real stakeholders of Dukinfield and Stalybridge: our residents.

I have lived in Tameside for most of my life and have always worked locally, within retail, transport and travel.

I decided to stand as candidate for Hyde Godley to ensure the option to vote for a local, Green candidate. If you want Green, vote Green!

I am frequently seen litter picking along with my children.

The Green Party prioritises striving for a cleaner, greener and healthier place to live.

I appreciate the need to encourage safe alternatives to car travel by encouraging those who can, to walk, cycle and to travel using affordable, reliable public transport.

I support local campaigns to save Tameside’s countryside and oppose plans to replace fields with tarmac, increasing the risk of flooding. Bulldozing greenbelt when levels of rainfall are increasing is a strategy for disaster.

Our green belt and other green spaces are essential for the health and wellbeing of people too.

My Journey as Chairman of GMCA  Since the year 2019 I have had the honor and privilege of serving as the Chairman of the Greater Manchester of Chattogram Association (GMCA). Additionally,

Growth and Development of GMCA When I first assumed the chairmanship of GMCA, our membership was modest, with only 20 dedicated individuals. Over the years, through persistent effort and community engagement, I am proud to say that our membership has grown exponentially. As of May 2024, we have 252 active members. This significant growth is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our committee members and the vibrant community we serve.

GMCA is more than just a committee; it is a community group that aims to foster unity and support among the Bangladeshi community in Greater Manchester. We organize multiple events throughout the year, providing platforms for cultural exchange, community support, and celebration.

A Landmark Event: The 19th May Gathering One of the most significant milestones in my tenure as chairman was organizing one of the largest events for the Bangladeshi community on the 19th of May. This grand event, held in Oldham, attracted over 3000 attendees, marking it as one of the biggest gatherings in our community's history.

The event was graced by distinguished guests, including the Ambassador from the Bangladesh Embassy the Mayor of Tameside Council, the Mayor of Oldham, , and several other notable figures. Their presence underscored the importance of our community and the strength of our cultural heritage.

The success of this event was a collaborative effort, reflecting the dedication and hard work of our GMCA members. It was a day filled with cultural performances, inspirational speeches, and a sense of unity and pride among the Bangladeshi community.

After much thought, reflection, and encouragement from many of you, I am honored to announce my candidacy for Member of Parliament for the constituency of Altrincham and Sale West. Our community is vibrant and diverse, filled with hardworking individuals who strive every day to make a better life for themselves and their families. It is this spirit of perseverance and unity that inspires me to serve you. The challenges we face are numerous, but together, we can overcome them. Our schools need better funding, our healthcare system requires more support, and our local businesses deserve robust backing to thrive in today's competitive environment. I pledge to be a voice for all of you, advocating tirelessly for the resources and policies that will benefit our community. I am not just running to hold a position; I am running to bring about meaningful change. My campaign will focus on:

1. Secure, Decent Housing as a Right: Everyone deserves a safe and stable place to call home. I will work to ensure that secure and decent housing is a right for all, not a privilege for the few.

2. Renationalising the NHS: Our National Health Service should serve the people, not private interests. I will fight to bring the NHS back into public ownership, ensuring high-quality healthcare for all.

3. High Quality Free Nursery Education and Childcare: Every child deserves the best start in life. I will advocate for free, high-quality nursery education and childcare to support our families and future generations.

4. High Quality Free Lifelong Learning: Education should not stop at any age. I will promote policies that provide free, high-quality lifelong learning opportunities, so everyone can continue to grow and thrive.

5. Peace Not War in Palestine: I believe in justice and peace for all. I will stand for a foreign policy that supports peace, not war, in Palestine and around the world. However, I cannot do this alone. I need your support, your ideas, and your energy. This campaign is not just about one person; it is about all of us, working together for a brighter future. Let us embark on this journey with hope, determination, and a steadfast belief in the power of our community. Thank you.

Sam is a lifelong Tameside resident who has lived in Newton for over 48 years. A devoted husband, father and grandfather, his family is at the centre of everything he does and his reason for stepping into local politics is simple: to help secure a better future for his grandchildren.

Having recently retired from his career as an HGV driver, Sam has built his life on hard work, reliability and getting the job done - values he will carry into public service.

Alongside this, he holds a BSc in Physics from Queen’s University, exemplifying his strong intellect and analytical approach to problem solving.

Sam is passionate about ensuring young people have access to practical skills and opportunities, helping them build confidence and direction in life.
 
Keen to support local businesses and promoting local job opportunities, the forefront of Sam's motivation is giving back and ensuring that Newton, Hyde and Tameside is a better place for the generations to come.

As a branch we could not be more thrilled to announce Sam as our candidate for Hyde Newton.

Grounded, approachable, hard-working and driven by strong family values, Sam will be a dependable voice for the people of the area.
"improving the community, organising popular Fundays, and helping bring the MELA to Hyde Park"

I’m standing in the local elections to give the residents of Hyde Newton a chance to vote for real change.

Like so many others, I have become disillusioned with the two historic parties of power and the divisive mainstream media that wants us to believe our neighbours are our enemies. I joined the Green Party last year with the hope of building a society that works for everyone – and my only regret is not doing it sooner.

I work for an animal welfare charity and I believe that our compassion should extend to all living beings and the environment.

I understand the very real challenges we face – with bills and household costs rising day on day while billionaires get richer in their sleep. The Green Party is the only party standing up to powerful people and institutions on behalf of regular people like you and I. Vote Green for hope in Tameside.

I am standing to give the people of Hyde Werneth the opportunity to vote for a Green candidate.

I’m proud to stand representing a party that believes in hope not division, and is working to build a fairer and greener world. If elected that is what I’ll be championing by pushing for practical steps such as improving home insulation to combat rising energy costs, and Improving public transport and safer walking and cycling routes to reduce dependency on cars and increase options for those who can’t or don’t want to drive.

The recent by-election has shown that a vote for the Green party is not just a protest against the mismanagement of Labour and the Tories, but a real chance to push for positive change.

Christopher is a proud resident of Hyde Werneth with strong family roots in Hyde, and a strong connection to the local area.

Educated at Bredbury Comprehensive and self-employed from the age of 16, Christopher has built a strong reputation for competency and discipline in his career. His experience in corporate security, working with a major national energy provider, has given him a solid grounding in responsibility, safety, and protecting the public.

Christopher brings stability and commitment -a commitment that he will channel into focusing on the issues that matter most locally: sensible traffic management, dealing with potholes, environmental stewardship, deterring antisocial behaviour and ensuring that fly-tipping is dealt with.  Christopher is intent on getting the basics right.

With a calm, friendly and approachable demeanour, Christopher is motivated by a genuine desire to serve the public and give something back.  Having previously felt politically homeless, Christopher was drawn into politics by a belief in a common sense, pragmatic and accountable approach to public service.

A keen gardener, golfer and football fan, he is passionate about encouraging young people into sport and recreation, helping to build discipline, life skills and provide them with the toolset required to have the best possible start in life.

As a branch, we are proud to announce Christopher as our candidate for Hyde Werneth.  He will be a steady, reliable voice for residents - grounded in common sense, civic pride and a commitment to the community.

I am standing to give the people of Longdendale the opportunity to vote for a Green candidate.

As a Green Councillor I would work to progress Tameside’s Climate Change and Environment Strategy.

Given the dramatic increase in the cost of living, the obvious actions to pursue are firstly home insulation to lower energy bills, provide green jobs and reduce CO2 emissions. Secondly, safe walking and cycling infrastructure and better and cheaper public transport. This would reduce fuel costs for poorer residents as well as reducing both pollution and CO2.

Green-led councils across the country are already working on these issues.

Greens are already winners in Tameside having recently won the Gorton and Denton by-election. We need more Greens to continue challenging Labour on the environment and council tax bills.

I strongly believe in the positive values that immigration brings and the important benefits it offers to our country.

I moved to Mossley in 2021 after spending most of my adult life in London, inspired by two good friends who had made the move ‘back up North’ a couple of years earlier — I like to call them my “scout party”! I fell in love with Mossley on my first visit, and it didn’t take long before I was looking for a home here. I feel incredibly lucky to live in such a special place. From the stunning views to its rich history and thriving community of musicians, artists and creators, Mossley has a unique character that’s hard to find anywhere else. The shift from inner-city London life has been a real (and very welcome) culture change.

While I’ve been fortunate to build a successful career as a software engineer, I’ve also experienced some of the challenges many people face. As a shared-ownership leaseholder affected by the cladding scandal and rising service charges, I’ve seen first-hand how unfair and frustrating the housing system can be. In recent years, hearing voices like Gary Stevenson and Zack Polanski speak about wealth inequality has strengthened my belief that we need a fairer system — one that asks those with the most to contribute more, and puts people before profit. That’s what has driven me to become more active in the Green Party.

I’m standing because I care deeply about fairness, community, and protecting what makes places like Mossley so special. I would love the opportunity to work alongside local residents to support our community and help Mossley be the very best it can be.

Gary is a proud Mossley resident with deep family roots in the area spanning generations. A devoted family man and recent grandfather, Gary is firmly invested in the direction and the future of Mossley.

Educated at Audenshaw High School and a proud supporter of Mossley FC, Gary combines strong local ties with over 20 years’ experience as a Regional Contracts Manager and Estimator in the insurance sector. His background brings practical, real-world understanding of planning, development, and delivering projects on-time and under budget.

Gary will use that experience to push back against overdevelopment, protect Mossley’s green spaces, and fight to ensure that planning decisions reflect the needs of people of Mossley.

Gary has also given over 40 years to local brass bands, including 25 years as a Band Secretary and as a judge for the British Youth Band Association, alongside serving as a Church of England Church Warden.

As a branch, we are proud to support Gary as our candidate. He will be a committed, principled voice and a strong advocate for the town and the people of Mossley inside Tameside Council.

It has been an honour to serve Mossley since 2016. I am a WillowWood Patron, trustee of Home-Start-HOST, and a proud member of our Mossley community. I have worked tirelessly supporting local groups and am a strong, hardworking and reliable voice for residents.

My achievements include securing a lease for Mossley Community Centre; protecting vital green spaces such as Cosgrove Gardens; fighting Brookfields with a Woodland Protection Order; challenging unsuitable developments on Hanover Street, Andrew Street, Stamford Road and Woodend View. I continue to support residents on Hey Farm, backed Article 4 rules strengthening oversight of HMOs, implemented two hours free parking, improvements to parks, public spaces and street furniture, and helped launch our award-winning Mossley Farmers Market.

I will continue: 
* supporting residents & community groups
* protecting Mossley’s character
* growing a vibrant cultural offer for everyone locally

I’m proud to stand again for Mossley.

My name is Mel Clifford, and I am standing in the Three Rivers Rural division of Hertfordshire County Council.  The division stretches from Heronsgate through Chorleywood, to Loudwater and Sarratt and on to Kings Langley and Bedmond.  A beautiful part of the county, and one that I am proud to campaign for.
I have lived in various parts of the Division since 1989, that’s 36 years.  My mother lived on the mobile home park on Toms Lane in Kings Langley, and I later lived at 97 Toms Lane myself.  I’m no party man, parachuted in by Central Office like our local MP.  I was lucky enough to be offered the chance to serve by my local Reform branch.  I thank them for that opportunity.

Who are my opponents?

The Tories – running Hertfordshire County Council for over 15 years, have spent us into debt.  £60,000 is being spent every DAY on interest alone.
The Liberals – running Three Rivers since 1986, who have just spent a million pounds upgrading a bridge to the aquadrome, while spending more to close off paths in the park.
Between them they have driven our council tax bills up and up, while providing less and less in return.

What do my opponents promise?
	The same things.
They say they’ll fix the roads – according to the data some of the worst in the country.  But they won’t.  THEY are the people that left them to crumble.
They say they’ll fight for the green belt.  But they won’t.  Both are in favour of unsustainable levels of migration.  And if you have that you HAVE to build more houses.  Meanwhile in Kings Langley the council has approved the expansion of a traveller site on green belt land, which they’ve now rename to  “grey belt”.  Some protection.
My opponents say they’ll clean up our rivers.  My division is home to important and rare chalk streams – places of beauty – places of rare wildlife – places of refuge for us all.  Places full of untreated sewage discharged from Maple Cross and Chesham sewage treatment works.  Why?  Because we’ve built huge numbers of new homes without investing in the infrastructure needed to support them.
Now I know full well that this is a local election.  I know that many things are outside the power of a local councillor to influence, let alone control.  I know that ultimately local and county councils are hostage to the policies of the central government of the time.
If that central government chooses uncontrolled mass migration, then councils must allow housing to be built for them to live in.  They must supply the schools for their children, the doctors surgeries to keep them well, the hospitals for when they are sick, the roads for them to get to work, the water supplies and the sewage treatment for their homes.
The Tories and Liberals won’t admit that mass immigration poses these challenges – they want MORE of it, and whatever their council candidates say is meaningless given this simple fact.
Only Reform will do the things that a central government MUST DO if local government is to have a chance to succeed.
Only Reform will secure our borders, bring down net migration, and end waste on DEI and net-zero initiatives.
Sorry – got carried away there.  Back to local matters:
If elected I do solemnly swear that I will do all I can to protect and defend the area I have made my home, and love so much.  I will hunt out wasteful projects, and oppose them.  I will seek more efficient ways to deliver key services.  I will push for real focus on the council doing the right thing by us all – no more and no less.  No net zero vanity projects.  No DEI initiatives.  Just delivery of the services we pay for.
But you, as voters, get to decide whether I get elected.  Whether a Reform candidate gets elected.
I urge you all, if you care about your town, your county, your country – when you leave here – talk to your neighbours, your friends, your workmates and families.  Ask them all to come to the polls on the 1st of May, and to vote Reform.
Historically we know May 1st as May Day.  In Britain we have celebrated it as the start of summer for years beyond count.
Let’s make May Day 2025 the start of a summer in Hertfordshire.
Let’s elect Reform.
Thank you.

I am pleased to formally announce my candidacy for County Councillor in the South Oxhey and Eastbury Division in the upcoming election on 1st May 2025. I am proud to be standing for Reform UK.

As a fourth-generation resident of the area, born on 4th February 2002, I have deep roots in South Oxhey and Eastbury. My mixed-race heritage—my father being from Nairobi, Kenya, and my upbringing within my mum’s white British family—has given me a broad perspective on our community. However, my politics are shaped by my values, not my background. Like Reform UK, I support net-zero immigration, and I believe it’s crucial to have open, honest discussions on this issue without fear of being silenced. Given today’s political climate, my background allows me to push for policies that many other candidates may shy away from, not because they lack conviction, but because they risk being unfairly labelled.

My motivation to serve stems from my family’s long tradition of public service. My great-grandad was a firefighter, my nan a nurse who retrained as a teaching assistant for children with special needs, my grandad a Chief Superintendent in the Met Police, and my mum currently works with adults with learning difficulties. I understand the struggles that ordinary families face because I’ve lived them—I wasn’t handed everything on a plate.

In my professional life, I studied business at college while training as a lifeguard and swimming teacher, before going on to study law at Hertfordshire University in 2020. In 2021, I was diagnosed with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis, which forced me to leave university and prioritise my health. Despite this setback, I rebuilt my career, progressing to become a lead swimming teacher and later an Area Swim School Lead, managing multi-million-pound leisure facilities and working closely with schools and councils. At 23, I bring fresh energy, a business mindset, and real-world experience—not the recycled promises of career politicians.

I am running for County Council because I am deeply concerned about the direction of our country and our local community. We’ve been let down for too long, and I refuse to stand by while South Oxhey and Eastbury are ignored. My key priorities include:
	•	Better Funding for Schools – Ensuring proper investment in education, especially for SEND students, and introducing more life skills programs.
	•	A New Secondary School for South Oxhey – A fight worth having. If the council can spend £218 million on developments that harm local businesses, they can invest in the infrastructure we actually need.
	•	Adult Education & Retraining – Working with West Herts College to create more opportunities for local people to upskill and build new careers.
	•	Support for Local Businesses – Establishing a business hub in an unused space, providing funding and mentorship for startups and existing businesses.
	•	Tackling Crime & Antisocial Behaviour – More police patrols, better street lighting, and stronger action on burglary and fly-tipping. More importantly, preventing crime by giving young people real opportunities.

I would like to make sure that residents of Aveley are the ones shaping their local area, giving power to the people in deciding what happens to their village. For too long we have been asked for our opinion during consultations, just to be ignored as private investors are prioritised. I have lived in Aveley for 22 years, and would stand for many issues I have noticed myself such as:

- Fixing potholes caused by the neglect of our roads
- Preventing the illegal use of our roads by HGV
- Preventing fly-tipping in known locations such as Ship Lane
- Clearance of public footpath 145 which has been massively overgrown and therefore illegally inaccessible for years
- Protection and further accessibility of our green spaces
- Activities for young people such as bringing back the youth club and further investment into the library
- More public bins to prevent rubbish on the streets
- Blocking construction of private luxury housing that no one in the area can actually afford, and instead building much needed affordable council housing
- Work with other councils across Thurrock to bring bus prices back to their previous prices, before the removal of the national £2 fare cap
- Standing against proposed data centre development near Aveley, such as the ones proposed for North Ockendon, and the former Arena Essex site. Both of which would pollute the area, destroy green belt land, and raise water and energy costs.

These are only a few of my own personal thoughts on what the area needs, but as stated before I would always prioritise and amplify the voice of my community. I am a working class lifelong resident of Aveley and as such would stand for the needs of Aveley. If elected my first action would be to speak with as many residents as possible, and prioritise the most pressing issues we as a community face.

On 7th May, vote for a party that puts people and the planet at the heart of every decision. **Vote Green.**

Dr. Anna Fryer has always been interested in public service – “Growing up in Cumbria, my Mum and Dad were always encouraging us to look after others – no wonder my three other sisters also became Doctors and Teachers!” Anna’s philosophy is simple- the reason I am standing is because I have spent 20 years working in the NHS and to make patients life better, we need more people like me with real experience in health in Parliament, who understand the NHS and patient care. The last few years in the NHS and Social Care have been a failure of Government. Quite simply our citizens have found the NHS has not been there for them when they needed it most. This is not the fault of NHS workers but a choice by the Conservatives not to plan our services and staffing properly. It has been heartbreaking watching patients waiting in the Emergency Department for hours and even days. Patients face huge barriers in accessing care, be it difficulties seeing their GP or long waiting lists. This is a failure that this government should be ashamed of. A vote for the Liberal Democrats is a vote to save our NHS after years of Conservative chaos. One issue that has been raised time and again by the people of Pendle and Clitheroe on the doorsteps is the horrifying conflict in the Middle East and the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza. Anna says “I have spoken to many people about this conflict, and the unimaginable horror facing civilians. Tracey was born in Urmston and has lived in Trafford most of her life. In the autumn of 2021 she set up the Petition “no cones on Chester Road” in a direct response to resident’s frustrations caused by increased congestion and pollution in close proximity to 4 primary schools. At the time of presentation to Trafford Council, it had achieved 2,742 signatures and media coverage. In addition to which, Tracey has actively assisted a local community group to “green the alleyways” securing a £6,000 grant from Groundworks.

Life for Tracey has been a bit of a rollercoaster and she expects that to continue in our current uncertain climate. Tracey sincerely wishes to aid residents in their ups and downs too.

I am a Project Manager working in Civil Nuclear & Defence, helping to keep nuclear power stations operating.  I am also a committed Christian and care deeply about the local community and its wellbeing.

I have lived in Sale most of my life and as a parent I fear for our young people’s future.  I want to see our area safe and thriving.

I am deeply concerned not only about record council tax rises and poor services, but also the proposal for a new ‘community centre with prayer room’ on the Goodwood Field.  The overwhelming feedback I have received on the doorstep is that it is not needed or wanted by the local community and they feel it is being forced upon them by Labour and the Three Meem Foundation (an Islamic charity) without either their consent or proper consultation.

I will work with anyone – Save the Goodwood Field campaign, The Conservatives, or any other group who seek to legitimately oppose the development of what many are calling a Mosque on this precious recreational green space that is in near constant use and was gifted to the community by a local Farmer many years ago.

If you vote for me, I give you my personal guarantee that I will do everything I can to prevent this project from going ahead on the Goodwood Field and represent your interests more effectively at the council.

"Locally, nationally and globally - The biggest threat we ALL face is that of catastrophic climate breakdown.  Locally, nationally and globally - no one is tackling this. If we ALL make small decisions locally to address this, then we can make a difference nationally and globally."

We need councils and councillors who are truly accountable to the electorate.

And we need a new kind of politics based on our national interest and on a wide and continuing public debate about what our national interest is. This way we can get government that actually represents us.

The public are fed up with tick-box consultation exercises where governments at the local and national level pretend to listen to ordinary people. And it's not good enough for politicians simply to tell us that "the science says" this or "the markets say" that so there is no alternative. We need a real political dialogue where new ideas can be contested and debated. This has to start at the local level.

In local elections, residents are concerned about potholes, waste collection, green spaces and our streets. In all of these areas, I will work to ensure that the council works with local people to support ground-up responses and actions so that residents can have real ownership of their community life.

Councillors often claim they cannot control the biggest part of their budget as it's spent on statutory services mandated by central Government. But councils look to outsource all this service provision to private companies, often owned abroad by venture capital. Why should our rising council taxes go to line the pockets of shareholders? I will campaign for more services to be provided in-house so that more of our taxes go to the local economy and councils are forced to be truly accountable for their budgets. This will not be done overnight. But even small steps will increase the knowledge available in-house, meaning that councils will be better able to negotiate with external providers and local government will build up its capacity to provide services.

Vote for me in Sale Central if you want a councillor who will work to close the gap between local government and the people it is supposed to serve.

I'm standing as a candidate in Sale Central because I want to represent young people and give them a seat at the table. I have deep concerns about climate change and I am proud to stand for social justice. It would be an honour to be the first Green Party councillor in Sale Central :)

I live on Culverden Park with my family so this part of Tunbridge Wells matters to me - it’s my home.

My priorities if I am elected are:

- stopping over-development - the Lib Dems council’s new Local Plan will force thousands of houses on Tunbridge Wells. But there are no guarantees on water supply, infrastructure or public services. We need to put the existing community first and make sure we only allow development once the infrastructure is secured. We need to learn the lessons of the water crisis.

- protecting the Common - I support the fantastic work of the Friends of the Common. I’ve been disappointed the Council has not used its financial or other resources better to support the community campaign. I am standing because I love this town and this part of Tunbridge Wells in particular. I hope you will support me.

I am standing for Pantiles ward because I care deeply about Tunbridge Wells and want to play a more active role in shaping its future. Through my work with the Green Weald Alliance and local residents, I have already been engaging with key issues affecting our community, from road safety along Frant Road to the proposed development at St Mark’s and the concerns around Ramslye Farm. I have also been following local issues such as the future of the Colonnade and how it is managed for residents and businesses. I have been acting in this space because these issues matter, but I am now seeking a clear mandate to do more and to represent residents formally.

We need development that is responsible, sustainable, and genuinely aligned with local needs. Building executive homes on green spaces does not solve affordability challenges or infrastructure pressures, and it risks damaging the character and heritage of our area, including important historical assets. I will advocate for a brownfield and vacant homes first approach, protect our green spaces, and ensure that residents have a strong, credible voice in the decisions that affect them.

I am standing for election as the Alliance candidate in Park so that I can continue to work hard for residents as a local, independent councillor, free from the influence of a national political party.

Why vote for me?

- I was part of the team that delivered a community funded playground in Calverley Grounds.

- I challenged the proposed development on the edge of Calverley Grounds for a new town hall, office block, underground car park and theatre. After several years, this project was cancelled. The development would have cost taxpayers at least £108 million, and was likely to exceed £150 million.

- I pushed for the unused space in the Town Hall to be rented out from 2017. The Town Hall is now a thriving building with many small businesses using the building alongside Tunbridge Wells Borough Council.

- I worked hard to save several bus routes serving Hawkenbury and Tunbridge Wells.

- My wife and I launched and organised the annual Town Wide Yard sale since 2017.

- I have helped residents pull together to challenge rogue builders.

- Now, I challenge the spending of £68 million to redevelop part of Royal Victoria Place. The cost is likely to rise above £100 million. There are much lower cost and effective plans that could bring life back into Ely Court and the old food court in the shopping centre.

- I will push for Royal Tunbridge Wells to get a Town Council and work to ensure it gets more than the default set of assets (the allotments) in the local government restructuring.

As a Conservative, I am championing the Tunbridge Wells First campaign.

We face the most important point for Tunbridge Wells for many years. The Borough Council, will soon be abolished and a new West Kent or ‘all of’ Kent’ Unitary Authority created. I am campaigning for all discretionary services, local assets and appropriate services are assigned to a new Royal Tunbridge Wells Town Council. The Borough Council, with its existing Leaders, is more concerned with their position the West Kent. In other Boroughs, councils are signing letters of intent to allocate these assets, revenue and local services to their main towns. Our Council has been negative, claiming only allotments are guaranteed for inclusion by a new RTW town council.

As Dep. Chairman of the (non-political) RTW Town Forum, I did the detailed work (later confirmed by the Council) that showed we only receive £1.4 million is services specific to out town while RTW residents pay £2.8m in extra tax which should be earmarked for our town. This includes payments for our parks, the Common, community space and other discretionary services.

The strong finances and low council taxes of the Borough of Tunbridge Wells is based on the many assets accumulated over the last 30 years or primarily Conservative councils. Without the Borough’s ownership on the car parks, the RVP shopping plaza and many other assets, our taxes would be much higher. We would also not had the opportunity to buy the RVP lease without the foresight of Conservative Councils. We stand to loose so much if we allow all of these to be absorbed into the new Unitary Authority. They should be retained by a new Town Council.

I my tenure as Deputy Leader of the Borough Council during COVID, we helped ensure we had a positive accounting financial result throughout. I also set up and led the cross party investigation into the Town Hall. This committed, and achieved a unanimous agreement to transition it to shared commercial office and work space. I worked with developers, bus and taxis companies to investigate ways of financing town centre transport - a concept not followed by the current Lib Dem  Leadership. I championed the seating areas in the High Street and supporting an entrepreneur to clean up the Challybeate spring - making it an attracting feature while saving the council precious funds. I helped investigate and encourage the redevelopment of the old cinema site, meeting and problem solving with the previous owners and the new owners - Retirement Homes (a subsidiary of AXA)

Now the council plans to build a new cinema attached to RVP, borrowing £68m. At current interest rates (4.8% pa) now 5 times higher than pre-COVID rates (0.9%), the annual costs will be 5 times higher than the previous project. It is therefore critical a full economic case is made public, otherwise we could and up with a non-financial project draining council funds for years. Understand the economics is so important rather than simply the headline numbers and exaggerated cost numbers.

Tunbridge Wells parks and other assets should be owned and controlled locally.

Since 2019 it has been my privilege to serve as your councillor for Pembury and now Capel.

We need representation from people who care about this community and have the skills and passion to stand up for it.

The homes built here must be suitable for long-term living and affordable for everyone. We must not allow the council to continue breaking their commitments to us – where is our promised health centre? Why are they building on our parks and removing the greenbelt protections of our land?

Lea Bridge is my home – and I pledge to represent my community in the council.

**About Solene**

I have lived and worked in East London for over 17 years and have long been vocal in campaigning with and on behalf of local resident groups. I am not a career politician, but a local and outspoken resident who has grown increasingly frustrated with party politicians who fail to attend community meetings, respond to emails or properly represent the people they were elected to serve. I believe I can do a better job of addressing residents’ concerns than the current Labour councillors, whom many feel are largely absent.

I care deeply about my neighbourhood and the diverse community that calls it home. I see serious issues being overlooked due to weak representation: a lack of meaningful engagement, overstretched GP services, large private-sector tower blocks, neglect of nature and green spaces, dangerously high air pollution, unsafe playgrounds and a shortage of spaces for young people. At the same time, the council continues to approve major unaffordable developments that will dramatically increase the ward’s population, without strengthening the already strained public services serving Lea Bridge.

**What Solene stands for**

Residents are being ignored.

Parents don’t even try calling the GP anymore — it’s overwhelmed and impossible to reach — so they’re forced to take their children straight to A&E.

Neighbours are worried about more than 10 tower blocks being built on contaminated Gasworks land, over six years and within the same half mile. Neighbouring 3 schools including 2 nurseries and no guarantees on monitoring air quality and toxic dust on and in homes.

Our green spaces are essential. They protect our health, preserve wildlife, clean polluted air, absorb heavy rainfall and help safeguard us on a flood plain. Building over them puts our future at risk.

The council appears quicker to cooperate with developers than to stand up for residents’ interests.

Poor transport planning is damaging daily life. We’ve lost a key bus route, there’s no service down Orient Way, trains are unreliable, and rushed LTNs and poorly designed cycle lanes are creating congestion and pollution. Local residents know these streets best — they must be at the heart of these decisions.

Meanwhile, community buildings sit closed and neglected. Jubilee Park Pavilion should reopen to serve all ages and abilities. The Waterworks Centre should once again be the vibrant educational hub and café our community deserves.

**About Rosie**

I am a Londoner born and bred, and I have lived in the Lea Bridge ward for over a decade. Raising my family here, I understand the importance of community and I am increasingly aware of the impact local government decisions have on our day-to-day lives. I have worked in the entertainment industry for 20 years as a circus artist, performing around the globe and teaching performing arts to adults and young people of all ages.

I love the joy and connection that live performance can bring, and the expansive way in which circus pushes the boundaries of what is humanly possible. I believe we need this same approach in our politics, which is why I join the Greens in 2021. Too often ordinary people are left feeling powerless against big business and monied interests, without a real say in decision-making. But when we come together, our power is limitless.

**What Rosie stands for**

Having been encouraged to stand as a councillor by fellow Waltham Forest Green Party members, I am keen to meet other Lea Bridge residents and hear their concerns. I aim to promote the needs of ward residents as strongly as possible. Lea Bridge is one of the most deprived areas of Waltham Forest, with the lowest number of GP surgeries relative to its population.

It is vulnerable to overdevelopment, and multiple projects in the pipeline will put the community’s health at risk. I hope to scrutinise all plans affecting Lea Bridge residents and advocate for my community. I am also outraged by the inaction our current councillors have shown in relation to the war crimes being committed by the state of Israel with the help of the UK government. I promise to push the council to fulfil its commitment to divest pension funds from all companies complicit in war crimes.

**About Rob Gardner**
Rob lives and works in Leyton, helping run his family’s long-established business. He’s been involved in community organising that supports small and independent businesses across East London, and has helped run divestment campaigns to prevent universities investing in fossil fuels and the arms trade.

**What Rob stands for**
I’m standing for council because Leyton deserves better representation. Decisions are often made without properly listening to residents or supporting local businesses. I want to change that by being visible, accountable, and focused on the issues people actually care about. I’m keen to make sure the community is properly represented in the council and ensure Greens bring about transformative change based on their values.

I am standing for election in Leyton because working-class families in our community are being pushed to the breaking point. We are being priced out of our own neighbourhoods by skyrocketing, unaffordable housing, squeezed by low pay and a lack of secure work, and abandoned by devastating local cuts to the essential council services we rely on every day. It is time to fight back against austerity and demand a council that puts the needs of ordinary people before profit.

​Cut Rents

Restore Jobs

Restore Services

Low pay and the need to defend our union rep left
bus drivers at Lea Interchange with no choice but to go on strike. We had fantastic support from passengers and from socialists and trade unionists in Waltham Forest, and we won!

If we can organise against bad bosses, we can organise against councils trying to implement cuts, and we can bring together people to fight for the funding we need. If I get elected I will bring my experience of organising in the workplace to organising in our communities to fight against council cuts, for jobs, homes and services for all
• **CUT RENTS**
• **CREATE JOBS**
• **RESTORE SERVICES**

**VOTE AGAINST AUSTERITY, WAR AND DIVISION**

**About Daisy Richards**
Daisy has had a lifelong connection to Waltham Forest,b having been born in Whipps Cross and now living in Leyton. After a rewarding eigth year teaching career, she now works as a therapist; helping people navigate mental health challenges with empathy and practical support.

Daisy understands the link between living standards and wellbeing. She is standing to implement community-centred changes in Leyton. Daisy is a member of Waltham Forest for a Free Palestine and the Waltham Forest Community Coalition.

**What Daisy stands for**
I am standing in Leyton because I genuinely care about our residents; my neighbours. We deserve a bigger say in how our ward is run, with decisions aligned with community values and priorities.

I want Leyton to be a place where people from all different backgrounds feel safe, supported and welcome, whilst ensuring the basic needs of every resident is met. It is essential that lifelong residents of Waltham Forest are able to remain in the borough and therefore ensuring housing is affordable is crucial.

I will amplify the voices of our community, to create the future we deserve.

**About Demetrius Williams**
I’m standing to be a Green Party councillor because our borough deserves councillors who are visible, honest and focused on what matters to residents.

As a local campaigner and Waltham Forest resident, I’ve worked with a number of local community groups that amplify underrepresented voices in the borough. This includes Waltham Forest for a Free Palestine, which is currently working to hold the council accountable to its pledge to divest its pension investments from companies complicit or linked to war crimes.

**What Demetrius stands for**
My priorities include:

_Housing and Green Spaces_
Push for genuinely affordable, high-quality homes that meet environmental standards and hold private developers to account. Protect our green spaces and preserve their biodiversity and community life.

_Health and Social Care_
Promote accessible, quality healthcare (especially for vulnerable residents) and strengthen local social care support.

_Safer, Cleaner Streets_
Tackle pollution, improve safety and keep our streets and public spaces clean, inclusive and well-maintained.

_Fair Local Economy_
Back small businesses and community groups that ensure support reaches those who need it most.

_Community Solidarity and Ethics_
Stand up for fairness, equality and environmental justice to ensure our borough acts with compassion.

I’ll put our community first. I’ll challenge complacency and lead with the energy, compassion and empathy needed to serve Leyton.

I was born in Whipps Cross and grew up in the area. I love living in Leytonstone, and that is mainly down to the people who live here. The community is so active in supporting others, and in making it a creative and engaging place to live in. I founded Leytonstone Folk; a monthly community music group, and I am involved in a number of local events and community groups. I feel really lucky to live here and would feel so honoured if elected.

I have been a teacher for 17 years, and have worked across mainstream, SEN and alternative provisions. I currently oversee provision for children who have barriers to education. I am a qualified Special Needs Coordinator and have been a Governor at a number of schools. I have learnt so much in my career that I am so grateful for. However, I have seen the number of barriers increase for families who are looking to get the right support for their children, and teachers becoming more stretched each year. We all deserve better and this is something I am really passionate about creating positive change for.

Prior to last year, I had rented in London for 18 years, so I know how challenging the housing market is, and how unbalanced and unfair it is. Rent increases are also impacting local businesses, and we really need to be putting pressure on the government to implement rent and business rate controls/decreases.

The environment and effective climate action is an area that needs a lot more focus. There are fantastic local initiatives around sustainability and collective food growing in the borough, and I would love to support this further and create more opportunities for growing, alongside other sustainability initiatives.

I value kindness and honesty, and making sure that everyone has access to the services they need. I want to listen, to help raise other’s voices, and I want to see more collaboration around decision making.

**About RoseMary Warrington**
Has lived in Leytonstone since 1985, joined the Green Party in 2009, is a retired IT Business Analyst, on the committees of Bushwood Residents Association, News from Nowhere Club, and Transition Leytonstone where I help run the Community Fridge.

**What RoseMary stands for**
I want the people of Leytonstone to thrive in a sustainable and strong community that works with the natural world, now and for future generations.

As your councillor I will be accountable and open, listening to your needs and concerns and working to provide the best possible service in a constrained and uncertain world.
