statement_to_voters:
**About Richard Wild**
Hi, I’m Richard. I was born in London and have been a resident of Markhouse now for over 20 years. I’m a criminologist and university lecturer but have always also been a human rights and trade union activist. I started a street group during lock down and do what I can supporting various local community and environmental groups.

It made sense to step up and see what I could do as a member of the Green Party in Waltham Forest but most importantly try to bring change and hope for my friends and neighbours in what are increasingly dark times.

**What Richard stands for**
Please vote for me as your councillor for Markhouse so that I can fight for you, for a safer, cleaner, greener and fairer Waltham Forest.

I think we can be much more ambitious together – improving air quality, public transport, affordable housing, and insulating to bring down bills. We need to be more radical and pro-social in our solutions in ways that supports everyone, are inclusive, prioritise the well-being of young people, the vulnerable and safeguards the future.

I would always seek to do this with the community, in a transparent and honest way, answerable to you.

*About David*

I live in St James Ward, my son goes to school here. My family are from Waltham Forest and my mum was a nurse at Whipps Cross. I work in the NHS as an art psychotherapist for CAMHS (Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services).

As a Unite rep I’ve doubled union membership in my workplace and been elected to the London and Eastern Regional Industrial Committee for Health.

I’ve been organising in this community for years, inside and outside of party politics. I’m standing as a councillor because it’s clear that only Labour or Green can win here, and this ward deserves better than what Labour has delivered.

*What David stands for*

St James is full of people already doing the work to make this a great place to live. What we need is a council that backs them rather than bypasses them.

I want to open up how decisions get made here, through genuine planning transparency, citizen assemblies and community-led development. On housing, that means exploring new methods of ownership for homes that are actually affordable.

For nature, that means council services that protect the green spaces we all enjoy. I’ve spent my career helping communities build from the ground up, and I’m ready to bring that to the council chamber.

I was born and raised in Walthamstow. was educated at Kelmscott School on Markhouse Road, learned to kick a football and ride a bike over St James Park and have lived at both ends of the ward. I work as a trade union organiser, fighting for social and economic justice for some of London’s most precariously employed and vulnerable public sector workers.

Growing up in our bit of Walthamstow has shaped my values and made me the person I am today, and it would be an incredible privilege to have the chance to represent you as your councillor and bring those values to Waltham Forest Town Hall.

I'm proud of the Waltham Forest Labour's record in our community:
- Regularly putting the borough in the top 5 for council house builders in the country (this is particularly important to me as a young person who's grown up in the borough and seen so many of my friends struggle with the choice between staying with their community or moving somewhere affordable)
- Delivering a brand new health centre for our community at Jazz Yard near St James Street
- Protecting and supporting local businesses, for example stepping in to keep CRATE St James open
- Proactively working with the police and other partners to tackle crime and antisocial behaviour in our community, whether that's knife crime affecting our young people, phone snatching at Blackhorse Road and St James stations or parcel theft across our ward

I promise if I'm elected in May, I will work tirelessly to serve and support our community.

I’ve lived in Walthamstow for 13 years, and many of you will know me from conversations on your doorstep. St James is a special place to me, and over the last four years as one of your councillors I’ve supported more than 1,000 local residents with housing problems, anti-social behaviour and other issues - a strong track record of getting things done for local residents.

I care deeply about this community and about making sure no one is left behind.

I’m not a career politician. I’ve worked since I was 15, and a Labour government changed my life. I’m now the CEO of a women’s centre and have spent over 20 years working in healthcare and supporting women and girls.

As your councillor, I’ve led work across the borough on health inequalities, initiated Waltham Forest becoming a Borough of Sanctuary, and supported declaring a nature emergency - putting those values into action locally.

Locally, I’ve helped secure the new St James medical centre and fought to save CRATE, protecting local businesses and jobs. I’ve also supported investment in our parks and green spaces, backed nature recovery and worked to create opportunities for local people. I’m Chair of Governors at a local primary school.

I’ll keep working hard for St James and standing up for local residents - and it would be an honour to have your support.

*About Martin*

I’ve lived in Waltham Forest since 2022, and grew up in Newham. I’m an NHS GP, so every day I see how poor housing, inequality and lack of access to care affect people’s health directly. I’m working hard to fix this.

I’ve led a cardiovascular outreach programme across Waltham Forest, and during the pandemic I protected vulnerable communities. I’ve heard many of our neighbours share a concern about inadequate GP provisions.

Only a loud Green voice on this council can advocate for fair care access.

*What Martin stands for*

I want to get the basics right: GP services, planning decisions made openly, and public money used to build long-term resilience rather than short-term profit. Councillors should answer to us residents, that’s the job.

The demolition of medical practices without adequate replacement is exactly what happens when developers aren’t held to account.

As a GP I understand the importance that strong health infrastructure and quality housing has on our wellbeing, and will be advocating for these on behalf of our community.

I'm not from here. I grew up in Aotearoa New Zealand, and was drawn to make St James my home because of its long history of artisans and makers. I own a small business, where I use my creative practice to imagine better futures.

I’ve used creativity to redesign parks, recruit teachers and help women advocate for better outcomes.

Having volunteered with care experienced young people for many years, I know a well run council could change everything for our young people. Our ward has a once in a lifetime chance to vote for hope, and I want to be part of that.

Labour has taken St James for granted and the evidence is on our streets: rising costs, dying trees, and young people with nowhere to go and nothing to do. We can’t afford a council that doesn’t work for us.

I want public money used to build community wealth for the long term. I want the council to invest proactively in the next generation rather than reacting when things go wrong.

And I want residents in the room when decisions get made about our futures, not told about them afterwards.

I have lived in Walthamstow for 20 years. I have actively helped build the incredible community spirit we have with an extensive list of volunteering locally including: volunteering at Eat or Heat our local food bank, co-founding Walthamstows first food pantry and refurbishing a building for a community living room that also provided early support to residents in need. I also co-founded Queens Boundary Community a resident’s group based in Markhouse ward.

Being part of protecting and enhancing our environment is important to me. I lead a local re-wilding group and together have greened Walthamstow Cemetery, a local park and rain gardens. Our cemetery meadow now hosts hedgehogs, bats, red list birds as well as rarer bees and butterflies.

I have organised a range of community cohesion events including park events, street parties, community iftars, exercise classes for women and children as well as commissioning Project Zero to support young adults in our local park.

I also chair my local Safer Neighbourhood Panel and volunteer for a local animal rescue  charity.

My career has been focussed within the charity and Local Government sector: two key areas of focus leading projects tackling climate change and more recently providing homes for Grenfell survivors.

I am passionate about Councils and the positive outcomes that can be achieved when we get it right: enhancing outcomes for our residents and improving our environment. I have the knowledge and experience that will enable me to get to work right away and my neighbours next door in Markhouse Ward can confirm that I will work hard and deliver!

**About Rbeeza Mobeen**
My name is Rbeeza, and I’ve lived in Walthamstow since primary school, so a lot of my formative upbringing was around these parts!

I’m now a social impact reporter for a fabulous little charity that combines art and activism to bring about social change, and love bringing my artsy expertise and lived experience as a first-gen migrant to our workshops and projects. You’ll probably find me at the libraries checking out a gazillion books (or asking for info on how to book the space for an event) or at the wetlands, doing a walk and talk with local charities.

I’m always looking to uplift the most marginalised voices in our community, and learning from those who came before me in the fights for justice.

**What Rbeeza stands for**
As a first-generation immigrant, I’ve seen what making non-abolitionist local reforms does to strengthen the existing social inequality in an area.

I stand for the populations residing in Waltham Forest: our communities, our livelihoods, and our chances at succeeding in life should be made easier and more accessible, rather than prioritising vacant luxury flats that none of us can afford.

I stand for the families in Waltham Forest whose politics are unheard and cast aside, and who feel that they’re being pushed to the sidelines as a result of ever-increasing socio-economic policies.

Caramel already works extensively in our community, and as your Councillor she will do even more for people.

A Chingford resident and higher education professional, Elizabeth is currently the only Labour Councillor in Chingford. Since being elected four years ago, Elizabeth has worked hard to support residents with thousands of issues and enquiries, and built a strong relationship with the local community in South Chingford as well as with local businesses. From securing investment in children’s play areas, to making our streets safer, Elizabeth has achieved results as a local Councillor. There’s more work to do and Valley needs a Labour team who will work with Elizabeth to get the very best deal for Valley.

Elizabeth's priorities for Valley are: • Make our streets cleaner and expand recycling • Conserve and expand our superb green spaces • Secure a new youth hub for young people in Chingford • Ramp up enforcement against fly-tippers • Make our streets safer and tackle speeding • Support Chingford Mount ‘s local economy to thrive • Continue to improve local play-spaces for children • Campaign for better transport links for South Chingford and Chingford Mount

*If I am elected as a councillor, I would work to strengthen community connections and ensure residents’ priorities are clearly represented.*
I've lived locally for almost 10 years and I work in higher education supporting student wellbeing. I am a  lifelong trade unionist and am standing as an independent to promote community-led politics and tackle growing inequality. I support the development of local People’s Assemblies to give residents a direct voice in shaping the future of South Chingford and the wider area. 
I am one of three *Chingford & Woodford Green Community Independents* standing, alongside *Saqeeb Howlader and Matt Romo.*
*Vote Independent in the local elections on Thursday 7 May and we pledge to:*
*Ensure the community has a say.* For too long, the needs of South Chingford have been ignored, and many of us locally feel that we have no voice. We pledge to hold People’s Assemblies for South Chingford, working with local community associations and the voluntary sector to support and empower the volunteers and community groups that serve our area and bring the community together.
*Develop a community plan for South Chingford.* Our area is poorly served for community services and public transport, and our town centre is run down. We will work with local community groups to create a South Chingford Area Plan that reaches beyond Chingford Mount, considering the needs of everyone living here.
*Hold developers to account.* South Chingford needs more housing, but it also needs development that invests in the local community. We pledge to hold developers to account on delivering quality local homes, including social housing, alongside the amenities that will improve our area.
*Develop a climate resilience plan.* Flooding, overheating and extreme temperatures which put our homes and families at risk are associated with the climate emergency. We pledge to embed climate resilience in everything we do, protecting our green spaces like Larks Wood, developing flood resilience across South Chingford and supporting home insulation and solar panels to cut living costs.
*Improve youth safety and services.* Many of you have told us of your anxieties about crime and the impact on the safety of our young people. We pledge to work with youth groups, community support teams and others to create safe spaces for young people and reduce the risk of anti-social behaviour and crime.
Call out the delays in replacing Whipps Cross Hospital. Our hospital is falling apart and now won’t be replaced for at least ten more years. We will campaign for the new Whipps Cross our community so desperately needs now.

As a new father and local resident, my priority is building a community where every family can thrive in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment. I am standing as an Independent to ensure our area is driven by our residents’ needs, rather than Westminster party lines. As a Fellow of the ACCA with an MBA, I offer the professional expertise and motivation to provide the rigorous oversight needed to protect our vital services. I am motivated by a sense of duty to ensure our ward is managed with integrity and a true focus on the needs of our community.

For much of my life I remained apolitical, but that changed as I witnessed a growing culture of mismanagement and a political landscape that too often relies on gaslighting and self-interest. This disillusionment deepened with the conflict in Gaza, which exposed a painful gap between the values of compassion we claim to hold as a nation and the reality of our political actions, which are now too often focused on division and empty slogans.

As a new father, I recognise that the foundations of my child’s future begin in our local community, in the very streets and services we use every day. I want Chingford to be an environment where everyone can thrive - a place defined by safety, opportunity, and a genuine sense of family and belonging. I have realised that we cannot simply wish for a better community; we have to be the ones to help build it. Driven by these values, I am standing for council to champion a vision centred on a true conscience, one that strives for an equitable society where everyone is treated with dignity, regardless of their background.

I have spent my professional life building expertise in financial and strategic matters, having earned my Fellowship with the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) and completed my Master’s in Business Administration (MBA). This professional background, combined with my experience in community governance as a Chair and Treasurer of local clubs and societies, equips me with the tools to provide the rigorous oversight needed to manage our resources responsibly. My focus is not simply on efficiency, but on ensuring that sufficient and proper provision is made for the services and priorities that are vital to our community. With your backing, I would like to bring this experience to work on your behalf, ensuring our local government operates with the integrity and fairness that our community deserves.

Find out more at www.cwgcommunity.org.uk

Promoted by Alistair Smailes on behalf of Chingford & Woodford Green Community Independents, c/o 110 Beech Hall Road, London E4 9NX

Born at Whipps Cross, I am a lifelong Chingford resident with 8 years experience working in the NHS and social care, instilling in me a sense of service to local people.

I know the area and will put residents’ voices at the heart of everything if elected, particularly those more in need.

Most recently I’ve worked in occupational therapy with older adults and disabled people in the community, assisting with assessments for home adaptations. Before that, in nursing, with adolescents in mental health crisis.

My first job in the NHS was in safeguarding, where I compiled information to track perpetrators of abuse and worked across agencies for the safety of residents. My first ever job was working at Sports Direct in Chingford for £5 an hour at 16.

In my new role working for NELFT in Waltham Forest, I am amplifying patient and carer voices, coproducing change and improvement to services, alongside those that use them and their families.

I’m proud to stand here, having competed with Chingford Rugby Club for 6 years and with Waltham Forest Gators in swimming.

A strong sense of community started out in the Scout Association, where I spent 11 years of my youth and volunteered frequently at Gilwell Park, running activities for young people.

I also volunteer at Hawkwood Nature Reserve, keeping local green spaces tidy where I grew up and volunteered at Highams Hub foodbank during COVID lockdown.

**About Ben Aaron Copsey**
Hi! I’m Ben, one of your Green Candidates for William Morris Ward. I’ve been living in Waltham Forest for nearly ten years, and have been active in the community for environment and people-first developments since day one in the borough!

I work in Access to Higher Education and am proud to say I’ve spent my professional life so far working towards educational equity for London’s amazing young people.

I know what we can do, together, when we put the effort in to listen, collaborate and put health, happiness and environment above austerity and developer profit margins.

**What Ben stands for**
As a Councillor I will stand very simply for the hope – and determination – that life for everyone in the borough can get better.

We deserve better air quality, protected green space and open land, investment in the areas of the borough that really need the help, and developments that work for the communities they’re in, instead of lining the pockets of developers at the cost of our health.

I will work for resident-led policy and democracy, clean air, green space, education, opportunities and enjoyment for our young people, and social justice at every level of government.

statement_to_voters:
**About Peter Ibrahim Kanyike**
I’m proud to have been born in Whipps, raised in Walthamstow, and went to school in Leyton and Leytonstone. My career is in health policy & strategy, systematically tackling inequalities and listening & working with community groups on their lived experiences.

Being a councillor would be an extension of my work serving and helping people to improve their lives.

I’m a revert to Islam for over 3 years, so you will find me in my local mosque or supporting the revert centre in Leyton. Otherwise, you will see me in the Gym in the Market or with my old schoolmates playing football in Goals Chingford every Sunday night!

**What Peter stands for**
As my career shows, I care about improving lives, especially those in need and the vulnerable. We have all been let down in our living standards for too long, yet I believe in hope and the possibility of change for good.

I found the Green Party as the place to continue this mission to help people across society, including those oppressed around the world through genocide and human rights abuses. From health services, to climate, to the local economy, to infrastructure & housing and beyond, I will work for a future where all people can contribute and are integrated into the decisions that impact their lives.

We will be a shining example to the rest of the country and I will deliver with honesty, transparency, accessibility and accountability.

**About Robyn Page**
I’m a proud Walthamstowaway, I’ve lived here since 2019. You’ll often find me queueing for a seeded loaf at Wild Grains bakery, enjoying a pint of Skoosh at Exale, or cycling down to the marshes on my bright red bike.

I’m a systems thinker, which makes me good at seeing the big picture. I’ve been using this skill for nearly two decades to solve complex problems in the arts industry. I’d love to use it to improve the lives of everyone in Waltham Forest.

I’m a knitter, a drummer, a cat lover, and I’m one of your Green candidates for council.

**What Robyn stands for**
I joined the Green Party as a student, because they were the only political party who understood that climate, social, and economic justice must go hand-in-hand. Sadly I think they’re still the only one.

A Plea for Restoration: From One Failing State to Another?
To the residents of our community,
I didn’t come to the United Kingdom just for a change of scenery. I came here for a future. 
Having grown up in South Africa, I have seen first-hand what happens when a nation’s infrastructure crumbles, when the rule of law becomes a suggestion, and when public funds vanish into the pockets of the incompetent. I lived through that "Third World" transformation—the potholes that become craters, the utilities that fail, and the sense of unease that settles over a neighbourhood when the authorities lose control.
I moved my life across the globe because Britain represented the "First World" standard: order, safety, and accountability. But lately, I look around and feel a haunting sense of déjà-vu. I see a country in decline, and I refuse to stand by and watch the UK repeat the mistakes of the country I left behind.
Faith, Morality, and Our Foundations
As a practising Christian, my world-view is shaped by the belief that a strong society must be built on a firm foundation. British society was built upon Christianity, traditional morals, and clear values. These are the pillars that once made this nation a beacon of stability for the rest of the world.
I value and respect these heritage values deeply. If we stop upholding the moral fabric that binds us—honesty, personal responsibility, and respect for our neighbours—we lose the very essence of what makes this country home. We must return to a system that rewards hard work and protects the vulnerable, rather than one that merely manages decline.
My Pledges to You:
 * End Council Waste: I’ve seen how "political stunts" drain a city dry. We will scrap vanity projects and bloated bureaucracy. Your hard-earned money should serve your family, not a councillor’s ideological agenda.
 * Put Frontline Services First: In a First World nation, the basics are non-negotiable. We will prioritise filling potholes, reliable bin collections, and community safety. If the basics aren't working, the council isn't working.
 * Keep Council Tax Under Control: With the cost-of-living crisis biting, we must protect households. Reform-run councils are already proving we can keep tax rises lower than any other party.
 * Help the High Street: We will cut parking charges to increase footfall and work with the police to fight shoplifting and anti-social behaviour. We need to make our town centres safe, moral environments for families once again.
 * Close the Immigrant Hotels: It is a scandal that your tax pounds house thousands of illegal immigrants in local hotels while our own people struggle. This is a matter of fairness and national stewardship.
 * Defend Local Democracy: You deserve a voice. When the establishment tried to cancel elections, Reform UK took them to court and won. We believe in the power of the voter.
I know what it looks like when a society begins to unravel. I’ve lived it. I came here to escape the decline, only to find it following me. But I am reminded of the words in 2 Chronicles 7:14. 
“If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land."
It is time to heal our land. We can demand better. We can vote for a party that values common sense, national pride, and the Christian values that built our civilisation. On election day, vote to keep this country "First World."
Vote Reform UK.

Malcolm has represented West Hill Ward since 1994 and has lived in Wandsworth for nearly 40 years. He has worked on all aspects of the Council’s services, including supporting residents over the AELTC’s plans for Wimbledon Park Golf Course; pressing for tighter controls on Lime Bikes; pushing TfL to improve the West Hill subway at the top of Beaumont Road; addressing the growing problem of litter in the area; promoting the interests of Council tenants and leaseholders; and addressing many thousands of individual problems with housing, schooling, social care and so on. He has published a book looking at the history of West Hill and Wimbledon Park Side over the last 200 years or more. He works in energy policy and is often seen and heard on TV and radio.

Good  evening everyone, I’m Jason Whiffin. I’ve lived in the area for about 12 years, and up by the Common for the past 9, and I’d like to thank you tonight for this opportunity to represent the Greens here in West Hill. 

I’d like if I may to open with a weather report.  It’s going to be 43 degrees tomorrow in New Delhi. That’s 109 degrees Fahrenheit. And the day after, and the day after that. It hit 40 degrees in New Delhi on 29 March this year and the long term forecast suggests that it’s going to stay in the mid 40s for several weeks more. The Indian Meteorological Department notes that such extended heat is unusual so early in the year and links it to climate change.

Which is why I’m here.  I believe we are sleepwalking into a climate catastrophe. And when I discovered that there was no one standing for the Green Party in West Hill in the local elections, I thought well, there’s no point getting annoyed and expecting someone else to step up, so I put myself forward so that anyone who wanted to register a Green vote could be counted.

It frustrates me that we have such a democratic deficit with our first past the post system that thousands of votes are disregarded every election time because they have been cast for a so-called “minority” party.  Climate change is going to affect all of us, and we deserve to have representatives on our councils who are putting it front and centre. This democratic deficit and the lack of representation fuels polarising views. The structure also makes the process in general adversary rather than collaborative. I believe we need collaboration more than ever to solve these huge problems, and if I was elected I would want to work with my fellow councillors to find the solutions.

My background is quite mixed.   I grew up on a council estate, went to the local comprehensive, have a degree in Economics and started my career in accountancy.  I moved to IT within Finance and now work for a large Finance corporation in the City. 

Cycling is a major passion in my life (I have cycled up South America); and I have a broad passion for the outdoors and nature.   I’m a member of the Wandsworth Cycling Campaign and have recently been appointed to the Stakeholder Group on the Wimbledon and Putney Commons Conservators to help with cycling. I commute into the city most days, and as a result I have become very aware of the challenge of encouraging low carbon travel in a city that is still so in thrall to the internal combustion engine. 

Earlier this month the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change told us we were going to have to pull every lever to reduce the amount of greenhouse gases we continue to pour into the atmosphere. Some of those levers are going to be marked Technology and Engineering. But given the timescales they have given us we are also going to have to pull the levers marked Behaviour Change and Mindset. And that’s an area that I think I can help with.

Many on this panel are very engaged within the community, and I do respect and appreciate that.  I’m not going to pretend I’m familiar with all the detail of the questions that may be asked this evening and I am not going to attempt to bluff.  

I am here as a green voice, and if there is no green angle on the question I won’t pretend to know all the answers.

However if by chance I was elected, I do sincerely believe my skills, experience and growth mindset would make me a valued councillor.

A vote for Reform offers a fresh approach to change and an opportunity for real improvement that benefits you.

Having lived in West Putney for many years with 2 rescue dogs, I have deep roots in our local community and I will act on your priorities, not just make empty promises.

As an IT software company director and business owner, I also served as Chairman of a Museums Trust charity. Actively raised funds for various charities and ran the London Marathon for endangered wildlife. Currently involved in environmentally friendly and nutritious meals to schools and local councils.

I will address key issues in our ward such as community safety and crime prevention, improving transportation, housing, public facilities, and supporting a successful high street. I will protect Putney's unique social environment and remove wasteful Council expenditure.

Working for Watford, Ian has led multiple campaigns to restore cut transport services, protect the Abbey Line rail link, maintain and improve local roads and green spaces and petitioned against local cuts from county council.

Born in Petts Wood, Bromley, Ian Stotesbury attended Ravenswood School before studying Physics and Astrophysics at the University of Birmingham. He grew up in a safe Conservative seat before moving to Birmingham where he first experienced active campaigns, outraged at the complacency so often seen in safe seats. After completing his degree in Physics he attended Cranfield University to study a degree in Astronautics and Space Engineering.

Ian is a passionate scientist, engineer and environmentalist. In his role as a Systems Engineer in the Space Industry he works on the design of spacecraft. He has been involved in the manufacture, test and launch of a number of spacecraft for both public and private customers.

The motivation for Ian to enter politics is to represent Watford as a hardworking but above all approachable MP for its constituents and be a voice for evidence based policy. He believes in government transparency and openness. He pledges to work tirelessly for Watford and the UK’s interest and set a new standard for approachability and accountability in parliament with highly regular updates of ongoing work, policy decisions and surgeries.

favourite_biscuit: anything in a family circle box ;)

statement_to_voters: I was born and educated in Watford and I've worked in IT for most of my working life. I believe in common sense solutions to problems, like the cost of living crisis. I welcome the opportunity to serve the residents in Hemel Hempstead East. I am committed to improve the area's qualities, support local businesses and elevate your voices..

I am an accountant and a yoga instructor. I have lived in North Watford for 25 years and I believe that many decisions made by our parliament are not for the benefit of the current residents. Residents are being overlooked in the name of profit and our money is being spent on things which we would not vote for if we had a choice. I want to be involved in the decisions being made to ensure that they are just and fair and made with the interests of the people of Watford and our environment at heart.

I’m running as candidate on behalf of the Green Party as I believe there is real hope for a better future.  I’ve lived in Watford for 25 years and my son was born here.  Watford as a town has changed dramatically since I’ve lived here I’ve seen rising rents, less green spaces and loss of public transport in the area, all things that need to be addressed and for too long all we’ve had is false hopes and promises.  A vote for me is a vote for real hope real change.

After gaining vocational qualifications in the late-1960s (Ordinary National Certificate in Business Studies; Higher National Certificate in Business Studies; and Diploma of the Institute of Purchasing & Supply), I worked in Central Africa for several years before a change in career as a professional musician. I also spent some time in living and working in Southern Africa, South America and Northern American during the later 1970s.

After I returned to the UK, I spent one year on a full-time Higher National Diploma in Computer Studies course, following which I completed a BA Honours Degree in Government & Politics and became a FE College Lecturer in Politics and Business Studies for most of the late 1980s and early 1990s.

I also completed an MA degree course in Government & Politics, as well as a Certificate in Education (Post-Compulsory Education) course. I also served as a GCE Advanced Level Examiner in Politics & Government for the University of London Board for 4 years.

I was elected as a local councillor in 1995 to 1999, during which time I was Chair of the Grants Committee, as well as Vice-Chair of a number of other council committees. I became a trustee and management board member for a number of local charities.

I decided not to seek re-election as a local councillor in 2000 in order to spend more time with my wife who unfortunately died at the comparatively young age of 49 years in 2001.

I subsequently became a manager of a local community centre in 2003 until retiring at the age of 66 years in 2011. I also served as the Chair of Governors of a local primary school during this period and subsequently became a Life Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts.

While retired and living as a state pensioner, I continue to take an active interest in politics and government. I am increasingly dismayed at the UK political party’s failure to honour a decision of the British people to leave the European Union following their vote in the 2016 referendum.

As a firm believer in and supporter of democracy, I see the old LibLabCon parties letting UK people down by their continuing attempts to reverse the result of the 2016 Brexit referendum, which is why I joined the Reform UK Party and act as Constituency Spokesman for St Albans.

It is high time the old stale parties were sidelined by the British electorate and replaced by a party committed to democracy and reform of the major institutions of UK governance, such as reforming the voting system and replacing the House of Lords.

There is only one party with the ambition and determination to reform and improve the current state of politics and governance in our country. That party is the Reform UK Party.

I have lived in Brookmans park for over 30 years and know the area very well.  I am now retired but I am still deeply involved in the local community and am the chair of the North Mymms Memorial Hall as well as being a councillor on the North Mymms Parish Council.

I am also a keen leisure cyclist which makes me very aware of the potholes!

Hi there! I’m Steph, your green candidate for Brookmans Park and Little Heath. I’m a trading strategist by day (working in environmental products), and the co-chair of our local Green Party by night!

I was born and brought up in Brookmans Park, and have spent my adult life appreciating how precious our area is – and wanting to ensure we maintain our beautiful home. I have been fortunate in my education and career, and I really do owe it to the community here in Brookmans Park for having watched out for me growing up, I wouldn’t have had the confidence or ability to step into the big wide world without it. It’s a special place for me, and I’m keen to give back to the people and community however I can.

My career has been dedicated to understanding how we can implement solutions to social and climactic challenges in an economically sound and efficient way. This has included work in Green Bonds, Emissions trading schemes and broader carbon markets (working for FTSE 250 and 100 companies).

My local priorities include:

-Supporting local businesses
-Opportunities for young adults
-Creating a safe & strong community
-Preserving the green belt
-Avoiding poorly planned development
-Cost of living
-Road and infrastructure condition
-Fly tipping, vandalism
-Re-wilding and local nature initiatives (including initiatives to increase opportunities for young people to engage with nature)

Outside of work, I love time spent reading, doing yoga and pilates, running, and generally finding beautiful adventures to go on! Get in touch if you feel like a walk in Gobions, cocktails at the Brookmans, or to join for a yoga session!

I have been a resident of Welwyn Hatfield for 10 years and am very pleased to be standing for the Heritage Party in this year’s elections.

I love my community, but I believe we are in desperate need of change from the old political parties that put vested interests before local people and have let us down many times.

The Heritage Party stands for simple, common-sense values and principles that will restore purpose and prosperity to our nation. We have a great heritage that has been given to us by our forefathers for us to enjoy and pass on to future generations.

Our core principles are free speech and liberty, national sovereignty, low immigration, self-sufficiency in skills and energy, traditional family values and financial responsibility in government. We believe in the preservation of our Green Belt and our places of historic interest.

Local governments must be efficient and accountable. We reject the plan to replace district and county councils with unitary authorities and Sadiq Khan-style county mayors.

We reject the woke ideologies of critical race theory, 100 genders and climate alarmism. Instead, we hold that Britain is a good country, there are two sexes – male and female – determined by anatomy and chromosomes, and we should not replace coal and gas power stations with wind turbines and solar panels that are causing household energy bills to go through the roof and are killing off nature and potential land for agricultural use.

We will repeal climate emergency declarations and scrap net zero locally.

Hi, I’m Lucy and I’m standing to be re-elected as your Green Party councillor for Haldens on Thursday 7th May.

For the past eight years, it truly has been a privilege to serve as a councillor for Haldens. I am appealing to have your trust again so I can continue supporting the community in what looks to be a busy and difficult upcoming year, starting with the new Local Plan and Local Government Reorganisation.

As your local councillor, I will be able to achieve even more for you, from working closely with the county councillor to fix potholes and grass verges, to pushing for fairer and greener housing policies and building.

I have been utterly dismayed by reports of a lack of care towards the housing of vulnerable persons, whether that be through allocations or repairs. As I stated in the chamber, it is not good enough, and I will continue to push for better.

This election is really clear, it’s either Labour, or you can vote for the Green Party and me on Thursday 7th May to make hope normal again for Haldens and Welwyn Hatfield.

My passion is education and as a local teacher I am deeply invested in delivering for our area and making it the best it can be - for all generations. I always believe we should support every individual with the opportunity to be a valuable member of our community and ensure people have the skills they need to thrive.

I love our town and its unique character and as your Councillor, I want to focus on preserving the beauty of nature in Welwyn Garden City. We are lucky to live in such green and vibrant area and I am committed to protecting our local environment.

Our Community is special and deserves a dedicated voice at Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council and with your support, I will work hard for Haldens ward - listening, acting and standing up for our community.

Hi, I’m Caleb and I have lived in Welwyn Hatfield my entire life, I grew up in Handside and attended Stanborough School. I’m an electrician by trade and help run a monthly open mic night at the Hatfield Tap.

I’ve witnessed first hand the damage cuts to local services have caused to our community, so I joined the Green Party to push for more accountability within local councils and to drive positive change for everyone that lives in this beautiful borough.

As a Councillor, resident of the ward and parent, I am deeply invested in our area and want to ensure our Garden City remains the best it can be, for residents today and for the next generation. I continue to support residents with issues large and small and always try to resolve local problems. As Lib Dems, I and my fellow Councillors are always active, keeping in touch all year round through regular Handside resident forums, newsletters or talking to you on the doorstep.

As the Executive Member for Housing, I am proud that our award winning social housing energy efficiency scheme is saving residents an average £420 a year and lowering their carbon footprint. as well as many other great initiatives.

I want to continue working hard for the residents of Handside ward - listening, taking action and standing up for our community.

I am standing as a candidate for the Liberal Democrats in Hatfield Central because I believe in open, fair and community-focused politics. I am committed to representing local residents with respect, promoting equal opportunities, supporting sustainable development, and working constructively to improve local services.

I aim to be a strong liberal voice that listens, engages and serves the community with integrity and transparency.

Hi, my name is Andy and I have lived in Hatfield since 2018 – building a family here with my wife and, more recently, my twin sons.

I have worked in education in Hertfordshire local government since 2022 and I’m standing for the Green Party as an advocate for our community, particularly those who are young or from global majority backgrounds. My sons both attend school in Hatfield and I intend to be a voice for them and other local residents, through a time of great change in our county and a period of national and global instability.

I strongly feel that the Green Party is the progressive choice for Hatfield residents, who hope for a kinder, fairer society.

I have lived and worked in the area for over 40 years and am embedded in the local community. My daughters and their young families live in Hertfordshire and are part of the wider community of Hertfordshire.

During my 4 years on the Hatfield Town Council I worked on the planning committee to ensure development was in keeping with the surroundings and not over development. I supported the development of the allotments in the town and supported local events for local residents.

I am standing in the local elections for the Borough Council because I want the place I live in to be the best it can be. Hatfield needs a strong voice in the council to push forward policies that enhance our town. There are lots of things about Hatfield to be proud of and recent improvements in the Town Centre show what can be done. Hatfield has a long history and a bright future which we should celebrate.

If elected I will join a growing number of Liberal Democrat councillors who will work hard to make your town a better place to live.

Hi, I’m Larry and I’m standing to be re-elected as your Green Party councillor for Hatfield East on Thursday 7th May.

I’ve been a borough councillor for four years, working hard to build a better home for us all.

A £70,000 renovation of Millwards Park was achieved under my leadership, helping to make it more accessible for disabled children. A new sensory area was also introduced for those children needing a little bit extra.

I speak up against overdevelopment of our green spaces. Green space is really important, not only for the environment, but our own health and wellbeing.

Your choice in this election is really clear, it’s either Labour and Lib Dems again, or you can vote for me, and the Green Party, on Thursday 7th May! Help change Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council!

I am standing as a candidate for Liberal Democrats for the South West ward of Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council because I believe our town and Borough deserves honest leadership, practical solutions and a stronger voice in local decision-making. I moved to Hatfield in May 2022 with my family. We weren’t just looking for a place to live- we were looking for a place to belong. We found it here. I felt honoured that my daughter could grow up here and attend local schools.

Living locally means I share and understand the many challenges that local residents face. I decided to stand for the Council as whilst ours is a tight-knit community, it often feels that most political parties care more about national issues than what is happening locally. For me, what you say is important, but what you do even more so and I know that the Liberal Democrat values best represent my own, especially their commitment to personal liberties and freedom of expression.

I strongly believe that more needs to be done to challenge the root causes of litter and fly tipping and that is why, if elected, I will continue to ensure stronger management of Houses of Multiple Occupation (HMOs), supporting the good landlords and challenging those who do not meet their responsibilities.

Hi, my name is Georgia and I’ve been living in Welwyn Hatfield for almost thirty years. I’m standing for the Green Party because I believe caring for people and caring for the environment are two intertwined goals. We need to build a fairer system for everybody while also protecting the planet in order to foster a kinder, more community-oriented world for future generations to enjoy.

My name is Adam Edwards. I’ve lived in Birchwood since 1989. My kids have benefited hugely from the local schools, the Mid-Herts Music Centre and from the QE2 hospital, where they were both born.  This is my community and I want the very best for our area for me, my family and all my neighbours.

Hatfield needs strong voices to stand up for everyone who lives here. If elected I would hold the council to account and work hard to get the best for the people I represent.

I have been campaigning for the past eight years to see upgraded paths and pavements, benefiting the elderly, parents with pushchairs, people in disabled buggies and those who cycle.  But there is more to do:  there’s no safe cycle route from Birchwood to the schools in Hatfield!  If we are to combat obesity and pollution, we need more people walking and cycling, leaving the roads less congested for those who have to use a car or van. To this end I’ve also been a member of WelHatCyling since the group was founded.  We chase up on faults and problems and I’ve led the group clearing litter from the Alban Way in Hatfield.

My greatest strength may well be my normality. I am a Dad before anything else. I hate injustice and unfairness and I am tenacious in tackling problems. I will always listen to you, try to understand your problems and work alongside you to try to resolve them. I hope I can count on your support.

Hello, I am Andreas and I have lived locally for 20 years, and in Hatfield since 2017. I work as a bioscience lecturer at the University of Hertfordshire and joined the Green Party in 2020. I am passionate about protecting our environment while supporting secure employment, a free and efficient NHS, social justice, and peaceful international cooperation.
Hi, I’m Esther and I have lived in Welwyn Hatfield for my whole life. I am standing for the Green Party because they are the best alternative to Reform.

As a younger voter, I see politics at the moment as a vicious battleground where there is a lot of focus on winning and losing. I believe we should be taking every opportunity to work together for the sake of our communities and to make the world a better place.

Hi, I’m Brad and I am deeply passionate about caring for the environment and ensuing that the borough, and the UK, can provide positivity for their citizens! I grew up in Welwyn Hatfield and worked for the borough council. I now work for a national charity.

Hello, my name is Ian. I was born at the QEII in 1964 and apart from three years in Birmingham obtaining a degree in Mechanical Engineering and five years post graduate research in Physics in the US, I have lived my whole life in Welwyn Hatfield. In 1996, working as a scientist, I was lucky enough to be able to afford to buy my own home, something which has become increasingly difficult these days. I believe that there is an urgent need to provide more affordable housing, ideally with an investment in new council homes.

I have been an environmental and anti-war activist since the late 1980s, particularly concerned about the effects of climate change, and getting involved with the Camps for Climate Action in the late 2000s. However, I had never been a member of political party until I joined the Green Party in 2014.

Locally, I have focused on active travel and sustainable transport, particularly on improving conditions for cycling. I helped set up the Hertfordshire Cycling Campaign and I am deputy chair and cycling representative on the Hertfordshire Local Access Forum, a statutory body concerned with access to the countryside.

I have been a self-employed gardner since 2010 and for leisure I enjoy going to festivals and walking in the mountains.

Hi, I’m Alice and I have lived in Welwyn Hatfield my whole life. I am standing for the Green Party because I hope to stop Reform and further cuts to vital local services, especially NHS services and benefits and support for those in need.

I believe a Labour run County Council can truly improve the lives of Hertfordshire residents. As your County Councillor, I want to be part of that.

I can represent residents effectively if elected to the county council. I will listen to them, understand their needs, and actively pursue their cases. I am committed to making a positive impact on the local area.

I’ve made Panshanger my home since 2023, drawn to its green spaces, Garden City heritage, and the sense of fellowship people share here. Getting to know neighbours and becoming part of local life has shaped how I see the community.

My work and volunteering have taught me to listen, understand how places function, and notice the daily challenges people face. From making buildings safer and more sustainable to helping in emergencies with the ambulance service, these roles have given me a practical outlook and a strong belief in caring for our area and everyone in it.

Helping communities grow is what drives me. I care about Panshanger’s character, the well-being of everyone who lives here, and the future of the place I now call home. I hope to use my experience, my ties to the area, and what I’ve learned from talking with residents to make a positive difference, bring people together, and support good decisions for our neighbourhood.

Hi, I'm Tanya and I'm standing to be elected as your Green Party councillor for Peartree on Thursday 7th May.

As a Peartree resident, I put Green values into practice every day. I founded CultureWood CIC, a social enterprise where we are passionate about nature connection, running forest school programmes for local schools and for the wider community, working with people of all ages. I lead a local community garden group at King George V, where we are literally digging in to protect our environment, and are creating a community and green space where we can learn, share, grow food, build resilience and improve the park for nature.

I'm standing because our ward needs a councillor who will fight just as hard to protect our green spaces, tackle the cost of living crisis, and ensure the council acts on its climate promises.

Your choice in this election is really clear, it’s either the Lib Dems again, or you can vote for me and the Green Party on Thursday 7th May and help change Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council!

As a fellow Peartree resident, I am deeply invested in delivering for our area and making it the best it can be for the residents of today and for future generations. With Local Government Reorganisation on the horizon, I want to stand up for our community by campaigning for the creation of a Welwyn Garden City Town Council. I want to continue tackling multiple housing issues, address parking problems alongside my fellow Peartree Councillors and address all the multitude of other issues residents bring to me.

In the last four years, I have played a substantial part in ensuring the Councils finances are on a secure footing as Cabinet member for Resources and more recently as the shadow for that position.

With your continued support, I will carry on working hard for Peartree Ward - listening, acting and standing up for our community.

Hi, I’m Phil and I have lived in Welwyn Garden City with my family for 20 years. I work as an earth scientist at a London university and am passionate about environmental education and inclusive access to the outdoors. I joined the Green Party in 2020 and have met a wonderful group of like-minded people who are working hard to spread the Green message of hope for people and planet.

As a Councillor, resident, parent and member of both the Orchard Tennis Club and WGC Cricket Club, I am deeply invested in our area.  I want to ensure our Garden City remains the best it can be for residents today and for the next generation. I continue to support residents with issues large and small from repairing verge damage to defending vulnerable residents with critical housing repairs.

As a Liberal Democrat group, we have kick-started the WGC Town Council process, supported our environment and our precious chalk streams and helped introduce parking permits for voluntary carers.

I will fight hard as your Councillor and use my experience to shape positive changes for the benefit of Sherrards and Welwyn Garden City residents.

**It is my pleasure to represent Welham Green and Hatfield South at Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council, Hatfield South at Hatfield Town Council and as the Executive member for Environment at Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council and Deputy leader of the Council.**

Since being elected in 2022, I’ve been working hard to be a voice for the community both in and out of of the Council chamber. Welham Green and Hatfield South is a diverse community with many concerns and aspirations for what they want from their Council. Me and my colleagues Paul and Adrienne are doing what we can to make Welham Green and Hatfield South the best place to live and work. This involves dealing with issues that affect our residents. Including Parking, Fly tipping and maintaining our Green spaces.

In May 2023, I was given the privilege of becoming the Executive member for Environment. This has given us the opportunity to fix the appalling state of grass cutting in our borough, neglected by the previous Conservative administration. My other priorities for this position will be maintaining a high quality of waste collection both residentially and at recycling centres as well as combating fly tipping.

As Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council’s youngest Councillor as well as a former student of the University of Hertfordshire, I do my best to represent members of the community that often feel neglected by modern Politics. I also run the Welham Green friendship group, a monthly get together setting to combat isolation in older members of our community, which is even more important in a post-Covid world.

Hi, I’m Joshua and I’m a lifelong resident of Welham Green. I believe in everyone getting a fair shot regardless of their background. I’m standing for the Green Party because I believe they’re the antidote to the worst of British politics, and they seek to put people and community over profit and capital.

I moved with our family from Welwyn Garden City to Welwyn in 1965, where my wife became a teacher, and our children attended local schools. I worked in medicines research until I left to start my own IT and sports consultancy company in 1996. I have managed a youth sports club since 1996, and over several years have raised Sport England funds in the borough for example, for Gosling Sports Park improvements, young school leaders’ projects, and older people’s exercise. As well as concerns for the environment

I am a member of the Royal Society of Biology, the British Computer Society, Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, and The National Trust.

I have always been passionate about maximising health opportunities for everyone and feel there is a lot more to be done in Welwyn and the borough.

Hello, I am William and I have lived in Welwyn Hatfield for nearly 20 years and have been a member of the Green Party for 35 years.

Now is the time to vote Green, as I strongly feel that we are the progressive choice for Welwyn Hatfield residents with policies that propose more innovative solutions at a local level to deal with long standing problems such as the cost of living and climate change.

We are the party for voters who want a kinder, fairer society.

Hi, I’m Andrew and I joined the Green Party as I believe our politics needs to be different. I believe in a politics that shares power more evenly across our society and prioritises our climate more than wealth creation for the few.

I am a married 50 year old accountant from the Northern part of Welwyn Garden City and my family and I have lived here for almost 20 years, so I know the area well.

I have been a member of the Liberal Democrats for several years now after realising that the policies of the two main parties no longer align with my views and what is important to me.

Hello, I'm David and I'm standing to be elected as your Green Party councillor for Welwyn West on Thursday 7th May.

As a parish councillor, I have worked closely with the Digswell Residents’ Association to increase and also enhance the quality of Welwyn’s green areas. I have assisted the DRA with:

-Opening up Digswell Orchard for residents

-Taking over the ownership and maintainence of the Wildings Nature Reserve from the RSPB to make it available for residents’ enjoyment and tranquility

-Preserving the historical nature of Digswell Village with our first and much loved village sign

-Maintaining the playing fields and riverside pathway.

I have also provided financial and legal assistance for the Singlers Marsh Action Group to attain Village Green status for Singlers Marsh. We are working to create a new skateboard park for the health and enjoyment of the youthful members of our community.

As your local councillor, I will work closely with the county councillor to fix potholes and grass verges, and will push for fairer and greener housing policies and building.

Your choice in this election is really clear, it’s another Conservative, or you can vote for me and the Green Party on Thursday 7th May and help change Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council!
I believe that something has to change in our politics today and the Liberal Democrats are the only party that can do that. I am standing in Welwyn West to help bring about that change.

I’m standing for election as a Liberal Democrat because my belief in democracy is personal, not abstract. Having grown up under a communist system, I understand what it means when voices are silenced—and why it matters that every voice here in West Lancashire is heard, respected, and represented.

I’ve lived and worked in this community since 2003. Over that time, I’ve seen how West Lancashire has changed—economically, socially, and demographically—and I know that the solutions we need must reflect the realities on the ground. I believe in strong local government: decisions made closer to the people they affect, with real accountability and local knowledge at their heart.

We face clear challenges. Housing must be affordable, but also sustainable, protecting our environment while supporting the traditional industries that define our area. Issues like flooding and sewage in our waterways aren’t just national concerns; they affect our fields, our homes, and our health right here. These are priorities I will fight to address.

Reform UK City of Westminster’s Nine Point Plan
1. Get Tough on Crime and Anti-Social Behaviour– The Conservatives cut CCTV when they were last in power, and closed our police stations. Labour Mayor Sadiq Khan has presided over a crime wave. Only Reform will fight crime by increasing frontline officer strength and adding CCTV coverage to keep you safe.
2. Cleaner, Tidier Streets – Westminster streets are dirtier than ever, with litter and dumping a regular feature. We will restore a Grade A street cleaning service as well as ensuring that dumpers are prosecuted, and e-bikes removed and their operators fined when parked badly. Graffiti will also be prioritised for immediate removal.
3. Co-ordinated Roadworks – Westminster roadworks are out of control, with journeys being disrupted daily because of the chaos of multiple schemes at the same time and roads repeatedly being re-dug. We will co-ordinate roadworks with AI to minimise disruption to your lives.
4. Cycleways That Work – We all want to see more cycling in Westminster but Conservative and Labour administrations have undertaken a war on pedestrians, disabled people and drivers through aggressive cycleway projects that make it difficult to cross roads, use cars or park. We will ensure that those who live in Westminster get the final say on future schemes so they work for all our road users..
5. Cut Waste and Save Money – Reform will promote value for money by targeting the millions wasted every year on pet ideological projects, weak major contracts, illegal migration and diversity schemes that prioritise social engineering over efficiency. Your Council Tax will stay low. Remember Labour lost £27 million of taxpayer’s money on a building company that went bust, and the Conservatives wasted £6 million on the failed Marble Arch Mound. Neither can be trusted with your money.
6. Oxford Street – We will oppose Mayor Khan’s plans which threaten congestion and mass disruption for local people and those looking to travel by bus or road.
7. Stop the Hate Marches – For too long, the City of Westminster has been plagued by repeat hate marches that cause an intimidating atmosphere, disrupt business, cause chaos and leave rubbish in their wake. We will demand that hate marches be prevented or moved so that local people can be free to get on with their lives.
8. Better Short-Term Let Enforcement – Illegal Airbnb and similar short-term rentals are causing disruption for local people when rules are broken. We will enforce regulations as well as the established day limits. 
9. Fairness for Council Housing Tenants and Leaseholders – Council residents frequently have to wait too long for repairs. We promise an end to this poor standard of service and will also investigate ways to improve fairness around surprise repair bills. 
Above all, Reform will adopt a common sense view about the policies that you actually want, not what ideologues from other parties or bureaucrats claim you want. Only Reform can save you from the chaos served up by both Labour and the Conservatives. 
Westminster needs Reform. Vote Reform on May 7th.

Westminster Council plans to install 350 new CCTV cameras by 2030 and we would work alongside the council to ensure this happens. 200 have already been delivered.

Please see below an example of a Green Party Councillor tackling crime in Bristol:

In 2023, Green councillor Mohamed Makawi, whose friend had been fatally stabbed in Castle Park, proposed a motion to bring down knife crime in Bristol that was passed by full Council.

Rather than simply calling for more policing, the Green motion outlined practical solutions and addressed the social factors underlying knife violence.

It introduced simple but vital steps to save lives, such as providing emergency bleed kits and staff training for night-time venues, and providing more lighting and CCTV to fix ‘blind spots’ in areas of high knife crime.

2. Planning (double-glazing): “Many houses on the Hyde Park Estate are unable to install double-glazing due to planning constraints. This results in increased noise pollution and poor energy efficiency. What can you do rectify or mitigate this?”

We want planning rules to allow residents to live in warm, quiet, energy‑efficient homes.
We will push the Council to adopt modern, conservation‑grade double‑glazing and secondary‑glazing solutions that are already permitted in other conservation areas.
Improving insulation and reducing energy waste is essential for both climate action and household bills  and we believe the Council should enable it, not block it.

I personally have also noticed an increase in noise pollution since Labour took over Westminster council. It seems a lot more construction is being allowed and whilst I appreciate this grows the economy, it feels as if residents’ needs have been neglected. I resorted to installing secondary glazing in my home after having a miserably loud building extension permitted directly opposite me. Westminster council needs reminding that people live here.

Westminster Council currently has 2500 cases of illegal subletting open for investigation. This is clearly a problem that overwhelms the council and needs more staffing, which we would push for.
We will push for proactive enforcement not just responding to complaints so residents aren’t left to police the problem themselves.
Short‑lets must not undermine community stability or reduce the supply of homes for people who actually live here.
We support strict enforcement of the 90‑day rule and stronger action against illegal short‑lets that cause noise, security issues, and loss of long‑term housing.
We want the Council to require registration of all short‑let properties, with proof of insurance, safety compliance, and tax obligations.

Any scheme must be co‑designed with residents, businesses and emergency services not imposed from above.
We support measures that cut rat‑running, improve crossings, and make streets safer for walking and cycling, while protecting access for disabled people and essential vehicles.
We would also push for better enforcement of speeding, idling and illegal manoeuvres, which residents consistently raise as daily problems.
The goal is simple: quieter, safer streets where people can move around without constant congestion and pollution.

That’s why I’m standing for West Oxfordshire District Council - to ensure the voices of Ducklington, Curbridge, Lew, and Colwell Green are heard and your priorities are delivered.

I’m an engineer who has worked in Formula 1 to deliver high quality projects on time and under tight budgets. That same approach is exactly what local government needs right now. Too often are fundamental services forgotten, while the Lib Dem-run council pushes ahead with projects that residents oppose, such as closing the Woodford Way Car Park in Witney to build new houses. This risks making it harder for key workers and customers to park, harming local businesses.

My priorities are clear: Conserving our way of life by freezing council tax, and insuring that infrastructure comes first with new homes, not last. Protecting our countryside by tackling fly tipping with tougher enforcement and holding Thames Water to account over the state of our rivers. And supporting our traditions by backing local businesses, farmers, and our cherished village events.

If elected on May 7th, I will work tirelessly for the Ducklington Ward to deliver real results for our communities.

Four years of my life were in an underfunded, understaffed, negligent care system. Now I'm on a mission to fix it. For half my life, I've advocated for underrepresented groups, especially care leavers; now, I run to represent them.

I am running in Ducklington because now is the time for me use my skills and experience to counter the divisive messages some groups are trying to put out, and the Witney and West Oxfordshire Liberal Democrats being the best people to counter that and take the actions that Ducklington village and the rest of our local area need to be taken.

I am standing for election because I want to improve th environmental health of West Oxfordshire for the benefit of children and adults, and to help empower people in West Oxfordshire to improve their daily lives.

I have lived in West Witney for eight years and in Oxfordshire for eight more. I regularly spend time in Ducklington with his family, at the lake and in the village. I am a trustee for an Oxfordshire-based charity and led a union chapel for four years, negotiating for better pay, working on behalf of colleagues during redundancy events, and helping individuals through casework.

I hold an MSci in physics and work in marketing analytics.

Penny has been living in Witney since 2000, and a member of the Green Party for about 10 years. Now retired, she taught mainly in Primary schools, including West Witney, although most of her work was in Oxford.   She is incensed about injustice in all its forms. The increasing gap between rich and poor concerns her very much.   Her passion for Human Rights has led her to be an active member of Amnesty International for most of her adult life.    Her other great interest is in the Environment. She supports the Wildlife Trust and the RSPB. She is concerned about habitat preservation and sustainable farming, and feels very strongly about food waste. Litter and fly-tipping are other issues that need to be addressed.   She strongly believes in public transport and safe cycling.    The Covid restrictions have benefitted big retailers at the expense of little shops. This is unfair and she would like to see more support for small businesses.

In Witney and West Oxfordshire we work as a highly effective Labour team, bringing constructive ideas and working for consensus to make our wonderful area even better. In the face of cuts. In the face of years of complacency.  North Witney needs reliable, well-lit routes into town and to schools on foot and by bike. It needs improvements to existing drainage and any new housing development needs engineering to prevent further flooding. I have not yet seen convincing assurances that the houses proposed towards Hailey have had that level of engineering planned or invested in. North Witney lacks a community centre. The schools and church buildings offer what they can. I will support projects that build community cohesion. On the Town Council, I have made the strong and persistent case for active travel infrastructure for walking and cycling. The sewage petition I ran last year helped to galvanise the District council in its dealings with the water company. A vote for me will be a vote for someone who asks questions to check people are being treated fairly when it comes to housing and benefits or to check our recycling goes where we think it goes. It's a vote for acting to make active travel and playing out safer, to improve air quality, to prevent climate change by opportunities such as community energy, to promote biodiversity... rather than just talking about these things.

Do you feel let down by the previous political parties like I do? I think Britain is an amazing country now and in the past. Reform UK appears to be the only party truly standing up for Britain. Nigel Farage its leader, says it as it is and does what he says.

Running to provide a young, fresh voice to Woodstock and Bladon.

I have grown up my entire life in Woodstock. It is amazing town with a vibrant community deeply rooted in its long traditions and history and rooted in its beautiful environment. But the town has become increasingly difficult for young people to stay, live and work in. Local services has not been kept to adequate standards and delays and confusion in planning processes and public works have been a constant feature of life here. If elected, I would fight for clarity in our planning processes and push to expedite construction and renewal of our key public services, and bring a perspective of young people to keep our town going for future generations.

Barry has lived in West Oxfordshire for over 30 years and runs his own consultancy and testing business from home. Originally a Chemical Engineer he has many years of experience of R&D and management, both in business and academia. He also spent four years working for the councils and government agencies of South East England setting up and running a regional office in Brussels for SEEDA & SERA.  His principal responsibility during that time was to work with our politicians to give the region a strong voice in Europe.  This involved building up relationships and influencing both politicians and European officials.  During his time in Europe he started to realise the vital importance of small businesses to the economy. On his return he became an active member of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) and was elected as Chair of the Oxfordshire Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) and Policy Chair for the whole Thames Valley.

Over the past 20 years his consultancy work has included business to business market-place development, testing services and consultancy. He has specialized in business start-up and innovation in areas of science and technology such as biotechnology and environmental monitoring.

For the last four years Barry has brought his organisational skills and experience to the West Oxfordshire Green Party where he took on the role of Chair for the West Oxfordshire Green Party and more recently as Chair of county wide Oxfordshire Green Party.

On a personal note he counts himself blessed to have had the support of a wonderful wife for over five decades and is extremely proud of his daughter, who studied locally at the Marlborough school and went on to get her MSc and PhD at Oxford University.

Why does Barry Wheatley wish to become your councillor? We are in challenging times and whether that’s running your own business, coping with the cost of living or working to protect our children’s and grandchildren’s futures, we must take urgent steps to build the mechanisms needed to provide not just short term, but long-term sustainable solutions.  Barry has been inspired by the positive change that has been achieved working in collaboration with other parties locally and the influence that the Green Party councillors are already making across town, district and county levels around the UK. His main reason for wanting to become a councillor, is to help push for that change and help make our corner of the country the best that it can be. If you want a cleaner, fairer, greener, prosperous future - vote Green. If elected as Councillor on West Oxfordshire District Council Barry will work hard to:  ·	Ensure that local businesses get the best support that we can give them and that village and town centres offer real opportunities to grow our local enterprises and create local worthwhile jobs.   ·	Stand up against housing development projects that do not address local needs and ensure that all forms of development have the right infrastructure in place before they are built and are constructed with the future in mind.  ·	Ensure we maintain our public places and countryside as living green spaces which enhance biodiversity.  This includes tackling pollution in all its forms, whether it is general litter and fly tipping, to pollution of the air we breathe or the water in our rivers.  Protecting not just our residents but also the flora and fauna that make our countryside so special

That was not Paul's idea of representing the people who elected him!

Paul is currently an Independent Bury St Edmunds Town Councillor (Deputy Mayor of Bury St Edmunds) and West Suffolk Councillor for St Olaves Ward in Bury St Edmunds, an area he has served as a Councillor since 2005. Paul is standing as an Independent Parliamentary Candidate for Bury St Edmunds at the next General Election on December 12, 2019.

It’s Paul's intense dedication, passion, and devotion to represent the people, that fuels Paul's fight for change. Explore his site to learn more about the issues that Paul is concerned with and his plans to tackle the problems faced by his constituents on a daily basis.

We come from many walks of life with different life experiences and different political views, but we can all unite in our desire to keep our community strong and good to live in. We may vote for national parties in national elections, but in local government the most important thing is to have capable representatives who live locally, like Isabel and myself who are both long term residents of Egham, who know the new ward well, and care about its future.

Egham town has elected Independent Resident councillors over many years. We are your neighbours; we live here and know the place and the local issues well. We’ll work with other councillors from any political party, for whatever brings most benefit to the new Egham ward and we’ll vote independently, unwhipped, however we think best for our community. Egham is simply a better place to live for having strong, local, Independent representation. Our concern is to safeguard the new Egham ward’s interests in the future, when there’ll be fewer representatives and decisions will be made more remotely, by people who may not know Egham at all.

Individual details are below, but if elected, our shared aims will be to:
 * Foster a collaborative approach, like Isabel has done as part of the Runnymede Council Alliance at RBC. This will be essential if, as likely, no single party gets overall majority.
 * Maintain services to support people living active lives, independently within their homes, in spite of budgetary pressures on the new authority.
 * Keep strong engagement with the River Thames Scheme to maximise benefits for those in high flood-risk areas in Egham Hythe and Egham.
 * Oppose gravel extraction at Milton Park and Whitehall Farms.
 * Fight for improved pedestrian access to Runnymede meadows.
 * Embed high standards for SEND at the new council.
 * Press the new authority to take potholes seriously.
 * Support the Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan, giving more choice on how to get places, reducing congestion and being good for health.
 * Attempt to crack the Pooley Green rail crossing nightmare - we will call the council to lead a task force to get action from the rail authorities.
 * Hold regular open sessions for advice, information and sharing of views.
