A long-term ward resident, I’m dismayed by the level of misinformation, petty party
politics and lack of accountability from some councillors. Did you know Guildford’s
handing the new Unitary a deficit budget (£6M by 2028/9), that it’s sitting on £7M of
developers’ funding for education, or that its external auditors have declined to sign 
off on its accounts for the last 5 years, and recently confirmed that the uncertainty in
how much money it has (or doesn’t) had increased further over the past year; are you
frustrated you cannot contact your councillor?

I’m standing to listen to residents and businesses, to help inform and influence the
debate and, if elected, collaborate with councillors from all parties to deliver the
infrastructure and services we expect. This year, when day-to-day control remains
with Guildford and Surrey, and the role of new unitary councillors is primarily to set
up the new council I’d shape the Unitary to best meet our community’s needs,
retaining Guildford’s unique identity.

PRIOTITIES From talking with residents, my priorities include:
•	Potholes: I’d reallocate budgets (eg  the further £300k Guildford has set aside for planning a Guildford Parish) for immediate fixes and ensure a long-term maintenance schedule.
•	Housing and development: I’d end the scandal of unoccupied homes, and support a new town centre vision repurposing unwanted retail/office space to housing and community areas, including medical and youth facilities, whilst safeguarding the more rural areas of the ward such as the Chantries. I’d support direct discussion with landlords and retailers, eg to help open the old House of Fraser store, I’d also review council procedures to ensure they are best supporting the third of residents who live in private rented accommodation (the highest proportion in the area).
•	Crime and safety: The tragedy of January’s fatal stabbing was one facet of a ward that suffers from the highest levels of anti-social behaviour and violent crime & sexual offences in the area (twice the average). Residents, in particular females, tell me they are afraid to go to some places at night and are intimidated by littering, graffiti and anti-social behaviour at other times. I’d ensure more timely council action to maintain an environment we’re proud of (including harnessing the efforts of community groups), improved lighting of paths, better facilities for our youth to meet, socialise and play, and – when the Surrey PCC role is abolished in 2028 and police oversight reverts to the council - that community policy is prioritised.
•	Transport and pollution: The main arteries into the town centre (Epsom, London and Shalford Roads) are routinely choked, leading to delays, frustration and perpetuating the illegally high levels of pollution in the town-centre AQMA. Guildford has invested substantial sums on external consultants to produce solutions for these issues but has failed to act on them – I would, including reinvigorating Park&Ride by introducing “per vehicle” charging and reopening dormant sites, and use new council powers to take more control of local bus routes, including reintroduction of the town-centre circular shuttle linking the railway station, High Street / North Street and bus station.
•	Delivering a democratic dividend and retaining Guildford’s unique identity: The Unitary authority is happening whether we like it or not, and I would work to ensure that rather than suffering the democratic deficit others foresee, we take control of our destiny to shape the Unitary to deliver a democratic dividend: having councillors truly accountable for what they do, introducing Neighbourhood Area Committees which bring together local groups to inform council decision making,  introducing neighbourhood wardens who walk their patch listening to issues and concerns and tactically fixing some.  I would liaise and collaborate with other Guildford councillors to ensure we retain its identify as we define then run the new council.

Throughout that time I have been active in the community: acting as a Governor at local schools, lobbying and holding to account councillors / MPs to deliver improvements for residents (eg on traffic / air quality, spending S106 monies, implementing new off-road cycle/foot provision), proactive commenting on local developments & planning proposals, a member of the adjacent Shalford Parish/Community Council, and regularly supporting community activity to litter pick and tidy our local environment. I am co-opted as an independent member onto Guildford Borough Council’s recently formed Audit & Risk committee.

•	Ensure the prompt allocation of £7M of developers' section106 contributions for Education for the benefit of pupils and their families; similarly for the other unallocated categories of S106 contributions.

I’m seeking selection for Guildford South West because I believe the Green Party can offer something increasingly important locally: credible, values-led politics delivered with care, and consistency.
I’ve lived in this part of Surrey for the past ten years and know it as a place of strong communities alongside real pressures. Families here are navigating stretched public services, rising living costs, and growing anxiety about the future. Too often, politics feels distant from these everyday realities. I want to help change that by building trust through visible, practical, and reliable local representation.
For much of my adult life, formal political activity wasn’t an option. While serving in the RAF, political neutrality was expected. Even after leaving service, it took time to find a political home that aligned with both my values and my belief in evidence-based, constructive public service. As the Green Party has grown in credibility, professionalism, and local impact, that alignment has become real. I’m standing now because I believe I can contribute meaningfully.
Professionally, I work in complex organisations delivering large-scale change. That means balancing competing priorities, working constructively with people who hold different views, and turning principles into outcomes that actually land. I bring a calm, analytical approach, strong organisational skills, and a deep respect for accountability. As a candidate, that translates into disciplined campaigning, clear communication, and a willingness to do the unglamorous work consistently.
My primary policy focus is education, particularly Special Educational Needs provision. This is not abstract for me. I am the step-parent of two teenage children who have been through the SEN system, including the tribunal process. I have seen first-hand how complex, adversarial, and exhausting the system can be. It is painful, expensive, and deeply unfair for families who lack the time, resources, or specialist knowledge to navigate it successfully.
That experience has given me a detailed understanding of how SEN provision actually works on the ground, where it breaks down, and how power imbalances affect outcomes. I believe councils have a crucial role in improving commissioning, transparency, and early intervention, and in advocating consistently for families rather than forcing them into conflict. This is an area where informed, persistent, and practical leadership matters enormously.
I am also deeply concerned about the growth of far-right narratives, including at local level. These movements thrive where people feel ignored, insecure, or unheard. The most effective response is not performative outrage, but steady, visible politics that listens, counters misinformation, and offers credible alternatives rooted in fairness, inclusion, and shared responsibility.
If elected, I would be a reliable and collaborative councillor. I’m ready to put my experience, values, and energy into serving both the party and the community seriously and well.

statement_to_voters:
As the Labour & Co-operative candidate for Shere, I represent shared values. I am a British European, raised across Surrey—from South London to Woking, then Guildford.

Diagnosed at seven with Dyslexia and Dyscalculia, I’ve developed a forward-thinking approach to solving problems. Special Educational Needs support deeply matters to me.

In recent years, our Council services have struggled to meet today’s challenges: caring for the natural world, fostering self-reliant neighbourhoods, engaging differing views, strengthening our roads, ensuring clean waterways are free from privatised waste, and providing a healthy standard of living that doesn’t cost us our wages or the Earth.

Poor Conservative decisions and divisive politics should not define our future. Broader representation on West Surrey Council can realise our community values, together we can make real progress. I pledge to serve Shere and work closely with all six hardworking Parish Councils. Yesterday’s problems should not shape tomorrow’s opportunities.

I believe the Green Party stands for something more than the politics of the day and that is why I want to represent you. It refuses to cling to a status quo that is leaving our communities behind and wants to build a stronger foundation from which something new can grow, bringing us together rather than dividing us, whatever our differences.

I have lived in the Shere area for twenty-three years and am actively involved in sporting and cultural life here. I am a member and past volunteer with the Surrey Wildlife Trust, an organisation close to my heart. I worked in healthcare from 1983 until my retirement, ending my career at the Maudsley Hospital in London. Outside of that I am a keen gardener and grow my own fruit and vegetables.

Living where I do, I see close up the damage that poor farming practices and pesticide use are doing to our countryside and I feel strongly about it. The pollution of our waterways by privatised water companies is equally unacceptable to me.

**What I will work towards**

If elected I will:

- Push to hold water companies and sewage works to account. The River Wey has seen sewage dumps nearly one hundred times lasting over one thousand hours. That cannot go on
- Work to restrict pesticide use and challenge farming practices that damage our natural environment
- Seek to deliver more social housing with sustainable features and developments that genuinely work for the communities they are built in
- Make sure consultations with local people are properly heard and that developers stick to their agreements

I am proud to call this place home and I will work hard to protect everything that makes it special.

I am standing because I want to see my community unite around common sense policies for the benefit of all the people who are a part of it.

**What I will work towards**

If elected I will:

- Work to ensure our roads are properly maintained. Potholes are a real problem in our area because of expensive third-party contractors using poor quality materials. I will push to bring roadworks teams in-house and ensure repairs are carried out to a proper standard
- Work to protect local assets from being sold into private hands as we face the significant debt we will inherit from the way the boundaries of the new West Surrey Unitary have been drawn up
- Seek to introduce community municipal investment so local people can invest in their own area to fill our cash reserves and fund community projects

I am here and I am ready to work hard for you and this community.

I’m a portfolio educator and community connector, passionate helping people turn ideas into action.

With over 25 years in education, my work now brings together facilitation, community engagement and creative thinking. I run local events, support community projects and create spaces where people can connect, reflect and move forward with confidence.

My approach is simple: listen well, bring energy, and help people find their voice.

My name is Laura Barker and I’m standing as the Liberal Democrat candidate in the Staines by-election on the 16th of October.

Staines is my home: I have lived here for over a decade. There is little I enjoy more than walking my dog Penny by the river. However, it saddens me to see the polluted state of the water, which has occurred as a result of corporate greed. Cleaning up our rivers is one of the Liberal Democrats’ top priorities.

I love Staines. Sadly, empty units on the high street and anti-social behaviour are making it less attractive. Many people in our town don’t feel safe, especially women. This is why the Lib Dems want to invest more money into community policing. Despite the best efforts of fantastic community organisations like the Spelthorne Litter Pickers, littering also continues to be a significant problem in Staines. When an area looks run down and neglected, crime only escalates.

Having seen what my husband, Cllr. Harry Boparai, has achieved as a local councillor I would also like the opportunity to improve the lives of local residents. As a mother to three children who attend local state schools, I know the challenges young people and parents face in our area. Conservative cuts to youth services, to our libraries, community hubs and youth centres, have decimated opportunities for young people and damaged the social fabric of our nation.

This is why I am privileged to work for an organisation which uses the power of sport to transform the lives of young people. I have seen first hand the importance of positive role models and, if elected, I will push for Spelthorne Borough Council to do more in this area.

Climate change poses the greatest threat to the future of our planet. I am appalled at the complacency of the Conservative and Labour governments in tackling the climate change emergency. The Lib Dems form the largest group in the current administration at Spelthorne Council, but we do not yet have an outright majority.

The more Lib Dem councillors you elect, the greener Staines will become. You only need to look at neighbouring Lib Dem controlled Richmond to see what can be achieved.

Please consider casting your vote for me on the 16th of October. You can contact me at laurakbarker@gmail.com

With best wishes

Laura Barker

Hello, my name is **Simon Lightman**, and I am standing as a **Green Party candidate** because I believe local politics should be rooted in care, honesty and long-term responsibility.

I want to help build a council that listens properly to local people, protects the places we share, and makes decisions with future generations in mind. Too often, communities feel that things are done _to_ them rather than _with_ them. Whether the issue is housing, roads, public services, sewage, green spaces or support for young people, local people deserve a stronger voice in shaping the future of their area.

My professional life has been built around education, sustainability and helping young people become active citizens. I have worked with schools, charities and community organisations to support youth leadership, environmental action and more meaningful participation in decision-making. I believe those same principles matter in local government. We need practical, joined-up solutions that improve everyday life now while also preparing our communities for the challenges ahead.

**If elected, I would work for greener, fairer and more accountable local government.** That means:
- Protecting nature and improving community infrastructure
- Supporting families and young people
- Pushing for better environmental standards
- Making sure public money is used ethically and responsibly

For me, standing for the Green Party is _not just about the environment._ It is about building communities where people feel heard, where decisions are made transparently, and where the future is treated as something **we are responsible for together.**

Mark settled in Waverley with his family 15 years ago to continue a business career that had taken them to live and work around the world. He has been a passionate local community volunteer, charity trustee and school governor.

Over the last four years, Mark (right) has been the Waverley administration’s Finance portfolio-holder and, with substantial private sector business experience, he believes in basic financial competence. The Lib Dem-led council has balanced the budgets and maintained services with no cuts (and even supplemented them) despite unprecedented pressures. Mark will continue to speak out for areas like ours outside of Farnham’s town centre to be treated fairly.

These elections in May are for local government, but Farnham Town Council has wrestled with the impacts of wider issues like Brexit, Covid and inflation while maintaining, even expanding, its local events and facilities. It’s frustrating that the Council doesn’t have primary powers over most infrastructure, but we hold those who do to account.

Mark will continue speaking out against inappropriate development, and for the basics like road repairs and better from the Farnham Infrastructure Project. He work with all Councillors for Badshot Lea and Moor Park’s residents.

If elected on 7 May 2026 as an Independent, I’ll be guided by the following principles:
- Keep the council out of party politics.
- Protect our rural way of life.
- Help residents with their problems

My immediate priorities, based on what residents have told me most concerns them, are:
- Protecting local interests during the momentous changes to local government. In particular, fighting to minimise Woking Council’s debts being unloaded on to local residents.
- Campaigning to save our wonderful countryside and villages from reckless over-development.
- Curbing anti-social behaviour - fly-tipping, excess noise, litter, petty crime.
- Getting on top of pothole repairs!
- Opposing the expansion of Farnborough Airport - our skies are too noisy as it is.
- Opposing gimmicky projects that sound good  but waste money without providing real help to people.

I am standing for Waverley Western Villages because I care deeply about this community and I have already had the privilege of serving it. I was first elected to represent my neighbours in Binscombe in a by-election in 2021 and that experience has only strengthened my commitment to fighting for the people who live here.

I grew up in South Africa during the transition from Apartheid to democracy under Nelson Mandela and attended one of the country's first non-racial schools. That experience shaped my belief in social justice, democratic accountability and the idea that politics should genuinely serve people. I came to the UK for what was supposed to be a gap year and somehow never left. My husband and I moved to Binscombe in 2019 and it quickly became home. I currently teach in a secondary school in Woking and see every day the pressures that families are facing.

The state of our natural environment is a great concern for many of us and something I feel strongly about. Native species are in decline, ecosystems are being polluted and biodiversity is decreasing. I also see firsthand in my work the impact of underfunded schools and the struggle families face when the right support for their children is not there.

**What I will work towards**

If elected I will:

- Promote habitat restoration and create nature corridors to protect the biodiversity of our local area
- Ensure we have the right people and resources in place to manage our green spaces for everyone
- Make sure SEND provisions in our schools are properly funded so that no family has to fight for the support their child needs
- Help our communities grow closer together by supporting local initiatives for young people including sports, arts and culture
- Give greater support to our key workers and push to improve access to sustainable energy for all

This is a beautiful part of the world and I will dedicate myself to keeping it that way.

Attia Aslam has lived in Surrey for over 20 years and is a secondary school teacher with a lifelong commitment to education and community wellbeing. A Woking Borough Councillor, she also works with charities and serves as an outreach officer for the Surrey Coalition of Disabled People.

Attia founded the Angelic Network and leads health, inclusion and digital access projects locally. She is passionate about equality, supporting vulnerable residents and protecting local services for future generations.

Tahir Aziz lives and works in Woking, where he runs his own mortgage advice and property management company. He is an experienced councillor, having worked for residents for seven years and Leader of the Labour Group in Woking Borough Council. As a member of the Planning Committee, he has consistently stood up for the rights of residents, campaigning for affordable homes and against overdevelopment of the town centre. He has also proposed reform of Woking Borough Council’s debt collection practices, campaigning for reduced use of bailiffs.

Cllr Anila Javaid is Labour’s candidate for Woking North and a Borough Councillor for Canalside. She is Chairman of Woking Labour and has spent over 20 years building and leading 7tnine Developments, a UK-based consultancy delivering business innovation, transformation, and performance improvement across the UK and internationally.
Anila brings a practical, evidence-led approach to public service: clear priorities, budget discipline, and a focus on outcomes residents can actually feel. Since being elected in 2023, she has supported hundreds of resident cases, working with residents, officers, and community partners to resolve problems and improve local services.
Her priorities are rooted in a simple principle: a fair deal for Woking. That means stronger negotiation on behalf of residents, better scrutiny of proposals, and transparent decision-making — particularly in areas where contracts and delivery arrangements shape everyday life, including waste and street services, housing management, regeneration programmes, and the IT systems behind access to support.
As Woking moves into a new unitary authority, Anila believes it is more important than ever to have representatives who will show up, ask the hard questions, and insist on measurable performance from delivery partners. Her commitment is to listen, act, and deliver — with integrity, accountability, and public money treated as precious.

Zafar Rasab has lived in Woking North since 1987 and attended local schools. Through running a general store and estate agency, he has helped generations of residents settle into the area and supported many community initiatives. Actively involved in local projects, Zafar is committed to strengthening community ties, supporting young people and promoting sustainable living. He wants to ensure Woking North remains a welcoming, connected and forward-looking place for families and local businesses.

Louise Morales was first elected to Woking Council in 2011 and Surrey County Council in 2025. She has served as Mayor, Chair of Planning and now Portfolio Holder for Planning Policy and sits on the Surrey County Council and Woking Borough Council planning Committees.

She is committed to improving planning, sustainability and active travel, and to shaping fair, future-focused policies for the new West Surrey Council.

Peter Graves has served as a Pyrford councillor for four years and was a member of the council executive with responsibility for waste management and green infrastructure. Peter is part of a great team for Woking South East, along with Ellen Nicholson.

My name is Ben Edward Maynard and I am standing to represent the Conservatives in Woking South East in the new West Surrey Unitary area.

I lived in Pyrford for 38 years and attended Pyrford First and Middle school and currently run my Domiciliary care agency in the area, a job i love, caring for the elderly every day.

I'm passionate about Woking south east and it would be a privilege to be their representative. Fixing the pot holes and protecting the green belt are just two of my top priorities. Ellen Nicholson is a Liberal Democrat candidate for the Woking South East Division to the new West Surrey Unitary Council on the 7th May 2026. Ellen is a successful NHS professional who lives locally, who uses her experience of getting things done from her professional expertise, as a councillor, a local hospital governor and former director of a SME, to deliver on the issues that matter most to residents.

"I love Surrey. I’m proud to live here. I moved to the UK from Poland with my family almost a decade ago and I couldn't have asked for a better home than Woking. From a teen that couldn't speak English, I am now a writer, tutor, volunteer, event organiser and law student - including administrative law.

I am standing as the Labour and Co-operative candidate for Pyrford because I believe the Liberal Democrat and Conservative Councillors, distracted by the huge debt they have created, are failing to listen to the residents and businesses of Pyrford. I’d like to give the residents of Woking a choice at this election.

The government has given us record taxation, debt and relies on immigration rather than training up the next generation.

All the globalist Westminster parties are pushing us down the road of conflict in Eastern Europe.

I am standing for the Heritage Party as I believe it offers something different. Socially conservative, government limited to what it needs to do, and guided by our Heritage of Christian values.

I'm a chartered Chemical Engineer with a background in operations, design and software. This gives me a strong view on the coming man made energy crisis, which is driving up the cost of living.

Its also time we had accountability for the disaster that has befallen Woking Borough Council with its financial ruin. In the end, central government is responsible for the lending of that money and should adopt the debt.

Be clear on the signal you want to send.

Woking-born Leslie Rice is proud of his hometown and works closely with residents on planning and Green Belt issues, pushing for environmentally responsible, community-led decisions. Residents tell us all the time that we need to fix our roads. That’s why I’m standing with Scott Lewis to deliver real improvements for Woodham, Row Town, and New Haw. I’ve worked locally to support our community, listening to concerns on transport, safety, and protecting our green spaces.

I have been a Councillor for over 10 years, representing Woodham, New Haw and Row Town at Surrey and Runnymede Borough Council. I am committed to community engagement, supporting local initiatives and ensuring residents’ voices are reflected in decision-making.

I’m Ronan McCaughey and I’m asking people in Woodham, Row Town and New Haw to vote for me on 7 May because I care deeply about our community.

I'm proud to be running as your Labour & Co-op candidate for Runnymede’s local elections on the 2nd of May 2024.    I am a father of two, and a member of my children's school’s PTA. Being there to support residents of Egham Hythe is what your Labour councillors Robert King & Rhys Davies have been doing and I want to support their vital work, especially as we have all been let down by the Conservative's years of financial mismanagement at Runnymede.

Chelsea has been a consistent volunteer and campaigner for local organisations, including volunteering full-time at the Runnymede food bank during the Covid-19 pandemic after losing her job because of Brexit. I have represented the residents of Worplesdon ward on Guildford Borough Council since being elected in 2023, and I currently serve as the Conservative Deputy Group Leader. Jason Martin cares about local communities, helping vulnerable people, giving people a voice and opportunities. While others may dismiss certain ideas, policies or plans, Jason will communicate and think through them with the both people involved and those that it would effect to ensure that the best outcome happens.
He cares about young and vulnerable people, especially in these times, when they are at risk of being left behind or forgotten in council, Jason will give them a voice. Hello, my name is Alex and I am standing as a Green Party candidate because I believe they are the best option to represent our local areas here in Guildford and Waverley.

I have been based around Guildford for the past nine years. I came from a career as a Navy aircraft engineer and now work in HR. I love the beautiful scenery and all of the stunning walks here. I also enjoy playing board games and running Dungeons and Dragons games in my free time, including for a non-profit.

The Green Party have a long history of fighting to preserve our beautiful natural spaces but we also have a strong sense of moral justice.

**What I will work towards**

If elected I will:

- Hold water companies and sewage works to account. **The River Wey has seen sewage dumps nearly one hundred times.** That cannot go on and we need to monitor it closely
- Fight to protect our local assets from being sold into private ownership as a result of the huge debt we will inherit from the recent regional restructure
- Ensure we continue to invest in our community and our infrastructure
- Push for more regular and reliable bus services so everyone can get around without a car

**Why vote Green?**

A Green Party councillor is free to make choices in the best interest of their constituents and is not bound by party leadership like all of the other major parties. So, if you want someone to represent you and your community, vote Green!

I am standing because as a local I am fully aware of the issues that affect the lives of each of us every day and if elected I will do my part to address those most important to you.

I work in a special needs school and see firsthand how beneficial having the right resources in place can be for children and their families. I also study at Merrist Wood which is right here in the area and that connection to this community matters to me deeply.

**What I will work towards**

If elected I will:

- Work to ensure that SEND provisions in our schools are properly funded and supported. Parents of children with special educational needs should not have to fight tooth and nail for even small amounts of help. I will work to make sure that support is there where it is needed and adapted to the needs of each child and their family
- Seek to help our communities grow closer together again by tackling anti-social behaviour and providing more community initiatives and leisure options such as sports, arts and culture events
- Work to give greater support to our key workers
- Push to improve access to sustainable energy through green skills training and building the right infrastructure

I love this area and I want to play my part in making it the best it can be for everyone who lives here.

I have worked and lived in the Worthing Area for the last 25 years. Only Reform UK has clear fully costed policies to protect and strengthen our Armed Forces and Veteran Community, protecting our borders by controlled immigration, and safeguarding our children by banning Transgender ideology being pushed in our schools.

The Conservatives are tired and have run out of ideas, the Labour Party simply has no idea, and, as we have seen in Worthing, would not stand up for ordinary people, or our traditions, instead opting to rewrite history to suit the fringe minority groups.

It is time for our Country to have a Fresh Start, and only the Reform UK Party can deliver that, so please lend me your vote to enable all of us to thrive.

statement_to_voters:
Statement for WSCC Elections 2026
This election is for a Councillor to serve for the last two years of the County Council before it is replaced by a Unitary Authority in 2028. There will be separate elections for that council next year. Ensuring that there is a smooth transition into the new council, with no interruption to our local services, will be challenging.  As your current County Councillor, I am asking for your vote on the 7th May so that I can complete this important work.

If re-elected, I will continue to work for:
•	Proper repairs to potholes and resurfacing as an alternative to patching.
•	Better enforcement to stop fly-tipping, anti-social parking and speeding on rural    rat runs.
•	Reduced congestion at the Felbridge junction and along the A22.
•	Investment in the town centre and more effective use of the financial contributions from developers to provide new community buildings and sports facilities.
•	The relocation of Imberhorne Middle School to Imberhorne Lane
•	Timely completion of Special Educational Needs assessments and delivery of the support recommended
•	A strategic approach to new housing that respects our Neighbourhood Plans, delivers the necessary new infrastructure and protects our countryside and heritage buildings.

As an Independent Councillor I don’t have to follow a party line, I am free to decide every issue on its merits and to work with other parties to implement the policies and services which are in your best interests.

I grew up in Scarborough and came South to read Physics at the University of Kent.  I studied molecular liquids for my PhD using the experimental reactors at Harwell and the Institute Laue Langevin in Grenoble.  After completing my thesis I joined the MOD working on the development of new land and air systems at Fort Halstead and Farnborough.  My work included the development of combat simulations to support procurement decisions.  I became a Fellow of the Institute of Physics in 1999 and transferred to the DTI to lead a review of the Research Councils and Project Manage the successful £250M Diamond Synchrontron  bid to Treasury.  I attended the Royal College of Defence Studies  in 2003 and my final appointment was as Director for Space Technology and Industrial Policy in the forerunner of the UK Space Agency.

I initially became involved in local government to help prepare the Crawley Down Neighbourhood Plan. I was elected to Mid Sussex District Council in 2019 and re-elected in 2023.   I lead the Council's Independent Group and have been the Cabinet portfolio holder for Sustainable Economy and Housing in a joint Lib Dem/Independent administration for the past 3 years. I was also elected to West Sussex County Council in 2021 as an Independent for East Grinstead and Crawley Down. At WSCC, I sit on the Performance and Finance Scrutiny Committee and the Planning Committee.  I am also a member of East Grinstead Town Council so I am the elected representative for my residents across all three tiers of local government.  This means that my residents can bring any problem with local government to me.  The problems that my residents seek my help for most are the lack of doctors appointments, the quality of social housing,  delays in the processing of EHCPs, and insufficient school places.  I have seen the anxiety that these problems create and improving these services is a priority for me.

As an amateur astronomer, I appreciate the value of pristine, unpolluted skies. Unfortunately, the South Downs Dark Skies Reserve appears to exist only on paper, as increasing levels of light pollution wash out our view of the Milky Way and disturb nocturnal fauna.

Light pollution does not respect boundaries. Even if lighting within the South Downs National Park is well controlled, skyglow from surrounding towns brightens the night sky across the entire region. In March this year, West Sussex County Council announced a £24 million spend on new street lighting, claiming to have considered light pollution while relying on specifications that use 4000K “cool white” LEDs — bluer than recommended for dark sky areas and operating at wavelengths known to increase skyglow. I’m a local man who understands local people and I have the skills to do the job. I'm from Storrington. I have lived here for several years. As your West Sussex County councillor, I'll get even more done for our area.

I am always free to speak up for local residents. Unlike other parties, the Green Party doesn't tell councillors how to vote. I can always put you ahead of party politics and stand up for what's right for Storrington, Sullington, Cootham, Amberley, Ashington, Washington, Parham and Wiston.

You face an important choice this May. The truth is, the old parties you've perhaps always voted for can't win round here this time.

I can win here in Storrington division. At the last local elections, the Greens won first place in Storrington. The Conservatives, Lib Dems and Labour don’t have enough support to win here, so it’ll be a clear, two-horse race between me and Reform this time.

After over 30 years of Education and Leadership I want to stand and deliver for the people of Tarring. I strongly believe that we have a duty to look after local people and ensure our council tax is used efficiently to improve services and the area we live in.

Cloe is a Worthing resident whose work and life is rooted in community work. She works in Learning Disabilities and has volunteered for various initiatives such as after school clubs. She believes the people of Tarring deserve better representation. The community in Tarring deserves to have its green spaces protected, functioning and safe roads, support for the vulnerable and someone who uplifts their voices.

Vote for Cloe if you want someone who cares for the community in Tarring.

Tarring’s voice won’t be lost or forgotten with Cloe.

As someone who grew up locally on a small holding in Sidlesham, Andrew knows the value of local farming and horticulture. He feels privileged to live in such a beautiful part of the country, enjoys sailing in Chichester harbour and swimming in the sea at the Witterings. Andrew is passionate about conserving the diversity of our natural environment and hopes we can keep it that way for future generations to enjoy.

“I’m tired of seeing politicians talking about ‘cutting costs’ when ‘costs’ are essential public services like refuse collection, road maintenance, and schools. Three Bridges is the heart of Crawley. I have lived in Crawley for over 40 years and have a wonderful family of 2 beautiful girls and a son who now lives in Japan.

Since I arrived in Crawley my vision was to settle down and retire in the town that has given me the most. During this period I have operated several businesses in the area, most of them had direct contact with the local residents. I understand the pressing needs of residents.

As I am very passionate about the community and the Town I will work very hard to promote positive change needed to improve the community.

In my final 5 working years I have worked in Local Government and understand the operations of the local council and this will speed up any changes required for the community.

I am looking forward to serving the community of Crawley.

James is a freelance musician living in Balcombe. He is the Choir Director at Holy Trinity, Hurstpierpoint, as well as a composer and theatre musical director. He is a passionate advocate for the arts and committed to creating inclusive creative and cultural opportunities, something he has worked towards in recent years as an arts charity trustee.

Previously a full-time teacher, he has an understanding of the specific challenges facing parents and teachers, particularly in the area of SEND provision. He has run outreach projects to several primary and secondary schools and has experienced first-hand the need for better funding and facilities, particularly in supporting the facilitation of individual skills and interests.

His professional training includes Keeping Children Safe in Education and other aspects of child safety and protection, first aid and fire safety, and courses on ADHD, mental wellbeing in children and young people, and online safety.

“I’m standing as the Green Party candidate for Worth Forest because I care deeply about our community and the future we’re building together here in West Sussex. Too often, local voices are overlooked while decisions are made without enough focus on long-term sustainability or the everyday needs of residents. I want to change that by championing practical, people-focused solutions—protecting our local environment, improving transport links, supporting community services, and ensuring development works for everyone. I believe in listening to residents, so that together we can create a healthier, fairer, and more resilient Worth Forest.”

With nearly a decade of unwavering commitment to the Green movement, I’m standing in East Worthing to offer a beacon of principled politics and genuine hope. I have a degree in Politics and International Relations and have spent years volunteering for causes I believe in. I want to be that alternative for the people of East Worthing — representing the area with compassion, force and an unwavering commitment to those I represent.

Natasha grew up in Worthing, and studied at Davison High School and Worthing Sixth Form, before leaving to study and work internationally. Having spent many years working in the private sector, including senior management roles I bring a strong track record of leadership, accountability, and delivery.

My top priorities are:
•	Revitalising the town centre, celebrating local heritage, and protecting small businesses
•	Improving the condition of our roads
•	Tackling crime, antisocial behaviour, and shoplifting

Only Reform UK is offering the bold change needed locally. 
Labour tried to take away your democratic right to vote - Lend me your vote to make real positive changes for all of Worthing.

I have been living in West Worthing for eight years and am passionate about the local area and what it has to offer the local residents – if only it was cared for by the people in charge of building its fairer communities, keeping its water supplies clean, fixing the potholes, and keeping Worthing a safe town for future generations to grow up in. As someone who has two jobs and still worries about paying the bills on time every month, I know the challenges and worries of everyday life and will work my hardest to keep this town special and help it grow.

Martin McCabe was born and raised in Worthing, Martin's goals are simple: to empower our community and demand a better politics that puts people first. A Building Engineer and lecturer, Martin is obsessed with making sure that politicians get the details right.

Martin has a strong record of standing up for local people. In 2018, he helped a local special needs charity find a new home so its work could continue. He has raised funds for local disability and women's football teams and campaigned for a People's Vote on Brexit. In May 2019, he is running the 100km London to Brighton ultra marathon to raise money for West Sussex Mind. Martin is the Chairman of the Adur and Worthing Liberal Democrats and our candidate for Tarring ward in the 2019 Worthing Council Elections.

I am standing in the Marine Ward by-election for Worthing Borough Council, held on Thursday 19 September. 

Having grown up in Worthing, I deeply cherish our town and feel grateful every day to live by the seaside. Whether it is the year-on-year increases in Council Tax or the lack of street cleaning in our local area, I know that Worthing is being let down by Labour. We need a Council that delivers for residents and if elected I will work every day to ensure that the Council works for you.

I'm a 30 year old Mathematician and Aerospace Engineer, I never saw myself as somebody who would run for office, but when I moved to Tyldesley a couple years back and started getting involved locally there and in Astley, I was floored by the controversy surrounding the Astley Warehouses and attempts to destroy the Greenbelt. Astley is a beautiful area full of amazing people, and having seen the awful ignorance from the council, I cannot simply stand by and let it happen. I aim to work with residents on the most pressing issues, to make sure Astley remains beautiful and that our voices do not continue to go unheard!

Hi! My name is Ashley Trigg, and I am the Green Party Candidate for Leigh Central and Higher Folds, a ward I have called home for the past 8 years!

I wanted to take this opportunity to tell you a little more about me, why I'm here and why I am running for council in the upcoming elections on **MAY 7th**.

I have been interested in politics for over a decade, after studying economics at A-level in college, despite hardly knowing was it was (I wanted to escape my physics class and economics was one of the only things I could move to in that time slot!).

Despite this interest, I never actively engaged in political activity. The two party system and the state of politics overall left me completely disillusioned, so I used my time to instead to focus on my career, where I now work as a Data Architect in the financial services industry. More recently, I have used my free time to get involved with volunteering, becoming a trustee of two charities as well as getting involved in several committees within the British Computer Society (BCS), the UK's chartered IT institute.

However, times are challenging. The Conservatives performed so poorly that the 2024 election saw a massive swing towards Labour, who have also let everyone down. A worsening cost of living crisis, a crumbling NHS, rising hate crimes and silence on international conflicts, not to mention a lack of environmental safeguarding following the rise of AI... Something has to be done.

Thankfully, the Green Party of England and Wales have stepped up to the plate following the election of Zack as leader, and we are now one of the largest parties in the UK with over 216,000 members. Our policies are offer the radical change  that this country desperately needs, and our people come from all walks of life with the intention to change our country for the better.

So I decided it was time to get involved and be a part of the change we sorely needed. I started by relaunching the Young Greens North West and building an amazing committee of Young Greens across the region, where we now lead over 6000 members across the region. Then, earlier this year, I was elected to the committee of Wigan and Leigh Green Party alongside another group of amazing volunteers.

So when it came time to elect candidates for the May 7th elections, I knew I just had to put my name forward for my ward, Leigh Central and Higher Folds. I have seen the struggles our town faces; litter in our streets, antisocial behaviour in our town centre, our amazing heritage buildings be left to rot or burn down. We recently received £12m investment for our town, but all that has gone towards to far is ripping up the road outside of our town hall to make the space look a little nicer in hopes that it will attract more people to the area. It's not enough.

Labour have let the country down, and our Labour council have let Wigan and Leigh down. The warehouses in Astley are a huge reminder that Wigan Council do not listen to or care much for this side of the borough, and people are looking for a change.
We have amazing Green Party candidates across all the seats in Wigan & Leigh, who are ready to hold Labour accountable for their actions.

I am not a politician, so you can believe me when I say that I will listen to the people of my ward and do everything I can to improve life for Leythers, support our local business, improve our town centre and protect our heritage buildings. Leigh must not be forgotten about and left behind.

Please feel free to contact me with your concerns about our area, I'd love to hear more about what I can do to help made a difference.

Yours Sincerely,
Ashley Trigg
